questions.question: Did Dennis expect people to remember the first age in spiritual bodies?

questions.question: Did Dennis expect the two witnesses before Antichrist?

questions.question: Did Dennis give a definite date for antichrist’s appearance?

questions.question: Did Dennis include the United States in the one-world system?

questions.question: Did Dennis place Job in the first earth age?

questions.question: Did Dennis regard God’s divorce of Israel as preventing all future restoration?

questions.question: How did Arnold distinguish the hour of temptation from ten-day trials?

answers.summary: Arnold calls the hour the whole five-month period and the ten days an individual trial limit. The precise Revelation reference is recalled approximately and remains pending confirmation.

Arnold placed Revelation 2:10’s imprisonment and trial in the future testimony before the false messiah. He interpreted ten days as an individual limit, distinguished it from the broader national period and said the Holy Spirit supplies the testimony.

questions.question: How did Arnold distinguish the political beast system from the antichrist?

answers.summary: Arnold describes the many heads as government systems and says the deadly wound affects the political peace system rather than one individual. He then places the dragon’s appearance and restoration of peace in his interpretation of Revelation 13.

Arnold says the prospective peace system is wounded before fully coming into effect. He connects the expectation with Revelation 13:4 and distinguishes its preparation from the false Christ’s arrival.

questions.question: How did Arnold distinguish translation from transliteration?

answers.summary: Arnold describes transliteration as representing sounds with another alphabet and translation as conveying meaning. He illustrates the distinction with the name Moses and the meaning drawn from water.
Arnold uses Moses, meaning drawn from the water, to illustrate the distinction he makes between carrying a name’s letters into another language and explaining its meaning.

questions.question: How did Arnold encourage someone told he could never learn?

answers.summary: Arnold rejects the discouraging label and encourages studying Scripture’s patterns and simplicity. He says disability does not eliminate the ability to learn.

Arnold reassured a learner that love for God and sincere effort matter without matching a teacher’s knowledge. He said God gives gifts and expects according to what is given, and that the Holy Spirit supplies testimony if delivered up.

questions.question: How did Arnold explain a believer’s authority over Satan?

answers.summary: Arnold cites Luke 10:19 and says believers have authority in Christ’s name rather than being powerless before Satan. This reports his spiritual teaching without verifying any individual claim of supernatural interference.
Arnold reads Luke 10:19 with the preceding and following thoughts. He emphasizes authority in Christ’s name but says being called and knowing the truth is a greater reason for gratitude.

questions.question: How did Arnold explain Acts 2:34 saying David did not ascend into heaven?

answers.summary: Arnold distinguishes David’s flesh body returning to dust from his soul returning to God. He contrasts this with what he calls Christ’s transfiguration and relates the passage to Psalm 110.
Arnold distinguishes David’s flesh body remaining in the grave from the soul’s condition and contrasts it with Christ’s risen body. He also mentions the separation of soul and spirit in Hebrews.

questions.question: How did Arnold explain casting pearls before swine?

answers.summary: Arnold compares truth to seed and says not to keep forcing it on people who reject it rudely. He encourages seeking receptive listeners and leaving growth to God.
Arnold warns that repeatedly pressing an unreceptive listener can do harm. He recommends offering a thought and allowing interest and understanding to develop.

questions.question: How did Arnold explain determining John the Baptist’s birth season?

answers.summary: Arnold linked it with Zechariah’s course of Abijah, gave June dates for the course and conception, and placed birth nine months afterward. He recommended a Christmas study. Those exact dates are his calculation, not verified historical dates.

Arnold corrected the listener: there were twenty-four courses, with Abia the eighth, rather than twenty-four courses of Abia. He directed the listener to 1 Chronicles 24:10. This answer identifies the course but does not calculate a complete birth calendar.

questions.question: How did Arnold explain familiar spirits?

answers.summary: Arnold identifies familiar spirits as demonic or evil spirits and points to the account of the woman at Endor in 1 Samuel 28. He says the phrase occurs in several biblical passages.

Arnold said a familiar spirit could impersonate a dead person in the Endor account. He also allowed that God could have permitted the real person to appear to teach Saul, leaving that possibility open in this answer.

questions.question: How did Arnold explain giants after Noah’s flood?

answers.summary: Arnold said the offspring he called Geber died in the flood and attributed later giants to a second influx of fallen angels or Nephilim. He referred to a Companion Bible appendix without remembering its number. The captions render the term imperfectly; this is his doctrinal explanation, not verified ancestry.
Dennis explains them through a second influx of fallen angels. He also warns of a future third influx and connects Paul’s warning about angels with the need for Christ’s protection.

questions.question: How did Arnold explain italic words in the KJV?

answers.summary: Arnold described italics as marking words supplied by translators to carry the sense into English. He urged care with such additions and recommended reading the translators’ prefatory letter and consulting the Companion Bible.
Dennis explains that they identify words supplied by translators to assist English reading rather than words directly present in the original-language text.

questions.question: How did Arnold explain memory surviving the death of the brain?

answers.summary: Arnold distinguishes the physical brain from the spirit, which he describes as a person’s intellect. He says that intellect returns to God and refers to Ecclesiastes 12:6–7.
Dennis interprets the dead knowing nothing in Ecclesiastes 9:5 as the dead flesh rather than loss of the soul’s memory and says remembered conduct is necessary for fair judgment.

questions.question: How did Arnold explain returning to the first works in Revelation 2?

answers.summary: Arnold describes renewed love and service to God rather than identifying it with only the first commandment. He contrasts that with teachings he considers human traditions.
Dennis applies the instruction to the church at Ephesus that left its first love. He interprets first works as studying God’s Word, the starting point for serving and pleasing Him.

questions.question: How did Arnold explain ruddy complexion?

answers.summary: Arnold described it as showing blood in the face, such as blushing or exertion, and directed the listener to the Hebrew entry he associated with Adam. This records his word study without drawing conclusions about any person’s value or status.

Arnold defended his use of ruddy complexion when discussing Adam and Eve, appealing to the Hebrew word Adam rather than the listener’s proposed English wording. This preserves his interpretation without treating complexion as proof of a modern racial classification.

questions.question: How did Arnold explain Satan’s final destruction?

answers.summary: Arnold cited Ezekiel 28:17–18 and Matthew 10:28 and described final destruction as ceasing to exist rather than endless conscious torment. He also said remembrance would end. These are his interpretations.
Dennis interprets Satan’s everlasting fate as final destruction of the soul, relating Revelation 20 to Ezekiel 28:18–19.

questions.question: How did Arnold explain Satan’s temple when asked about a physical building?

answers.summary: Arnold interpreted Satan’s temple as his many-membered body of deceived followers, paralleling his explanation of Christ’s temple. He did not promise construction of a physical building in three days.
Asked again how Satan could stand in a temple if none existed, Arnold referred back to the temple of followers he had just described. The chapter reference recalled in the captions is uncertain.

Arnold welcomed the listener’s proposal that deceived believers could form the temple in which antichrist appears, calling it a good thought he may not have considered before. He did not present it as an established exclusive interpretation.

questions.question: How did Arnold explain Shekinah glory?

answers.summary: Arnold explains Shekinah as God dwelling there. He does not accept the questioner’s description of it simply as an unpleasant burning fire for sinners.

Arnold spelled the captioned term S-H-E-C-A-N-I-A-H and explained it as God dwelling there, giving Strong’s 7935 and 31. That stated spelling and lexical identification remain flagged instead of silently replacing them with a different word or entry.

questions.question: How did Arnold explain the continued presence of those he called Kenites?

answers.summary: Arnold placed them within the negative side of his interpretation of testing in this age and linked the outcome to Genesis 3:15. This disputed theological ancestry claim is recorded for study, not endorsed or assigned to present individuals or populations. Parts of the listener’s terminology are inaudible in the captions.

Arnold appealed to 1 Chronicles 2:55 and John 8 in arguing that the people he called Kenites continued after the flood. His ancestry and record-keeping accusations are unverified doctrinal claims and do not establish an identity for modern people.

questions.question: How did Arnold explain the dead know not anything in Ecclesiastes?

answers.summary: Arnold applies the statement to the deceased flesh body rather than the spiritual body. He connects it with Ecclesiastes 12 and the spirit returning to God. One verse number is misstated in the captions and is not used as a precise citation.

Arnold read Ecclesiastes 9’s dead language as concerning the flesh body returning to dust, while the person continues in a spiritual body with the Father under his reading of Ecclesiastes 12:6–7. He did not separately establish that the deceased watch everything on earth.

questions.question: How did Arnold explain the name Jesus?

answers.summary: Arnold traces Jesus to Yeshua and gives Yahoveh’s Savior or God’s Savior as its meaning.
Arnold gives Yeshua, Yahoveh’s Savior, as the meaning behind Jesus.

questions.question: How did Arnold explain the people in the graves in John 5:28–29?

answers.summary: Arnold connected the passage with Christ preaching to those who had died before him, interpreting them as souls in paradise across the gulf rather than bodies awaiting an opportunity in the ground. He said some accepted that preaching.

Asked about John 5:28–29, Arnold connected it with people appearing after Christ’s death and said they were spiritual rather than flesh bodies, visible as evidence that Christ defeated death. His example of a local shopkeeper was an illustration, not a named biblical person. The connection between the question’s passage and his explanation remains flagged.

questions.question: How did Arnold explain the purpose of raising Lazarus?

answers.summary: Arnold agreed that Lazarus’s raising demonstrated Christ’s power over death, then connected the crucifixion and torn temple veil with access to God. His exact captioned Corinthians verse number for the victory-over-death language remains held rather than corrected.
Arnold says Lazarus was with the Father and presents his restoration as a demonstration of Christ’s victory over death.

questions.question: How did Arnold explain the Sabbath-day journey in an end-time warning?

answers.summary: Arnold described it as a limited journey under Hebrew law and said such a short distance would be insufficient to flee Jerusalem in the warning he was discussing. His distance estimate is reported as his explanation, not a modern travel restriction.
Dennis relates the warning about flight on the Sabbath in Matthew 24 to restricted travel in that setting and urges fleeing Judea when the desolator appears.

questions.question: How did Arnold explain the Tower of Babel?

answers.summary: Arnold directed the listener to Genesis 11 and interpreted the tower as an attempt at self-provided protection after the flood. He extended the warning to a hypothetical attempt at immortality through cloning; that extension is his speculation, not established science.
Arnold points to Genesis 11 and says people tried to build toward heaven for security, after which God scattered them.

questions.question: How did Arnold explain using the name Jesus when Hebrew has no letter J?

answers.summary: Arnold explains that English and Hebrew use different letters and pronunciations, giving Yeshua as the Hebrew form. He says teachers should speak in a language their audience understands.

Arnold explained that Jesus and Jehovah were English forms and gave Hebrew pronunciations as his alternatives. He did not treat use of the English name in prayer as invalid merely because Hebrew lacks the letter J.

questions.question: How did Arnold explain what happened to Jesus’ flesh body?

answers.summary: Arnold describes it as transfigured rather than left in the tomb. He uses the transfiguration account as support and distinguishes Christ’s case from ordinary flesh returning to dust.
Arnold describes Christ’s risen body as transfigured and relates it to the mount of transfiguration with Moses and Elijah.

questions.question: How did Arnold explain women being covered by Christ?

answers.summary: Arnold interprets the covering as knowledge of God’s word and protection against deception, linking it with the seal in Revelation 9:4 rather than a physical veil alone.
Arnold interprets the covering in 1 Corinthians 11:10 as Christ and scriptural knowledge protecting against deception by fallen angels.

questions.question: How did Arnold explain “our image” in Genesis?

answers.summary: Arnold distinguishes the plural wording in Genesis 1:26 from verse 27 and relates the discussion to Jesus’ statement about seeing the Father in John 14.

Arnold interpreted our image as God addressing his children and including his own coming in Christ. He described mature spiritual bodies as not aging or becoming sick. This records his interpretation rather than a demonstrated description of bodies.

questions.question: How did Arnold identify Michael the archangel?

answers.summary: Arnold directed the listener to Daniel 10 and 12, described Michael as Israel’s chief prince and God’s servant, and rejected identifying Michael as Christ. He warned against angel worship and distinguished archangels from Christ’s birth through a woman.

Asked about Daniel 12:1–2, Arnold described Michael as Israel’s protecting archangel and as restraining Satan. He referred to Revelation 12:6–7 and anticipated Satan and his angels being cast down as part of his false-messiah teaching. He did not separately explain Daniel 12:2’s resurrection language.

questions.question: How did Arnold interpret 2 Thessalonians 2:7?

answers.summary: Arnold identifies the restrained figure as the antichrist, held by Michael in heaven until being cast to earth. He refers to the surrounding verses and Revelation 12.

Arnold identified Michael and his angels as the restrainer while saying the Comforter remains present. He separately suggested Michael was the other protecting cherub and explicitly called that an educated guess without proof.

questions.question: How did Arnold interpret blood offerings in Ezekiel’s millennial chapters?

answers.summary: Arnold says Christ’s blood sacrifice was once for all and interprets the offerings as sacrificial love, pointing to Hosea 6:6.
Arnold interprets Ezekiel’s millennial offerings as love rather than flesh sacrifices, because he expects spiritual bodies then.

questions.question: How did Arnold interpret Eve being made from Adam’s rib?

answers.summary: Arnold interprets the word rendered rib as a curve and connects it with a feminine DNA helix. This is his stated interpretation, not an independently verified scientific or linguistic conclusion.

Arnold interprets the word rendered rib as a curve and proposes that it refers to a feminine component of Adam’s DNA used to form Eve. This preserves his stated belief rather than presenting it as verified Hebrew scholarship or genetics.

questions.question: How did Arnold interpret Isaiah 53’s description of Christ’s appearance?

answers.summary: Arnold interprets Isaiah 53:2 as describing Christ as beautiful and lacking nothing, and relates seeing Christ to seeing the Father in John 14.
Arnold interprets Isaiah 53 as describing Christ as beautiful and lacking nothing.

questions.question: How did Arnold interpret meeting Jesus in the air?

answers.summary: Arnold interpreted air as breath of life and meeting Christ in a spiritual body rather than flying into the sky. He connected this with the change in 1 Corinthians 15:52. This is his linguistic and scriptural interpretation.

Dennis reads the subject as the state of the dead and interprets air as the breath of life, associating it with the change to spiritual bodies. He says Christ comes to earth and rejects a fly-away interpretation.

questions.question: How did Arnold interpret the common origin of nations in Acts 17:26?

answers.summary: Arnold claims the original means one clay rather than one blood and links that with his separate-creation teaching. This is an unverified linguistic and ancestry claim, not established textual scholarship or genetics.

Arnold argues that clay or dust rather than blood is intended in Acts 17:26. His manuscript and Greek claims are not independently established; the FAQ does not adopt them as textual or genetic facts.

questions.question: How did Arnold interpret the mansions or abiding places in John 14?

answers.summary: Arnold understood the prepared place as rest and peace through the Holy Spirit, with the Father and Son abiding in believers. He urged reading beyond verse 4; the Greek term is first misstated and then corrected in the captions, so no exact Greek spelling is supplied here.

Arnold interpreted golden streets as spiritual purity and mansion as a resting or abiding place, connecting John 14 with God dwelling with believers through the Comforter. He said this rest could be experienced now, while also discussing the millennium and eternity. These are his interpretations.

questions.question: How did Arnold interpret the oil and wine in Revelation 6:6?

answers.summary: Arnold interprets the oil through anointing imagery and the wine through Christ’s blood. He treats the instruction not to hurt them as protecting the teaching amid scarcity. This is his symbolic reading.
Arnold corrected the listener’s blood-or-oil wording to oil and wine. He associated the oil with anointing and the wine with Christ’s blood and communion, saying they should not be interfered with.

questions.question: How did Arnold interpret the rest of the dead in Revelation 20:5?

answers.summary: Arnold describes them as spiritually dead but conscious in spiritual bodies with mortal souls. He says they can be taught through the millennium and face judgment afterward. The captioned Greek terms require confirmation.

Arnold distinguished those who had already overcome from those he believed would receive teaching during the millennium because they lacked an opportunity to understand. The captions concerning the overcomers’ part are awkward and should not be used to assert their absence from millennium service.

questions.question: How did Arnold interpret the sea giving up the dead in Revelation 20:13?

answers.summary: Arnold interpreted the sea as people and the dead as spiritually dead in spiritual bodies. He placed the passage at the later resurrection and Great White Throne judgment, distinguishing the second death as death of the soul. These are his interpretations.
Arnold refers back to Revelation 17 and interprets the sea as people, including those spiritually dead, rather than people buried at sea.

questions.question: How did Arnold reassure a listener about small children during antichrist’s appearance?

answers.summary: Arnold said an innocent child would be fine and described antichrist as arriving in the role of a savior rather than openly attacking children. He warned that the danger he had in mind was deception and loss of the soul. This is his prophetic interpretation.
Arnold says God judges fairly and does not take advantage of babies’ innocence or a person’s disability, emphasizing an opportunity to understand.

questions.question: How did Arnold reassure a listener struggling to understand the Bible?

answers.summary: Arnold says his remark about a child understanding is not meant to belittle anyone, and encourages relaxing, resting in Christ and listening to Scripture rather than accumulated teachings.
Arnold encourages steady study without strain, keeping Christ’s teaching simple rather than letting human traditions complicate it.

questions.question: How did Arnold reassure a listener worried about fixed income under a one-world system?

answers.summary: Arnold urges the listener not to be consumed by worry and expresses trust in God’s care. He does not provide a concrete forecast about benefits, banks or payment access.

Arnold reassured the disabled listener that resisting false Messiah meant refusing worship, not buying a tent or proving allegiance through a tattoo. He separately suggested modest food reserves for ordinary disruptions such as storms or strikes. This is his religious answer and not a prediction about benefit payments.

questions.question: How did Arnold reassure a veteran troubled by killing in war?

answers.summary: Arnold directed the listener to Psalm 144 and regarded defending national freedom in combat as honorable service. He did not investigate the particular acts or circumstances; his reassurance should not be expanded into a judgment about every act in war.

Arnold supported military defense of the nation and its religious freedom, referring to Psalm 144 and his own combat experience. This records his pastoral position, not a legal determination about a particular killing or permission for private violence.

questions.question: How did Arnold reassure someone afraid of the antichrist period?

answers.summary: Arnold refers to Luke 10:19 and the protection of the three men in the fiery furnace. He encourages confidence in God and describes the Holy Spirit speaking through believers as an opportunity to witness. Part of the listener’s question is unclear in the captions.

Arnold reassured the listener through his elect testimony teaching, referring to Mark 13, Luke 21 and Christ’s authority over enemies in Luke 10:19. He said the Holy Spirit would supply speech rather than requiring a rehearsed defense.

questions.question: How did Arnold reconcile Lazarus being raised with being appointed once to die?

answers.summary: Arnold distinguished flesh death from his interpretation of a final death of the soul. He described Lazarus’s raising as a demonstration of Christ’s power over bodily death and distinguished spiritual bodies from immortality. His Matthew verse number was tentative.
Dennis says the later details are not written, but reasons that Lazarus lived out his life and eventually died again.

questions.question: How did Arnold relate free will to the influence he called evil spirits?

answers.summary: Arnold described ignorance, occult involvement or impaired judgment as possible openings and urged using Christ’s authority in Luke 10:18–19. He explicitly qualified his bottle illustration with not always. These are his religious claims, not diagnoses of addiction or mental illness.
Arnold says a righteous person can fall and qualifies that possession involves opening oneself to a demonic spirit; he points to authority in Christ’s name.

questions.question: How did Arnold relate the God of the Old Testament to Jesus?

answers.summary: Arnold explains the divine names through God’s roles and describes the Son appearing in a dimension people could see. The captions repeatedly render the names uncertainly, so their spellings and linguistic explanation need audio confirmation.

Arnold connects the Word in John’s opening with the Spirit in Genesis and describes Christ as present with God from the beginning. A caption calls John an epistle while quoting the Gospel opening; it is flagged rather than silently quoted.

questions.question: How did Arnold respond to a question about men hitting women?

answers.summary: Arnold condemns hitting women and refers to 1 Timothy 5:8 about responsibility for family. His answer does not provide a practical safety plan; its violent anecdote is not reproduced as advice.
Arnold tells the assaulted woman to report the attackers to police, seek protection and act within the law rather than treating turn the other cheek as a duty to endure abuse.

questions.question: How did Arnold say a listener could learn his Bible-study method?

answers.summary: Arnold credits study and recommends studying along with the ministry or studying independently, including attention to the biblical languages.
Arnold says Scripture and its source languages are the center of his study, with history also mentioned. He describes it as a lifelong task rather than recommending a new teacher’s explanations.

questions.question: How did Arnold say Satan recognizes allegiance without reading minds?

answers.summary: Arnold says outward refusal or acceptance of worship makes allegiance apparent. He describes the mark as understanding and commitment rather than a visible sign.
Arnold says Satan can see what people do and does not need to read their minds to know their actions.

questions.question: How did Arnold say the two witnesses would be recognized before the antichrist?

answers.summary: Arnold says their teaching and abilities will make them recognizable. He relates their earlier arrival to his comparison of the witnesses’ solar-day period with Satan’s lunar-month period, while maintaining his shortened five-month chronology.

Arnold first said most likely, then qualified that believers would know the two witnesses while the whole world would not necessarily recognize who they were. His qualification is retained rather than turning it into universal recognition.

questions.question: How did Dennis advise a beginner seeking Christ and Bible study?

answers.summary: Dennis encourages repentance and welcoming Christ, then studying alongside a trusted teacher and using the chapel newsletter’s suggested studies as building blocks.
Dennis recommends foundational studies including Genesis 1–6 and Revelation, followed by study guided by the Holy Spirit.

questions.question: How did Dennis advise sharing faith after a listener lost friends through repeated efforts?

answers.summary: Dennis recommends offering a thought that invites interest, being prepared to answer from Scripture, and not repeatedly pressing an unreceptive person. He distinguishes planting a seed from making it grow, which he leaves to God.
Dennis approves sharing chapter-by-chapter Scripture, while stressing preparation to answer from the Bible and leaving the growth of understanding to God.
Dennis appreciates a new believer’s enthusiasm but advises considering whether the audience welcomes the subject and protecting credibility rather than pressing every encounter.

questions.question: How did Dennis advise someone concerned about supporting false doctrine?

answers.summary: Dennis emphasizes the famine for hearing God’s Word and warns against supporting teaching opposed to Christ’s doctrine. He interprets wishing such teachers godspeed as sharing in their deeds.
Dennis warns that financial support goes beyond the greeting forbidden in his reading of 2 John. He applies that warning here to supporting rapture teaching.

questions.question: How did Dennis answer a question about identifying descendants of the lost tribes?

answers.summary: Dennis says identifying ancestry is difficult and gives his view about people whose ancestors migrated from Europe to America.
Dennis says it is difficult to determine accurately and points to Galatians 3:29 about being Abraham’s seed in Christ.

questions.question: How did Dennis answer a question about women preachers?

answers.summary: Dennis praises Deborah and Huldah, mentions Philip’s daughters and points to the promised outpouring of the Spirit on sons and daughters.
Dennis points to Miriam, Deborah, Huldah and Philip’s daughters, and to the Spirit being poured out on sons and daughters.

questions.question: How did Dennis answer about disposing of old anointing oil?

answers.summary: Dennis says Scripture does not specify a disposal method and sees no religious objection to disposing of unusable oil and replacing or cleaning its vial.
Dennis says he pours spoiled olive oil onto the ground. He explicitly identifies this as his own practice, not a procedure he can document from Scripture.

questions.question: How did Dennis answer about rapture believers who die before the antichrist?

answers.summary: Dennis emphasizes the promise to those who die believing in Christ rather than agreeing that their prior rapture belief automatically requires a further test.
Dennis says a pastor who died believing in Christ before the antichrist’s appearance is with the Lord despite having taught a rapture, and likely now understands the error.

questions.question: How did Dennis answer how one can know the Bible is from God?

answers.summary: Dennis mentions faith and interprets Psalm 22 as describing Christ’s crucifixion in advance.
Dennis attributes the Old Testament to God’s inspiration through human servants and offers Psalm 22 as an example of prophecy he believes supports that conviction.

questions.question: How did Dennis answer speculation about rebuilding Jerusalem’s temple?

answers.summary: Dennis redirected the listener from speculation about a construction site or a red heifer toward Christ’s body as the temple and believers as members of it. He warned against making those proposed physical events the basis of expectation.
Dennis says it is not required and distinguishes the temple Jesus said would be raised in three days as his body.

questions.question: How did Dennis answer where God came from?

answers.summary: Dennis refers to Exodus 3:13–14 and explains God’s name as I will be what I will be. He says God has existed from the beginning and did not need anyone to create Him.
Dennis describes God as eternal, without beginning or end, and connects this with the name expressed to Moses as I am that I am.

questions.question: How did Dennis answer whether angels are male or female?

answers.summary: Dennis emphasizes the absence of giving and taking in marriage in spiritual bodies, then uses the collective bride-of-Christ image spiritually. He does not provide a direct male/female proof text.
Dennis says the biblical descriptions of angels present them as young males.

questions.question: How did Dennis answer whether the sixth and seventh trumpets will be heard?

answers.summary: Dennis describes the trumpets as events before Christ returns and points to Matthew 24 and Mark 13. He does not directly resolve whether a sound will be heard.
Dennis says he does not believe the trumpets are audible sounds, interpreting them as events preceding Christ’s return.

questions.question: How did Dennis answer whether to seek forgiveness from the Father or Son?

answers.summary: Dennis discusses Christ as God with us and then directs prayer to the Father in Jesus’ name, following his reading of the Lord’s Prayer.
Dennis directs prayer to the heavenly Father and says Christians should pray in Jesus’ name.

questions.question: How did Dennis comfort a man whose wife had died?

answers.summary: Dennis acknowledges grief, says her spirit remains alive, and expresses hope of reunion for believers in Christ. He does not specify her activities after death.
Dennis describes her as in paradise with the Lord and offers hope of reunion. He acknowledges the trauma of losing a spouse and contrasts the short flesh life with eternity.

questions.question: How did Dennis connect dinosaur fossils with earth ages?

answers.summary: Dennis uses carnivore and herbivore teeth as examples of past animal life. He interprets Job’s behemoth as a dinosaur and places dinosaurs before human flesh life, saying the first age ended in an upheaval and the second tests humanity’s allegiance.
Dennis says dinosaurs belonged to the first earth age and were not on Noah’s ark, and points to the behemoth in Job 40.

questions.question: How did Dennis counsel a listener troubled by memories of the past?

answers.summary: Dennis distinguishes treasured memories from repeated guilt over repented sins. He urges trusting God’s forgiveness and remembering to forgive oneself.
Dennis urges trusting God’s forgiveness and learning to forgive oneself rather than repeatedly reliving repented wrongdoing.

questions.question: How did Dennis describe anointing a home?

answers.summary: Dennis describes blessing olive oil in prayer, applying a small amount at the doorway and praying against evil in Christ’s name. He advises an inexperienced person to seek help from a spiritually mature believer. This records his religious practice.

Dennis describes setting aside blessed olive oil for anointing, placing a little on a doorway and asking for evil to leave in Jesus’ name. He emphasizes filling the home with Christ rather than treating the oil as permanent protection.

questions.question: How did Dennis describe being delivered up before antichrist?

answers.summary: Dennis says the elect refuse worship of antichrist and are brought before him. He instructs them not to prepare their speech because the Holy Spirit will testify against antichrist and for Christ.
Dennis expects a physical delivery and imprisonment, citing Mark 13 and Revelation 2:10; he says television coverage is possible.

questions.question: How did Dennis describe Shepherd’s Chapel’s Easter-season observance?

answers.summary: Dennis describes it as Passover, centered on Bible teaching and communion, rather than directly approving every family custom the listener listed.
Dennis describes biblical teaching and communion, identifies Christ as Passover and notes that a broadcast communion service is available.

questions.question: How did Dennis describe the appearance of spiritual bodies?

answers.summary: Dennis says he believes angels appear young, pointing to the young man at Jesus’s tomb in Mark 16:5.
Dennis says age is less significant in a spiritual body. He personally believes people will appear around Christ’s age at crucifixion, while explicitly saying he cannot document that age biblically.

questions.question: How did Dennis describe the final fate of the wicked?

answers.summary: Dennis associated final hell with Revelation’s lake of fire and described its victims as gone permanently rather than preserved for endless suffering. His captioned Greek-word discussion is unclear and is not silently standardized.
Dennis says no, interpreting the wicked consuming away like smoke as final destruction rather than endless conscious burning.

questions.question: How did Dennis describe the ministry’s approach to infant baptism?

answers.summary: Dennis says infants are dedicated to God and baptism is left until they can choose it themselves. In this answer he advocates immersion rather than sprinkling.
Dennis recommends baptism after an infant baptism when the person can make an informed decision, while cautioning against repeated baptism after backsliding.

questions.question: How did Dennis discuss gender and marriage after the resurrection?

answers.summary: Dennis says he believes there will be one gender, cites Jesus’s teaching that the resurrected do not marry, and uses the church as Christ’s bride as a spiritual comparison.
Dennis answers no and bases his explanation on Jesus’ teaching that people do not marry in the resurrection. This is Dennis’s interpretation of that passage.

questions.question: How did Dennis distinguish killing from murder when asked about war?

answers.summary: Dennis interprets the commandment as prohibiting premeditated murder and says defense against an invading enemy does not break God’s law.
Dennis distinguishes killing in wartime self-defense from premeditated murder and says it does not automatically bar someone from heaven.

questions.question: How did Dennis distinguish mental illness from possession?

answers.summary: Dennis says mental illness and possession are different and encourages medical care in addition to prayer.
Dennis expressly distinguishes mental illness from demon possession and encourages following medication prescribed by a medical doctor.

questions.question: How did Dennis distinguish military service from murder?

answers.summary: Dennis interpreted the commandment as forbidding premeditated murder and distinguished it from fighting for one’s country and self-defense. This summarizes his theological distinction, not a blanket judgment about every wartime action.
Dennis distinguishes premeditated murder from self-defense and regards defending one’s country in a kill-or-be-killed situation as different from murder.

questions.question: How did Dennis distinguish paradise from torment across the gulf?

answers.summary: Dennis identified paradise with the favorable side in his interpretation of Luke 16 and contrasted it with the rich man’s torment. His retelling of the dialogue is not exact verse wording and should be checked against the passage.
Dennis places Abraham and Lazarus on one side and the rich man on the other, saying the gulf cannot presently be crossed.

questions.question: How did Dennis distinguish sixth-day humanity from Adam in Genesis?

answers.summary: Dennis interpreted Genesis 1 as the creation of all peoples on the sixth day and Genesis 2 as a later creation of Adam for Christ’s genealogy. This is Dennis’s interpretation; the listener’s proposed wording was not presented as a verbatim Bible verse.

Dennis interpreted Genesis 1 as the creation of all peoples before the later lineage of the twelve tribes. He distinguished Adam’s creation after the seventh-day rest in his reading of Genesis 2. This is an attributed interpretation.

questions.question: How did Dennis distinguish terrestrial and celestial bodies?

answers.summary: Dennis calls the terrestrial body earthly flesh and the celestial body spiritual, relating the distinction to flesh returning to earth and spirit returning to God.

Dennis identifies celestial with the heavenly or spiritual body and terrestrial with the earthly flesh body. Only this question is answered in the saved passage despite the listener mentioning two questions.

questions.question: How did Dennis explain a biblical acrostic?

answers.summary: Dennis describes acrostics using the sequence of Hebrew letters, pointing to Psalms 37 and 119. He also says sacred names can be found in letter patterns and credits Bullinger’s Companion Bible notes for identifying acrostics.
Dennis uses Psalm 119: its successive groups of eight verses begin with successive Hebrew letters. He relates the 22 letters to its 176 verses.

questions.question: How did Dennis explain animal sacrifices in Ezekiel’s millennium chapters?

answers.summary: Dennis says there will be no flesh in the millennium and interprets the desired sacrifice as love, drawing on Hosea 6:6.
Dennis says literal blood sacrifice is impossible in the millennium because there is no flesh. He interprets the desired sacrifice as love and knowledge of God.

questions.question: How did Dennis explain BC and AD?

answers.summary: Dennis explains BC as Before Christ, with the numbered years decreasing toward Christ’s birth, and AD as Anno Domini, the year of our Lord.

sources.lesson: Wednesday 2/17/21 I & II Kings 22:43 - 1:18; Wednesday 2/17/21 I & II Kings 22:43 - 1:18

answers.summary: Dennis explains it as the abbreviation of the Latin anno Domini, meaning in the year of our Lord.

questions.question: How did Dennis explain begotten in Genesis and John?

answers.summary: Dennis distinguishes the Hebrew idea of bearing offspring from the Greek term he describes as only-born in John 3:16, applying the latter to Jesus as God’s only begotten Son.
Dennis explains monogenes as only born and says Christ was given rather than taken from someone else.

questions.question: How did Dennis explain being harvested out of season?

answers.summary: Dennis says he is speaking spiritually of people deceived into worshiping the antichrist before Christ’s return.
Dennis interprets it spiritually as accepting Antichrist before the true Christ returns. He says knowing the season means avoiding that premature spiritual harvest.

questions.question: How did Dennis explain biblical language about God having a wife?

answers.summary: Dennis points to the marriage imagery involving Jerusalem in Ezekiel and the bill of divorce to backsliding Israel in Jeremiah.
Dennis cites the image of God spreading his skirt over Jerusalem and explains it as a figure of speech for marrying her.

questions.question: How did Dennis explain cleansing after helping a relative during the millennium?

answers.summary: Dennis interprets Ezekiel 44 as the elect leaving the temple to help immediate family not in the first resurrection, then spending seven days away because of contact with the spiritually dead.
Dennis distinguishes helping immediate family in the millennium from the listener’s gulf wording. He says contact with the spiritually dead entails seven days of uncleanness.

questions.question: How did Dennis explain clothing in heaven?

answers.summary: Dennis connected the fine linen in Revelation 19 with the saints’ righteous acts. He also cited works following a person at death and used the length of a robe as an illustration of those acts.
Dennis interprets heavenly linen as the righteous acts of the saints and says the resulting clothing depends on a person’s works.

questions.question: How did Dennis explain earthly evil while Satan is restrained in heaven?

answers.summary: Dennis says Satan’s spirit and servants remain active. He explicitly labels as personal opinion his belief that the third who followed Satan are now living in flesh.
Arnold describes evil spirits as influencing thought while Satan and his angels remain physically restrained and urges choosing the Holy Spirit’s guidance.

questions.question: How did Dennis explain Eve as the mother of all living?

answers.summary: Dennis says the phrase concerns the Messiah coming through her lineage and eternal life through Christ rather than all peoples descending from her in the flesh.
Dennis gives the meaning life giver and interprets mother of all living spiritually through the Messiah coming through her lineage.

questions.question: How did Dennis explain fallen angels interacting with women despite another dimension?

answers.summary: Dennis says they left their heavenly habitation and came to earth, interpreting Genesis 6 and Jude through his teaching that they refused birth through a woman.
Dennis says the angels left their habitation, came to earth, and took the daughters of Adam as wives; he refers to Jude 1:6 and Genesis 6.

questions.question: How did Dennis explain God as a consuming fire?

answers.summary: Dennis refers to Hebrews 12:29, describing God’s fire as destroying wickedness while bringing warmth to those who love Him.
Dennis says God controls the consuming fire and contrasts its effect on the person consumed with warmth for one who loves and serves God.

questions.question: How did Dennis explain Hebrews 6:1–6 after a believer sins?

answers.summary: Dennis advises repentance rather than being saved or baptized again and relates repeated salvation to crucifying Christ again.
Dennis says the response is repentance rather than treating Christ as needing to be crucified again. He contrasts forgiveness through Christ’s blood with the earlier animal sacrifices.

questions.question: How did Dennis explain Isaiah 28:10–13?

answers.summary: Dennis relates precept upon precept and line upon line to teaching the Bible chapter by chapter and verse by verse. He says a topical sermon drawing on several passages can also be appropriate.
Dennis directs the listener to Isaiah 28:10 and 13.

questions.question: How did Dennis explain Matthew 16:28 about not tasting death?

answers.summary: Dennis connects seeing the kingdom come to Christ’s resurrection, rather than saying the listeners would live until the second advent.
Dennis interprets Matthew 16:28 through Christ’s crucifixion, resurrection and return to God’s right hand, rather than the second advent.

questions.question: How did Dennis explain Mystery Babylon?

answers.summary: Dennis identifies Mystery Babylon with the mother of harlots and describes her as representing those who worship the antichrist.
Dennis portrays her as representing people spiritually unfaithful to Christ through worshiping antichrist.

questions.question: How did Dennis explain obeying the laws of the land?

answers.summary: Dennis appealed to rendering to Caesar what is Caesar’s and urged lawful conduct to preserve credibility and avoid imprisonment that would hinder service. He did not develop exceptions in this answer.

Dennis explains: the pastor references Matthew 22:17-21, where Jesus instructs people to 'Render unto Caesar that which is Caesar's,' emphasizing the importance of following civil laws of the land while also adhering to God's law.

questions.question: How did Dennis explain sacrifices in Ezekiel’s millennium chapters?

answers.summary: Dennis interpreted the future setting as spiritual rather than flesh existence and the desired sacrifice as love and knowledge of God. His captioned Hosea chapter-and-verse wording is malformed and is not silently repaired.
Dennis interprets Ezekiel’s millennial sacrifices as love rather than flesh animals and points to Hosea 6:6.

questions.question: How did Dennis explain Strong’s entries for Cain and Kenite?

answers.summary: Dennis directed the listener to the Hebrew dictionary and interpreted the patronymic notation between entries 7017 and 7014 as descent from Cain. This preserves his linguistic and ancestry interpretation without classifying modern people.
Dennis points to Hebrew 7017 and describes it as a patronymic associated with Cain.

questions.question: How did Dennis explain the early and latter rains?

answers.summary: Dennis distinguishes the seasons of physical rain in that region from spiritual rain, which he says falls where and when God wills.
Dennis recommends Deuteronomy 11 and uses rain as an image of truth first germinating and later maturing into fruitful understanding.

questions.question: How did Dennis explain the exception for a married sister in Ezekiel44?

answers.summary: Dennis applies the passage to the elect helping relatives in the millennium and says marriage moved a woman into her husband’s family in the familial system he describes. He voices personal discomfort while presenting this as his reading.
Dennis says the unmarried-sister qualification concerns immediate family membership, not marriages continuing in the millennium. He reads marriage as transferring a sister into her husband’s family.

questions.question: How did Dennis explain the falling away before Christ’s return?

answers.summary: Dennis identifies it as apostasy, not a rapture, and connects it with the revelation of Satan as antichrist before Christ’s return to earth.
Dennis calls it apostasy: rebelling against God despite knowing what He wants. He connects the great falling away with the events preceding the son of perdition.

questions.question: How did Dennis explain the first being last and the last first?

answers.summary: Dennis says the passage is not about race and relates it to his teaching about the elect and their witness in the last generation.
Dennis applies the saying to the elect being chosen first but born late enough to witness against antichrist. This is his interpretation of the parable.

questions.question: How did Dennis explain the key of David?

answers.summary: Dennis points to Revelation 3:7 and connects the key with his interpretation of identifying the Kenites.

Dennis associates it with understanding Scripture, Jesus’ descent from David, and his interpretation of the false claims in the synagogue-of-Satan passages. He notes that Smyrna and Philadelphia were the two churches Christ did not fault.

questions.question: How did Dennis explain the purpose of communion?

answers.summary: Dennis describes the bread as symbolizing Christ’s body and the wine or grape juice as symbolizing His blood.
Dennis describes the bread and wine or grape juice as symbols, taken in remembrance of Christ’s sacrifice and resurrection.

questions.question: How did Dennis explain the requirement to be born again in John 3?

answers.summary: Dennis explains the term as from above and relates the passage to being born of woman, contrasting that with his interpretation of the fallen angels.
Dennis briefly explains born again as born from above and defers the listener’s remaining questions to a later broadcast.

questions.question: How did Dennis explain the song of the Lamb?

answers.summary: Dennis says Revelation 15 does not specify the song’s contents and reports that some identify it with the Psalms or the whole Bible.
Dennis says he believes it refers to all the Psalms rather than identifying a single chapter.

questions.question: How did Dennis interpret a woman learning in silence?

answers.summary: Dennis applies attentive silence to men and children as well, emphasizing that people cannot listen and learn while talking over the teaching.
Dennis interprets it as a prohibition on chatter during teaching and says the same applies to men and children.

questions.question: How did Dennis interpret all Israel shall be saved?

answers.summary: Dennis interpreted Israel as all twelve tribes descended from Jacob rather than everybody living in the modern geographic state. He did not explain every individual’s eventual response in this brief answer.
Dennis says yes and connects the promise with the Deliverer turning ungodliness away from Jacob.

questions.question: How did Dennis interpret an unclean spirit returning to an empty house?

answers.summary: Dennis interprets the house as a person and urges filling life with Christ and the Holy Spirit rather than leaving it spiritually empty after deliverance.
Dennis identifies the house with the person and says cleansing should be followed by filling one’s life and mind with Christ and the Holy Spirit rather than leaving it empty.

questions.question: How did Dennis interpret offerings in Ezekiel’s millennial chapters?

answers.summary: Dennis reads Ezekiel 40–48 as millennial and interprets acceptable offerings in terms of love and knowledge of God rather than renewed flesh-animal sacrifice.

Dennis places Ezekiel 40–48 in the millennium with spiritual bodies. He emphasizes love and knowledge of God rather than literal burnt offerings, and separately identifies the Old Testament firstfruits instruction in Deuteronomy.

questions.question: How did Dennis interpret sleep in the dust in Daniel12:2?

answers.summary: Dennis reads dust as representing a low or degraded state and compares it with the serpent’s humiliation in Genesis.
Dennis reads sleeping in the dust as a degraded condition and relates awakening to life or shame to the change at the final trumpet.

questions.question: How did Dennis interpret the beast’s mark in the hand and forehead?

answers.summary: Dennis interprets the hand as service or work for antichrist and the forehead as the mind’s deception.
Dennis interprets the forehead as the deceived mind and the hand as work performed for antichrist, not a physical identifying mark.

questions.question: How did Dennis interpret the dead know nothing in Ecclesiastes?

answers.summary: Dennis applies the statement to dead flesh, which returns to dust, while the spirit and its intellect return to God.
Dennis says the dead flesh knows nothing while the spirit has returned to God.

questions.question: How did Dennis interpret the half hour of silence in Revelation 8?

answers.summary: Dennis connects the half hour with two and a half months in his explanation of the antichrist’s appearance.
Dennis relates the hour of temptation to five months and therefore half an hour to two and a half months, saying heaven is quiet because Satan is on earth. This is his prophetic interpretation.

questions.question: How did Dennis interpret the mansions of John 14?

answers.summary: Dennis emphasizes abiding with Christ rather than houses made of lumber and bricks. He says that relationship can begin now.
Dennis interprets mansions as abiding with Christ, emphasizing a relationship available now rather than only a future physical house.

questions.question: How did Dennis interpret the prohibition on bodily markings?

answers.summary: Dennis cites Leviticus 19:28, noting its connection with mourning the dead. He allows that this context may also qualify the marks prohibition and says having a tattoo does not automatically condemn someone forever.
Dennis acknowledges two possible readings: a general ban on marks or a ban on marks for the dead. He associates the practices in that verse with heathen mourning customs.

questions.question: How did Dennis interpret the prophets and law prophesying until John?

answers.summary: Dennis identifies John as John the Baptist and treats the written biblical prophets and Christ’s teaching as sufficient for salvation. He urges skepticism toward contemporary claims to be a prophet of God.
Dennis urges caution about anyone claiming to be a present-day prophet and says the biblical prophets and Christ’s recorded teaching provide what believers need.

questions.question: How did Dennis interpret the sea being no more in Revelation 21?

answers.summary: Dennis reads the sea symbolically as people, referring to Revelation 17:15, and describes the future bodies as spiritual.
Dennis interprets the waters symbolically as peoples and applies no more sea to the end of flesh existence. He also says the Genesis firmament’s natural watering arrangement will be restored.

questions.question: How did Dennis interpret the sickle and blood imagery in Revelation 14?

answers.summary: Dennis reads it as spiritual harvest and judgment at Christ’s return, linking the blood imagery with God’s wrath rather than describing ordinary grape harvesting.
Dennis interprets Revelation’s blood-to-bridles imagery as spiritual judgment and the outpouring of God’s wrath, insisting that the scene is not ordinary flesh warfare.

questions.question: How did Dennis interpret the ten virgins and their oil?

answers.summary: Dennis interprets the virgins as Christ’s bride and oil as the Holy Spirit and truth. He connects readiness with recognizing antichrist and remaining faithful until Christ’s return.
Dennis interprets the virgins’ oil as truth that enables recognition of the true bridegroom. He applies the shut door to those deceived by antichrist.

questions.question: How did Dennis interpret the wheel within a wheel?

answers.summary: Dennis reads Ezekiel’s wheels as vehicles transporting God’s throne and accompanying beings. He recommends Arnold’s Horses of the Bible study and distinguishes this interpretation from a claim about alien visitors.
Dennis interprets Ezekiel’s imagery as vehicles bringing God’s throne and attendants to earth, and refers to Arnold’s Horses of the Bible for fuller study.

questions.question: How did Dennis reassure a backsliding believer about Hebrews 6?

answers.summary: Dennis interpreted Hebrews 6 as a reason to repent rather than try to repeat initial salvation or recrucify Christ. He emphasized asking forgiveness and receiving a fresh start. This is his reading of the passage.
Dennis said the person should repent rather than be saved again. He appealed to Hebrews 6:4–6 and described repeated salvation as trying to crucify Christ again.

questions.question: How did Dennis reconcile Genesis 4:1 with his belief that Satan fathered Cain?

answers.summary: Dennis proposed that Eve had already conceived before Adam knew her, interpreted the next birth as twins with different fathers and appealed to Cain’s absence from Genesis 5. These are his serpent-seed and ancestry claims, not established parentage or genetics.
Dennis says Eve had already conceived by the serpent before Adam knew her. He interprets the continued labor in the next verse as Cain and Abel being twins with different fathers.

questions.question: How did Dennis relate a thousand years to the Lord’s day?

answers.summary: Dennis cites 2 Peter 3:8 and acknowledges uncertainty about how people will experience that time.
Dennis agrees that the thousand years are described as the Lord’s day and again points to 2 Peter 3:8.
Dennis cites a thousand years as one day with the Lord and distinguishes spiritual existence from a human lifetime. He does not identify every millennium teacher in this answer.

questions.question: How did Dennis respond to a listener asking whether women are less than men?

answers.summary: Dennis says God uses women and cites Deborah, Huldah, Philip’s daughters and the Spirit being poured out on sons and daughters.
Dennis cites women prophets and Philip’s daughters in support of women teaching, and points to the Spirit being poured out on sons and daughters.

questions.question: How did Dennis respond to a question about divorce?

answers.summary: Dennis points to Jesus’s discussion of marriage in Matthew 19 and expresses his view that God hates divorce.

Dennis says divorce is not the unforgivable sin and encourages repentance for one’s part in it, rejecting treatment of divorced people as second-class citizens. He cannot identify the earlier remark the listener means.

questions.question: How did Dennis respond to present-day claims of being a prophet?

answers.summary: Dennis urges great caution about modern claimants and directs listeners to the biblical prophets. He also names Miriam, Huldah and Philip’s daughters as biblical prophetesses.
Dennis warns against modern personal predictions resembling fortune-telling and directs listeners to the biblical prophets instead.

questions.question: How did Dennis say a disabled believer can serve the Lord?

answers.summary: Dennis suggested encouragement, a smile, visiting sick or elderly people, and witnessing about faith. He emphasized that a disabled person’s positive testimony can encourage others; he did not make disability a barrier to service.
Dennis encourages taking each day as it comes and says a person’s faith despite physical limitations can be a powerful witness to others. He also stresses Christ’s authority over spiritual enemies.

questions.question: How did Dennis understand the leaves for healing in Revelation 22?

answers.summary: Dennis says he believes the leaves remove boredom and bring happiness. He presents this as his belief.
Dennis identifies the leaves’ source, the tree of life, with Jesus Christ.

questions.question: How did the Murrays explain biblical high places of worship?

answers.summary: Arnold briefly described high places as places of worship and called the expression a figure of speech. The captioned pavement wording is not expanded into a specific architectural claim.

Dennis described them as unauthorized places of worship. He said even worship directed toward Yahweh there violated the instruction to worship at the temple in Jerusalem, including the burning of incense and animal sacrifices.

questions.question: How did the Murrays explain Israel and Judah as separate houses?

answers.summary: Arnold explains the separation through different captivities of northern and southern tribes. He does not separately narrate the earlier political division in this brief answer, so that historical distinction remains unresolved.

Dennis described the split after Solomon into ten northern tribes under Jeroboam and the southern kingdom associated with Judah. He said they remained divided and interpreted Ezekiel 37’s two sticks as their future reunion.

questions.question: How did the pastors explain eyes to see and ears to hear?

answers.summary: Arnold describes spiritual understanding rather than physical sight or hearing. He says physical impairments do not determine whether a person can understand God’s message.

Dennis said Christ’s calls to hear particularly addressed the elect. He referred to Romans 11:7–8 and Isaiah 29:9–10 for a spirit of slumber. He did not simply equate every lack of understanding with laziness.

questions.question: How do I find out what is God's purpose in my life?

answers.summary: Dennis recommends studying God’s Word and developing a relationship with the Father to understand one’s purpose.
Dennis recommends growing in Scripture knowledge and praying for a sign when uncertain about a calling, using Gideon as the example.

questions.question: How does Dennis describe the fig-tree generation?

answers.summary: Dennis lists forty-, seventy- and one-hundred-twenty-year generation lengths and connects the fig-tree generation beginning in 1948 with fulfillment at Christ’s return, without giving a return date here.
Dennis connects the shoot being set out with Israel becoming a nation in 1948 and emphasizes Christ’s instruction to learn the parable.

questions.question: How long did Dennis say the antichrist will be on earth?

answers.summary: Dennis describes a five-month period and says the antichrist will be physically present for two and a half months.

Dennis says the tribulation was shortened for the elect and interprets Revelation 9 as a five-month locust season. In this answer he distinguishes Antichrist’s personal rule as half that period, two and a half months.

questions.question: How often did Arnold suggest anointing oneself when ill?

answers.summary: Arnold said daily anointing was not sinful but suggested allowing time rather than repeating mechanically. He distinguished prayer from chanting. His weekly suggestion was pastoral advice, not a treatment schedule or promise of cure.
Arnold says once is sufficient and also advises following the health laws while praying.

questions.question: How should a believer respond to a spouse who mocks Christianity?

answers.summary: Dennis points to Paul’s discussion of mixed-belief marriages. He says to be an example and distinguishes disagreement from interference with the believer’s freedom to worship.

Dennis points to 1 Corinthians 7. He says if the spouse allows the believer and children to practice their faith, they can model Christian living and pray for the spouse rather than force a conversation.

questions.question: How should I respond when family rejects my Bible witness?

answers.summary: Dennis encourages planting the seed without taking offense, while leaving its growth and the opening of understanding to God.
Dennis acknowledges the frustration and says the listener’s responsibility is to plant the seed, leaving its growth to God.

questions.question: How will the antichrist convince atheists to worship and serve him?

answers.summary: Arnold expects antichrist’s deceptive miracles to impress even atheists and warns against underestimating that deception.
Arnold expects the miracles in Revelation 13 to persuade many atheists to worship the false Christ.

questions.question: Is it a sin to be divorced and living with someone who doesn't know God?

answers.summary: Dennis recommends 1 Corinthians 7 for the listener’s question about living with an unbelieving partner after divorce.
Dennis recommends 1 Corinthians 7 and declines to make a decision about the marriage from the limited information supplied.

questions.question: Is Revelation 20:4 literal?

answers.summary: Dennis identifies the overcomers of Revelation 20:4 with those who refuse antichrist and reign with Christ during the millennium, linking this with the first resurrection.
Dennis describes Revelation 20:4’s overcomers as refusing antichrist and reigning with Christ for a thousand years.

questions.question: May a family stay home and study with the Chapel?

answers.summary: Dennis welcomes the family and says he sees no objection to their learning God’s word that way.

Dennis says to tithe where God’s Word is taught so that teaching can continue. He cites Christ’s presence where people gather in His name and applies that to people studying together through the broadcast.

questions.question: May I anoint myself if elders are unavailable?

answers.summary: Dennis says yes, locating healing power in God rather than the elder or oil. He describes prayerful use of olive oil as an act of obedience in Jesus’ name.
Dennis says yes when there is no one present the person considers an elder. He attributes healing to God, not the elder’s own power.

questions.question: Must Antichrist come between May and September in a particular year?

answers.summary: Dennis says no year is known except to the Father. He explains that the locust comparison concerns a five-month duration and does not establish literal May-through-September arrival dates.
Dennis says no: he gives a five-month duration and explicitly cautions that the May-to-September locust season does not establish May as the start of Antichrist’s tribulation.

questions.question: Must someone speak in tongues to enter heaven?

answers.summary: Dennis rejects that requirement. He contrasts unintelligible speech requiring an interpreter with the Pentecost event, where listeners understood the disciples, and says the Holy Spirit’s language is understood without an interpreter.
Dennis says no and cites John’s promise of everlasting life. He distinguishes intelligible languages and Pentecost’s universally understood speech from unintelligible speech needing an interpreter.

questions.question: To whom did Dennis tell the listener to address prayer?

answers.summary: Dennis says to pray to the heavenly Father in Jesus Christ’s name, following Jesus’ model prayer.
Dennis instructs prayer to the Father in Jesus’ name and emphasizes asking that God’s will, rather than merely personal wishes, be done.

sources.lesson: Wednesday 2/17/21 I & II Kings 22:43 - 1:18; Wednesday 2/17/21 I & II Kings 22:43 - 1:18

questions.question: Was Dennis still teaching while Arnold’s recordings continued?

answers.summary: Dennis says he was teaching, including Sunday messages, and that the ministry would keep airing Arnold’s lessons while people requested them. This describes the broadcast arrangement at that time.
Dennis says the current Kings recording and Arnold’s earlier recordings would both continue to air, explaining the programming in the historical setting of the question.

questions.question: What anointing practice did Dennis describe for the home and oneself?

answers.summary: Dennis describes praying over a small vial of olive oil, anointing doorposts or one’s forehead, and praying in Jesus’s name. This is his description of a religious practice, not confirmation of a harmful presence.
Dennis describes setting aside olive oil with prayer and applying a small amount to doorposts while ordering evil away in Jesus Christ’s name. This is a description of his religious practice.

questions.question: What baptism wording and method did Dennis describe at Shepherd’s Chapel?

answers.summary: Dennis said any Christian could baptize a willing person, then described stating the person’s name, baptizing in the name of Father, Son and Holy Spirit, anointing with a small amount of olive oil and full immersion. He presented this as Chapel practice rather than an exact scriptural formula.
Dennis cites Matthew 28:19 and regards the Father, Son and Holy Spirit as inseparable, rather than treating the Acts reference to Jesus’ name as excluding the others.

questions.question: What did Arnold mean by heaven being closed during the millennium?

answers.summary: Arnold distinguished those already in the first resurrection from those who must await the second. He said the latter would not complete their overcoming during the millennium until Satan’s release supplied the final test.
Arnold distinguishes overcoming at the first resurrection from entering eternal life after testing at the end of the millennium, referring to Revelation 20.

questions.question: What did Arnold say about Enoch’s role and writings?

answers.summary: Arnold calls Enoch a prophet using Jude 14 but rejects attributing books to him. He connects Enoch’s preaching with his interpretation of fallen angels and the Genesis flood setting. His authorship and ancestry claims remain attributed views.

Arnold distinguished two Enochs and expressed doubt about the authorship of books circulating under Enoch’s name. He permitted cautious reading while advising comparison with Scripture; he did not firmly establish the authorship or explain the full canon history.

questions.question: What did Arnold say happens to flesh bodies when Christ returns?

answers.summary: Arnold explained the change in terms of a different dimension and said flesh and blood cannot enter the kingdom. He deferred the requested details about the bodies to his coming study of Zechariah 14, so this occurrence remains an incomplete explanation.

For a second listener asking about flesh bodies at Christ’s return, Arnold said apparently they would return to dust, then again deferred a fuller explanation to Zechariah 14. He repeated his description of a different dimension.
Dennis says flesh ends but the spirit does not. He interprets the last-trump change as entering spiritual bodies and emphasizes that flesh and blood cannot inherit God’s kingdom.

questions.question: What did Arnold say the protecting cherub guarded against?

answers.summary: Arnold discusses free will and Satan’s own pride as dangers to the mercy seat. He calls Michael the other cherub most likely rather than certain.

Asked why the mercy seat needed protection, Arnold emphasized freely given love, free will and Satan’s pride in his reading of Ezekiel 28. A damaged sentence about what God knows remains held; it is not rewritten into a definitive claim about divine foreknowledge.

questions.question: What did Arnold teach about disability and spiritual bodies?

answers.summary: Arnold says God protects the innocent and teaches that disability will not remain in the spiritual body during the millennium.

Arnold described spiritual bodies as complete and healthy rather than retaining missing limbs, excess weight or aging from flesh life. He called the flesh a temporary dwelling and the spiritual body the real home.

questions.question: What did Arnold teach that the elect did in the first earth age?

answers.summary: Arnold describes the elect as having stood against Satan and defended God’s throne. He connects that stand with their role in resisting deception.

Arnold said those who stood against Satan in his first-earth-age teaching came willingly to help misled brothers and sisters. He connected their purpose with witnessing in Mark 13 and described their destiny. This is his doctrinal account, not independently verified history.

questions.question: What did Dennis mean by a shadow government?

answers.summary: Dennis defined it as a supposed arrangement in which private actors exercise power behind elected officials. He offered Absalom’s activity in 2 Samuel 15 as an upcoming biblical illustration rather than proving any modern conspiracy.

Dennis describes a supposed arrangement in which private people exercise power behind elected officials. He uses Absalom in 2 Samuel 15 as his biblical analogy, not as proof of a particular modern conspiracy.

questions.question: What did Dennis say about fleeing Judea?

answers.summary: Dennis points to Jesus’s instruction to flee Judea when the abomination of desolation is seen and distinguishes it from the elect being delivered up.
Dennis regards the event as future and says the flight protects against Antichrist’s presence and control, rather than escaping Christ’s anger.

questions.question: What did Dennis say about how Paul died?

answers.summary: Dennis says the account is not biblical but that some historians believe Paul was beheaded in Rome under Nero.
Dennis says Paul’s death is not described in the Bible and recounts the belief that he was beheaded in Rome.

questions.question: What did Dennis say about the appearance and timing of the third influx of fallen angels?

answers.summary: Dennis says they will appear attractive and deceive people, and places their arrival just before Christ returns, comparing it with the days of Noah.

Dennis places their return at the war in heaven in Revelation 12: Michael and his angels prevail and cast Satan and his angels onto earth. He calls this the third influx and connects it with the warnings about returning angels.

questions.question: What did Dennis say Maschil means in the Psalms?

answers.summary: Dennis defines Maschil as instruction or understanding and identifies thirteen Psalms with that designation.
Dennis explains Maschil as instruction or understanding in the superscriptions of thirteen psalms.

questions.question: What did Dennis suggest doing with Bible translations a listener no longer trusted?

answers.summary: Dennis favors the KJV with Strong’s for checking original languages. He says Scripture does not prescribe disposal of old Bibles and offers burial or burning as his own suggestions.
Dennis says Scripture does not give a disposal instruction, then offers burning or burial as his preference to avoid passing on a translation he considers misleading.

questions.question: What did Dennis tell a mother unsure whether to attend her gay daughter’s wedding?

answers.summary: Dennis tells her to pray for God’s counsel and reminds her that her daughter will remain her daughter regardless of how she handles the invitation. He does not explicitly instruct her to attend or decline.
Dennis declines to make that personal decision for the listener. While stating his religious objection to homosexuality, he tells her to pray about the circumstances and decide for herself.

questions.question: What did Dennis think happens after the elect’s ten-day tribulation?

answers.summary: Dennis says he thinks they will be released and able to go home after the ten days. He presents that outcome as his expectation, not a quoted promise of release.
Dennis expects release after the elect’s ten-day testimony period and links their protection to Revelation 9. He distinguishes the two witnesses’ deaths from that expectation.

questions.question: What did Dennis think Paul’s thorn in the flesh was?

answers.summary: Dennis says he believes it was probably poor eyesight, presenting that identification as his opinion. He emphasizes Christ’s response that grace is sufficient and strength is made perfect in weakness.
Dennis believes it was impaired eyesight. He connects that view with Paul’s large handwritten letters and use of scribes, presenting it as his interpretation.

questions.question: What distinguishes the sixth and seventh trumpets?

answers.summary: Dennis says Antichrist deceives at the sixth trumpet, while Jesus returns at the seventh. He connects the last trumpet with the change from flesh to incorruptible bodies.
Arnold distinguishes the false Christ at the sixth from the true Christ at the seventh.

questions.question: What divine name did Arnold give for God as provider?

answers.summary: Arnold gives Jehovah Jireh in response to a question about praying for a financial blessing and explains it as God providing. He does not promise a particular financial outcome.
Arnold connects God’s name with I am that I am and explains Jehovah-jireh as the Father who provides.

The listener had noted other meanings in Strong’s. His answer is a contextual argument within his serpent-seed teaching, not proof of ancestry or an assertion that every occurrence of the Hebrew word has that sense.

Arnold redirected the listener from eating to touching and asserted a sexual sense of the Hebrew word. The Hebrew term is absent from the captions, so it is not reconstructed. This records his interpretation, not an established translation of every occurrence.

questions.question: Why did Arnold emphasize Jesus being called Son of David?

answers.summary: Arnold linked the title with recognizing the true Christ and his reading of Luke 3 as Mary’s genealogy through Nathan. He also described Mary as connected with Aaron and David. These genealogical details are his interpretation.
Arnold connects the title with knowing the lineage of the true Christ and distinguishing him from the false Christ.

questions.question: Why did Arnold object to using the NIV for his teaching?

answers.summary: Arnold rejects it for his teaching and criticizes its wording in Isaiah 14 and Ezekiel 13. This summary reports his view rather than independently assessing those translations.
Arnold criticizes the NIV wording of Isaiah 14 and recommends the KJV with Strong’s Concordance for examining Hebrew, Greek and Aramaic words. This reports his translation preference and reasoning.

questions.question: Why did Arnold recommend unleavened bread for communion?

answers.summary: Arnold says leaven symbolizes sin and connects unleavened bread with the departure from Egypt. He compares yeast spreading through dough with sin spreading through a family.

Arnold appealed to his beliefs about food and yeast when explaining unleavened Passover bread. The source makes health claims that have not been independently checked; this is a historical teaching summary rather than dietary or cancer advice.

questions.question: Why did Arnold say God allowed Job to suffer?

answers.summary: Arnold presents Job’s endurance as an example for believers and the elect. He emphasizes listening to God instead of accepting the friends’ accusations and says Satan failed to turn Job against God.

Arnold rejected describing God’s treatment of Job as betrayal. He believed Job was trusted to endure a lesson that would help many others recognize false accusations and teaching, and urged thinking beyond immediate self-interest.

questions.question: Why did Arnold say Jesus cursed the fig tree?

answers.summary: Arnold treats the act as a teaching sign warning against the false Christ and contrasts a bad tree with Christ as the tree of life. He also links Jeremiah 24 and the fig-tree imagery with his final-generation interpretation.

Arnold connected the cursed fig tree with good and bad figs in Jeremiah and with his fig-tree-generation reading of Mark 13. He dated that generation’s beginning to 1948; that date is his prophetic interpretation.

questions.question: Why did Arnold say Jesus used Son of Man?

answers.summary: Arnold explained the title as referring to Christ’s life in a human flesh body. He connected it with John 1’s account of the Word becoming flesh.
Arnold says Son of Man refers to Christ’s flesh ministry without denying that he is the Son of God.
