answers.summary: Arnold did not prohibit it. He advised studying in whatever order the listener felt led, emphasizing careful understanding rather than reading merely to finish.

questions.question: Did Arnold prohibit touching leather made from swine?

answers.summary: Arnold said he distinguished using leather from eating swine and did not prohibit the former. He appealed to his reading of Leviticus 11; this is his interpretation rather than an exhaustive account of all contact rules.

questions.question: Did Arnold promise prehistoric animals in the millennium?

answers.summary: Arnold says Isaiah 11 mentions present-day animals but does not establish prehistoric animals in the millennium, and cautions against limiting God.

questions.question: Did Arnold provide contact details for a guest from another television program?

answers.summary: Arnold said he did not know the guest and could not supply the requested address. He suggested contacting that program’s host. Damaged names and contact wording are not reconstructed or presented as current contact information.

questions.question: Did Arnold recognize living people as new prophets?

answers.summary: Arnold said no, distinguishing teaching the biblical prophets from claiming new prophecy. He referred generally to Joel and said the foretold message was already available for study. This records his view.

questions.question: Did Arnold recommend asking a non-Christian to perform baptism?

answers.summary: Arnold discouraged involving a non-Christian, partly because of the risk of making the act a mockery. He affirmed that one Christian may baptize another, though some denominations may not recognize it.

questions.question: Did Arnold recommend cursing someone who repeatedly takes another person’s belongings?

answers.summary: Arnold says a curse is unnecessary and advises putting a stop to the taking. The closing words of the answer are incomplete in the captions, so no specific remedy is inferred.

questions.question: Did Arnold recommend relying on relatives to help after death rather than believing now?

answers.summary: Arnold strongly discourages postponing faith in expectation of later family help. He urges the listener to accept God and help others rather than depend on them to secure salvation.

questions.question: Did Arnold recommend repeatedly asking forgiveness for an already-forgiven act?

answers.summary: Arnold distinguished repeating repentance for an already-forgiven act from repenting of a new act, even if it is the same kind of sin. He encouraged asking for strength of character to stop repeating it.

questions.question: Did Arnold regard a civilization before Adam and Eve as opinion or established teaching?

answers.summary: Arnold regarded it as documented teaching rather than opinion and appealed to Genesis. The captioned chapter-and-verse wording is damaged; no more precise reference is invented. This is his interpretation, not verified archaeology.

questions.question: Did Arnold regard buying a lottery ticket as automatically sinful?

answers.summary: Arnold distinguished limited recreation spending from compulsive gambling that consumes food or housing money. He allowed personal recreation spending only when it did not deprive the family and was not a habit the person could not resist. This records his pastoral distinction.

questions.question: Did Arnold regard Job’s friends’ speeches as inspired counsel?

answers.summary: Arnold said their accusations were not wise counsel from the Holy Spirit, even though Scripture records their speech. He emphasized identifying who is speaking and not turning the friends’ mistaken accusations into teaching authority. His description of Job 38:2 is paraphrase, not its exact wording.

questions.question: Did Arnold regard military service as incompatible with loving enemies?

answers.summary: Arnold said no and defended honorable service as protecting freedom, families and worship. He compared correction with love, while not analyzing every possible military action or order in this answer.

questions.question: Did Arnold regard minor prophets as less important than major prophets?

answers.summary: Arnold says minor refers to their shorter length, not lesser importance, and says both must be understood.

questions.question: Did Arnold regard praying about the same problem every day as vain repetition?

answers.summary: Arnold distinguished daily prayer about problems from chanting and answered that prayer and thanksgiving could both be appropriate. He did not treat the listener’s repeated request as chanting.

questions.question: Did Arnold regard prosperity gained by cheating as God’s blessing?

answers.summary: Arnold distinguished honest wealth from ill-gotten gains and said apparent prosperity does not mean wrongdoing escapes God’s notice. He recommended Psalm 37 for reassurance rather than treating another person’s money as proof of divine approval.

questions.question: Did Arnold regard Satan’s temptation of Jesus as a personal encounter?

answers.summary: Arnold said Satan was personally present and used Scripture with distortions to tempt Jesus. He urged learning the wilderness account in Matthew as preparation to recognize such misuse of Scripture.

questions.question: Did Arnold regard taking a better job after receiving a blessing as ungrateful?

answers.summary: Arnold encouraged improvement and said a better job could also be a blessing, even after a previous job had been prayed for. He advised leaving without burning bridges.

questions.question: Did Arnold reject an earlier conversion because a person later corrected mistaken beliefs?

answers.summary: Arnold reassured the listener that earlier salvation could be real despite mistakes learned along the way. He then withdrew his own joking criticism of the song I’ll Fly Away, distinguishing its words about death from the rapture use he opposed.

questions.question: Did Arnold relate the breath of life in Adam to the Comforter?

answers.summary: Arnold answered that in a sense he did, because God’s breath is the breath of life. The answer was brief and did not develop a complete distinction between these terms.

questions.question: Did Arnold require a dying believer to confess aloud to another person?

answers.summary: Arnold tells the listener that her mother’s prayer to Christ mattered, says prayer need not be aloud, and warns relatives against judging her.

questions.question: Did Arnold require an unemployed widow to pay a tithe from existing possessions?

answers.summary: Arnold answered that a tenth of zero income is zero and rejected the demand described by the listener. This was his answer to an out-of-work widow, not a determination of every possible income situation.

questions.question: Did Arnold require anointing before sharing biblical truth?

answers.summary: Arnold says truth may be shared without anointing, allows self-anointing if desired, and emphasizes doing the work needed to avoid misleading people.

questions.question: Did Arnold require asking an offended person for forgiveness in every case?

answers.summary: Arnold said to ask God and use judgment about approaching the other person, considering danger or additional harm. He expected a sincere Christian to be willing to forgive but warned that not everyone claiming that label would respond well.

questions.question: Did Arnold require being tempted by Satan as proof of salvation?

answers.summary: Arnold rejects that claim and says it should be documented from Scripture rather than accepted from people.

questions.question: Did Arnold require keeping unleavened bread for seven days?

answers.summary: Arnold says Christ became the believer’s Passover, cites 1 Corinthians 5 and emphasizes keeping Christ every day.

questions.question: Did Arnold require knowing Hebrew to inherit eternal life?

answers.summary: Arnold said no. He described English translations as usable and Strong’s Concordance as an optional way to investigate Hebrew, Greek and Aramaic meanings. He distinguished deeper language study from loving Christ and trusting the price he paid.

questions.question: Did Arnold require men and women to sit separately in church?

answers.summary: Arnold said the Bible does not require front or back seating by sex. He called it a church tradition and encouraged the listener to think independently if uncomfortable with it.

questions.question: Did Arnold require naming a human teacher whenever sharing something learned from Scripture?

answers.summary: Arnold said to give God the credit and not worry about crediting a human teacher for every point learned. He valued teachers while attributing spiritual understanding to God’s Holy Spirit.

questions.question: Did Arnold require physical circumcision for salvation?

answers.summary: Arnold said no. He interpreted present circumcision as of the heart or mind, applying to women and men who believe in Christ, and reassured the elderly man in the question.

questions.question: Did Arnold require public annual repentance?

answers.summary: Arnold says to repent to Christ promptly after sin rather than wait for an annual public event. He rejects exposing forgiven matters for public gossip.

questions.question: Did Arnold require shouting for God to hear prayer?

answers.summary: Arnold said no, explaining that God knows thoughts and can hear silent prayer. He emphasized order and discipline rather than volume or screaming.

questions.question: Did Arnold require special words for a prayer about healing?

answers.summary: Arnold said to speak to God plainly, describe the trouble and recall God’s promises. He referred to Ezekiel 18:4, Isaiah 43 around verse 26, James 5 and his dietary reading of Deuteronomy 14 and Leviticus 11. His anointing and diet recommendations are pastoral teaching, not a guarantee of recovery.

questions.question: Did Arnold restrict Christ’s salvation to Israelites?

answers.summary: Arnold rejected the listener’s description of others as second-class citizens and said the Savior was for every race, color and creed. He retained his scattered-Israel interpretation but made acceptance of Christ, rather than the proposed ancestry alone, central to salvation.

questions.question: Did Arnold say a believer must match other people’s Bible knowledge?

answers.summary: Arnold reassured the listener about understanding the basic truth and emphasized the simplicity of Christ’s teaching. He described genuine wisdom as explaining complicated matters in language others can understand.

questions.question: Did Arnold say a child’s death was punishment for a parent causing deaths?

answers.summary: Arnold emphatically rejected that conclusion and urged the listener not to assume guilt. He used Luke 13 and the tower of Siloam to distinguish an accident from a measure of the victims’ sin.

questions.question: Did Arnold say a deceased person can remain on earth as a ghost?

answers.summary: Arnold said the person returns to God rather than remaining as a ghost. He distinguished this from evil spiritual influence that he believed could operate if God allowed it.

questions.question: Did Arnold say a large-print Companion Bible was available?

answers.summary: Arnold said a large-print edition could be ordered at the time of that broadcast. This answer is historical and does not confirm current stock or pricing.

questions.question: Did Arnold say a listener must admit religious visitors to her home?

answers.summary: Arnold says the listener may decline or ask visitors to leave. He distinguishes God’s judgment from a visitor’s authority and says teachers should document their claims from Scripture.

questions.question: Did Arnold say a person must remain with abusive relatives in heaven?

answers.summary: Arnold reassured the listener that heaven would not force continued abuse and spoke categorically against abusers being there. That categorical statement is preserved as his answer and flagged for comparison with passages where he leaves individual judgment to God.

questions.question: Did Arnold say a salt covenant requires staying in a church whose teaching one rejects?

answers.summary: Arnold suggests the covenant was properly to God rather than an organization and says the listener is free to leave if the ministry does not represent God. He objects to using a covenant as pressure to remain.

questions.question: Did Arnold say a widow may date or remarry?

answers.summary: Arnold says death ends the marriage vow and a widow may date or remarry in Christ’s way.

questions.question: Did Arnold say Adam, Abel and Seth all looked like Jesus?

answers.summary: Arnold said they had their own individual appearances and distinguished that from his explanation of Jesus as the Father’s exact image. He did not give physical descriptions of those individuals.

questions.question: Did Arnold say age or disability reduces a person’s worth to God?

answers.summary: Arnold answers no, criticizes impatience toward older people and encourages respect and assistance. He reassures the listener that God loves his children regardless of age.

questions.question: Did Arnold say angels have knees?

answers.summary: Arnold says yes and bases his answer on people being made in the image of God and the angels.

questions.question: Did Arnold say believers must stop communion or take it secretly during the antichrist period?

answers.summary: Arnold said believers may continue communion and need not hide it. He urged remaining ready for testimony and not letting another person stop the practice.

questions.question: Did Arnold say birth outside marriage excludes a child from heaven?

answers.summary: Arnold said the parents’ sin does not fall on the child and that birth outside marriage does not exclude salvation or heavenly service. He distinguished this from his interpretation of the Hebrew word mamzar.

questions.question: Did Arnold say Christ returns without touching earth?

answers.summary: Arnold rejected that claim. He expected Christ to return to earth, touch down and establish his kingdom, rather than remain away while removing a few believers.

questions.question: Did Arnold say earthly punishment automatically replaces God’s later judgment?

answers.summary: Arnold tentatively suggested 1 Corinthians 6:2 as the passage the listener might mean, but explicitly said it did not quite say what she had described. He did not affirm the proposed automatic exemption from later judgment.

questions.question: Did Arnold say Esau’s birthright was simply taken from him?

answers.summary: Arnold says Esau sold his birthright for food and valued his appetite above the blessing.

questions.question: Did Arnold say faith removes all temptation to do wrong?

answers.summary: Arnold said fleshly weakness could still tempt believers and emphasized following the inward spiritual person. He added that no one was perfect and that people sometimes fell short and needed forgiveness. He did not promise automatic freedom from temptation.

questions.question: Did Arnold say fallen angels can appear as children?

answers.summary: Arnold says no, distinguishing being cast out in an existing body from birth through a woman. His separate comments about spirits entering children are religious claims, not a diagnosis of any child.

questions.question: Did Arnold say falling short after becoming a Christian cannot be forgiven?

answers.summary: Arnold says the person should repent and refers to Christ’s teaching about forgiving seventy times seven.

questions.question: Did Arnold say family disapproval determines whether someone reaches heaven?

answers.summary: Arnold says only God judges that outcome. He acknowledges part of the listener’s story is missing and does not infer what the reported call and return meant.

questions.question: Did Arnold say God can forgive angry words spoken after a child dies?

answers.summary: Arnold reassured a bereaved parent that God loves and forgives his children. He encouraged renewed love for God and said the deceased child was with him, rather than declaring the parent beyond forgiveness.

questions.question: Did Arnold say God created the fallen angels bad?

answers.summary: Arnold told a young listener that the angels became bad through their own choices rather than God making them bad, and connected this with people having a choice about whom to follow.

questions.question: Did Arnold say God intervenes for people with free will when asked?

answers.summary: Arnold says yes when they ask, while distinguishing his belief that God intervenes in the elect’s lives without their asking. He links that distinction with Romans 8 and responsibility at judgment.

questions.question: Did Arnold say God still heals people today?

answers.summary: Arnold says God remains a healer and encourages the listener to pray. He also mentions anointing. The answer expresses his belief and prayer for the listener; it does not establish that a healing occurred.

questions.question: Did Arnold say God’s children had free will in the first earth age?

answers.summary: Arnold says yes and connects free will with genuine love.

questions.question: Did Arnold say growing up without an earthly father prevents loving God?

answers.summary: Arnold said it does not, referring to his own upbringing away from his father. He urged personal responsibility and providing a good example to one’s own children.

questions.question: Did Arnold say hard times can teach a person?

answers.summary: Arnold said they can, giving mistakes and their unpleasant consequences as an example of learning not to repeat something. He did not say every hardship was caused by the sufferer’s wrongdoing.

questions.question: Did Arnold say having cancer meant God’s Spirit could not be in a person?

answers.summary: Arnold rejected that conclusion. He said God’s Spirit could reach everywhere, urged prayer and anointing, and used Christ’s contact with people with leprosy to argue against treating illness as proof of God’s absence.

questions.question: Did Arnold say he was running for president?

answers.summary: Arnold said no, emphasizing Bible teaching as his priority. He distinguished that from supporting someone he considered godly and said he was not entering partisan politics. This records a historical broadcast reply.

questions.question: Did Arnold say honestly gained wealth prevents entering heaven?

answers.summary: Arnold says no and distinguishes wealth received through honest work and God’s blessings from ill-gotten gains.

questions.question: Did Arnold say humans could kill Satan when he appears?

answers.summary: Arnold answers no and places Satan’s final destruction under God’s authority. He distinguishes the death of the flesh from the second death and refers to Matthew 10:28 and Ezekiel 28.

questions.question: Did Arnold say hybrid DNA from his fallen-angel interpretation survives today?

answers.summary: Arnold answers no and says the flood destroyed those hybrids while preserving the ark’s occupants. These are his ancestry claims, not established genetics.

questions.question: Did Arnold say imperfect Bible pronunciation endangers salvation?

answers.summary: Arnold reassures the listener that understanding the message and loving God matter, and acknowledges his own pronunciation difficulties.

questions.question: Did Arnold say Jacob and Esau had different fathers?

answers.summary: Arnold expressly denied saying Jacob and Esau had different fathers. He said the listener had confused them with his separate Cain-and-Abel interpretation. The listener cited Romans 9:10; Arnold accepted that Jacob and Esau shared a father.

questions.question: Did Arnold say Jesus was created?

answers.summary: Arnold rejects the premise that God created Jesus and points to Isaiah 7:14, Emmanuel as God with us.

questions.question: Did Arnold say learning through his Bible teaching would be penalized at judgment?

answers.summary: Arnold says no and emphasizes studying God’s Word, thinking for oneself and using Scripture as the standard.

questions.question: Did Arnold say loved ones can help someone who died without overcoming?

answers.summary: Arnold places such help in the millennium rather than the present. He warns against assuming knowledge of a dying person’s final thoughts and describes the elect helping relatives under his interpretation of Ezekiel 44. The captioned verse span needs confirmation.

questions.question: Did Arnold say members of the locust army have souls?

answers.summary: Arnold said they have souls and spirits and therefore are subject to judgment. He did not describe them as soulless machines or insects in this answer.

questions.question: Did Arnold say memories of past sins mean a person is not saved?

answers.summary: Arnold said remembering a forgiven mistake is natural experience that can prevent repetition. He distinguished memory from continuing guilt and urged the listener not to doubt Christ’s saving work.

questions.question: Did Arnold say one Christian may baptize another?

answers.summary: Arnold says any Christian may baptize another Christian, while noting that some churches may not recognize it.

questions.question: Did Arnold say Passover was observed before Moses?

answers.summary: Arnold says no and places its institution in Moses’ time.

questions.question: Did Arnold say people on different sides of paradise’s gulf can see one another?

answers.summary: Arnold says the rich man seeing Lazarus supports visibility across the gulf. He then describes the elect helping relatives during the millennium under his interpretation of Ezekiel 44. He does not clearly establish unrestricted present communication.

questions.question: Did Arnold say religious people can also be spiritually blinded?

answers.summary: Arnold said outward religious habits do not guarantee love for God or willingness to hear Scripture. He criticized divisive traditions and advised testing a teacher’s fruit rather than trusting religious appearances.

questions.question: Did Arnold say salvation can be bought with money?

answers.summary: Arnold says salvation cannot be bought and treats the claim as belittling Christ’s sacrifice.

questions.question: Did Arnold say Satan can actually change people into spiritual bodies?

answers.summary: Arnold said Satan cannot give life or effect the genuine change into spiritual bodies. He distinguished that inability from Satan’s capacity to make things appear otherwise.

questions.question: Did Arnold say Satan could fool believers into thinking they had changed into spiritual bodies?

answers.summary: Arnold answers no and contrasts vulnerable flesh with what he describes as a perfected spiritual body free from ordinary gravity. These physical descriptions are his beliefs, not independently established properties.

questions.question: Did Arnold say Satan is present before being openly seen in the five-month period?

answers.summary: Arnold affirmed presence during the first two and a half months but said he might not be seen then. He said the two witnesses would keep believers informed. The listener’s Mount of Olives premise is not separately documented in the answer.

questions.question: Did Arnold say Satan would be released for another thousand years?

answers.summary: Arnold corrected the listener: Revelation 20 says a short season after the thousand-year reign. He additionally proposed it would not exceed five months and thought it shorter. That limit is his inference, not an explicit duration supplied by the passage.

questions.question: Did Arnold say Satan would be released in 2012?

answers.summary: Arnold explicitly denied having predicted Satan’s release in 2012. He distinguished his teaching about the fig-tree generation from naming a particular year and described the Mayan calendar concern as the end of a calendar segment.

questions.question: Did Arnold say Satan would torture believers into receiving the mark?

answers.summary: Arnold reassured a fearful new believer that Satan would present himself as a saving Christ and deceive through apparent love rather than appear as a torturer. He emphasized God’s protection in his interpretation.

questions.question: Did Arnold say Satan’s appearance aged or changed from creation?

answers.summary: Arnold said angels do not age and described Satan as retaining the beauty he read in Ezekiel 28. He attributed Satan’s fall to pride and the heart rather than physical aging.

questions.question: Did Arnold say Shem, Ham and Japheth were triplets?

answers.summary: Arnold said they were separate single births, not triplets. He did not supply their individual birth dates in this answer.

questions.question: Did Arnold say someone could serve God while working an ordinary sales job?

answers.summary: Arnold said earning a living and setting a Christian example at work could be service to God. He encouraged study and said people seeking instruction might indicate a ministry opportunity, rather than telling the listener to leave his job.

questions.question: Did Arnold say someone who repented of cursing parents remained excluded from Passover?

answers.summary: Arnold emphasized forgiveness after repentance and asking the parents’ forgiveness. He thought the listener was struggling to forgive herself and urged changed conduct rather than continued despair.

questions.question: Did Arnold say testimony before the antichrist happens in groups?

answers.summary: Arnold says groups, interpreting the ten-day trial language as an individual maximum within a longer period. The exact Revelation reference he recalls needs checking.

questions.question: Did Arnold say the absence of a visible visitor at death means a person was abandoned?

answers.summary: Arnold reassured a bereaved mother that she would not necessarily see activity in a different spiritual dimension. He did not treat the absence of a visible sign as evidence that her son lacked help.

questions.question: Did Arnold say the antichrist can force a sealed believer to believe in him?

answers.summary: Arnold said no, while warning that Satan can make things appear otherwise than they are. He emphasized knowing the order of events, trusting the Holy Spirit and the protection he read in Revelation 9:4. Part of the listener’s wording is unclear.

questions.question: Did Arnold say the antichrist must arrive in May?

answers.summary: Arnold affirms a five-month period but says the stage of the locust must be recognized before counting. He refers listeners to upcoming historical Passover messages rather than giving an unqualified May-arrival rule.

questions.question: Did Arnold say the beings called Geber in the captions had souls?

answers.summary: Arnold answers that every entity has a soul and discusses an opportunity to respond properly. The caption term Geber needs confirmation against the audio before a more specific identification is assigned.

questions.question: Did Arnold say the conduct in 2 John 11 could be forgiven?

answers.summary: Arnold said it was forgivable through repentance. He interpreted the warning as including wishing support or donating to teaching he regarded as false, using rapture teaching as an example.

questions.question: Did Arnold say the flowers in his studio were real, and did he require them in worship?

answers.summary: Arnold confirmed that the studio flowers were fresh and expressed gratitude for their beauty and God’s creation. He did not establish the listener’s proposed requirement that worship must include fresh flowers.

questions.question: Did Arnold say the introductory CD had any cost to its recipient?

answers.summary: Arnold said free meant no charge for that introductory offer and distinguished it from other recordings for which support was expected. This describes that broadcast’s offer and does not establish current terms or stock.

questions.question: Did Arnold say the sixth seal had begun in this recording?

answers.summary: Arnold answers no and says he considers it close, with events still to occur. That statement belongs to this historical recording and is not a current assessment.

questions.question: Did Arnold say the spirit returns to God immediately after death?

answers.summary: Arnold points to Ecclesiastes 12:6–7 and says the spirit returns to God while the flesh returns to dust.

questions.question: Did Arnold say the spiritual body is already present during flesh life?

answers.summary: Arnold answers yes and describes the spiritual body as dwelling within the flesh body and departing when the silver cord breaks. He distinguishes the soul, or self, from its spirit, which he calls the intellect.

questions.question: Did Arnold say the Stone of Scone had visited the United States?

answers.summary: Arnold said it had never been in the United States and claimed it had been hidden in Canada during World War II before being returned. This records an unverified historical assertion from the broadcast, not an established travel history of the stone.

questions.question: Did Arnold say the Ten Commandments are discussed elsewhere in Scripture?

answers.summary: Arnold said yes and connected Christ’s two commandments with the ten, dividing them into spiritual and civil responsibilities. He also distinguished murder from killing in his reading of the commandment. This records his explanation without supplying a precise Gospel citation he did not give.

questions.question: Did Arnold say the two witnesses were already present in this recording?

answers.summary: Arnold says no in this recording and describes their supernatural abilities as recognizable.

questions.question: Did Arnold say those struck by the final hailstones miss judgment?

answers.summary: Arnold says everyone comes to judgment. He places the hailstones at the end of this earth age and says the change to spiritual bodies means those bodies are not harmed by them.

questions.question: Did Arnold say which insects and worms would be present in heaven?

answers.summary: Arnold did not give a definite list. He emphasized the changed conditions of Isaiah 11, including animals no longer being carnivorous, and acknowledged limits to what he could infer.

questions.question: Did Arnold see jury duty as forbidden judging?

answers.summary: Arnold approved jury service as a biblical responsibility, describing peers deciding from facts and corroborating witnesses. He distinguished that task from the spiritual judgment he told listeners to leave to God. This is his religious answer, not legal advice.

questions.question: Did Arnold support an unmarried mother dedicating her child to God?

answers.summary: Arnold answers positively and says a parent’s sin is not placed on the child, referring to Jeremiah 31:29. The other recalled legal reference is uncertain and not supplied as precise documentation.

questions.question: Did Arnold support children being baptized in another Christian church?

answers.summary: Arnold says yes when the children understand baptism as publicly affirming Christ’s death and resurrection. He says one Christian can baptize another and encourages the parent’s support.

questions.question: Did Arnold teach that a person’s final destiny is fixed at birth?

answers.summary: Arnold rejected a fixed heaven-or-hell assignment at birth. He emphasized decisions, faith and actions under free will and claimed that God had not already determined every person’s response. This is his theological position.

questions.question: Did Arnold teach that all people descend from Adam and Eve?

answers.summary: Arnold answers no and appeals to separate creation days and the genealogies of Genesis 4–5. His claimed scientific support is not independently established here; the entry records his interpretation.

questions.question: Did Arnold teach that angels can read a person’s mind?

answers.summary: Arnold said neither angels nor Satan can read minds; he reserved that knowledge to God. He then emphasized that God’s complete knowledge makes his judgment fair, including reward for faithful service.

questions.question: Did Arnold teach that antichrist would come from the tribe of Dan?

answers.summary: Arnold rejected that teaching, identifying antichrist with Satan rather than an ordinary member of Dan. He appealed to Ezekiel 28 and 2 Thessalonians 2.

questions.question: Did Arnold teach that apostles or ministers must remain unmarried?

answers.summary: Arnold answers no, points to Peter’s mother-in-law in Mark 1:30 and says some teachers were married while others were not. He also discusses Aquila and Priscilla as married teachers.

questions.question: Did Arnold teach that every soul will be saved during the millennium?

answers.summary: Arnold rejected universal salvation, distinguished spiritual bodies from mortal or immortal souls in his interpretation, and referred to Revelation 20’s final judgment. He also said listeners must not decide individual destinies. The question’s five-month premise after seeing Christ was not clearly resolved in this response.

questions.question: Did Arnold teach that God sends curses or burdens on people?

answers.summary: Arnold uses Jeremiah 23:33 to distinguish God lifting burdens from people bringing trouble on themselves. He says God may withdraw intervention and rejects the idea that another person can place a spiritual curse on a Christian.

questions.question: Did Arnold teach that Jesus was a vegetarian?

answers.summary: Arnold rejected that claim, referred to the fish account in John 21 and distinguished someone choosing vegetarianism from claiming Jesus practiced it. He qualified his approval of meat with his clean-food interpretation.

questions.question: Did Arnold teach that people communicate in paradise?

answers.summary: Arnold answered yes and said people recognize family members who have died. He described the departed as alive with the Father despite bodily death and referred to communication on both sides of paradise.

questions.question: Did Arnold teach that people in his first earth age lacked souls?

answers.summary: Arnold rejected that premise, saying every living person has a soul. He explained Satan stealing souls as deception drawing people from God rather than removing the existence of a soul.

questions.question: Did Arnold teach that people killed one another in the first earth age?

answers.summary: Arnold answers no because he describes them as spiritual beings whose final destruction only God can cause. He refers to Matthew 10:28.

questions.question: Did Arnold teach that spiritual bodies reproduced in the first earth age?

answers.summary: Arnold answers that there were no reproductive organs in that age and distinguishes it from this age and his account of fallen angels. This is his theological explanation rather than a verified biological description.

questions.question: Did Arnold teach that women cannot be in heaven?

answers.summary: Arnold explicitly rejects that idea and refers to sons and daughters prophesying in Acts 2.

questions.question: Did Arnold tell a beer drinker to stop seeking God?

answers.summary: Arnold rejected telling the listener to stop seeking God. He criticized judgmental treatment, advised forgiving the person and also told the listener to exercise self-control and represent God well.

questions.question: Did Arnold tell a child Christ would return when the child turned thirteen?

answers.summary: Arnold gave no such date and said only the Lord knows the time. He did not know the child’s current age from the letter.

questions.question: Did Arnold tell a parent to tithe on child-support payments?

answers.summary: Arnold said no because that money was for the child’s needs. For a financially stretched single parent unable to give a full tenth, he suggested an offering after expenses while leaving the decision with her. This records his ministry advice.

questions.question: Did Arnold think a deceased person from the wrong side of the gulf would comfort someone dying?

answers.summary: Arnold tentatively said probably not, then warned the listener not to judge which side someone occupied. The reported medical circumstances are unclear in the captions; neither a visitation nor its cause is independently verified by this answer.

questions.question: Did Arnold think a person in heaven would have regrets?

answers.summary: Arnold gives his opinion that someone who makes it to heaven would be happy rather than regretful. He labels this as his own opinion.

questions.question: Did Arnold think Cain knew who his father was in Arnold’s serpent-seed interpretation?

answers.summary: Arnold said probably not, emphasizing innocence. He repeated his interpretation of Genesis 3–4 but did not claim direct evidence of Cain’s personal knowledge.

questions.question: Did Arnold think déjà vu could be a glimpse of a first earth age?

answers.summary: Arnold says it is possible, without stating it as certain.

questions.question: Did Arnold think God needed bodyguards because he was afraid?

answers.summary: Arnold denied that God was afraid and described Michael and Gabriel as trusted servants maintaining order and discipline. He said they had not needed flesh birth and connected God’s power with his interpretation of Ezekiel 39. These are his doctrinal claims.

questions.question: Did Arnold think Jesus died on a cross or a stake?

answers.summary: Arnold argued for a Roman cross on the basis of Roman responsibility for the execution and his reading of Psalm 22. He acknowledged differing discussions of the Greek terms but did not conduct a detailed historical comparison in this answer.

questions.question: Did Arnold think Jesus remembered his Father as a child?

answers.summary: Arnold said his thought was yes, citing Jesus’ wisdom at twelve and the Spirit’s presence in the infancy account. He did not separately explain why ordinary people do not remember a prior existence. His distinction remains attributed belief.

questions.question: Did Arnold think Michael and Gabriel had lived through flesh life?

answers.summary: Arnold answered no and repeatedly labeled his explanation opinion. He speculated that their earlier service made flesh life unnecessary, without claiming documentation of what they accomplished.

questions.question: Did Arnold think Revelation 17’s ten kings could be rulers of countries?

answers.summary: Arnold answered that these were rulers in the final generation and said that identification was possible, rather than naming specific leaders.

questions.question: Did Arnold think Satan could confuse or possess God?

answers.summary: Arnold reassured the eight-year-old that an evil spirit could not confuse God, describing God as supreme and supernatural.

questions.question: Did Arnold think Satan could freely cross paradise’s gulf?

answers.summary: Arnold denied that Satan or anyone else could cross the gulf at that time. He recommended Luke 16, distinguished Job 1:6’s earlier freedom from his belief in Michael’s present restraint, and allowed possible crossing during the millennium.

questions.question: Did Arnold think Satan’s influence meant God had lost control?

answers.summary: Arnold said God remained on the throne and in control while permitting Satan’s evil spirit to act. He urged using the authority he associated with Luke 10:19 rather than submitting to that influence.

questions.question: Did Arnold think someone with spiritual understanding could fail to notice an evil influence?

answers.summary: Arnold calls it possible and says people may not recognize what contributes to a fall. This records his spiritual explanation without diagnosing an individual as having an evil spirit.

questions.question: Did Arnold think the antichrist could be a woman?

answers.summary: Arnold said no because he identified the antichrist as Satan himself, whom he described as male. He also rejected identifying that figure as an ordinary person born of a woman.

questions.question: Did Arnold think time matters to a spiritual body?

answers.summary: Arnold says a spiritual body does not age and describes time as unimportant in that state.

questions.question: Did Arnold think women knowingly married fallen angels in his Genesis interpretation?

answers.summary: Arnold said perhaps not in every case and placed blame and punishment on the fallen angels in his reading of Jude 6. He described hybrid offspring and linked their destruction with the flood. These are his interpretations, not established accounts of human reproduction.

questions.question: Did Arnold treat an unwanted divorce and remarriage as an automatic bar to pastoring?

answers.summary: Arnold said no in the listener’s described circumstances, appealing to forgiveness and Romans 11:29. He qualified his answer with the pastor being genuinely called and repentance for any wrongdoing of his own. This is pastoral interpretation, not a legal ruling.

questions.question: Did Arnold treat Dan or Ephraim’s omission as excluding individuals from salvation?

answers.summary: Arnold rejected that conclusion, distinguishing national prophetic roles from an individual’s choice and personal salvation. He expressly included people regardless of tribe or race.

questions.question: Did Arnold treat deception by antichrist as an automatic final sentence to the second death?

answers.summary: Arnold said people deceived into worshipping Satan were not automatically doomed to the second death. He emphasized millennium instruction and reserved final judgment for God rather than human declarations.

questions.question: Did Arnold treat Elijah and Enoch as possible two witnesses?

answers.summary: Arnold corrected the listener’s pair from Elijah and Ezekiel to Elijah and Enoch. He called them very likely candidates, preserving that level of uncertainty rather than declaring a settled identification.

questions.question: Did Arnold treat illness as proof someone had offended God?

answers.summary: Arnold recommended Job as a counterexample to friends blaming illness on wrongdoing. He said illnesses exist in the world and referred to Satan’s role in Job 1, while urging prayer and obedience. He did not establish the medical cause of the listener’s illness.

questions.question: Did Arnold treat instantly in Ecclesiastes 12 as a printed word or an inference?

answers.summary: Challenged because instantly was absent from the passage, Arnold defended an immediate return of the spirit by reasoning from the silver cord breaking. He described aging and the body returning to dust. His answer offers an interpretation of the timing, not evidence that the English word instantly appears in those verses.

questions.question: Did Arnold treat Matthew 24 and Mark 13 as fully fulfilled in AD 70?

answers.summary: Arnold rejects that interpretation and centers the chapters on Christ’s return and the fig-tree generation. His answer does not separately analyze every historical layer of the passages.

questions.question: Did Arnold treat Peter’s vision as permission to eat any food?

answers.summary: Arnold said no and connected food created to be received in 1 Timothy 4:3 with Leviticus 11. He described scavengers as useful for their created purpose. His dietary and health claims are reported as religious interpretation, not individual nutritional advice.

questions.question: Did Arnold warn against asking God for patience?

answers.summary: Arnold rejects that warning and encourages asking God for help with patience, distinguishing that request from the problems impatience can cause.

questions.question: Did beast of the field in Genesis 3 mean other people?

answers.summary: Dennis says it refers to animals. He explains subtle as cunning or tricky and relates the animal comparison to the serpent designation.

questions.question: Did Cain and Abel have sisters?

answers.summary: Dennis says Adam and Eve had further children and explains his view that Seth’s family came from them, before the later Mosaic incest prohibitions.

questions.question: Did Christ’s sacrifice change circumcision for Christians?

answers.summary: Dennis says blood ordinances were nailed to the cross with Christ. He describes Christian circumcision as circumcision of the heart, applying to women and men alike.

questions.question: Did Dennis accept a flat-earth teaching?

answers.summary: Dennis rejects it, describes Earth as round and says he does not know why that teaching is spreading.

questions.question: Did Dennis accept a Jewish listener’s confession of Jesus as Christian faith?

answers.summary: Dennis says yes and welcomes the listener, who says she has confessed Jesus as Savior and been baptized.

questions.question: Did Dennis accept a man’s claim to have opened the sixth seal?

answers.summary: Dennis says no man can open the seals and directs the listener to Revelation 6.

questions.question: Did Dennis accept Mary’s assumption into heaven as biblical?

answers.summary: Dennis affirms Mary as Jesus’s mother but says her being taken up is a human tradition, distinguishing it from his reading of Elijah and Enoch.

questions.question: Did Dennis accept the claim that Jesus had a child with Mary Magdalene?

answers.summary: Dennis rejects the claim and says it cannot be documented from the Bible.

questions.question: Did Dennis acknowledge a change from five months to two and a half months?

answers.summary: Dennis explicitly says the teaching changed. He interprets the five months as the hour of tribulation and the half hour of silence as Satan’s two-and-a-half-month presence on earth.

questions.question: Did Dennis advise abandoning dialysis while trusting in healing?

answers.summary: Dennis says belief in God’s power to heal must accompany trust in qualified physicians. He explicitly warns against stopping needed dialysis and says medical testing determines whether it remains necessary.

questions.question: Did Dennis advise being saved again after backsliding?

answers.summary: Dennis encourages belief in Christ and repentance after backsliding, warning against treating salvation as something to obtain repeatedly.

questions.question: Did Dennis advise Christians to associate only with other Christians?

answers.summary: Dennis says people in need must be reached and warns that restricting oneself to Christian company can become a holier-than-thou attitude.

questions.question: Did Dennis advise notifying estranged children of their mother’s death?

answers.summary: Dennis says he would notify next of kin unless the listener had promised his mother otherwise. He describes funerals as being for the living and urges prayer in the difficult family situation.

questions.question: Did Dennis advise praying for the devil?

answers.summary: Dennis says no, because he regards Satan’s destruction as already settled in Scripture, and agrees with praying for God’s will instead.

questions.question: Did Dennis advise praying to a man?

answers.summary: After correcting his reading of the question, Dennis says not to pray to a man and directs the listener to the heavenly Father.

questions.question: Did Dennis advise preparing testimony against the antichrist ahead of time?

answers.summary: Dennis urges Bible study but says not to premeditate that testimony; he says to wait for what the Holy Spirit gives in the hour of delivery.

questions.question: Did Dennis advise seeking a confrontation with Antichrist?

answers.summary: Dennis says no, pointing instead to the instruction to flee Judea when the abomination stands there. He distinguishes that from the elect being delivered up for Spirit-given testimony in due course.

questions.question: Did Dennis affirm life after death?

answers.summary: Dennis affirms everlasting life through belief in Christ and points to Paul’s discussion of terrestrial and celestial bodies.

questions.question: Did Dennis agree that God is infinite in wisdom, power and love?

answers.summary: Dennis agrees with the listener’s description and calls God’s wisdom, power and love limitless.

questions.question: Did Dennis agree that Jesus never drank wine?

answers.summary: Dennis challenges that conclusion by citing Jesus’ statement about not drinking again of the vine until the kingdom. He also mentions the water-to-wine miracle, while acknowledging that account does not say Jesus drank it.

questions.question: Did Dennis agree that Lazarus in Luke 16 was imaginary?

answers.summary: Dennis disagrees with the dictionary interpretation reported by the listener and connects the name with Eleazar and his interpretation of a priesthood needing resurrection.

questions.question: Did Dennis agree that paradise was destroyed when Christ died?

answers.summary: Dennis rejects the claim, explains the key of David through Messiah’s lineage, and places final judgment in Revelation 20.

questions.question: Did Dennis allow limits on helping relatives who repeatedly misuse help?

answers.summary: Dennis says yes, advising separation from persistently unchristian conduct while warning the person as a brother rather than treating them as an enemy.

questions.question: Did Dennis allow repentance during the millennium?

answers.summary: Dennis says final judgment has not yet occurred and describes the millennium as a teaching period, while warning against postponing repentance or treating it as a second chance after knowingly rejecting truth.

questions.question: Did Dennis answer whether Satan could rapture people?

answers.summary: Dennis warns that antichrist will use deceptive miracles, but does not directly establish a literal rapture capability.

questions.question: Did Dennis apply Israel’s ancient king-selection rule to modern voting?

answers.summary: Dennis says that rule concerned Israel’s kings and tells the listener to vote for the person they judge best qualified for the job today.

questions.question: Did Dennis apply Luke 1:15’s abstinence instruction to every child?

answers.summary: Dennis says the passage concerns John the Baptist specifically, whom he describes as under a Nazarite vow from birth like Samson. He separately urges pregnant mothers to avoid alcohol.

questions.question: Did Dennis apply no work, no food to people trying to find work?

answers.summary: Dennis applied 2 Thessalonians 3:10 to people able to work who refuse to do so. He distinguished those trying to find work or temporarily needing help and supported offering them a helping hand.

questions.question: Did Dennis approve a step-grandchild calling someone Grandma?

answers.summary: Dennis said yes and encouraged reciprocal recognition of the child as a granddaughter.

questions.question: Did Dennis approve asking forgiveness each night for possible sins?

answers.summary: Dennis approves, while emphasizing sincere repentance and a change of heart rather than permission to continue sinning.

questions.question: Did Dennis approve helping an incarcerated relative?

answers.summary: Dennis calls modest help and encouragement compassionate. He says to check the institution’s rules before sending study materials or other items.

questions.question: Did Dennis approve of divination by Christians?

answers.summary: Dennis says Christians should not practice divination to determine future events.

questions.question: Did Dennis approve praying for baptized relatives who changed beliefs?

answers.summary: Dennis says such prayer is appropriate and suggests reassuring them of God’s love. He emphasizes God’s patience and desire for repentance rather than portraying faith only as fear of punishment.

questions.question: Did Dennis approve prepaying utilities for his expected antichrist period?

answers.summary: Dennis approved the listener’s proposal to prepay electricity, water and trash service while setting aside food. His brief answer was preparation advice within his end-time interpretation, without a guarantee about any provider or future event.

questions.question: Did Dennis approve sharing Scripture to correct errors online?

answers.summary: Dennis says yes when the person is knowledgeable and feels led by the Holy Spirit.

questions.question: Did Dennis approve supporting children in Ethiopia?

answers.summary: Dennis says showing compassion to people in need is acceptable and points to Matthew 25.

questions.question: Did Dennis approve using the pulpit to shame an individual?

answers.summary: Dennis says a preacher should build up the congregation, not single someone out for humiliation. He distinguishes intentional shaming from a listener feeling that a broadly addressed message applies personally.

questions.question: Did Dennis approve writing study notes in a Bible?

answers.summary: Dennis describes extensive notes and cross-references in his own Bible and treats them as useful teaching aids.

questions.question: Did Dennis assign a fixed number of years between trumpets?

answers.summary: Dennis says trumpets mark events rather than fixed time intervals and recommends Arnold’s study on the seven seals and trumpets.

questions.question: Did Dennis assign antichrist a particular national region?

answers.summary: Dennis described a claim over the whole world rather than one region and said national identities would not be the basis of that rule.

questions.question: Did Dennis associate right- or left-handedness with good luck?

answers.summary: Dennis says there is no biblical basis for one hand being lucky. He then offers his interpretation of Ehud’s description in Judges.

questions.question: Did Dennis assume a spirit had departed because a person needed mechanical breathing support?

answers.summary: Dennis does not assume a person’s spirit has departed merely because machines sustain breathing and recommends making one’s wishes known to family beforehand.

questions.question: Did Dennis assume Genesis 6 describes childbirth of already full-grown giants?

answers.summary: Dennis says the offspring grew into giants rather than necessarily being giant-sized at birth and says the passage does not explicitly describe rape. His subsequent oversized-baby story is humor, not evidence.

questions.question: Did Dennis attribute David not building the temple to lack of architectural skill?

answers.summary: Dennis says the reason was shedding blood, not architectural incompetence, and notes that Solomon also had help building the temple.

questions.question: Did Dennis attribute Stonehenge to aliens?

answers.summary: Dennis says aliens are not described in God’s Word and refers the listener to a book about Stonehenge and Druidism, explicitly distinguishing it from Scripture.

questions.question: Did Dennis attribute the Egyptian pyramids to aliens?

answers.summary: Dennis explained biblical strangers as human foreigners and did not offer an alien-builder explanation. For further pyramid study he recommended two works in the ministry’s reference library; those authors are not used as independent teaching authorities here.

questions.question: Did Dennis authenticate a purported letter describing Jesus’ appearance?

answers.summary: Dennis says he does not know whether the letter is valid, though he finds it interesting. He does not certify its description of Jesus.

questions.question: Did Dennis authorize praying to or worshiping archangels?

answers.summary: Dennis says no, pointing to the angel who refused John’s worship and called himself a fellow servant.

questions.question: Did Dennis automatically condemn everyone who dies by suicide?

answers.summary: Dennis explicitly says the Chapel does not pronounce that judgment. He leaves it to God, who knows the person’s heart and mind.

questions.question: Did Dennis bar divorced people from communion?

answers.summary: Dennis says no and welcomes the listener to communion, emphasizing Christ’s worthiness rather than treating divorced people as second-class Christians.

questions.question: Did Dennis believe a mother would recognize her son after death?

answers.summary: Dennis says he believes she will still recognize him and relates that hope to his reading of family relationships in Ezekiel 44.

questions.question: Did Dennis believe animals exist in heaven?

answers.summary: Dennis appeals to Isaiah’s peaceful animals and explains them as spiritual rather than flesh creatures.

questions.question: Did Dennis believe departed loved ones can see the stars we see?

answers.summary: Dennis says he believes the heavenly bodies can be enjoyed from both dimensions, while acknowledging that we cannot see departed loved ones from here.

questions.question: Did Dennis believe departed people freely communicate with the living?

answers.summary: Dennis says he does not believe general communication is allowed, while allowing that God might send an angel as a messenger for a specific purpose.

questions.question: Did Dennis believe God experiences sadness?

answers.summary: Dennis says yes, reasoning that people were made in God’s image and share feelings and emotions.

questions.question: Did Dennis believe God knows in advance what each person with free will will do?

answers.summary: Dennis says he does not believe God knows those choices in advance and explains this in terms of his teaching on the earth ages.

questions.question: Did Dennis believe God personally walked and talked with Adam and Eve?

answers.summary: Dennis answered yes and compared it with God appearing and speaking to Moses.

questions.question: Did Dennis believe Job lived alongside dinosaurs?

answers.summary: Dennis corrected the listener: he placed Job as a flesh man after the dinosaurs and understood God’s reference to behemoth in Job 40 as looking back to a first earth age. He said that age contained spiritual beings rather than flesh humans. He did not give a date or duration for it.

questions.question: Did Dennis believe Judas was Satan’s son?

answers.summary: Dennis rejected the listener’s suggestion that Judas was Satan’s son. He acknowledged different names or roles attributed to Satan but said that proposed parentage did not follow.

questions.question: Did Dennis believe Leah and Rachel were twins?

answers.summary: Dennis says he does not think so, while acknowledging that the description of elder and younger does not exclude twins.

questions.question: Did Dennis believe Mary sinned during her life?

answers.summary: Dennis says it is not written and presents his guess that she sinned in the flesh, unlike Jesus.

questions.question: Did Dennis believe miscarried or aborted babies must be born again in the flesh?

answers.summary: Dennis says he does not believe so and reasons that they have met the requirement of being in the flesh.

questions.question: Did Dennis believe people remember their flesh lives after death?

answers.summary: Dennis says he believes they do, reasoning that judgment would otherwise not be fair.

questions.question: Did Dennis believe people would recognize Jesus after death?

answers.summary: Dennis says he believes they will, connecting this with his teaching that Christ existed from the beginning and people lived in spiritual bodies before flesh life.

questions.question: Did Dennis believe Peter could forgive himself for denying Jesus?

answers.summary: Dennis says he thinks Peter eventually did. He treats Peter’s failure as a warning against overconfidence and an encouragement to remain faithful under pressure.

questions.question: Did Dennis believe someone could sell a soul to Satan?

answers.summary: Dennis says no, because all souls belong to God and only God has power to destroy a soul.

questions.question: Did Dennis call all three pilgrimage feasts high Sabbaths?

answers.summary: Dennis distinguishes the three major ingatherings from his own use of high Sabbath specifically for Passover. He recommends Arnold’s God’s Calendar study rather than completing a solar calculation here.

questions.question: Did Dennis call asking someone to swear to God unforgivable?

answers.summary: Dennis says the listener can repent and be forgiven, distinguishing this from his explanation of blaspheming the Holy Spirit.

questions.question: Did Dennis call correcting someone’s wrongdoing forbidden judgment?

answers.summary: Dennis appeals to Ezekiel’s watchman passages as a duty to warn, and to2Thessalonians as instruction to admonish as a brother rather than an enemy while maintaining boundaries.

questions.question: Did Dennis call cursing God while intoxicated the unforgivable sin?

answers.summary: Dennis says it can be repented of and forgiven. He distinguishes it from his interpretation of refusing the Holy Spirit’s testimony when delivered up.

questions.question: Did Dennis call every descendant of Abraham a child of Israel?

answers.summary: Dennis says no and distinguishes the line through Isaac from Ishmael.

questions.question: Did Dennis call for a physical fight against antichrist?

answers.summary: Dennis says it is a spiritual conflict, points to Ephesians 6 and Mark 13, and describes the Holy Spirit speaking through the elect.

questions.question: Did Dennis call modern technology inherently good or bad?

answers.summary: Dennis says its use determines whether it helps or harms. He contrasts spreading Scripture to many homes with distributing pornography and connects wider outreach with Jesus’ greater-works statement.

questions.question: Did Dennis call murder the unforgivable sin?

answers.summary: Dennis says murder is not the unforgivable sin, while distinguishing his view of salvation in the flesh from God’s eventual judgment. He leaves judgment with God and says the victim will be present.

questions.question: Did Dennis claim certainty about fallen angels having belly buttons?

answers.summary: Dennis speculates that, in his view that they were not born of women, they probably would not. He ends by saying he does not know.

questions.question: Did Dennis claim certainty that Judas was forgiven?

answers.summary: Dennis says Matthew records Judas repenting but not explicitly receiving forgiveness. He guesses that Judas probably was forgiven, rather than presenting certainty.

questions.question: Did Dennis claim certainty that people in the garden were vegetarians?

answers.summary: Dennis says they may or may not have been, then directs the listener to the dietary distinctions in Leviticus 11.

questions.question: Did Dennis claim Scripture specifies how fallen angels traveled to earth?

answers.summary: Dennis acknowledges it is not written, then offers his belief that they used vehicles like those he interprets in Ezekiel 1. He refers listeners to Arnold’s Horses of the Bible study.

questions.question: Did Dennis clarify an earlier statement that people cannot serve God in prison?

answers.summary: Dennis acknowledges he should have spoken more clearly. He affirms good work by prisoners and prison ministries and distinguishes that from avoidable imprisonment interfering with a particular calling.

questions.question: Did Dennis classify ducks as clean or unclean for food?

answers.summary: Dennis says ducks are unclean. He gives no further explanation in this brief answer.

questions.question: Did Dennis classify sharks and seals as clean food?

answers.summary: Dennis excludes both under his application of the requirement for fins and scales.

questions.question: Did Dennis classify tobacco smoking as sorcery?

answers.summary: Dennis says no, while calling smoking unhealthy. In this answer he distinguishes his use of sorcery for illicit drug dealing from legitimate pharmacy work.

questions.question: Did Dennis clearly say whether returning fallen angels could be distinguished from humans?

answers.summary: Dennis began an answer about distinguishability, then backed up to discuss the absence of hybrids and angelic restraint. The saved response does not clearly complete the specific question about recognizing returning angels.

questions.question: Did Dennis conclude that being like angels means everyone will be male?

answers.summary: Dennis discusses the absence of marriage in the resurrection and the feminine image of the bride of Christ, without giving a categorical literal gender answer.

questions.question: Did Dennis condemn incest between a mother and son?

answers.summary: Dennis condemns sexual relations between a mother and son as incest.

questions.question: Did Dennis condemn sadness or prayers for a seriously ill friend?

answers.summary: Dennis says it is natural to miss someone and proper to pray for the friend’s health and longer life, while praying in God’s will. He distinguishes grief over separation from hope that the deceased is with the Lord.

questions.question: Did Dennis condemn taking prescribed medicine as sorcery?

answers.summary: Dennis explicitly distinguishes prescribed treatment from illegal drug dealing, encourages following the physician’s directions, and warns against secretly altering doses while the doctor assumes the prescribed dose is being taken.

questions.question: Did Dennis confirm that 666 means WWW in Greek?

answers.summary: Dennis says he does not know what the listener means by that claim, then gives his own interpretation of 666 as the sixth trump, seal and vial.

questions.question: Did Dennis confirm that particular UFO sightings were angels?

answers.summary: Dennis replied that nothing flying is unidentified to God. He did not verify any particular sighting or identify it as an angel.

questions.question: Did Dennis connect first shall be last with the first and last Adam?

answers.summary: Dennis says he does not see that connection. He interprets first and last as the elect who stood with God before and live in the final flesh generation to testify against Antichrist.

questions.question: Did Dennis connect Job’s destructive fire with Satan’s signs in Revelation?

answers.summary: Dennis says yes, attributing the fire in Job to Satan acting within the permission described earlier in the chapter.

questions.question: Did Dennis connect the word woman with woe or fallen angels?

answers.summary: Dennis rejects both suggestions. He says the English resemblance to woe does not establish that meaning and distinguishes women from the fallen angels in his reading of Genesis 6.

questions.question: Did Dennis consider a dying person’s report of seeing deceased relatives possible?

answers.summary: Dennis says he believes relatives may be sent to help someone cross over near death. He offers this as his explanation of the reported experience, without verifying this individual event.

questions.question: Did Dennis consider a prayer for an incurably ill spouse’s suffering to end sinful?

answers.summary: Dennis calls the listener compassionate and says he sees nothing wrong with asking God either to heal the spouse or receive him. He is discussing prayer, not taking action to cause death.

questions.question: Did Dennis consider all prophecy already fulfilled?

answers.summary: Dennis says much has been fulfilled but points to remaining prophecy concerning the antichrist, including passages in Psalms, Ezekiel, Revelation, Isaiah and Jeremiah.

questions.question: Did Dennis consider an inheritance income for tithing?

answers.summary: Dennis says he would treat it as income, while encouraging the listener to pray and follow God’s guidance.

questions.question: Did Dennis consider caring for a disabled elderly friend a righteous act?

answers.summary: Dennis says yes and acknowledges the stress and hard work of caregiving, reminding caregivers not to neglect their own care.

questions.question: Did Dennis consider cremation sinful?

answers.summary: Dennis says no: he understands the body returning to earth and the spirit returning to God as independent of the method of bodily disposal.

questions.question: Did Dennis consider donating casino winnings acceptable?

answers.summary: Dennis says donating winnings is acceptable and cautions against gambling with money needed for bills or family needs.

questions.question: Did Dennis consider eating unclean food a sin against the soul?

answers.summary: Dennis says the food laws concern fleshly health rather than the soul. He recommends following them but acknowledges that he sometimes eats shrimp and does not observe them perfectly.

questions.question: Did Dennis consider every small lottery or bingo wager wrong?

answers.summary: Dennis says modest entertainment spending is not specifically forbidden, but emphasizes control and moderation. He warns against gambling money needed for groceries, rent or children’s education and says to seek help if it becomes a problem.

questions.question: Did Dennis consider every vision or dream a message from God?

answers.summary: Dennis says no and notes that hallucinations and other experiences can have causes other than divine revelation.

questions.question: Did Dennis consider evil spirits to be of Satan?

answers.summary: Dennis says evil spirits are satanic but discourages imagining one everywhere. He emphasizes that believers need not fear them and points to authority in Jesus’ name.

questions.question: Did Dennis consider it wrong to choose not to have a funeral?

answers.summary: Dennis says there is nothing biblically wrong with that choice and notes that funerals can help surviving family members.

questions.question: Did Dennis consider it wrong to pray the prayer of Jabez?

answers.summary: Dennis says there is nothing wrong with asking God for blessings and treats Jabez’s prayer as an example. He emphasizes living a life God can bless and both studying and doing what is pleasing to Him.

questions.question: Did Dennis consider it wrong to say peace?

answers.summary: Dennis says there is nothing wrong with saying peace. He separately interprets calls for world peace through his end-times teaching and distinguishes the end of an age from destruction of the world.

questions.question: Did Dennis consider playing video games after Bible study wrong?

answers.summary: Dennis said wholesome entertainment can have a place alongside study. He advised moderation, prayer and discipline, especially because the listener had previously struggled to limit play. He also urged parents to monitor games and Internet use. His further suggestion linking violent games with school violence was his opinion, not a finding established by this review.

questions.question: Did Dennis consider protecting one’s home incompatible with trusting God?

answers.summary: Dennis distinguishes practical protection of a home from trusting an earthly object for salvation. He says salvation comes through God and Christ, not through a weapon.

questions.question: Did Dennis consider selling ordinary ceramics a violation of the command against idols?

answers.summary: Dennis says making or selling cups, bowls and similar objects is not wrong when they are not made for worship.

questions.question: Did Dennis consider seven too young for baptism?

answers.summary: Dennis says readiness depends on understanding and personally accepting Christ, not a fixed age. He describes asking young candidates about that decision.

questions.question: Did Dennis consider shrimp permissible under his teaching on food laws?

answers.summary: Dennis says no, applying the requirement that water creatures have fins and scales and classifying shrimp as unclean.

questions.question: Did Dennis consider suicide the unforgivable sin?

answers.summary: Dennis says no and leaves the person’s judgment to God, who knows their heart and mind and judges fairly. He does not claim to decide this deceased person’s outcome.

questions.question: Did Dennis consider the Old Testament still worthy of study?

answers.summary: Dennis insists the Old Testament remains worthy of study and relates 1 Corinthians 10:11 to its examples and warnings.

questions.question: Did Dennis count caring for a disabled elderly parent as good works?

answers.summary: Dennis says yes, especially recognizing the caregiver’s own disability. He explains that believers have different gifts and not everyone serves as an evangelist.

questions.question: Did Dennis count inviting people to Bible teaching as planting seeds?

answers.summary: Dennis says yes and emphasizes that not everyone needs to quote Scripture from memory to contribute to the work.

questions.question: Did Dennis count preaching as a substitute for a tithe?

answers.summary: Dennis says he does not consider teaching or preaching a tithe and notes that the Levites were also required to tithe.

questions.question: Did Dennis decide whether a listener should leave a church that taught only John?

answers.summary: Dennis says he cannot choose her church and allows that she may be there to help others. He also cautions against supporting teaching contrary to Christ, citing2John.

questions.question: Did Dennis decide whether a listener who drinks alcohol would go to heaven?

answers.summary: Dennis cites biblical wine examples but leaves the listener’s salvation between that person and the Lord.

questions.question: Did Dennis decide whether Judas ultimately receives forgiveness?

answers.summary: Dennis leaves Judas’s final judgment to God, notes his repentance and says he would not have wanted Judas’s role in fulfilling prophecy.

questions.question: Did Dennis declare Judas already in hell?

answers.summary: Dennis says no one is in hell at that time, refers to the two sides of the gulf and Judas’ repentance, and leaves the final judgment to God.

questions.question: Did Dennis describe a wife as the tail of her husband?

answers.summary: Dennis rejects that wording, cites mutual honor and describes spouses as one flesh who should not offend each other.

questions.question: Did Dennis describe another way into God’s kingdom besides Christ?

answers.summary: Dennis says entry is through Jesus Christ and cites 1 John 2:22.

questions.question: Did Dennis describe Christ’s return as frightening for everyone?

answers.summary: Dennis says it will be wonderful for those waiting for Christ, but shameful for those realizing they worshiped the antichrist.

questions.question: Did Dennis describe each trump as lasting the same length?

answers.summary: Dennis says the trumps are not equal fixed periods and describes his view of the fifth, sixth and seventh trumps.

questions.question: Did Dennis describe entering the afterlife as another birth?

answers.summary: Dennis says people are born into flesh, while at death the flesh returns to earth and the spirit returns to God.

questions.question: Did Dennis describe Hagar as belonging to Sarah’s tribe?

answers.summary: Dennis says Hagar was Sarah’s Egyptian maidservant, not of the same tribe, and describes her role as Ishmael’s mother.

questions.question: Did Dennis describe Joseph as Jesus’s stepfather?

answers.summary: Dennis says Joseph can be regarded as Jesus’s stepfather while distinguishing Joseph’s genealogy from Jesus’s. He challenges the listener’s description of Joseph as a concubine.

questions.question: Did Dennis describe meeting Christ in the air as leaving earth?

answers.summary: Dennis interprets air as the breath of life and meeting Christ in spiritual bodies at the last trumpet, while Christ returns to the Mount of Olives.

questions.question: Did Dennis describe ordinary bodily death as transfiguration?

answers.summary: Dennis distinguishes ordinary death, in which flesh returns to earth and spirit to God, from the rare transfiguration accounts he discusses. He specifically labels Moses’ inclusion as his belief. He does not answer the question about pain directly.

questions.question: Did Dennis describe Paul’s death as explicitly recorded in Scripture?

answers.summary: Dennis distinguishes it from the biblical account and says some historians place Paul’s beheading in Rome under Nero around AD 67–68.

questions.question: Did Dennis describe the ancestry he called Kenite as spiritual or physical?

answers.summary: Dennis described it as physical and appealed to his reading of Strong’s Hebrew entries and the serpent-seed interpretation. This preserves his teaching without treating it as verified genetics or assigning that ancestry to modern people.

questions.question: Did Dennis describe the Holy Spirit’s abiding presence as unconditional?

answers.summary: Dennis says the promise is conditioned on loving Christ and keeping His commandments.

questions.question: Did Dennis describe the lake of fire as temporary correction?

answers.summary: Dennis says its effect is permanent destruction, not a punishment after which its occupants return to eternity with God.

questions.question: Did Dennis describe the trumpets in Revelation as periods of time?

answers.summary: Dennis says they are events that must occur before Christ returns and refers to Matthew 24 and Mark 13.

questions.question: Did Dennis distinguish a minister’s pay from preaching for money?

answers.summary: Dennis contrasted serving wealth with a worker receiving support. He allowed payment while saying money should not be the motive for preaching, and advised noticing ministries focused chiefly on financial pressure.

questions.question: Did Dennis distinguish communist people from the communist system?

answers.summary: Dennis says God loves the people while opposing the system. He illustrates his distinction with Christians undergoing baptism despite difficult conditions.

questions.question: Did Dennis distinguish hunting from animal sacrifice for sins?

answers.summary: Dennis approved hunting and distinguished it from killing an animal as a sacrifice to cover sin. He said the latter had been fulfilled by Christ and noted that biblical hunting provided food; he did not claim Scripture specifically documented sport hunting.

questions.question: Did Dennis distinguish Mary’s husband from Joseph with eleven brothers?

answers.summary: Dennis says these are different men separated by centuries. He recommends looking up the name in a Bible dictionary to distinguish people sharing a name.

questions.question: Did Dennis distinguish Moses’ father-in-law Reuel from other men with that name?

answers.summary: Dennis says Jethro is a title meaning his excellency and identifies Reuel as the given name. He says several people in the Bible bear the name Reuel and recommends a Bible dictionary to distinguish them.

questions.question: Did Dennis distinguish paradise from heaven?

answers.summary: Dennis uses the terms for the same destination while distinguishing the two sides of the gulf in his interpretation of Luke 16.

questions.question: Did Dennis distinguish paying a minister from preaching for money?

answers.summary: Dennis says a worker deserves support but money must not be the motivation for preaching. He contrasts serving God with serving wealth.

questions.question: Did Dennis distinguish sleeping in Christ from being dead in Christ?

answers.summary: Dennis says they describe the same people: believers who have died and are already with the Father.

questions.question: Did Dennis distinguish the seven eyes from the 7,000 elect?

answers.summary: Dennis identifies the seven eyes as a symbol of the 7,000 elect, referring to both Zechariah 3 and 4.

questions.question: Did Dennis encourage a nine-year-old to teach or share Scripture?

answers.summary: Dennis encouraged beginning to share faith with friends while first learning the word. He recommended following in a personal Bible to learn where its books are located rather than relying only on screen text.

questions.question: Did Dennis encourage attributing one’s burdens to God?
