answers.summary: Dennis warns against saying God imposed a burden and directs the listener to Jeremiah 23, including its warnings about false prophets.

questions.question: Did Dennis encourage prayer before eating?

answers.summary: Dennis says to receive food with thanksgiving and appreciates families pausing to pray before meals.

questions.question: Did Dennis encourage private punishment for rape or child molestation?

answers.summary: Dennis describes severe penalties in his interpretation of Old Testament law, but explicitly says Christians must obey the law of the land and leave crimes to the courts. He rejects taking punishment into one’s own hands.

questions.question: Did Dennis endorse2033 as a calculated year for Christ’s return?

answers.summary: Dennis says Scripture does not supply the proposed fixed two-thousand-year absence and emphasizes that no person knows the return’s hour.

questions.question: Did Dennis equate a listener’s blindness with God being angry?

answers.summary: Dennis says no, refers to the man born blind in John 9 and reassures the listener of God’s love. He suggests a purpose without identifying the cause of her condition.

questions.question: Did Dennis equate a listener’s family troubles with the two tribulations he taught?

answers.summary: Dennis says no. He distinguishes the antichrist’s deception from the distress of realizing that deception when Christ returns.

questions.question: Did Dennis equate a soul flying away at death with the rapture?

answers.summary: Dennis says no. He connects Psalm 90 with the spirit returning to God and the flesh returning to earth at death.

questions.question: Did Dennis equate charitable gifts with tithing?

answers.summary: Dennis commends helping people in need but distinguishes charity from tithes supporting the teaching of Scripture.

questions.question: Did Dennis equate Christ’s resurrection with His second advent?

answers.summary: Dennis says no, distinguishing the resurrection from the future return at the seventh trump and the change from flesh bodies.

questions.question: Did Dennis equate difficulty memorizing Scripture with inevitable deception?

answers.summary: Dennis distinguishes memorization from understanding and reassures the listener that knowing antichrist comes first is what matters in this concern.

questions.question: Did Dennis equate discernment with refusing all contact with people who do wrong?

answers.summary: Dennis says believers should avoid adopting wrongful conduct without becoming self-righteous or abandoning opportunities to teach and help others.

questions.question: Did Dennis equate eunuchs with homosexual people?

answers.summary: Dennis says the terms are not equivalent. He explains eunuch as a keeper of bedchambers or a household official, noting that the broader usage need not describe a person’s physical condition.

questions.question: Did Dennis equate evil spirits with the restrained fallen angels?

answers.summary: Dennis says no. He suggests an evil spirit might be associated with a deceased person but explicitly does not treat that as the only explanation, and distinguishes it from the angels’ restraint.

questions.question: Did Dennis equate Ezekiel44’s seven-day cleansing with Satan’s release?

answers.summary: Dennis says not necessarily and places Satan’s short release near the end of the millennium. He describes the identity of the binding angel as his belief rather than certainty.

questions.question: Did Dennis equate God with nature?

answers.summary: Dennis says no, while describing nature as revealing God’s creation. He advises worshiping the Creator rather than the things created.

questions.question: Did Dennis equate purgatory with the gulf in paradise?

answers.summary: Dennis rejected purgatory as a human tradition and distinguished it from the two sides of the gulf in his reading of Luke 16.

questions.question: Did Dennis equate saying God with blasphemy of the Holy Spirit?

answers.summary: Dennis says no and distinguishes using God’s name from his teaching about refusing the Holy Spirit when delivered up.

questions.question: Did Dennis equate selling a goat with participating in its later religious sacrifice?

answers.summary: Dennis says the buyer is responsible for what happens after the sale and does not equate the Christian seller’s transaction with sacrificing to another religion’s god.

questions.question: Did Dennis equate the many antichrists with the angels in Jude?

answers.summary: Dennis distinguishes his interpretation of fallen angels who were not born of women from warnings about people claiming to be Christians.

questions.question: Did Dennis equate the rebellious third with 7,000 fallen angels?

answers.summary: Dennis says these are different groups. He describes twelve billion total souls as an undocumented educated guess, not a biblical count, and uses it only to illustrate what one third would mean.

questions.question: Did Dennis equate the unmarried sister in Ezekiel 44:25 with lacking Christ as husband?

answers.summary: Dennis rejects that added identification and says the passage concerns immediate family members.

questions.question: Did Dennis equate thinking about God on earth with already being in heaven?

answers.summary: Dennis distinguishes God dwelling among Israel in the past from His present throne in heaven and future return to earth.

questions.question: Did Dennis exclude a listener born before 1948 from being useful in God’s plan?

answers.summary: Dennis reassured the listener that her birth year did not settle the issue. He described the elect being present during antichrist’s time and emphasized the importance of the remnant passing truth along as well.

questions.question: Did Dennis exempt people without biblical teaching from accountability?

answers.summary: Dennis says all are accountable, while describing the millennium as a time of instruction for people who lacked an opportunity to learn truth.

questions.question: Did Dennis expect a listener to see his mother again after death?

answers.summary: Dennis says yes and distinguishes physical death from the final death he places after judgment.

questions.question: Did Dennis expect a rebuilt sacrificial temple before Christ’s return?

answers.summary: Dennis says no and identifies Christ as the temple. He cites Revelation’s description of God and the Lamb as its temple and Jesus’ promise to raise the temple in three days as referring to his body.

questions.question: Did Dennis expect animals in eternity?

answers.summary: Dennis says yes and refers to Isaiah 11 and Revelation 4:11.

questions.question: Did Dennis expect antichrist to appear male?

answers.summary: Dennis says antichrist will appear male while pretending to be Jesus, and cautions that he will not be in a flesh body.

questions.question: Did Dennis expect antichrist to be a flesh-born man?

answers.summary: Dennis identifies antichrist as a role of Satan and says Satan comes in a spiritual body, without birth in flesh.

questions.question: Did Dennis expect antichrist to behead Christians who refuse worship?

answers.summary: Dennis argues that beheading people would undermine antichrist’s claim to be Jesus. He says the elect are protected and that 7,000 represents a spiritually complete number, not a limit he independently fixes.

questions.question: Did Dennis expect Antichrist to martyr the elect?

answers.summary: Dennis says the elect are protected by God’s seal and distinguishes the two witnesses, whom he says are slain. He cites the limit on the locust army harming those sealed.

questions.question: Did Dennis expect arthritis to affect a spiritual body?

answers.summary: Dennis says a spiritual body is not subject to arthritis rather than specifying a physical substance from which it is made.

questions.question: Did Dennis expect believers to ascend away when Christ returns?

answers.summary: Dennis says Christ descends to earth rather than believers departing to heaven. He connects the return to the Mount of Olives.

questions.question: Did Dennis expect believers to leave earth for heaven after the millennium?

answers.summary: Dennis says God’s throne comes to earth and heaven is wherever God is, rather than describing a later flight away.

questions.question: Did Dennis expect believers to remain at work in the world during antichrist’s appearance?

answers.summary: Dennis says yes, interpreting the field as the world and describing a continuing task of witness against antichrist.

questions.question: Did Dennis expect believers to see Moses and the prophets after death?

answers.summary: Dennis expects this for those with the Lord, emphasizing that the patriarchs and prophets live with God rather than being extinct.

questions.question: Did Dennis expect Bible study to remain valuable in eternity?

answers.summary: Dennis says yes, because Christ’s words never pass away.

questions.question: Did Dennis expect Christ to return with an army?

answers.summary: Dennis says there is an army in heaven and describes Christ returning as king with the armies of heaven.

questions.question: Did Dennis expect Christians to meditate on Scripture every moment?

answers.summary: Dennis says people also have family and other responsibilities. He encourages daily study and doing the Word, referring to James 1.

questions.question: Did Dennis expect conditions to improve before the sixth trump?

answers.summary: Dennis says he believes things will worsen and points to Matthew 24.

questions.question: Did Dennis expect discord in eternity?

answers.summary: Dennis says no and cites Proverbs 6:19.

questions.question: Did Dennis expect flesh bodies to be needed after death?

answers.summary: Dennis says the flesh returns to earth and people have a spiritual body, citing Ecclesiastes 12:6–7.

questions.question: Did Dennis expect forgiven sins to be remembered in heaven?

answers.summary: Dennis says he does not think so, comparing forgiven sins to writing erased from a board. He encourages the listener to trust forgiveness rather than repeatedly returning to the same guilt.

questions.question: Did Dennis expect God to dwell above the earth or on a renewed earth?

answers.summary: Dennis described the new earth as the same earth renewed in a new age. He said God’s throne would come here and associated Jerusalem’s name meaning the Lord is there with that future dwelling.

questions.question: Did Dennis expect God to restore the earth’s original condition?

answers.summary: Dennis interpreted Revelation 21’s new heaven and earth as rejuvenation of what God created to be inhabited.

questions.question: Did Dennis expect God’s eternal dwelling to be on earth?

answers.summary: Dennis described eternity on a rejuvenated earth, with evil removed and Jerusalem as God’s chosen place. He appealed to Revelation 21–22 and consuming-fire imagery. The captions name Timothy for another allusion; that uncertain citation is not silently corrected.

questions.question: Did Dennis expect horses and other animals in heaven?

answers.summary: Dennis says horses will be there, though he does not picture them with wings. He uses Isaiah’s peaceful animals to explain his expectation of spiritual animals without predation.
Dennis refers this second listener to his preceding answer about horses and animals in heaven.

questions.question: Did Dennis expect ISIS to take over Jerusalem in this answer?

answers.summary: Dennis rejected that expectation. The listener’s handwritten place name was uncertain to him, and this records his broadcast-era prediction rather than a verified current-events conclusion.

questions.question: Did Dennis expect kings in the future earth age?

answers.summary: Dennis says yes, referring to the kings of the nations in Revelation 21 and to Christ as King of kings.

questions.question: Did Dennis expect ordinary life to continue during antichrist’s appearance?

answers.summary: Dennis says ordinary life continues and describes the elect being delivered up for ten days, citing Revelation 2:10.

questions.question: Did Dennis expect people in heaven to communicate with one another or with earth?

answers.summary: Dennis expected communication among people in heaven and believed they would share an understandable language. He did not expect ordinary communication with people still on earth, though he allowed that God might permit an exceptional circumstance.

questions.question: Did Dennis expect people on the right side of the gulf to be without robes?

answers.summary: Dennis agrees that those on the right side would not be naked and associates their robes with righteous works; the captioned verse references need further checking.

questions.question: Did Dennis expect people on the wrong side of the gulf to be present for millennium teaching?

answers.summary: Dennis says yes and describes the millennium as a time of teaching God’s Word and discipline, and what he thinks is their last hope before final judgment.

questions.question: Did Dennis expect people to remember earthly life after death?

answers.summary: Dennis says he believes they will, reasoning that judgment of works would otherwise be difficult to understand. He also expresses his belief that mental capacity will be greater, without presenting a measured comparison.

questions.question: Did Dennis expect people to remember their flesh lives in heaven?

answers.summary: Dennis says he believes so and reasons that people would remember what they are judged for.

questions.question: Did Dennis expect people to travel the universe in the future age?

answers.summary: Dennis says he believes they will, imagining vehicles like those in his interpretation of Ezekiel 1. His remarks about Arnold receiving such a vehicle are explicitly personal belief, not a documented observation.

questions.question: Did Dennis expect racial separation in eternity?

answers.summary: Dennis said he did not believe people would be kept separate by race and emphasized belonging to Abraham’s seed in Christ regardless of ethnicity. His captioned Revelation chapter-and-verse number is invalid and is not silently corrected.

questions.question: Did Dennis expect recognition of a deceased spouse immediately after death?

answers.summary: Dennis says he believes recognition will be immediate, explicitly calling it his personal educated guess that he cannot document.

questions.question: Did Dennis expect reunited family members to recognize and embrace each other?

answers.summary: Dennis says he believes they can and points to his interpretation of Ezekiel’s family relationships as support for recognition.

questions.question: Did Dennis expect the Chapel to keep teaching through the sixth and seventh trumpets?

answers.summary: Dennis said they would teach as long as able and expected teaching in the millennium after the seventh trumpet, while doubting that it would be through television.

questions.question: Did Dennis expect the cloven tongue to be the language of eternity?

answers.summary: Dennis said he thought so and expected one language in the third earth age. He related the present variety of languages to Babel. His identification of the future language remained an opinion, not a certainty.

questions.question: Did Dennis expect the two witnesses to bring the final plagues?

answers.summary: Dennis says he does not think so, distinguishing their power in Revelation 11 from the vials in Revelation 16.

questions.question: Did Dennis expect worldwide currency before Antichrist?

answers.summary: Dennis says he did not expect a fully worldwide currency until Antichrist appeared and healed the political system’s deadly wound. He cites the euro as an example of movement toward common currency, not proof of fulfillment.

sources.lesson: I & II Samuel 30:23 - 1:9; I & II Samuel 30:23 - 1:9

questions.question: Did Dennis explain how God chooses a soul for a person?

answers.summary: Dennis says he does not know how God chooses, expresses his belief in God’s fairness, and says the soul is placed at conception.

questions.question: Did Dennis fear that the heavenly city would lack room for believers?

answers.summary: Dennis reassures the listener that people will be in spiritual bodies, not flesh bodies crowded into a cube. He does not correct or calculate the dimensions quoted by the listener here.

questions.question: Did Dennis find a Bible saying it is better to place seed in a harlot than spill it?

answers.summary: Dennis says that claim is not biblical. He identifies the relevant spilling-seed account as Onan refusing to raise offspring for his deceased brother.

questions.question: Did Dennis find a biblical account of the death of Mary’s husband Joseph?

answers.summary: Dennis says it is not written. He distinguishes that absence from a belief that Joseph died while Jesus was young and traditions about Joseph of Arimathea.

questions.question: Did Dennis find a biblical statement that Paul fell off a donkey?

answers.summary: Dennis says Scripture does not state that Paul fell from a donkey on the Damascus road. He distinguishes that from Paul being struck down and blinded.

questions.question: Did Dennis find a verse specifying 7,000 unsuccessful false teachers?

answers.summary: Dennis says he knows warnings of false teachers but not the quoted 7,000 statement, and asks for a specific passage before explaining it.

questions.question: Did Dennis find Michael and Gabriel described as the full pattern?

answers.summary: Dennis says that description is written of Satan in his interpretation of Ezekiel 28, but is not written of Michael or Gabriel.

questions.question: Did Dennis find names for Philip’s four daughters?

answers.summary: Dennis says Acts names no individual daughters, only that Philip had four virgin daughters who prophesied, which he explains as teaching.

questions.question: Did Dennis find Scripture supporting genealogies and miracles recorded on walking staffs?

answers.summary: Dennis says recording those events on a staff is not biblical; he supplies no supporting passage for the proposed practice.

questions.question: Did Dennis find the saying about indistinguishable seasons in the Bible?

answers.summary: Dennis says no and instead points to the continuing summer and winter in Genesis 8:22 and the renewed earth in Revelation 21.

questions.question: Did Dennis find the Wailing Wall by that name in the Bible?

answers.summary: Dennis says it is not mentioned under that name.

questions.question: Did Dennis find the worldwide web or nuclear plants described in the Bible?

answers.summary: Dennis answered no to both parts of the listener’s question without further explanation.

questions.question: Did Dennis forbid anointing a home more than once?

answers.summary: Dennis says anointing again when needed does not necessarily doubt the first prayer. He stresses using Jesus Christ’s name and attributes power to God rather than the oil.

questions.question: Did Dennis forbid eating at a restaurant that serves alcohol?

answers.summary: Dennis says he does not consider even a glass of wine with a meal inherently sinful, so he does not forbid the restaurant on that basis.

questions.question: Did Dennis forbid every alcoholic drink?

answers.summary: Dennis recommends moderation rather than treating all alcohol as forbidden and cites the advice to take a little wine for the stomach.

questions.question: Did Dennis forbid using Bible translations besides the KJV?

answers.summary: Dennis says no and describes consulting Moffatt for another view while studying. He still recommends owning a KJV so it can be used with Strong’s to investigate the original-language words.

questions.question: Did Dennis give a biblical age for Mary at her death?

answers.summary: Dennis says the Bible does not state Mary’s age at death. He refers to an outside book for traditions about her later years, without giving an age here.

questions.question: Did Dennis give a definite age for spiritual bodies?

answers.summary: Dennis says he believes angels appear young, citing the young man at the tomb, but does not establish a precise age in the thirties.

questions.question: Did Dennis give a definite total number of the elect?

answers.summary: Dennis distinguishes the 7,000 he calls very elect from the 144,000, some of whom he thinks may initially be deceived before recognizing the testimony. He does not insist on a fixed final count, saying it is whatever number God identifies as his elect.

questions.question: Did Dennis give a double rainbow special biblical significance?

answers.summary: Dennis discusses the rainbow as the sign of God’s covenant in Genesis 9:13–15, without assigning the double rainbow its own special meaning. He contrasts Noah’s flood with what he interprets as Satan’s flood of deception in Revelation 12:15–16.

questions.question: Did Dennis give a number of angels destroyed with Satan after the millennium?

answers.summary: Dennis says that number is not written. He distinguishes it from his interpretation of 7,000 slain at Christ’s return.

questions.question: Did Dennis give a specific guarantee of electricity during antichrist’s rule?

answers.summary: Dennis does not specify which utilities will operate. He instead expresses confidence that God provides what His elect need to accomplish His will, using Israel’s wilderness provision as an example.

questions.question: Did Dennis give an exact date for antichrist’s arrival?

answers.summary: Dennis says no one knows the exact hour and that events follow God’s schedule. He identifies the fifth trumpet as current in this recording and antichrist with the sixth.

questions.question: Did Dennis give an exact length for the prodigal son’s absence?

answers.summary: Dennis says the length is not written; the son stayed away long enough to spend his inheritance and become destitute before returning.

questions.question: Did Dennis give biblical support for a minister offering an autographed Bible for $500?

answers.summary: Dennis says no and questions the value placed on the minister’s signature.

questions.question: Did Dennis give each trumpet a fixed duration?

answers.summary: Dennis says trumpets announce events rather than equal periods of time. In this recording he identifies the fifth as current and distinguishes antichrist’s sixth trumpet from Christ’s seventh.

questions.question: Did Dennis give numbers for how many people of each race God created?

answers.summary: Dennis said the answer was not written in Scripture and emphasized that God called his creation good. He did not supply population figures.

questions.question: Did Dennis identify a biblical prediction called World War Three?

answers.summary: Dennis says he knows of none and expresses his belief that God will not allow humanity to destroy the earth that will be His dwelling.

questions.question: Did Dennis identify a favorite Bible verse?

answers.summary: Dennis says he likes all of them and mentions 2 Timothy 2:15 as a verse favored by his mother.

questions.question: Did Dennis identify a thief on the cross as Dismas?

answers.summary: Dennis says he had not heard that name and that it is not biblical.

questions.question: Did Dennis identify all the nonrebellious two-thirds as the elect?

answers.summary: Dennis says no, describing a much smaller group that stood especially firmly with God. He associates their role with the first resurrection and stresses avoiding Antichrist worship and blasphemy against the Holy Spirit.

questions.question: Did Dennis identify America as the daughter of Babylon?

answers.summary: Dennis says no, explaining Babylon as confusion and connecting its deception with believing antichrist is Christ.

questions.question: Did Dennis identify Ariel as an archangel in the King James Bible?

answers.summary: Dennis says no and points to Isaiah 29, where he says Ariel refers to Jerusalem; he gives lion or hearth of God as meanings.

questions.question: Did Dennis identify Bathsheba with the Queen of Sheba?

answers.summary: Dennis says they are different people: Bathsheba belongs to David’s account, while the Queen of Sheba visits Solomon.

sources.lesson: Wednesday 2/17/21 I & II Kings 22:43 - 1:18; Wednesday 2/17/21 I & II Kings 22:43 - 1:18

questions.question: Did Dennis identify Brexit as the definite deadly wound of Revelation 13?

answers.summary: Dennis calls the event a type and mentions its worldwide effects, while refusing the proposed date. He does not establish a definite fulfillment.

questions.question: Did Dennis identify cities found underwater with first-earth-age cities?

answers.summary: Dennis says he does not believe they are the cities described in Jeremiah 4.

questions.question: Did Dennis identify different groups receiving the Spirit in John 20 and Acts 2?

answers.summary: Dennis says the same disciples receive the Holy Spirit on two different occasions.

questions.question: Did Dennis identify Elijah with Jesus?

answers.summary: Dennis explicitly says no. He distinguishes the prophet from Christ and explains John the Baptist’s coming in Elijah’s spirit in response to the listener’s question.

questions.question: Did Dennis identify Ezra as the Gentile ruler named in prophecy before birth?

answers.summary: Dennis corrects the listener: Ezra was a Levitical priest; the ruler he meant was Cyrus of Persia. He connects Cyrus’s victory over Babylon with Judah’s opportunity to return and rebuild.

questions.question: Did Dennis identify fallen angels as Greek and Roman mythological gods?

answers.summary: Dennis says no and distinguishes his belief in actual fallen angels from mythology, citing Genesis and Jude.

questions.question: Did Dennis identify Gideon’s 300 men with Elisha’s vision of the heavenly army?

answers.summary: Dennis separates the accounts: Gideon’s reduced army demonstrates reliance on God, while Elisha prays for his servant’s eyes to see the protecting heavenly forces.

questions.question: Did Dennis identify Joseph as Jesus’s biological father?

answers.summary: Dennis says no, identifying Jesus as God’s only begotten Son and distinguishing Joseph’s genealogy in Matthew from what he describes as Mary’s in Luke.

questions.question: Did Dennis identify King James with the New Testament James?

answers.summary: Dennis distinguished King James from the New Testament James and described the later king’s connection with the English translation. The captioned elapsed-time unit is erroneous or unclear and is not used as historical dating here.

questions.question: Did Dennis identify Lot’s sons as two tribes of Israel?

answers.summary: Dennis says Ammon and Moab were not tribes of Israel. Answering the incest question, he notes that the prohibitions in Leviticus were given centuries after Lot.

questions.question: Did Dennis identify Michelangelo with Michael the archangel?

answers.summary: Dennis says no and says Michael has not been and will not be born in flesh.

questions.question: Did Dennis identify modern UFO sightings with Ezekiel’s vision?

answers.summary: Dennis describes Ezekiel’s vision as God’s vehicle and throne, but says a modern sighting should not automatically be identified with it.

questions.question: Did Dennis identify Revelation 11’s two witnesses with antichrist and the false prophet?

answers.summary: Dennis rejected that identification and described the witnesses as helping accomplish God’s plan by supplying truth to the elect. He connected them with Zechariah’s anointed ones and the song of Moses. His stated interval after their death is retained in the source for audio checking, not silently recalculated.

questions.question: Did Dennis identify Revelation 18’s great merchants as descendants of giants?

answers.summary: Dennis says no, interprets great as prosperous and well regarded, and states his belief that there are no modern descendants of those giants.

questions.question: Did Dennis identify separate five-month periods in Revelation 9?

answers.summary: Dennis says it is the same five-month period and interprets the locusts as the antichrist’s army rather than insects.

questions.question: Did Dennis identify Sunday worship as the mark of the beast?

answers.summary: Dennis answers no and directs the listener to the ministry’s teaching about the mark for further explanation.

questions.question: Did Dennis identify Thaddeus with Timothy?

answers.summary: Dennis says they are different: Thaddeus was among the original twelve, whereas Timothy came later under Paul’s instruction.

questions.question: Did Dennis identify the beggar Lazarus with Martha and Mary’s brother?

answers.summary: Dennis distinguishes the Lazarus raised in John 11 from Lazarus in the Luke 16 parable.

questions.question: Did Dennis identify the Enoch in Genesis 4 with the Enoch in Genesis 5?

answers.summary: Dennis says they are different men with the same name, belonging to the different genealogies listed in the two chapters.

questions.question: Did Dennis identify the false prophet, antichrist and beast as the same thing?

answers.summary: Dennis identifies the false prophet with antichrist but distinguishes Revelation 13’s first beast, which he calls a political system, from its second beast, which he identifies as antichrist.

questions.question: Did Dennis identify the headings in Psalm 119 as months or Hebrew letters?

answers.summary: Dennis identified them as the Hebrew alphabet, with twenty-two sections of eight verses and the verses in each section beginning with the corresponding Hebrew letter in the original language. He called the psalm an acrostic.

questions.question: Did Dennis identify the lowercase lord in Matthew 24:50 as the son of perdition?

answers.summary: Dennis says the parable refers to Christ, not the son of perdition; capitalization alone does not support the proposed identification.

questions.question: Did Dennis identify the mark of the beast as a good angel?

answers.summary: Dennis says no and refers the listener to the ministry’s introductory study for a fuller explanation.

questions.question: Did Dennis identify the Serenity Prayer as a biblical passage?

answers.summary: Dennis says it is not a passage of Scripture and attributes the familiar prayer to Reinhold Niebuhr.

questions.question: Did Dennis identify the serpent as Satan born in a flesh body?

answers.summary: Dennis calls the serpent one of Satan’s roles and says Satan has not been and will not be born of a woman. He relates the image language in Genesis to his explanation.

questions.question: Did Dennis identify the tree of knowledge of good and evil with Satan?

answers.summary: Dennis says yes and rejects the familiar apple story as the text’s explanation, noting that Genesis does not name an apple.

questions.question: Did Dennis identify the United Nations as the completed one-world political system?

answers.summary: Dennis described the United Nations and European Union as developments in that direction. He pointed to the EU’s common currency and urged watchfulness rather than declaring the final political system fully formed. This summarizes the broadcast’s historical comments, not current political analysis.

questions.question: Did Dennis identify the weapon Cain used against Abel?

answers.summary: Dennis says the account does not identify a weapon. He declines to turn a guess about the killing into a biblical statement.

questions.question: Did Dennis identify wisdom crying in Proverbs 1:20 with the two witnesses?

answers.summary: Dennis says no; he reads it as wisdom calling for people to respond.

questions.question: Did Dennis include the United States in his explanation of nations surrounding Jerusalem?

answers.summary: Dennis says it would be part of the one-world political system in his interpretation.

questions.question: Did Dennis interpret a confused patient’s disturbing words as the devil speaking?

answers.summary: Dennis says no and cautions against treating statements arising from dementia or Alzheimer’s as responsible, deliberate speech.

questions.question: Did Dennis interpret all Israel shall be saved as every individual being saved regardless of conduct?

answers.summary: Dennis says no, explaining that he believes the statement concerns the twelve tribes collectively and does not exempt individuals from judgment.

questions.question: Did Dennis interpret being born of water as a baptism requirement?

answers.summary: Dennis interprets John 3:5 as flesh birth through a woman, contrasting it with his teaching about fallen angels refusing that birth.

questions.question: Did Dennis interpret Deuteronomy’s name as God never forgets?

answers.summary: Dennis instead describes its Hebrew title as the words and compares the Hebrew names of the other books of Moses with their opening phrases.

questions.question: Did Dennis interpret Eden’s four rivers as four races?

answers.summary: Dennis says they are actual rivers, identifying Hiddekel with the Tigris and noting the Euphrates retains its name.

questions.question: Did Dennis interpret Haggai 2:22 as a prediction about the automobile industry?

answers.summary: Dennis says no. He interprets it through conflict among kingdoms and their overthrow at Christ’s return, when he says there will be one king.

questions.question: Did Dennis interpret Jonathan giving David his clothing as an anointing?

answers.summary: Dennis says the passage does not mention anointing and interprets the gifts as expressing their close friendship.

questions.question: Did Dennis interpret outer darkness as outer space?

answers.summary: Dennis said it meant being outside God’s kingdom, not outer space. He connected Matthew 22:13 with the virgins lacking oil in Matthew 25 and interpreted the oil as truth.

questions.question: Did Dennis interpret Proverbs 31:15 only as praying for a household?

answers.summary: Dennis first reads it as providing food for the family, while allowing a spiritual application of concern for their spiritual nourishment.

questions.question: Did Dennis interpret take no thought for tomorrow as a ban on planning?

answers.summary: Dennis says it means not worrying, while sensible planning remains necessary. He distinguishes that from taking the expression absolutely literally.

questions.question: Did Dennis interpret the aliens in Hebrews 11:34 as extraterrestrials?

answers.summary: Dennis said the armies of aliens meant foreign peoples rather than space creatures. He also referred to God and souls with him in heaven within his teaching about life before and after flesh existence.

questions.question: Did Dennis interpret the blood prohibition as banning a rare steak?

answers.summary: Dennis says the instruction concerns draining blood when an animal is slaughtered rather than the listener’s description of a steak. This summarizes his interpretation, not a food-safety assessment.

questions.question: Did Dennis interpret the five months as human or divine time?

answers.summary: Dennis says he is not certain, but thinks human time is intended. His uncertainty is explicit.

questions.question: Did Dennis interpret the fruit eaten in Eden as literal fruit?

answers.summary: Dennis answered no, connecting the tree of knowledge with the serpent and Eve’s seduction in his interpretation. He noted that Genesis does not name an apple. His explanation is kept separate from Scripture’s actual wording.

questions.question: Did Dennis interpret the Witch of Endor’s apparition as Samuel or an evil spirit?

answers.summary: Dennis described an evil spirit masquerading as Samuel and warned against attempts to communicate with the dead or familiar spirits. He also referred to the witch’s surprise in 1 Samuel 28:12 without fully explaining his phrase that she got more than she bargained for.

questions.question: Did Dennis judge the eternal fate of a person who died by suicide?

answers.summary: Dennis says the decision belongs to God, and says God takes circumstances such as mental illness into account.

questions.question: Did Dennis keep the Day of Atonement or fast?

answers.summary: Dennis says no to both. He contrasts the annual atonement ritual with sins being covered through Christ’s blood.

questions.question: Did Dennis know how long Adam and Eve were in Eden before the temptation?

answers.summary: Dennis says the duration is not written. He guesses it was not long, explicitly offering a guess rather than a documented interval.

questions.question: Did Dennis know how long Adam lived before Eve was made?

answers.summary: Dennis says the length is not written and points to Adam’s genealogy in Genesis 5.

questions.question: Did Dennis know of anyone before Bullinger describing Esther’s acrostics?

answers.summary: Dennis says he does not know of an earlier writer. This is a statement of his knowledge, not proof that Bullinger was historically first.

questions.question: Did Dennis know Satan’s name before the rebellion?

answers.summary: Dennis says the name is not written for that period and labels his suggestion that it was Satan as an educated guess.

questions.question: Did Dennis know the exact words John spoke when baptizing Jesus?

answers.summary: Dennis says the exact baptismal words are not written. He distinguishes John’s initial hesitation and the voice from heaven from a recorded baptismal formula.

questions.question: Did Dennis know what happened to the Urim and Thummim?

answers.summary: Dennis says their fate is not written. He offers only an educated guess that they went with the ark to God, possibly with Elijah; he distinguishes that speculation from Revelation’s reference to the ark in heaven.

questions.question: Did Dennis know whether biblical giants suffered illnesses?

answers.summary: Dennis says he knows of no written account establishing that, then makes humorous comments about a giant’s headache or toothache.

questions.question: Did Dennis know whether souls could still refuse birth into flesh?

answers.summary: Dennis calls this an interesting question and supposes they probably could refuse, while saying he does not believe God would allow another arrival as fallen angels. He presents that conclusion as his belief.

questions.question: Did Dennis know whether the seven cleansing days are human or divine days?

answers.summary: Dennis explicitly says he is unsure. He cites the day/thousand-years comparison and says time is essentially irrelevant in spiritual bodies.

questions.question: Did Dennis know whether the six-day creation people worshiped God?

answers.summary: Dennis says it is not written.

questions.question: Did Dennis know who instructed John the Baptist to baptize?

answers.summary: Dennis says it is not written and offers the Holy Spirit as his guess; he also says Scripture does not state whether John himself was baptized.

questions.question: Did Dennis know who the two witnesses will be?

answers.summary: Dennis says no one knows for sure and offers Moses and Elijah as his educated guess, citing the transfiguration.

questions.question: Did Dennis limit biblical watchmen to ministers?

answers.summary: Dennis says the elect act as watchmen by watching and warning others that antichrist precedes Christ.

questions.question: Did Dennis limit God’s commands to the Ten Commandments?

answers.summary: Dennis says no: other divine instructions are commands too. He points to Genesis 2 and recommends finding command-related words in Strong’s Concordance to trace examples.

questions.question: Did Dennis limit prayer to church or discourage daily prayer?

answers.summary: Dennis says people may pray as often as they wish. He allows congregational prayer and recommends a private place for personal prayer rather than praying to be seen.

questions.question: Did Dennis limit salvation to 144,000 people?

answers.summary: Dennis says no. He distinguishes Revelation’s numbered group from the many believers who will have eternal life, while leaving the ultimate number to God.

questions.question: Did Dennis limit the Old Testament to learning rather than daily living?

answers.summary: Dennis says commandments such as honoring parents and not stealing still govern conduct, while distinguishing blood ordinances ended through Christ.

questions.question: Did Dennis limit the salvation promise in Acts 16 to the jailer?

answers.summary: Dennis says the promise applies to everyone who believes in Jesus Christ and supports that answer with John 3:16.

questions.question: Did Dennis locate advice from Bathsheba to Solomon about choosing a wife?

answers.summary: Dennis says he knows of no such advice and directs attention to1Kings1–2, especially the succession dispute involving Adonijah.

questions.question: Did Dennis locate heaven on a planet or in clouds?

answers.summary: Dennis describes it as another dimension, normally unseen unless God permits people to see it.

questions.question: Did Dennis locate Islamic teachings in the KJV Bible?

answers.summary: Dennis says the teachings of Islam are not found in the King James Bible.

questions.question: Did Dennis make water baptism in a church an absolute condition of salvation?

answers.summary: Dennis says no, pointing to the criminal beside Jesus and John 3:16, while affirming baptism as a good expression of faith following Jesus’ example. He interprets born of water as flesh birth in this answer.

questions.question: Did Dennis mean five months subtracted from three and a half years?

answers.summary: Dennis says no: he interprets the tribulation as shortened to five months total. Although he mentions the locust season, he explicitly says this does not fix Christ’s return at the end of September.

questions.question: Did Dennis name a child who would succeed him at Shepherd’s Chapel?

answers.summary: Dennis says he has no children and trusts God to raise up leadership if needed. He cites Joshua and Samuel as leaders who did not inherit their role from the preceding leader as sons.

questions.question: Did Dennis name the people Barabbas killed?

answers.summary: Dennis says the individuals are not named one by one in Scripture and recounts the choice between Barabbas and Jesus.

questions.question: Did Dennis object to a barbecue on Easter?

answers.summary: Dennis says a barbecue or large meal is acceptable, while advising against the Easter-egg practices he rejects.

questions.question: Did Dennis object to a friendship with someone of another faith?

answers.summary: Dennis says he does not believe God hates the friendship, provided it does not influence the listener away from God.

questions.question: Did Dennis object to addressing Father, Son and Holy Spirit individually?

answers.summary: Dennis said the listener’s prayer practice was acceptable if understood within his teaching that Father, Son and Holy Spirit are roles or offices of one heavenly Father rather than three separate entities.

questions.question: Did Dennis object to admiring the moon and stars?

answers.summary: Dennis says there is nothing wrong with admiring God’s creation, while distinguishing that from the prophetic uses of lunar and solar time.

questions.question: Did Dennis object to asking God to convey a message to deceased loved ones?

answers.summary: Dennis says he sees no objection, provided the request is made subject to God’s will. He does not promise that God will grant it.

questions.question: Did Dennis object to drinking in moderation or listening to music?

answers.summary: Dennis refers to a little wine in 1 Timothy 5:23 and says there is nothing wrong with music, mentioning David’s musicianship.

questions.question: Did Dennis object to makeup and nice clothing?

answers.summary: Dennis recommends moderation, distinguishing ordinary appearance from his description of provocative advertising by prostitutes in the Old Testament.

questions.question: Did Dennis object to saying bless you after a sneeze?

answers.summary: Dennis approved the expression as wishing someone good health. He also recalled German greetings; the captioned foreign-language words and their explanations have not been verified.

questions.question: Did Dennis object to saying bless you without saying God?

answers.summary: Dennis says he prefers God bless you but sees nothing wrong with the shorter phrase.

questions.question: Did Dennis object to shaving a balding head?

answers.summary: Dennis says he knows of no biblical objection to the listener shaving his head. He distinguishes that from his explanation of a priestly hairstyle prohibited in Leviticus.

questions.question: Did Dennis object to silent prayer when delivered up?

answers.summary: Dennis says silent prayer is possible but cautions the elect not to deny the Holy Spirit speaking through them.

questions.question: Did Dennis object to women wearing pants to church?

answers.summary: Dennis welcomes women wearing pants at Shepherd’s Chapel and advises respecting another church’s dress code when visiting.

questions.question: Did Dennis object to working for a lesbian employer?

answers.summary: Dennis says a Christian should give an employer good work. He sees no problem in the stated employment relationship, qualifying his answer if the employer tried to change the listener’s sexual orientation.

questions.question: Did Dennis offer a written book called God’s Calendar?

answers.summary: Dennis says no written work was offered in this answer, but recommends Arnold’s recorded study called God’s Calendar.

questions.question: Did Dennis offer a written Chapel work on the trumpets?

answers.summary: Dennis describes the Chapel’s offerings as broadcast and audio teaching rather than a written edition, and identifies Seventh Trump and Seven Seals studies as starting points.

questions.question: Did Dennis offer personal written replies to Bible questions?

answers.summary: Dennis says questions are answered on air and that the Chapel lacks the time and staff to provide individual written responses.

questions.question: Did Dennis permit anointing a car with olive oil?

answers.summary: Dennis says yes, then clarifies that a person anoints and asks God to bless rather than personally supplying the blessing. He compares this with anointing a home and emphasizes Jesus’ name.

questions.question: Did Dennis permit listeners to petition government about moral issues?

answers.summary: Dennis affirms peaceful, nonthreatening exercise of free speech and urges preservation of credibility rather than conduct leading to imprisonment.

questions.question: Did Dennis permit prayer for help before being brought before antichrist?

answers.summary: Dennis says yes and adds that he expects the two witnesses to guide the elect as that period approaches.

questions.question: Did Dennis permit self-anointing when no elders are nearby?

answers.summary: Dennis says the listener may anoint her own forehead with a small amount of olive oil and pray for healing. He presents this as a religious practice.

questions.question: Did Dennis permit silent prayer while awaiting the Spirit’s testimony?

answers.summary: Dennis says prayer for God’s strength is always appropriate, while still urging the elect to wait for the Holy Spirit rather than speak from their own prepared thoughts.

questions.question: Did Dennis permit silent prayer?

answers.summary: Dennis says people can pray anywhere, silently or aloud as circumstances suit, and God knows even when other people cannot tell they are praying.

questions.question: Did Dennis permit taking communion at home?

answers.summary: Dennis says communion can be taken as often as the believer feels the need and describes the Chapel’s observance at the three major gatherings.

questions.question: Did Dennis permit using a previously used vial for anointing oil?

answers.summary: Dennis says a thoroughly cleaned vial can be used and advises praying for God to bless the oil for anointing.

questions.question: Did Dennis personally fast, and what caution did he give?

answers.summary: Dennis says he does not personally abstain from food or drink as fasting. He describes afflicting oneself more broadly as forgoing something pleasurable, and advises anyone considering food fasting to consult their physician first.

questions.question: Did Dennis place a rapture before or after Satan’s expulsion?

answers.summary: Dennis rejects a rapture at either point and emphasizes Christ returning to earth. He recommends Arnold’s Rapture Theory study for a fuller explanation.

questions.question: Did Dennis place antichrist’s origin in Germany, and what role did he give the two witnesses?

answers.summary: Dennis says antichrist is cast from heaven, not originating in Germany. He describes the two witnesses as communicating God’s plan and truth to the elect.

questions.question: Did Dennis place Armageddon and Hamon-gog in flesh life?

answers.summary: Dennis places these battles after Christ’s return at the beginning of the millennium, when he says people are in spiritual bodies. He portrays Christ’s victory as swift.

questions.question: Did Dennis place every event of Revelation 12 in one earth age?

answers.summary: Dennis says the chapter spans a large period: he assigns the dragon drawing a third to a first-age rebellion and the threatened male child to the present-age account of the Messiah.

questions.question: Did Dennis place flesh humans alongside dinosaurs in his first-earth-age teaching?

answers.summary: Dennis says no, placing dinosaurs in the first age while saying humans were not then in flesh bodies.

questions.question: Did Dennis place human stone-arrow hunting in the first earth age?

answers.summary: Dennis places human hunting in the present age and says people were not in flesh bodies in his first-age interpretation. He places dinosaurs in the earlier age.

questions.question: Did Dennis place Satan’s expulsion from heaven after the seventh trumpet?

answers.summary: Dennis rejects the listener’s claim that Satan is expelled after the seventh trumpet. He says it happens before that trumpet, when Michael and his angels prevail against Satan and his angels, and directs the listener to Revelation 12:6 and following.

questions.question: Did Dennis place testimony before antichrist in flesh or spiritual bodies?

answers.summary: Dennis said the elect would still be in flesh because Christ had not yet returned. He also said both elect and non-elect people would remain in flesh until that return.

questions.question: Did Dennis place the creation of souls on the sixth day?

answers.summary: Dennis says no; he believes souls were created together in the first earth age and distinguishes that from flesh creation in Genesis 1.

questions.question: Did Dennis place the end of the fig-tree generation at the millennium’s beginning?

answers.summary: Dennis says yes, describing it as people living in flesh up to Christ’s return, when he says the change to incorruptibility occurs.

questions.question: Did Dennis place the first earth age before the earth existed?

answers.summary: Dennis says no: in his teaching earth already existed during that age, with dinosaurs but no human flesh.

questions.question: Did Dennis place the Ten Commandments in the first earth age?

answers.summary: Dennis corrects the listener: the commandments recorded in Scripture belong to the second age in his teaching. He identifies Exodus 20 and Deuteronomy 5.

questions.question: Did Dennis plan to publish written Bible commentaries?

answers.summary: At the time of this recording, Dennis says no written commentaries were planned and that earlier plans for Daniel and Revelation were no longer in effect. He attributes the limitation to time spent preparing broadcasts. This is a historical statement, not current availability.

questions.question: Did Dennis predict that Satan would accuse the two witnesses of being antichrist?

answers.summary: Dennis called that accusation possible, not certain. He said the elect would recognize the witnesses through their role in supplying truth, referring to Zechariah 4.

questions.question: Did Dennis predict what antichrist might offer prisoners?

answers.summary: Dennis speculates that antichrist would do anything to gain worship, using release from prison as a hypothetical example rather than citing an explicit prophecy.

questions.question: Did Dennis prescribe a fixed mourning period?

answers.summary: Dennis cites thirty-day mourning for Moses and Aaron but says there is no required universal period. He recognizes that grief takes different people different amounts of time and encourages prayer for the bereaved.

questions.question: Did Dennis present Isaiah’s reported death as recorded in the KJV?

answers.summary: Dennis says the account of Isaiah being sawn in two is tradition, explicitly distinguishing it from a recorded KJV account.

questions.question: Did Dennis prohibit marrying someone who had previously divorced?

answers.summary: Dennis says no, recognizes grounds for divorce and emphasizes repentance and forgiveness. He rejects treating divorced believers as second-class Christians and discusses abuse and infidelity as serious marital wrongs.

questions.question: Did Dennis prohibit pierced earrings or makeup?

answers.summary: Dennis says he knows no biblical prohibition on pierced earrings and recommends moderation in appearance, while warning against adopting the appearance he associates with prostitution.

questions.question: Did Dennis promise a listener would retain her exact hairstyle and clothing after death?

answers.summary: Dennis says he believes spiritual and flesh appearances resemble one another, but leaves the details uncertain until death or Christ’s return. He does not promise a particular hairstyle or outfit.

questions.question: Did Dennis promise healing to everyone who asks?

answers.summary: Dennis cites prayer and anointing in James5 but emphasizes praying according to God’s will and placing that will above personal wishes. He does not offer an unconditional guarantee here.

questions.question: Did Dennis promise people would recognize their pets in heaven?

answers.summary: Dennis says spiritual animals will exist and that recognizing one’s pets is very possible, rather than giving an unconditional promise.

questions.question: Did Dennis promise that personal pets would greet people after death?

answers.summary: Dennis points to animals in Isaiah 11 and says he likes to think pets are included. He presents that extension as a hope rather than a definite biblical promise.

questions.question: Did Dennis pronounce hell on Christians observing Easter eggs or a Christmas birthday?

answers.summary: Dennis declines to act as judge, urges compassionate sharing of what he considers truth, and acknowledges that some people lack the same understanding.

questions.question: Did Dennis provide local students’ names and addresses for fellowship?

answers.summary: Dennis says the ministry does not disclose students’ names and addresses for confidentiality reasons and describes voluntary encounters between viewers as an alternative.

questions.question: Did Dennis provide names for the criminals crucified beside Jesus?

answers.summary: Dennis says the Bible does not name them. He notes that one believed in Jesus and received the promise of paradise.

questions.question: Did Dennis read 1 Timothy 4 as abolishing the food laws?

answers.summary: Dennis says no. He emphasizes foods God created to be received in verse 3 and interprets that category through Leviticus 11, rather than reading verse 4 alone.

questions.question: Did Dennis read Isaiah 65:20 as automatic destruction at age 100?

answers.summary: Dennis rejects that reading and says age does not limit a spiritual body. He places the passage in the millennium after the change at the last trumpet.

questions.question: Did Dennis read the flood in Joshua 24:2 as the end of the first earth age?

answers.summary: Dennis says the Hebrew term refers to a river and identifies this instance with the Euphrates, not a world-age flood.

questions.question: Did Dennis read the slothful-worker passage as being about suicide?

answers.summary: Dennis says no and explains the KJV’s comparison with a great waster as ruin or decay rather than suicide. He recommends comparing the listener’s rendering with the KJV.

questions.question: Did Dennis read the ten virgins as proof of a rapture?

answers.summary: Dennis said no. He interpreted the oil as truth, the bridegroom as Christ and the unprepared virgins as people deceived by antichrist. He emphasized preparation before the bridegroom returns.

questions.question: Did Dennis recommend a complete fast?

answers.summary: Dennis says he personally does not recommend fasting. For someone considering it, he advises prayer and consulting a physician about whether they are healthy enough; he does not prescribe a duration.

questions.question: Did Dennis recommend anointing with water?

answers.summary: Dennis knows no instruction to do so and describes the Chapel’s practice of using olive oil in Jesus’ name. He stresses that power belongs to Christ, not the oil.

questions.question: Did Dennis recommend baptism after a ceremony that did not recognize Christ?

answers.summary: Dennis recommends baptism in the name of the Father, Son and Holy Spirit in that circumstance. He distinguishes it from repeating Christian baptism after sin, for which he advises repentance.

questions.question: Did Dennis recommend baptism as an adult after an uncomprehended childhood baptism?

answers.summary: Dennis recommends an informed personal decision to be baptized in that circumstance. He distinguishes it from repeating salvation after sin, for which he calls for repentance.

questions.question: Did Dennis recommend beginning Bible students focus on lost books?

answers.summary: Dennis advises becoming well grounded in Scripture first, then testing other reading against God’s Word. He does not forbid broader reading.

questions.question: Did Dennis recommend mailing cash donations?

answers.summary: Dennis discourages sending cash through the mail and recommends a check or money order instead. This describes the ministry guidance in this recording.

questions.question: Did Dennis recommend praying in an unintelligible tongue?

answers.summary: Dennis says no and points to Acts 2, describing the miracle as communication understood by listeners.

questions.question: Did Dennis recommend prepaid grocery cards for the antichrist period?

answers.summary: Dennis considered prepayment a possible preparation but warned that, in his scenario, a card might have to be exchanged for one requiring antichrist worship. He stressed refusing that worship and also suggested stored food and silver for barter. These were his speculative preparation suggestions, not assurances about payment systems or investments.

questions.question: Did Dennis recommend putting a Bible in anointing oil?

answers.summary: Dennis rejected soaking a Bible as unbiblical. He advised putting a small amount of virgin olive oil in a vial, asking God to bless it for obedient use, keeping it for anointing and anointing in Jesus Christ’s name. He attributed the power to God, not the oil.

questions.question: Did Dennis recommend the Book of Jasher mentioned in Joshua?

answers.summary: Dennis says he is familiar with it but does not consider the offered work biblical and does not provide it through the Chapel library.

questions.question: Did Dennis recommend using leftover blessed anointing oil for cooking?

answers.summary: Dennis says disposing of it is not disrespectful but personally objects to using oil set apart for anointing for ordinary cooking. He explicitly labels this his opinion, not a written biblical rule.

questions.question: Did Dennis regard all drinking of wine as sinful?

answers.summary: Dennis points to Paul’s instruction about a little wine and rejects a blanket claim that wine itself is sinful. His cited example concerns a little wine, not unlimited drinking.

questions.question: Did Dennis regard all of Revelation as still-future prophecy?

answers.summary: Dennis says some has already happened. He distinguishes Satan’s current spiritual influence from a future personal appearance on earth after expulsion by Michael.

questions.question: Did Dennis regard every member of the heavenly host as good?

answers.summary: Dennis describes the host as angels or a heavenly army and distinguishes good angels from evil ones. He refers to angels cast out with Satan.

questions.question: Did Dennis regard farm-raised catfish as clean food?

answers.summary: Dennis says farming does not make catfish clean under his reading of Leviticus 11:9–10. He explains that aquatic food must have fins and scales, and catfish lack scales.

questions.question: Did Dennis regard farm-raised catfish as clean food?

answers.summary: Dennis says farming does not change the fins-and-scales rule or his classification of catfish as scavengers. He distinguishes his dietary teaching from a claim that eating catfish sends someone to hell.

questions.question: Did Dennis regard Hebrews 11 as a vision?

answers.summary: Dennis says no and describes it as the faith chapter, recounting examples of faith across biblical history.

questions.question: Did Dennis regard Jeshurun and Jesurun as different entities?

answers.summary: Dennis says the spellings refer to the same Israel and associates the description with forgetting God amid prosperity.

questions.question: Did Dennis regard organ donation as a righteous act?

answers.summary: Dennis says he believes it is a valuable gift that can help another person after the donor no longer needs the flesh body.

questions.question: Did Dennis regard owning a gun as a lack of faith?

answers.summary: Dennis says lawful gun ownership does not by itself indicate lack of faith and frames it as provision for protection. He urges learning applicable laws and taking the responsibility seriously.

questions.question: Did Dennis regard Paul’s scriptural writings as inspired?

answers.summary: Dennis includes Paul’s writings in the statement that all Scripture is inspired by God.

questions.question: Did Dennis regard private vows as a substitute for a marriage license?

answers.summary: Dennis recommended obtaining a marriage license and emphasized responsibility toward children if a relationship ends. His comments about legal protection are recorded as his advice in the broadcast, not a verified statement of current family law.

questions.question: Did Dennis regard prosperity as proof that someone’s beliefs please God?

answers.summary: Dennis says earthly prosperity does not establish divine approval. He emphasizes storing treasure in heaven and distinguishes worldly success from entering God’s kingdom.

questions.question: Did Dennis regard salmon as clean under the biblical dietary rules?

answers.summary: Dennis says yes because it has fins and scales.

questions.question: Did Dennis regard same-sex conduct as unforgivable?

answers.summary: Dennis says no. In his interpretation, a sincere change of heart and conduct can be forgiven during life, without waiting until death.

questions.question: Did Dennis regard separation from a stealing relative as wrongful judgment?

answers.summary: Dennis calls it discernment, permits protecting one’s property and recommends warning the relative as a brother rather than treating him as an enemy.

questions.question: Did Dennis regard Solomon as a type of Antichrist?

answers.summary: Dennis says he does not see Solomon as a type of Antichrist, while acknowledging the listener’s proposed comparison involving gifts and prosperity.

questions.question: Did Dennis regard studying with Shepherd’s Chapel on television as attending church?

answers.summary: Dennis answers yes, telling the listener that studying with the Chapel is being in church. He appeals to Jesus’ statement about gathering in his name and says the viewers are gathered in that name.

questions.question: Did Dennis regard three seeds placed in Adam’s mouth as biblical?

answers.summary: Dennis answers that the story of three seeds being placed in Adam’s mouth when he died is not biblical.

questions.question: Did Dennis regard tilapia as clean to eat?

answers.summary: Dennis says he believes tilapia has fins and scales and therefore meets his reading of Leviticus. He corrects the listener’s addition of gills to the stated rule.

questions.question: Did Dennis regard Zondervan as a Bible author?

answers.summary: Dennis identifies Zondervan as a publisher rather than the author and says he holds its Bibles in high regard. This is his opinion in the recording.

questions.question: Did Dennis relate Romans 1 to the world of the broadcast’s day?

answers.summary: Dennis says its discussion of same-sex relations reminded him of contemporary conduct, which he interpreted as contrary to God’s will.

questions.question: Did Dennis require a donation before answering a letter on television?

answers.summary: Dennis says donations do not determine which questions he reads and explains that other people open the mail.

questions.question: Did Dennis require a particular body of water or time of day for baptism?

answers.summary: Dennis says the Bible specifies neither a particular body of water nor a particular time of day for baptism.

questions.question: Did Dennis require a seriously ill listener to be baptized again after baptizing herself?

answers.summary: Dennis says he is confident God accepted her baptism and sees no need to call someone to rebaptize her.

questions.question: Did Dennis require an additional act to activate the Holy Spirit in a believer?

answers.summary: Dennis says the Spirit is already active where Christ is present. He rejects requiring unintelligible speech as proof and contrasts it with the understood languages of Acts 2.

questions.question: Did Dennis require burial facing east?

answers.summary: Dennis describes burial orientation as human tradition rather than a biblical requirement and says north–south burial is not a spiritual problem.

questions.question: Did Dennis require Christians to keep all the Old Testament feast days?

answers.summary: Dennis says no, distinguishing the law’s sacrificial observances from grace through Christ. He says the ministry observes Passover because it understands Christ as the Passover lamb, while still encouraging study of the ancient feasts.

questions.question: Did Dennis require confessing a repented lie to the person deceived?

answers.summary: Dennis makes the answer depend on circumstances. He says a lie exposing someone to danger should be corrected, while questioning disclosure that would only renew hurt after the matter is over. He recommends prayer and explicitly lacks the listener’s details.

questions.question: Did Dennis require confessing sins to clergy?

answers.summary: Dennis says confession before another person is not a commandment and stresses confessing to God.

questions.question: Did Dennis require fasting when medication must be taken with food?

answers.summary: Dennis says he does not fast and does not advise the listener to skip food required with medication. He emphasizes humility before God rather than giving up food and water.

questions.question: Did Dennis require flowing water for baptism?

answers.summary: Dennis said a baptismal tank is acceptable. He distinguished the water from cleansing through Christ’s blood, while explaining his preference for the Chapel’s outdoor baptisms at Spavinaw Creek.

questions.question: Did Dennis require incense when praying?

answers.summary: Dennis distinguishes the priests’ former incense duties from approaching God through Christ under grace and says incense is not required.

questions.question: Did Dennis require kneeling or standing for prayer?

answers.summary: Dennis says prayer is possible anywhere and in any posture. He explains Ezekiel’s falling down as awe at God’s appearance, not a universal posture rule.

questions.question: Did Dennis require membership in a particular denomination for salvation?

answers.summary: Dennis says John 3:16 names no denomination and expects no denominational divisions in eternity, only God’s teaching.

questions.question: Did Dennis require memorizing all of the Song of Moses word for word?

answers.summary: Dennis says familiarity and understanding matter rather than exact memorization, noting he does not have every word memorized himself. He relates the song to overcoming antichrist.

questions.question: Did Dennis require naming and claiming a monetary gift?

answers.summary: Dennis says he does not think so. Interpreting the question as about anonymous giving, he says God knows who gave.

questions.question: Did Dennis require perfect pronunciation of God’s name in prayer?

answers.summary: Dennis says God knows the heart and would rather hear sincere prayer than be neglected because someone fears mispronouncing His name. He spells the name YHVH.

questions.question: Did Dennis require reading ability for salvation?

answers.summary: Dennis says belief in Christ, rather than literacy, is the requirement in John 3:16. He suggests a library or literacy program if the listener wants to learn to read.

questions.question: Did Dennis require removing bread products from the home at Passover?

answers.summary: Dennis says the concern for Christians is false doctrine rather than clearing the house of leavened foods, using Jesus’ warning about Pharisee and Sadducee teaching.

questions.question: Did Dennis require resting a backyard vegetable garden every seventh year?

answers.summary: Dennis says he does not think so, distinguishing varied garden crops from fields repeatedly planted with one crop. He explicitly labels this his opinion and says he cannot document it biblically.

questions.question: Did Dennis require seven days of unleavened bread for Christian Passover observance?

answers.summary: Dennis directs the listener to communion and Christ as the bread of life. He says the Chapel observes communion at Passover, while allowing more frequent communion rather than requiring seven days.

questions.question: Did Dennis restrict adultery language to physical intercourse?

answers.summary: Dennis says Scripture also uses adultery figuratively for idolatry and unfaithfulness to God.

questions.question: Did Dennis say a disabled believer must stand to testify through the Holy Spirit?

answers.summary: Dennis reassures the listener with multiple sclerosis that sitting on a mobility vehicle would be acceptable and affirms the value of serving despite disability.

questions.question: Did Dennis say a gay person must not teach the Bible?

answers.summary: Dennis explicitly denies having said that and corrects the listener’s attribution, while maintaining his religious opposition to same-sex relationships.

questions.question: Did Dennis say a Kenite could accept Christ and be saved?

answers.summary: Dennis says people he identifies as Kenites face the same judgment rather than a separate fate. He explicitly warns against condemning them all and says accepting Christ makes one a child of God.

questions.question: Did Dennis say a listener must debate a former pastor visiting their home?

answers.summary: Dennis says receiving the visitor is the listener’s choice. He sees value in sharing a corrective thought but distinguishes an ordinary discussion from the future testimony before antichrist.

sources.lesson: Wednesday 2/17/21 I & II Kings 22:43 - 1:18; Wednesday 2/17/21 I & II Kings 22:43 - 1:18

questions.question: Did Dennis say a man with long hair can serve God?

answers.summary: Dennis says yes and discusses 1 Corinthians 11:14 and the importance of having Christ over one’s head.

questions.question: Did Dennis say a nuclear war would destroy the earth?

answers.summary: Dennis says no and points to Revelation 21 as part of his explanation that God’s throne will descend to earth.

questions.question: Did Dennis say a person baptized while believing the rapture was still saved?

answers.summary: Dennis says yes and distinguishes the baptism from the rapture teaching the person had received.

questions.question: Did Dennis say a person can be both a watchman and one of the elect?

answers.summary: Dennis says yes and encourages watching events while studying Scripture to understand their place in his account of the trumps.

questions.question: Did Dennis say a person can find salvation late in life?

answers.summary: Dennis uses the laborers in Matthew 20 to say people who begin serving God late in life can receive salvation. He separately distinguishes his teaching about the unforgivable sin.

questions.question: Did Dennis say a person dying suddenly must wait in darkness?

answers.summary: Dennis rejects that idea and says the spirit returns to the Lord immediately at death.

questions.question: Did Dennis say a person must be saved again after backsliding?

answers.summary: Dennis advises repentance and forgiveness rather than treating it as requiring Christ to be crucified again.

questions.question: Did Dennis say a person unable to attend church can take communion at home?

answers.summary: Dennis says yes and also says self-anointing is acceptable if elders cannot get to the person.

questions.question: Did Dennis say a person who falls away must be baptized again?

answers.summary: Dennis says to repent rather than be baptized again, and discusses Hebrews 6 in his answer.

questions.question: Did Dennis say a person with a terrible past could still go to heaven?

answers.summary: Dennis encourages sincere repentance and confidence in God’s willingness to receive the person, distinguishing God’s love for a person from approval of wrongdoing.

questions.question: Did Dennis say a spiritual body can die?

answers.summary: Dennis calls destruction of the soul the second death. He reassures the young listener in terms of faith in Christ, doing right and repenting after failure.

questions.question: Did Dennis say a spouse’s forgiveness alone settles adultery before God?

answers.summary: Dennis distinguishes asking the spouse from asking God, says adultery is not unforgivable, and emphasizes sincere repentance before God.

questions.question: Did Dennis say a wedding vow requires staying with a spouse who molested a child?

answers.summary: Dennis answers no: he does not interpret in sickness and in health as requiring that. He distinguishes the spouse’s need for help from a requirement to remain married, while expressly declining to decide the listener’s marriage for her.

questions.question: Did Dennis say a widow’s present suffering was punishment for a prior earth age?

answers.summary: Dennis says no and describes people as born innocent into flesh. He encourages companionship, Bible study and suitable volunteering to help with loneliness.

questions.question: Did Dennis say Adam also partook of the tree of knowledge?

answers.summary: Dennis says yes and identifies that tree with Satan in his role as the serpent.

questions.question: Did Dennis say Adam and Eve were created like angels?

answers.summary: Dennis says no, distinguishing their formation from the dust from his account of angels in the first earth age.

questions.question: Did Dennis say all Romans were Gentiles?

answers.summary: Dennis distinguishes ancestry from Roman citizenship and gives Paul, whom he identifies as a Benjaminite and Roman citizen, as an example.

questions.question: Did Dennis say an infant who died without baptism could be in heaven?

answers.summary: Dennis reassures the parent and denies that the ministry teaches baptism as an absolute condition for salvation. He points to the believing criminal beside Jesus and interprets birth of water as physical birth.

questions.question: Did Dennis say anger is always sinful?

answers.summary: Dennis distinguishes righteous indignation from uncontrolled anger, citing Jesus overturning the money changers’ tables.

questions.question: Did Dennis say babies die as punishment for their parents’ sins?

answers.summary: Dennis says no, distinguishing personal wrongdoing from inherited blame. He believes souls remain alive after bodily death and offers his personal view that a short earthly life can spare suffering.

questions.question: Did Dennis say babies who die go to heaven or hell?

answers.summary: Dennis says babies are innocent and go to heaven. He then distinguishes the two sides of paradise in his explanation of the gulf.

questions.question: Did Dennis say baptism removes the need for later repentance?

answers.summary: Dennis says no: baptism does not prevent future sin, and believers still need to repent of subsequent sins.

questions.question: Did Dennis say being born in the flesh rules out being among the elect?

answers.summary: Dennis says it does not. He connects the elect’s presence in the flesh with the Holy Spirit’s witness when they are delivered up.

questions.question: Did Dennis say believers must escape earth to avoid God’s wrath?

answers.summary: Dennis says God can distinguish righteous people from the wicked, using Joshua and Caleb and the three men in the furnace as examples of selective protection.

questions.question: Did Dennis say believers need to fear demonic spirits?

answers.summary: Dennis affirms their existence but emphasizes authority over them in Jesus’ name rather than fear.

questions.question: Did Dennis say believers on the right side of the gulf remain spiritually dead?

answers.summary: Dennis rejects that reading of his teaching. He says those who died believing in Christ are with him and have eternal life, reading1Thessalonians4 as a discussion of the dead rather than a rapture.

questions.question: Did Dennis say believers retain power when the antichrist appears?

answers.summary: Dennis says yes, stressing that the power is in Jesus Christ’s name.

questions.question: Did Dennis say believers were waiting only for the two witnesses?

answers.summary: Dennis says other events must occur and recommends studying Christ’s accounts of the signs before His return in the three synoptic gospels.

questions.question: Did Dennis say believing truth gives someone the ability to see angels?

answers.summary: Dennis says God may allow an angel to be seen, but a person cannot gain control of seeing that dimension by their own actions.

questions.question: Did Dennis say Cain’s mark was placed on his forehead?

answers.summary: Dennis says no and distinguishes Cain’s mark from Revelation’s forehead language, which he interprets as deception in the mind rather than a tattoo.

questions.question: Did Dennis say Christians must approach God through a priest?

answers.summary: Dennis distinguishes Old Testament priestly mediation from access through Christ. He interprets the torn temple veil as allowing direct approach to God.

questions.question: Did Dennis say Christians should follow the old law or the new covenant?

answers.summary: Dennis distinguished laws, statutes and ordinances rather than discarding everything in the Old Testament. He said prohibitions on murder and stealing still apply, while blood-sacrifice ordinances were fulfilled at the cross. He recommended Arnold’s study on the law.

questions.question: Did Dennis say Christians should obey speed limits?

answers.summary: Dennis says Christians should obey local laws, including paying taxes and observing speed limits. He connects this with Jesus’ instruction about rendering to Caesar.
