questions.question: Did Dennis say Christians stop being capable of sin?

answers.summary: Dennis says everyone in flesh still falls short except Christ and warns against telling young people that baptism makes further sin impossible.

questions.question: Did Dennis say Christ’s ascent and return necessarily involve a flying vehicle?

answers.summary: Dennis says the cloud could have been a vehicle like Ezekiel’s description, presenting that as a possibility. He emphasizes the Mount of Olives as the place of return.

questions.question: Did Dennis say committing murder makes someone a Kenite?

answers.summary: Dennis says no, distinguishing the act of premeditated murder from genealogy.

questions.question: Did Dennis say conversion automatically forgives all future sins?

answers.summary: Dennis says no: Christians still fall short and should sincerely repent and ask forgiveness. He describes forgiven sin as erased rather than remaining for judgment.

questions.question: Did Dennis say deceased believers must return in flesh to face antichrist?

answers.summary: Dennis says those who died believing in Christ are already with him and will not return in flesh to face antichrist. He connects their spiritual return with Christ’s army.

questions.question: Did Dennis say depression or anxiety prevents a Christian from entering heaven?

answers.summary: Dennis says no, affirming salvation for the believer in Jesus despite those conditions.

questions.question: Did Dennis say each disciple represented a particular tribe?

answers.summary: Dennis says no such connection is written. He offers his belief that the 24 elders include the patriarchs and disciples.

questions.question: Did Dennis say every death occurs at a fixed time?

answers.summary: Dennis says God can lengthen days, while accidents also happen, citing the tower of Siloam.

questions.question: Did Dennis say every soul is already in the book of life?

answers.summary: Dennis says no. He connects the Lamb’s book with resisting Antichrist and describes those who do not take part in the first resurrection as spiritually dead during the millennium.

questions.question: Did Dennis say every spirit returns to God at death?

answers.summary: Dennis says all return to paradise but distinguishes the two sides of the gulf; returning to God does not mean everyone has the same condition there.

questions.question: Did Dennis say everyone born in flesh belonged to the rebellious third?

answers.summary: Dennis says no. He distinguishes all souls passing through flesh life from the third that followed Satan, and describes their presence in the fig-tree generation as his belief rather than a stated certainty.

questions.question: Did Dennis say everyone faces punishment at judgment?

answers.summary: Dennis says judgment includes rewards for good works as well as punishment. He describes the departed as with God rather than remaining in graves, and distinguishes the two sides of the gulf.

questions.question: Did Dennis say evil spirits on earth can procreate?

answers.summary: Dennis says evil spirits exist on earth but cannot procreate. He points to Jesus’ example and says believers should exercise authority against evil in Jesus’ name.

questions.question: Did Dennis say evil spirits still possess people?

answers.summary: Dennis answers yes while warning against seeing an evil spirit everywhere. He emphasizes ordering evil away in Jesus’ name, citing the authority described in Luke 10.

questions.question: Did Dennis say failing to do something God wanted is necessarily unforgivable?

answers.summary: Dennis says forgiveness is possible and encourages the repentant person to forgive themselves rather than continually revisiting a forgiven failure.

questions.question: Did Dennis say forgiven evil works remain for judgment?

answers.summary: Dennis says repentant sins are blotted out and encourages the listener to forgive themselves.

questions.question: Did Dennis say forgiving someone requires accepting further abuse?

answers.summary: Dennis encourages forgiveness but distinguishes forgiveness from forgetting or putting up with physical abuse, citing Matthew 6:14–15.

questions.question: Did Dennis say Genesis requires people to be vegetarians?

answers.summary: Dennis says no, pointing to permitted animal foods in Leviticus 11. He explains that meat can mean food generally in older English, and says vegetarianism is permissible but not required.

questions.question: Did Dennis say God can chastise spiritual bodies?

answers.summary: Dennis says God can chastise or destroy a spiritual body and distinguishes immortal souls from those liable to the second death. He ultimately identifies Matthew 10:28 after initially hesitating over the reference.

questions.question: Did Dennis say God loves everyone?

answers.summary: Dennis says no and cites Malachi 1:2–3, Romans 9:13 and Proverbs 6 in his answer.

questions.question: Did Dennis say God necessarily intended everyone to be vegetarian?

answers.summary: Dennis says not necessarily and points to the distinction between clean and unclean meats. He does not provide a full chronology of dietary instructions here.

questions.question: Did Dennis say humans or Satan establish Revelation’s one-world political system?

answers.summary: Dennis says humans bring about the first beast’s political system; after its deadly wound, Satan appears as antichrist claiming to rescue it.

questions.question: Did Dennis say illness necessarily means a person is paying for sins?

answers.summary: Dennis says no and describes sickness as part of life in the flesh.

questions.question: Did Dennis say illness-related poor memory prevents acceptable Bible study?

answers.summary: Dennis says a listener is not required to memorize Scripture and that God knows when someone is trying.

questions.question: Did Dennis say inability to read the Bible prevents salvation?

answers.summary: Dennis says no. He points to belief in Jesus rather than literacy as the condition in John 3:16.

questions.question: Did Dennis say infant sprinkling without later immersion condemns someone?

answers.summary: Dennis said lack of immersion did not by itself mean condemnation. He nevertheless encouraged a person sprinkled as an infant to choose baptism knowingly, following Christ’s example and its symbolism of death, burial and resurrection.

questions.question: Did Dennis say Jacob’s family lived in Canaan before going to Egypt?

answers.summary: Dennis says yes and explains that famine led the family to seek food in Egypt, where Joseph had gained authority.

questions.question: Did Dennis say Jesus entered heaven in flesh and blood?

answers.summary: Dennis describes a transfigured body and cites the exclusion of flesh and blood from God’s kingdom. He distinguishes his further suggestions about Enoch, Elijah and Moses as uncertain, explicitly unable to document the last.

questions.question: Did Dennis say Jesus grew up with His disciples?

answers.summary: Dennis says no and refers instead to traditions about Joseph of Arimathea and Glastonbury, explicitly distinguishing this material from the biblical account.

questions.question: Did Dennis say Jesus had descendants whose bloodline can be traced?

answers.summary: Dennis says Jesus had no children and points to a spiritual relationship through Christ.

questions.question: Did Dennis say Jesus knows our thoughts?

answers.summary: Dennis answered yes, identifying Jesus and God as one. He appealed to John’s presentation of Christ and Jesus’ statement in John 14 that seeing him is seeing the Father.

questions.question: Did Dennis say Jonah’s fish delivered him directly to Nineveh?

answers.summary: Dennis said Jonah 2:10 described the fish depositing Jonah on dry land, not at Nineveh. He distinguished that event from the later command in Jonah 3:1–2 to go to Nineveh.

questions.question: Did Dennis say King David was directly descended from Joshua?

answers.summary: Dennis says no, identifying Joshua with Ephraim and David with Judah while saying both descend from Jacob.

questions.question: Did Dennis say knots in the Last Supper tablecloth are biblical?

answers.summary: Dennis says he does not believe that is biblical.

questions.question: Did Dennis say Lot’s daughter was handed over and killed?

answers.summary: Dennis said Lot offered his daughters but they were not handed over and killed. He distinguished Genesis 19 from the account in Judges of the Levite’s concubine being abused and dying.

questions.question: Did Dennis say lying under an oath on the Bible can be forgiven?

answers.summary: Dennis says it is not the unforgivable sin and urges sincere repentance, accepting responsibility and turning away from wrongdoing.

questions.question: Did Dennis say marriage to a believer automatically saves an unbelieving spouse?

answers.summary: Dennis says no and refers to 1 Corinthians 7 for mixed-belief marriages. He does not treat becoming one flesh as automatic shared salvation.

questions.question: Did Dennis say marrying a previously married person automatically condemns someone?

answers.summary: Dennis says there are biblically valid reasons for divorce and emphasizes repentance and forgiveness, pointing to the woman in John 8.

questions.question: Did Dennis say memorizing the songs of Moses and the Lamb proves someone is an overcomer?

answers.summary: Dennis says it remains to be seen and emphasizes not worshiping the antichrist. He also discusses his view of what the song of the Lamb may encompass.

questions.question: Did Dennis say Michael was released onto earth before Satan?

answers.summary: Dennis rejected that premise and placed Michael’s battle with Satan in heaven. He said Michael’s side prevails and casts Satan and his angels onto earth.

questions.question: Did Dennis say not attending church sends someone to hell?

answers.summary: Dennis says the Bible does not say that.

questions.question: Did Dennis say obeying civil law requires participating in everything it permits?

answers.summary: Dennis says no. Responding to same-sex marriage, he distinguishes legal permission from an obligation to participate or agree. His answer describes the listener’s personal choice rather than a demand to disobey the law.

questions.question: Did Dennis say oceans disappear immediately when Christ returns?

answers.summary: Dennis says seas remain at Christ’s return. He locates their disappearance at the later return of God’s throne in Revelation 21 and emphasizes the spiritual setting.

questions.question: Did Dennis say offspring of fallen angels could receive salvation?

answers.summary: Dennis says yes, reasoning that God places a soul in each embryo and that these descendants can love and serve God. This is his interpretation.

questions.question: Did Dennis say one angel can destroy another soul?

answers.summary: Dennis reserves the second death, destruction of the soul, to God and says no souls had yet been destroyed at the time of recording.

questions.question: Did Dennis say one believer can obtain salvation for an entire household?

answers.summary: Dennis says each person’s salvation is between that person and God; one family member cannot believe on behalf of the others. He encourages prayer for the family.

questions.question: Did Dennis say only God controls a person’s tongue?

answers.summary: Dennis rejects that claim and points to Jesus’ warning that words coming from the mouth can defile a person, which he would not attribute to God causing them.

questions.question: Did Dennis say ordinary Israelites were forbidden to bury the dead?

answers.summary: Dennis says no and distinguishes restrictions on priests, including stricter restrictions on the high priest, from the general population.

questions.question: Did Dennis say ordinary people can read minds?

answers.summary: Dennis answered no and said only God can read a person’s mind. He explicitly included Satan among those he said could not do so.

questions.question: Did Dennis say ordinary people wrote the Bible?

answers.summary: Dennis says people wrote it under God’s inspiration, appealing to 2 Timothy 3:16.

questions.question: Did Dennis say past alcoholism rules out being elect?

answers.summary: Dennis does not pronounce the listener elect or excluded. He emphasizes that everyone falls short in flesh and urges repentance, love and service to God.

questions.question: Did Dennis say people across the gulf can see each other and know their condition?

answers.summary: Dennis says yes, pointing to the rich man seeing Lazarus with Abraham while being unable to cross.

questions.question: Did Dennis say people already dead would be deceived by antichrist on earth?

answers.summary: Dennis says those already dead will not be deceived by that earthly appearance and distinguishes them from people still alive in flesh.

questions.question: Did Dennis say people blinded to truth are denied an opportunity to learn?

answers.summary: Dennis says God has blinded some people but will provide an opportunity to hear truth. He describes the millennium as a period of teaching before final judgment.

questions.question: Did Dennis say people enter the lake of fire immediately at death?

answers.summary: Dennis said people do not enter that final lake immediately at death and described two sides of paradise from Luke 16. He urged sincere repentance and reassured a believer about final condemnation.

questions.question: Did Dennis say people have responsibilities to their families?

answers.summary: Dennis says yes and points to 1 Timothy 5:8.

questions.question: Did Dennis say people on both sides of the gulf have spirit bodies?

answers.summary: Dennis answers yes. He cites 1 Corinthians 15:50 and says flesh and blood cannot enter God’s kingdom, so people on either side of the gulf are in spirit bodies.

questions.question: Did Dennis say people on opposite sides of the gulf are currently teaching each other?

answers.summary: Dennis says no, explaining that the gulf cannot presently be crossed in either direction.

questions.question: Did Dennis say people taught the rapture are automatically doomed?

answers.summary: Dennis says they are not doomed to hell simply because they believed in the rapture. He describes the millennium as a time of teaching for those who never had an opportunity to hear what he calls the truth, including people raised with rapture teaching.

questions.question: Did Dennis say people were born in flesh in both the first and second earth ages?

answers.summary: Dennis says no. In his three-age teaching, souls existed in the first age and were to enter flesh in the second, which he describes as an opportunity to choose Christ after Satan’s rebellion. He recommends Arnold Murray’s Three World Ages study.

questions.question: Did Dennis say people who died before Christ’s return already have spiritual bodies?

answers.summary: Dennis says they changed at death and points to Ecclesiastes 12:6–7.

questions.question: Did Dennis say reading Scripture alone was enough?

answers.summary: Dennis says the Chapel teaches being doers as well as hearers of the Word.

questions.question: Did Dennis say repentance after practicing a pagan religion could be forgiven?

answers.summary: Dennis says sincere repentance and asking forgiveness wipe the slate clean. He encourages the returning believer to serve God instead of repeatedly doubting forgiveness.

questions.question: Did Dennis say Samson chose the Nazarite vow himself?

answers.summary: Dennis says Samson was designated a Nazarite from birth by God’s instruction rather than taking the vow on his own initiative.

questions.question: Did Dennis say Satan and demons are hostile toward believers?

answers.summary: Dennis answers yes to the listener’s question about their hatred. He gives no detailed explanation of the particular shooting mentioned.

questions.question: Did Dennis say Satan can hear spouses or read their written words?

answers.summary: Dennis says Satan can hear speech and understand writing but cannot read thoughts; God knows the heart and mind. He does not grant spouses a special exemption from that distinction.

questions.question: Did Dennis say Satan can know a person’s heart and mind?

answers.summary: Dennis says only God knows the heart and mind, while Satan and his can hear and use words spoken aloud.

questions.question: Did Dennis say Satan was already chained when this program was recorded?

answers.summary: Dennis distinguishes the restrained fallen angels from Satan. He places Satan’s chaining in the millennium, followed by a short release, and identifies the imprisoning angel as Michael only as his belief.

questions.question: Did Dennis say Satan’s followers could disguise themselves?

answers.summary: Dennis interprets Satan’s ministers appearing as ministers of righteousness as deceptive disguise. He does not specifically establish the proposed disguise as a deceased relative.

questions.question: Did Dennis say Scripture promises forgiveness 490 times per day?

answers.summary: Dennis said the passage does not specifically say per day. He connected Peter’s question about forgiving a brother with seven times seventy and extended the illustration to God forgiving sincere repentance.

questions.question: Did Dennis say Scripture proves Paul was a murderer?

answers.summary: Dennis says Paul persecuted Christians before his conversion but says the claim that he was a murderer cannot be documented from Scripture.

questions.question: Did Dennis say Scripture records eating the healing leaves in the first age?

answers.summary: Dennis says it is not written for the first age, while pointing to Revelation22’s promised tree and leaves in the future age.

questions.question: Did Dennis say Shepherd’s Chapel has affiliated churches in each state?

answers.summary: Dennis says the ministry has no affiliate churches and is located in Gravette, Arkansas. He welcomes remote study when listeners cannot find a suitable local Bible-teaching church.

questions.question: Did Dennis say Shepherd’s Chapel offered a correspondence course?

answers.summary: At the time of the recording, Dennis says it did not offer one and had no plans to do so.

questions.question: Did Dennis say sincere repentance can be forgiven after inviting Satan into one’s life?

answers.summary: Dennis reassures the listener that sincere repentance can be forgiven after previously asking Satan into his life and points to Acts 3:19.

questions.question: Did Dennis say Sodom and Gomorrah were destroyed together?

answers.summary: Dennis said both were destroyed at the same time and distinguished dictionary dates from the event’s date. His approximate historical dating was not independently checked.

questions.question: Did Dennis say someone could already have been delivered before antichrist?

answers.summary: Dennis says that event had not happened at the time of this recording because antichrist’s presence and the corresponding assembly in Jerusalem were still future in his interpretation.

questions.question: Did Dennis say spirits return to flesh bodies in graves?

answers.summary: Dennis agrees with the listener that the flesh body is no longer needed and points to being absent from the body and present with the Lord.

questions.question: Did Dennis say the antichrist will perform miracles?

answers.summary: Dennis says the antichrist will have supernatural powers that deceive people and urges spiritual preparedness. The particular healing-power comparison is not separately resolved.

questions.question: Did Dennis say the bride of Christ becomes Revelation’s harlot?

answers.summary: Dennis says no, contrasting God’s elect with Mystery Babylon and its confusion and apostasy.

questions.question: Did Dennis say the Chapel teaches the Ten Commandments?

answers.summary: Dennis says yes, naming Exodus 20 and Deuteronomy 5. He distinguishes commandments from sacrificial ordinances he regards as fulfilled by Christ’s sacrifice.

questions.question: Did Dennis say the elect may speak with family before being delivered up?

answers.summary: Dennis says yes, while saying they should not premeditate what the Holy Spirit will speak when they are delivered up.

questions.question: Did Dennis say the elect must leave the millennium temple to help relatives?

answers.summary: Dennis says Ezekiel 44 does not require them to leave, while describing compassion and the desire to help as characteristic of the elect.

questions.question: Did Dennis say the Elijah ministry was occurring?

answers.summary: Dennis says he believes their ministry plays a role in turning people to God, while explicitly denying a claim that he is Elijah.

questions.question: Did Dennis say the end-time famine is literally thirst for water?

answers.summary: Dennis corrects that statement to a famine of hearing God’s word, pointing to Amos 8:11.

questions.question: Did Dennis say the fallen angels are aligned with Satan?

answers.summary: Dennis says they are and refers to Jude 1:6 and Revelation 12 when describing their future expulsion with Satan.

questions.question: Did Dennis say the King James Bible identifies an apple in Genesis?

answers.summary: Dennis says Genesis does not mention an apple and encourages listeners to examine the text.

questions.question: Did Dennis say the number thirteen is unlucky in daily life?

answers.summary: Dennis associates thirteen with rebellion in biblical numerics but says treating Friday the thirteenth as unlucky is superstition.

questions.question: Did Dennis say the parable of the tares is happening now?

answers.summary: Dennis says it has been unfolding for centuries and advises leaving the tares for God’s harvest rather than uprooting them.

questions.question: Did Dennis say the phrase eighth-day creation is written in Genesis?

answers.summary: Dennis distinguishes Genesis 1 from the formation of Adam in Genesis 2 and says eighth day is the Chapel’s description, not wording explicitly stated in Scripture. He relates his explanation to the thousand-year comparison in 2 Peter.

questions.question: Did Dennis say the serpent required a physical form to seduce Eve?

answers.summary: Dennis says no and compares his interpretation of the serpent with his teaching about the fallen angels in Genesis 6.

questions.question: Did Dennis say the seventh trumpet follows the sixth immediately?

answers.summary: Dennis says there is an interval for deception. In this answer he assigns five months to the political beast and says he believes antichrist personally has two and a half months. This qualification remains separate from five-month-total answers.

questions.question: Did Dennis say the third who followed Satan were distributed among all races?

answers.summary: Dennis says he sees no reason they would not be, explicitly qualifying it as his opinion rather than a documented claim.

questions.question: Did Dennis say the two great commandments abolish the others?

answers.summary: Dennis treats love of God and neighbor as a summary of the commandments and their relationships rather than their cancellation.

questions.question: Did Dennis say the two witnesses represent Jews and Gentiles?

answers.summary: Dennis says no, connects the witnesses to the anointed ones in Zechariah 4 and describes their role in preparing the elect.

questions.question: Did Dennis say throwing a Bible makes someone antichrist?

answers.summary: Dennis said no. He considered throwing it disrespectful but did not identify that person as antichrist.

questions.question: Did Dennis say trouble comes only from a person’s own choices?

answers.summary: Dennis says choices can cause trouble, but also teaches that God blesses obedience and sends curses for disobedience, referring to the covenant warnings.

questions.question: Did Dennis say whether Judas was saved?

answers.summary: Dennis says Judas repented and leaves the judgment of Judas’s salvation to God. He also describes two sides of the gulf in paradise.

questions.question: Did Dennis say women would recognize returning fallen angels as angels?

answers.summary: Dennis says they would not and emphasizes his interpretation of Christ as a covering in the warning about angels. This is kept distinct from answers about recognition by fruits.

questions.question: Did Dennis set a limit on how often to anoint oneself?

answers.summary: Dennis says Scripture states no numerical limit and emphasizes faith and prayer that God’s will be done.

questions.question: Did Dennis settle seven days versus seven thousand years in this answer?

answers.summary: Dennis does not choose between the listener’s alternatives here. He emphasizes that time does not limit God and refers to the comparison of a day and a thousand years.

questions.question: Did Dennis specify a church dress code?

answers.summary: Dennis says the local Chapel has no dress code and welcomes people in comfortable clothing, including jeans or overalls, to hear the Word.

questions.question: Did Dennis specify calendar months for the antichrist’s five-month period?

answers.summary: Dennis says the shortened period is five months, but explicitly warns that his locust-season illustration does not fix it to May through September.

questions.question: Did Dennis specify how people travel in heaven?

answers.summary: Dennis speculates that it will be more sophisticated than earthly transport and looks forward to finding out; he provides no definite vehicle or biblical mechanism.

questions.question: Did Dennis specify the interval between Egypt’s ten plagues?

answers.summary: Dennis says Scripture does not state the interval and declines to assign a duration. He recalls the final plague as decisive for Pharaoh’s release of Israel.

questions.question: Did Dennis specify which side of the gulf received the giants’ souls?

answers.summary: Dennis does not assign them a side. He says God chooses the soul placed in a body and judges every soul fairly, referring to Jeremiah’s calling.

questions.question: Did Dennis take joy comes in the morning as a clock-time prediction of Christ’s return?

answers.summary: Dennis interprets the morning as the beginning of the Lord’s Day. He says believers should watch continually because the hour is unknown, rather than expect a particular morning time.

questions.question: Did Dennis teach from the New Testament?

answers.summary: Dennis says he frequently used the New Testament in Sunday messages, while acknowledging the listener’s observation about his live book studies at that time. He says broadcasts would continue including Arnold’s studies alongside his own.

questions.question: Did Dennis teach Jeremiah lived in flesh in the first earth age?

answers.summary: Dennis corrects that misunderstanding: he places Jeremiah’s soul, not a flesh body, in the first age. He uses God knowing Jeremiah before his birth to explain his position.

questions.question: Did Dennis teach once saved always saved?

answers.summary: Dennis says he does not consider the teaching biblical and describes a backslider as someone who comes to the truth and falls away, advising repentance.

questions.question: Did Dennis teach that a soul undergoes a cleansing fire when it returns to God?

answers.summary: Dennis says the described burning or cleansing baptism is not biblical.

questions.question: Did Dennis teach that access to the Father is through Jesus?

answers.summary: Dennis answers yes, interpreting John 14:6 as saying that people come to the Father only through the Son.

questions.question: Did Dennis teach that all people descend from Noah?

answers.summary: Dennis said no and appealed to his interpretation of the separate creation of peoples in Genesis 1. His further assertions about racial ancestry and biological impossibility are unverified doctrinal claims, not accepted here as genetics or a measure of anyone’s worth.

questions.question: Did Dennis teach that animal sacrifices ended at the cross?

answers.summary: Dennis says animal sacrifice and other blood ordinances were ended by Christ’s crucifixion. He identifies love as the sacrifice God desires now.

questions.question: Did Dennis teach that Christ went to hell and was reborn?

answers.summary: Dennis says there is no truth to the claim and distinguishes it from the account of Christ preaching to the imprisoned spirits.

questions.question: Did Dennis teach that descendants of fallen angels were present today?

answers.summary: Dennis said no, describing the flood and the sword of Israel as removing the groups in his interpretation. He referred to the fallen angels being restrained in Jude. These are attributed interpretations, not claims established about any living group.

questions.question: Did Dennis teach that Jesus, Satan and Moses literally have horns?

answers.summary: Dennis says no and describes horns as symbolic of power in the examples discussed.

questions.question: Did Dennis teach that multiple marriages make forgiveness impossible?

answers.summary: Dennis says adultery can be forgiven and uses Jesus’ treatment of the woman in John 8 as his example. His imagined writing in the dirt is explicitly a guess.

questions.question: Did Dennis teach that people on the gulf’s wrong side could receive instruction during the millennium?

answers.summary: Dennis says they cannot cross the gulf during the present period, but says those who never had a chance to hear truth will be taught in the millennium.

questions.question: Did Dennis teach that people were once angels?

answers.summary: Dennis says yes and associates the sons of God in Job with angels who existed with God before flesh life.

questions.question: Did Dennis teach that there are animals in spiritual bodies?

answers.summary: Dennis says yes, interpreting Isaiah’s peaceful animals as no longer carnivorous flesh creatures and saying animals were created for God’s pleasure.

questions.question: Did Dennis teach unconditional once-saved-always-saved security?

answers.summary: Dennis emphasizes repentance for sins and says the elect’s refusal of the Holy Spirit would be unforgivable, although he does not expect that refusal.

questions.question: Did Dennis tell a diabetic listener to stop insulin to demonstrate faith?

answers.summary: Dennis explicitly says not to stop insulin and to follow her doctor’s orders. He interprets the promised healing through Christ here as spiritual salvation rather than a guarantee of a healthy flesh body.

questions.question: Did Dennis tell a listener to discard all rock music?

answers.summary: Dennis says not all rock music is satanic. He advises removing music the listener regards as satanic while allowing enjoyment of music without that content.

questions.question: Did Dennis tell a listener to leave home at the sixth trump?

answers.summary: Dennis says no and explains that the instruction to flee in Matthew 24 concerns Judea. He also says no one knows the hour.

questions.question: Did Dennis tell a listener to replace a 1977 Abingdon Strong’s Concordance?

answers.summary: Dennis advises keeping it, particularly valuing its comparative concordance, and expresses caution about later revisions of Strong’s work. This is his assessment at the time.

questions.question: Did Dennis tell believers to hasten Christ’s return through political conflict?

answers.summary: Dennis says God determines the timing. He supports peaceful voting according to conscience and rejects armed action against the government, emphasizing credibility.

questions.question: Did Dennis tell believers to wait until they were worthy before taking communion?

answers.summary: Dennis says waiting for personal worthiness would mean never taking communion. He does not identify a circumstance for abstaining in this brief answer.

questions.question: Did Dennis think a deceased spouse continually watches the living?

answers.summary: Dennis says he does not believe the departed can ordinarily see this dimension, unless God allows it. He allows that God may permit a brief reassuring visit, presenting this as his belief.

questions.question: Did Dennis think a person could recognize an unknown biological parent after death?

answers.summary: Dennis says he thinks the person probably would, while emphasizing that God is everyone’s Father.

questions.question: Did Dennis think a righteous person can replace Christ as mediator?

answers.summary: Dennis distinguishes righteous prayer, which God hears, from claiming a special personal ability to direct God’s compassion. He says God deals fairly with his children and rejects a person assuming Christ’s mediating role.

questions.question: Did Dennis think a soul faithful in his first earth age could later follow Satan?

answers.summary: Dennis answered that it was possible and said teaching the word was intended to prevent deception. This is an answer within his earth-age interpretation, not an independently established account of pre-birth conduct.

questions.question: Did Dennis think a soul knows its future destination when placed in the womb?

answers.summary: Dennis says he does not think so. In his three-age interpretation, entering flesh without knowledge of past or future allows an innocent choice between God and Satan.

questions.question: Did Dennis think an elect person could have struggled with alcoholism?

answers.summary: Dennis says yes, recognizes alcoholism as a disease, and emphasizes overcoming it. He places election in the first age rather than treating a past addiction as automatic disqualification.

questions.question: Did Dennis think angels require manna?

answers.summary: Dennis infers this from the description of Israel eating angels’ food, rather than citing a separate account of imprisoned angels’ meals.

questions.question: Did Dennis think animals could be possessed by evil spirits?

answers.summary: Dennis says yes, appealing to the gospel account of spirits entering swine. He does not establish that the listener’s own animals were affected.

questions.question: Did Dennis think animals would consume the abandoned flesh at the end of the age?

answers.summary: Dennis says animals will not be carnivorous then and trusts that God has a plan, without giving a detailed disposal mechanism.

questions.question: Did Dennis think babies remain babies in heaven?

answers.summary: Dennis says he believes angels appear to be about 30 to 33 and describes age as irrelevant to the spiritual body.

questions.question: Did Dennis think Eve knew she was pregnant in his serpent-seed interpretation?

answers.summary: Dennis thought she knew, if not immediately then soon afterward, and appealed to Genesis 3:15–16. This records his serpent-seed interpretation, not verified parentage or genetics.

questions.question: Did Dennis think evil spirits were more numerous in Jesus’ day?

answers.summary: Dennis says he does not believe their numbers differ in that way today. He emphasizes Christ’s grant of authority over them in his name.

questions.question: Did Dennis think fallen angels could repent?

answers.summary: Dennis answered no and described Satan and fallen angels as condemned, while also expecting their temporary release and casting to earth. His digression about Paul’s head-covering passage includes an uncertain book reference and is not silently corrected here.

questions.question: Did Dennis think fallen angels have navels?

answers.summary: Dennis says he does not think so because, in his teaching, they were not born of women. He presents this as an inference.

questions.question: Did Dennis think fallen angels needed transfiguration to have children?

answers.summary: Dennis says no, connecting Genesis 1’s image language and Genesis 6 with his interpretation that the angels could have children with women without transfiguration.

questions.question: Did Dennis think false teaching saddens Jesus?

answers.summary: Dennis says yes and recalls that Jesus wept in the flesh. He regards the teaching criticized by the listener as human tradition that obscures Scripture.

questions.question: Did Dennis think God transformed the Egyptian magicians’ rods?

answers.summary: Dennis answered no. He described the magicians’ acts as illusion or trickery, named them from 2 Timothy 3:8, and used the account as a warning to prepare against deceptive displays. He also distinguished Antichrist as supernatural.

questions.question: Did Dennis think God was pleased with Elijah despite his discouragement?

answers.summary: Dennis says yes, citing God’s taking Elijah as his reason. He separately labels his belief that Moses was transfigured as opinion.

questions.question: Did Dennis think heaven was on earth in the first earth age?

answers.summary: Dennis says he does not believe so. He places heaven on earth after the millennium and final judgment when God’s throne returns.

questions.question: Did Dennis think Jesus felt abandoned when quoting Psalm 22?

answers.summary: Dennis interprets the cry as teaching from the cross and directing hearers to Psalm 22’s crucifixion prophecy, including the casting of lots for garments.

questions.question: Did Dennis think Jesus was crucified on a cross or a stake?

answers.summary: Dennis said he believed it was a Roman cross because the Romans were in authority, while saying the distinction was not central to his answer.

questions.question: Did Dennis think Luke was a Gentile?

answers.summary: Dennis says he does not think so, but does not provide a definitive ancestry proof here. He notes Luke’s medical vocabulary and withdraws a proposed Acts example because it concerned Peter.

questions.question: Did Dennis think Moses went to the right side of the gulf?

answers.summary: Dennis says he is sure Moses is on the right side, and discusses the account of Moses striking the rock.

questions.question: Did Dennis think people remember this age during the millennium?

answers.summary: Dennis says he believes they do, reasoning that accountability for forgotten acts would be unfair.

questions.question: Did Dennis think Satan could avoid the elect’s testimony by not calling them?

answers.summary: Dennis says the testimony will happen because he regards it as promised in God’s Word.

questions.question: Did Dennis think Satan could avoid the elect’s testimony by refusing to summon them?

answers.summary: Dennis says the elect’s delivery before antichrist is part of God’s plan and Satan cannot change that plan.

questions.question: Did Dennis think Satan is alone in the abyss during the millennium?

answers.summary: Dennis says no one else is named as going there for the thousand years, so he thinks Satan is alone, before release for a short season.

questions.question: Did Dennis think Satan would bow to Christ?

answers.summary: Dennis says he thinks Satan is included when Philippians 2:10 says every knee will bow to Jesus. Asked whether Satan would mean it, he says he does not know and does not think so.

questions.question: Did Dennis think some deceased believers return with Christ?

answers.summary: Dennis says some will return in Christ’s army and believes ancestors may be among them, referring to Revelation 19.

questions.question: Did Dennis think someone could be both pastor and evangelist?

answers.summary: Dennis says it is possible but difficult. He distinguishes bringing people to the Lord from feeding an established congregation with fuller Bible teaching and warns against repeating only salvation messages.

questions.question: Did Dennis think someone could have behaved badly in the first age as well as this one?

answers.summary: Dennis answers that it is possible, without claiming knowledge of this listener’s prior conduct.

questions.question: Did Dennis think someone could share heavenly garments with a deceased sister?

answers.summary: Dennis says each person’s works follow them and each is judged by those works, so he does not think heavenly clothing can be exchanged to substitute for another person’s deeds.

questions.question: Did Dennis think souls had different skin colors in the first age?

answers.summary: Dennis says he thinks souls were all the same color and admits others may disagree. He emphasizes common parentage under God and belonging to Abraham’s seed through Christ.

questions.question: Did Dennis think the antichrist would need an excuse to promise a rapture?

answers.summary: Dennis says no, arguing that people already taught to expect escape from tribulation would be ready to accept it without recognizing the false messiah.

questions.question: Did Dennis think the criminal crucified beside Christ had necessarily been baptized?

answers.summary: Dennis doubts that the criminal had been baptized and refers back to his interpretation of water birth, rather than making baptism a prerequisite in that episode.

questions.question: Did Dennis think the sixth-day woman was created from a rib like Eve?

answers.summary: Dennis says he does not think so but acknowledges it is not specifically written. He interprets the male-and-female wording as suggesting their creation together or close in time.

questions.question: Did Dennis think the two witnesses would know their purpose?

answers.summary: Dennis answered yes, adding that God’s elect know their purpose as well.

questions.question: Did Dennis think there would be young children in eternity?

answers.summary: Dennis says he thinks probably not because, in his teaching, God created all souls together and spiritual age is unlike flesh age. He interprets Isaiah’s child-and-snake imagery as assurance of safety rather than proof of ordinary childhood in eternity.

questions.question: Did Dennis think those across the gulf could see God?

answers.summary: Dennis says he thinks so, drawing on the rich man seeing across the gulf in Luke 16 and recommending 2 Esdras for additional description. The conclusion about seeing God is presented as his belief.

questions.question: Did Dennis treat an unnamed past wrongdoing as an automatic sentence to hell?

answers.summary: Dennis says the unnamed wrongdoing is not automatically the unforgivable sin and advises sincere repentance and asking forgiveness.

questions.question: Did Dennis treat Basic Instruction Before Leaving Earth as the origin of Bible?

answers.summary: Dennis likes the mnemonic but distinguishes it from his explanation of the Greek word for book and the association with Byblos and papyrus.

questions.question: Did Dennis treat broken promises to God as automatically unforgivable?

answers.summary: Dennis says sincere repentance can receive forgiveness. He cannot identify the listener’s quoted teaching about lying to the Spirit, and distinguishes it from his interpretation of refusing the Spirit’s testimony when delivered up.

questions.question: Did Dennis treat continuing illness after salvation as proof of weak faith?

answers.summary: Dennis says no. He says salvation does not promise freedom from bodily illness and describes faithful people with illness or disability as potentially powerful witnesses.

questions.question: Did Dennis treat foreclosure as automatic evidence of wrongdoing?

answers.summary: Dennis distinguishes loss through circumstances beyond someone’s control from deliberately diverting payments to harmful conduct. For wrongdoing he recommends repentance, not despair that forgiveness is impossible.

questions.question: Did Dennis treat Lot’s wife becoming salt as an event still awaiting fulfillment?

answers.summary: Dennis says it already happened, then connects Sodom language with end-time imagery. Asked about the son of perdition taking followers away, he says the events happen here on earth.

questions.question: Did Dennis treat pain in old age as punishment for earlier sins?

answers.summary: Dennis answered no and described bodily difficulties as part of aging. He encouraged following a doctor’s instructions rather than assuming pain proves divine punishment. This is a summary of his pastoral answer, not a diagnosis.

questions.question: Did Dennis treat Satan’s expulsion in Revelation 12 as already accomplished?

answers.summary: Dennis says the expulsion he is discussing is future, when Michael casts Satan and his angels to earth in the antichrist role.
Dennis says Satan is in heaven at the recording’s time and describes a future defeat by Michael and expulsion to earth.

questions.question: Did Dennis treat the gulf in Luke 16 as unreal because it appears in a parable?

answers.summary: Dennis says a parable teaches reality and affirms a gulf between two conditions in paradise. He recommends 2 Esdras 7 as additional reading for his interpretation.

questions.question: Did Dennis understand Christ’s white horse literally?

answers.summary: Dennis said he thought the white war horse of Revelation 19 was literal and distinguished Christ from the earlier rider he identified with antichrist in Revelation 6. His Greek-word explanation is preserved as his interpretation.

questions.question: Did Dennis understand the end times as the end of humanity?

answers.summary: Dennis says an age ends and another begins, with flesh giving way to spiritual life at Christ’s return. He also directs the listener to Jesus’ teaching about worry.

questions.question: Did Dennis use old soul to mean a soul older than other souls?

answers.summary: Dennis says he believes all souls were created together and that souls do not age as flesh does.

questions.question: Did Dennis use the gospels of Philip and Thomas?

answers.summary: Dennis says those books are not part of his King James Bible and that he has little interest in them. He also acknowledges that the listener’s phrase about holding reference is unclear.

questions.question: Did Dennis view doctors resuscitating a person as interfering with God?

answers.summary: Dennis says no and regards medical skill as a gift. He also encourages people to state their wishes about life-prolonging care so family members are not left to guess.

questions.question: Did go and sin no more refer only to adultery?

answers.summary: Dennis says Jesus forgave the woman’s past sins and called her to avoid all sin, doing her best, rather than only avoiding adultery. He also notes the inconsistency of bringing only the woman before Jesus.

questions.question: Did God create evil?

answers.summary: Dennis says God did not create evil, and connects evil choices with free will and James 1:13.

questions.question: Did God take Moses up to heaven after he died?

answers.summary: Dennis interprets Moses’ burial, Jude 9 and his appearance with Elijah as supporting his view that Moses was transfigured rather than remaining in a grave.

questions.question: Did God tell someone to cut a baby in half?

answers.summary: Dennis explains that Solomon proposed this as a test to identify the true mother, not as an intention to kill the child. He relates the judgment to Solomon’s request for wisdom from God.

questions.question: Did Jesus abolish the food laws?

answers.summary: Dennis interprets Christ’s fulfillment of the law as leaving the food laws in effect. He cites the statement about not changing a jot or tittle and says the crucifixion did not change the flesh body’s needs.

questions.question: Did Jesus have brothers and sisters?

answers.summary: Dennis names James, Joses, Judah and Simon as Jesus’ four half-brothers and notes that sisters are also mentioned. He says they shared Mary as mother, while distinguishing Jesus’ virgin birth from Joseph’s parentage.

questions.question: Did Jesus know who his disciples were before he met them?

answers.summary: Dennis says he is certain Jesus knew his disciples before meeting them. He reasons that Jesus called them to follow him rather than first asking their identities.

questions.question: Did Jesus preach salvation only to earlier kings?

answers.summary: Dennis says the preaching extended to those who had died before the crucifixion, not merely kings, and connects it with a fair opportunity to hear the gospel.

questions.question: Did Job remember the first earth age?

answers.summary: Dennis says people enter flesh life innocent and without memory of the first earth age.

questions.question: Did Paul’s trip to the third heaven cause his eye trouble?

answers.summary: Dennis says he does not think so because Paul went in his spiritual body. He thinks the eye trouble was more likely connected with his experience on the road to Damascus.

questions.question: Did Peter’s sheet vision abolish food laws?

answers.summary: Dennis says no, interpreting the vision as teaching Peter not to call people, particularly Gentiles seeking God, unclean. He also cites Christ’s statement about the law’s jot and tittle.

questions.question: Did Satan create evil spirits?

answers.summary: Dennis says Satan cannot create souls or spirits. He says God created spirits that subsequently became evil, rather than creating them evil. He treats demons and evil spirits as broadly the same category.

questions.question: Did Satan say in the Bible that he would rather reign in hell than serve in heaven?

answers.summary: Dennis says he knows no biblical passage containing that statement. He instead describes Satan seeking to reign on earth in his role as Antichrist after being cast out of heaven.

questions.question: Did Shepherd’s Chapel offer ordination to its students in this recording?

answers.summary: Dennis says it did not, because the ministry could not oversee what distant students taught. He encourages those led to teach to seek other means of ordination.

questions.question: Did Solomon write Proverbs before or after his idolatry?

answers.summary: Dennis gives his view that Proverbs and Ecclesiastes were written before Solomon participated in the idolatry associated with his foreign wives.

questions.question: Did the ancient adultery penalty apply only to women?

answers.summary: Dennis says the law penalized both adulterer and adulteress. He distinguishes adultery from the multiple marriages permitted in ancient society and explains the latter as increasing population.

questions.question: Did the people of the first Earth age hunt, grow food, and did they have flight? Did they fly?

answers.summary: Dennis places people in spiritual bodies in the first age, says they would not hunt flesh for food and treats their ability to fly as a probability.

questions.question: Do all people go to heaven until judgment?

answers.summary: Dennis says yes but distinguishes the two sides of the gulf in paradise. He describes different conditions on those sides rather than equating arrival there with final salvation.

questions.question: Do current wars prove we are about to reach the sixth trumpet?

answers.summary: Dennis cites Christ’s warning that wars and rumors of wars do not mean the end has arrived. He says God controls the timing and the Father alone knows the hour of Christ’s return.

questions.question: Do deceased loved ones forget us, and can their spirits visit?

answers.summary: Dennis says loved ones remain recognizable, citing family recognition in Ezekiel. He also expresses his belief, based on reports told to him, that God may permit a one-time comforting visit; he does not describe recurring visits as normal.

questions.question: Do false teachers know they are teaching falsely?

answers.summary: Dennis says some deliberately deceive while others act in ignorance. He emphasizes greater accountability for teachers and the need to study carefully before teaching.

questions.question: Do good works mean only preaching or talking about God?

answers.summary: Dennis says no: the many-membered body requires different spiritual gifts, not only speakers. He directs the listener to Paul’s teaching on gifts and to being a doer as well as a hearer.

questions.question: Do I have to go to a particular church to be saved?

answers.summary: Pastor Dennis Murray states that churches don't save. Jesus Christ saves, and any church that claims to exclusively offer God's salvation isn't a member of the body of Jesus Christ.

questions.question: Do I need to be baptized again in the name of the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit if I was baptized in Jesus' name?

answers.summary: Arnold interprets baptism in Jesus’ name as encompassing Father, Son and Spirit and allows another baptism if the person feels a conviction.

questions.question: Do people who die still go to either side of the gulf or did Jesus change that when he descended?

answers.summary: Dennis says the gulf remains after Christ’s descent and distinguishes its two sides through Luke 16. One conflicting chapter name in the saved passage remains unresolved.

questions.question: Do the estimations in Leviticus 27 apply today?

answers.summary: Dennis says they do not apply today and explains them as valuations connected with vows and their redemption.

questions.question: Do those deceived by the anti-Christ have a chance?

answers.summary: Dennis says there are no second chances, while arguing that many people deceived by false teaching have never had a first opportunity to understand. He describes the millennium as teaching and expresses hope that some can thereby be kept from the lake of fire.

questions.question: Do we have a right to discern people, especially the elect?

answers.summary: Arnold distinguishes discernment from judgment and calls compassion a sign he expects among God’s elect.

questions.question: Do you feel that the anti-Christ is here now?

answers.summary: Arnold says antichrist is not yet here relative to the recording and expects a conspicuous arrival accompanied by deceptive miracles.

questions.question: Do you have scripture on the importance of prayer?

answers.summary: Dennis points to Jesus teaching prayer in Matthew 6:9 and following and to Manasseh’s prayer in 2 Chronicles 33:18–19.

questions.question: Do you know what happened to or where is the cross that Jesus was crucified on?

answers.summary: Dennis says Scripture does not state what became of the crucifixion cross. He imagines that the wood has long since disappeared, making clear that this is his supposition.

questions.question: Do you know what happens during the tribulation, what forms of misery, and so forth, will be happening?

answers.summary: Arnold distinguishes Satan’s deceptive tribulation from Christ’s coming and says believers should allow the Holy Spirit to speak without preparing their own testimony.

questions.question: Do you think it is wrong for a 48-year-old man to go back to school and get a better education?

answers.summary: Arnold supports the adult listener returning to education and recommends asking a school counselor about options.

questions.question: Do you think that Arnold is still getting rewards in heaven now for the tapes that you show on TV?

answers.summary: Dennis answers yes to the question about Arnold’s continuing rewards. He describes Arnold’s recorded teaching as continuing work on earth and calls it double duty. He then shares his own picture of Arnold accompanying Christ, rather than presenting that picture as a documented promise.

questions.question: Does 1 Corinthians 14:35 forbid women from teaching?

answers.summary: Dennis says women can be gifted teachers and interprets the instruction as maintaining quiet while instruction is given, applying that principle to men and children too. He cites sons and daughters prophesying.

questions.question: Does 2 Thessalonians 3:10 mean disabled people should not eat?

answers.summary: Dennis says the passage addresses able people unwilling to work, not people unable to work because of disability.

questions.question: Does Acts 5:30 mean Jesus was not crucified on a cross?

answers.summary: Dennis says he understands the reference to a tree as compatible with crucifixion on a Roman cross, not evidence against it.

questions.question: Does an infant’s salvation depend on baptism after death?

answers.summary: Dennis says an infant is innocent and reassures the bereaved listener that the child is with Christ. He says baptism performed after death does not accomplish that salvation.

questions.question: Does an upside down cross have meaning?

answers.summary: Dennis distinguishes the tradition about Peter’s upside-down crucifixion from biblical documentation and notes its later use as an anti-Christian symbol.

questions.question: Does both your spirit and your soul go to God after death?

answers.summary: Arnold calls spirit the intellect of the soul and says it accompanies the soul after death.

questions.question: Does Dennis believe the lake of fire already exists?

answers.summary: Dennis says it does not yet exist. He distinguishes the destruction of the beast and false prophet in Revelation 19 from the later judgment of those who follow Satan after his release.

questions.question: Does Dennis connect the rainbow flag with Antichrist?

answers.summary: Dennis says he does not believe it is connected.

questions.question: Does Dennis find a biblical prohibition on first cousins marrying?

answers.summary: Dennis says he does not find that prohibition in Leviticus 18. He distinguishes the elderly listener’s circumstances from childbearing couples, whom he advises to consult a physician about possible problems.

questions.question: Does dust or clay have significance in the Bible?

answers.summary: Dennis responds by pointing to God forming Adam from the dust of the ground. He does not explain each of the listener’s examples involving Jesus.

questions.question: Does First Timothy forbid women from teaching Scripture?

answers.summary: Dennis interprets learning in silence as orderly conduct while teaching is underway, applying it to everyone. He rejects using it to bar women from teaching and cites biblical prophetesses and the promise that sons and daughters will prophesy.

questions.question: Does fleeing Jerusalem refer to Christ’s return or Antichrist’s arrival?

answers.summary: Dennis says the flight warning applies when the abomination of desolation stands where it should not. He distinguishes that from Christ’s return, when people receive spiritual bodies.

questions.question: Does following Scripture on a television screen count as Bible study?

answers.summary: Dennis says yes, while recommending an open Bible so the listener can make notes and learn where the books are located.

questions.question: Does God allow Satan to remain so people can choose whom to follow?

answers.summary: Dennis says yes, relating this earth age to that choice. He also describes Satan as imitating Christ to deceive people.

questions.question: Does God become tired of repeated home anointing?

answers.summary: Dennis says he does not believe so and emphasizes God’s patience. He locates authority over evil in Jesus’ name rather than the oil or the person.

questions.question: Does God have a hand in elections?

answers.summary: Dennis reads the statement that powers are ordained by God as indicating God’s authority over who holds power.

questions.question: Does God have children?

answers.summary: Dennis says all people are God’s children and distinguishes Jesus Christ as God’s only begotten Son.

questions.question: Does God have food?

answers.summary: Dennis reasons from angels’ food and manna that God has food as well. He also connects the fruit and healing leaves in Revelation’s picture of eternity with nourishment.

questions.question: Does God hear me when I pray and tell him that I love him, and does he know if it's sincere love or not? Because I'm not sure myself.

answers.summary: Dennis says God knows sincere thoughts and hears silent prayer, emphasizing submission to God’s will.

questions.question: Does God still love someone whose prayer seems unanswered?

answers.summary: Dennis says God loves the listener even when he disapproves of conduct. He distinguishes an unanswered request from not being heard and encourages sincere repentance and regular study, acknowledging that people still fall short.

questions.question: Does going to heaven at death automatically mean everlasting life?

answers.summary: Dennis distinguishes the two sides of the gulf and says everlasting life requires belief in Christ. He says unrepented sins remain subject to judgment.

questions.question: Does having multiple divorces necessarily condemn someone?

answers.summary: Dennis points to the Samaritan woman whom Christ used to reach others despite her marital history. He emphasizes forgiveness and rejects church rules that treat divorced people as second-class members.

questions.question: Does honoring abusive parents require staying in contact or accepting their beliefs?

answers.summary: Dennis distinguishes honoring parents for bringing one into the world from agreeing with their beliefs. In this case he supports separation and says to warn without treating them as enemies.

questions.question: Does Isaiah 30:25 predict the New York Twin Towers?

answers.summary: Dennis says no, interpreting the rivers as truth and the falling towers in relation to Babel’s confusion.

questions.question: Does Isaiah’s reference to infants mean spiritual bodies have children?

answers.summary: Dennis says no, reading the passage as the end of premature death and explaining that spiritual bodies do not age.

questions.question: Does loving others require accepting someone’s violence?

answers.summary: Dennis says Christians are not required to accept someone striking them. He distinguishes love of others from approval of evil and cites things God hates.

questions.question: Does my dad, who has passed away, know that I am watching you?

answers.summary: Arnold tells the listener that her father knows she is studying the Word. He says her father is with the Father and encourages her to continue the study her father had directed her toward. This source-specific assurance remains attributed to Arnold.

questions.question: Does our work stop when we die and enter Paradise?

answers.summary: Dennis says no and expects people to have work to accomplish rather than remain idle.

questions.question: Does Pastor Dennis think we Christians should speak out politically against the evil of this nation, or should we just stand by idly? Also will Pastor Dennis let us know when the sixth trump starts?

answers.summary: Dennis encourages Christians to exercise their political rights and vote, and says antichrist’s claim in Jerusalem will identify the sixth trumpet.

questions.question: Does poor memory prevent salvation?

answers.summary: Dennis says John 3:16 does not require a good memory. He emphasizes belief in Christ rather than the ability to remember information.

questions.question: Does poverty mean God does not love someone?

answers.summary: Dennis says a person can live in poverty and still be rich in the Lord’s eyes. He cites Smyrna in Revelation 2:9 and explains its riches in terms of possessing what he calls the truth.

questions.question: Does saying 'forsaking all others' in wedding vows include forsaking your children over your husband?

answers.summary: Arnold interprets forsaking all others in marriage vows as sexual fidelity to one’s spouse, not abandoning one’s children.

questions.question: Does Scripture compare planets with sand on the seashore?

answers.summary: Dennis says the listener is likely thinking of God’s promise to multiply Abraham’s seed like the stars and seashore sand, emphasizing an innumerable multitude.

questions.question: Does Scripture name a woman seated beside Jesus at the Last Supper?

answers.summary: Dennis says the passage describes Jesus sitting with the twelve and does not name a woman there. He distinguishes the biblical account from a painting’s interpretation.

questions.question: Does Scripture support caring for elderly family members?

answers.summary: Dennis cites the instruction to provide for one’s household and says Christians should care for their family.

questions.question: Does serious illness prevent someone from serving as a Christian witness?

answers.summary: Dennis reassures this listener that verbal witnessing is only one kind of good work. He describes trusting God through illness and facing adversity as another example to others.

questions.question: Does the antichrist come from Africa?

answers.summary: Arnold rejects that interpretation. He says Revelation’s lion imagery concerns deception and identifies Revelation 12 as his explanation of Satan being cast from heaven.

questions.question: Does the Bible explicitly identify Joseph of Arimathea as Mary’s uncle?

answers.summary: Dennis says he could not find an explicit biblical statement. He attributes that identification to historical tradition and the book Traditions of Glastonbury rather than a direct verse.

questions.question: Does the Bible give examples of women prophesying?

answers.summary: Dennis names Miriam, Deborah, Huldah and Philip’s daughters. He also points to Joel and Acts saying that both sons and daughters will prophesy.

questions.question: Does the Bible mean I don't have a chance to go to heaven if I don't understand it fully?

answers.summary: Dennis says salvation does not require complete understanding of the Bible and directs the listener to belief in Christ in John 3:16 while encouraging continued study.

questions.question: Does the Bible name Haggai’s son or family?

answers.summary: Dennis says Haggai’s parentage, tribe and children are not recorded in the Bible. He describes Haggai’s message as urging the returned people to rebuild God’s house instead of prioritizing only their own homes.

questions.question: Does the Bible say that a person doesn't have to pay back money loaned to them?

answers.summary: Arnold rejects the claim that Scripture releases someone from repaying a family debt and refers to 1 Timothy 5:8.

questions.question: Does the Bible say whether Solomon repented of idolatry?

answers.summary: Dennis says Solomon’s repentance is not recorded and refuses to judge him. He also mentions Christ’s preaching to those who had already died.

questions.question: Does the fearful in Revelation 21:8 condemn someone with anxiety or a mental disorder?

answers.summary: Dennis says he understands fearful here as faithless, not someone experiencing anxiety or phobias. He distinguishes the listener’s son’s symptoms from the unbelief he sees in the passage.

questions.question: Does the Holy Spirit in us mean that the intellective God is in us?

answers.summary: Arnold Murray says a form of the intellective God is in us through the Holy Spirit. This intellect is absorbed and can be accessed when reading Scripture, similar to how our spirit is the intellect of our soul, though only about 10% of knowledge is retained in the flesh body.

questions.question: Does the mention of the seven trumps mean we will actually hear the sound of a trumpet when they begin, and if so, will they be sounded one after another or spread out over time?

answers.summary: Dennis explains the trumpets as specific events that must occur before Christ returns, rather than simply audible trumpet blasts. He points to Matthew 24 and Mark 13 and recommends Arnold’s separate study on those chapters.

questions.question: Does the prohibition on swearing refer to curse words?

answers.summary: Dennis distinguishes making vows or oaths, particularly invoking God’s name, from what people commonly call cursing. He says that is the concern in the passage he cites.

questions.question: Does the word spurious mean the Lord was illegitimate?

answers.summary: Arnold says spurious messiah means antichrist, not that the true Christ was illegitimate.

questions.question: Does two or three gathered mean God is absent when I am alone?

answers.summary: Dennis says no. He reads the passage as describing a gathering without requiring a grand building and pairs it with God’s promise not to leave or forsake his people.

questions.question: Does worshiping Antichrist require a physical gesture?

answers.summary: Dennis says the key is accepting Antichrist as Jesus or God, rather than a particular posture or spoken formula. He also rejects the listener’s claim that the Chapel says everyone deceived by Antichrist is automatically doomed to hell.

questions.question: Elaine in Pennsylvania asked about the fate of a bipolar person who denies God after being raised in the church.

answers.summary: Dennis Murray stated that God knows our strengths and handicaps, is compassionate, and loves His children. He emphasized that God is not looking for people to zap, and many churches focus too much on fear rather than teaching His love.

questions.question: Explain the difference in your soul and your spirit. When you die, where does your soul and your spirit go?

answers.summary: Arnold describes the soul as self and spirit as its intellect or thought process, accompanying it in whichever body it occupies.

questions.question: Ezekiel 28:18, it seems to say Satan will be brought to ashes. In the sight of all them that behold thee. Is this his fate? To burn, or burn in hell?

answers.summary: Dennis identifies the king of Tyrus in Ezekiel 28:18 with Satan. He interprets being reduced to ashes and Revelation 20:14–15 as the final death of the soul, rather than ordinary flesh being burned.

questions.question: For what reason do you think God has humans here for? A special purpose?

answers.summary: Arnold explains: the pastor explained that God has humans here because they are his children and he loves them, and he wants to determine if they will love him or follow Satan, as part of separating souls for the next earth age.

questions.question: Has the word God been removed from the Old Testament?

answers.summary: Dennis rejects that premise, pointing out its repeated presence at the opening of Genesis. He says the Lord has multiple names.

questions.question: Have human souls existed eternally?

answers.summary: Dennis says God created souls in the first earth age; they are not without beginning. He distinguishes them from God and Christ, whom he describes as eternal, and says souls were intended to be born once in flesh.

questions.question: Have you considered setting up a school for teaching ministry?

answers.summary: Dennis says he and Arnold learned through Scripture study and reference tools rather than formal Bible college and emphasizes learning to study independently.

questions.question: Have you seen the movie Noah?

answers.summary: Dennis explains: the pastor hasn't seen the movie and can't confirm if it's a lie, but he commends the listener for comparing the movie to Scripture and emphasizes that truth aligns with God's word, while falsehood doesn't align with it and is a lie.

questions.question: Hazel in North Dakota asked for an explanation of Acts 19:5-6, especially regarding speaking in tongues.

answers.summary: Dennis Murray explained that the tongues spoken in Acts 19:5-6 were the same as in Acts 2:3, a language understood by people from all over the world without needing interpretation, reflecting the unique nature of the event in Acts 2:3 and its repetition in Acts 19:5-6.

questions.question: How are Arnold and Dennis Murray related?

answers.summary: Dennis identifies Arnold Murray as his father and himself as Arnold’s son.

questions.question: How are the two people on the cross by Jesus?

answers.summary: Dennis explains that the men crucified beside Jesus were criminals, distinguishes Christ’s innocence and recounts the promise of paradise to the one who believed.

questions.question: How can a young child give God a picture they drew?

answers.summary: Dennis suggests putting it on the refrigerator and explaining simply that God can see and enjoy it there.

questions.question: How can angels still be present if souls are born into flesh?

answers.summary: Dennis explains that not all souls inhabit flesh at the same time; he describes those not currently in flesh as being in spiritual bodies and distinguishes that from final judgment.

questions.question: How can Christ be a stone of stumbling?

answers.summary: Dennis contrasts Christ as sanctuary for believers with the shock of those who discover they worshiped Antichrist. He interprets their realization of deception as stumbling at Christ, the Word.

questions.question: How can Christians avoid evil company without judging people?

answers.summary: Dennis says not to adopt others’ evil ways, while warning against a holier-than-thou attitude. He points to Isaiah’s criticism of self-righteous separation.

questions.question: How can I do good works on a limited income?

answers.summary: Dennis says good works need not cost money. He suggests visiting lonely people, reading to someone, listening, and offering an encouraging smile or some time.

questions.question: How can I forgive someone who keeps insulting me?

answers.summary: Dennis distinguishes forgiving in the heart from continuing to spend time with an abusive person. He encourages forgiveness even without a request so that anger does not keep harming the injured person.

questions.question: How can I get rid of an American Standard Bible I have? Can I throw it away or would that be a sin?

answers.summary: Dennis explains: pastor Murray states that the Bible does not instruct on destroying a worn-out Bible, and suggests burning or burying it as acceptable methods, similar to disposing of a symbol of freedom like the flag.

questions.question: How can I learn who wrote the Old Testament books?

answers.summary: Dennis points to book titles and Companion Bible introductions for authorship information, noting that some identifications are educated judgments. He stresses Scripture’s inspiration by God over the identity of its human writer.

questions.question: How can I teach my family God's true words?

answers.summary: Arnold affirms the listener’s efforts to teach young people about God’s love and promises prayer.

questions.question: How can I witness before the Antichrist if I cannot afford to travel to Jerusalem?

answers.summary: Dennis says that if God wants the listener there, he will arrange it. He emphasizes readiness and the gospel armor rather than purchasing a journey.

questions.question: How can I witness to someone who is not spiritual?

answers.summary: Dennis suggests offering a brief thought about God, leaving room for the person to ask questions, and being prepared to answer. He cautions against repeatedly pressing someone who has no interest.

questions.question: How can Isaiah describe Christ as silent when Jesus did speak?

answers.summary: Dennis agrees that the prophecy concerns not defending or rescuing Himself from crucifixion. He says Christ accepted the suffering necessary for forgiveness rather than refuting His accusers to escape it.

questions.question: How can Jesus say seeing Him is seeing the Father if flesh cannot see God?

answers.summary: Dennis explains that Christ came in flesh while God’s kingdom is in a different dimension inaccessible to flesh and blood. He connects Jesus’ identity with Emmanuel, God with us.

questions.question: How can someone cope with losing a close family member?

answers.summary: Dennis acknowledges how traumatic bereavement is and says understanding that loved ones are with the Father, rather than in a grave, brings comfort.

questions.question: How can someone distinguish Antichrist from the true Christ?

answers.summary: Dennis teaches that people remain in flesh during Antichrist’s presence but change to spiritual bodies when Christ returns at the seventh trumpet.

questions.question: How can someone grow stronger in the Lord?

answers.summary: Dennis connects strength with faith and says faith grows through hearing God’s word. He also says the presence of Christ and the Holy Spirit should not be separated.

questions.question: How can someone know they have the Holy Spirit?

answers.summary: Dennis says the Father, Son and Holy Spirit are inseparable and that having Christ in one’s heart includes the Holy Spirit. He describes sensing guidance and relates baptism in Father, Son and Holy Spirit to the listener’s final question.

questions.question: How can someone overcome another harmful habit after quitting drugs?

answers.summary: Dennis congratulates the listener on sobriety and encourages prayer for strength, attention to spiritual priorities and continued Bible study to support better choices.

questions.question: How can someone share teaching that differs from what others learned growing up?

answers.summary: Dennis advises studying first and then showing the passages in Scripture. He says people may not receive it and describes the believer’s role as planting a seed while leaving its growth to God.

questions.question: How can someone tell whether they are a Christian?

answers.summary: Dennis asks whether the listener believes Jesus is God’s Son and accepts Him as Savior. He connects Christian identity with belief in Christ’s flesh life, crucifixion for sins and salvation through Him.

questions.question: How can someone understand Scripture amid conflicting traditions and translations?

answers.summary: Dennis distinguishes hearing Scripture from understanding it. He encourages studying the Word with a teacher who teaches truth, whether at the Chapel or elsewhere, and says children can understand when taught.

questions.question: How can the two witnesses be killed if they have supernatural powers?

answers.summary: Dennis says they are in flesh and their extraordinary powers come from God; he does not call them inherently supernatural beings. He describes their death, rising and ascent in connection with Christ’s return.

questions.question: How can we be sure the Christian Bible is truth and the way to God and not another religion and their manuscript?

answers.summary: Dennis recommends Scripture study to strengthen faith through Romans 10:17 and appeals to Psalm 22’s correspondence with the crucifixion.

questions.question: How can you counteract the beliefs of other religions without judging and trying to teach them?

answers.summary: Arnold advises against trying to force teaching on people who do not want it and recommends teaching those willing to hear.

questions.question: How can you tell for sure if you're a Cainite? If I really am a Cainite and accepted Jesus Christ as my Lord and Savior in my heart and truly have repented, am I still a Cainite?

answers.summary: Pastor Dennis Murray explains that a Cainite is a descendant of Cain, a race of people. Accepting Jesus Christ doesn't change your bloodline, but spiritually, you become a child of the living God.

questions.question: How certain was Arnold about people recognizing someone unseen at death?

answers.summary: Arnold described bedside experiences in which dying people seemed to recognize and speak to someone he could not see. He explicitly said he had not experienced that transition himself and could not say whether the unseen person answered; he offered a possible comforting explanation, not proof.

questions.question: How could all the Israelites fit in the tabernacle, and where did David sing?

answers.summary: Dennis says the people did not all enter at once. He says David’s locations are not specified, offering a guess that singing occurred in both palace and sanctuary.

questions.question: How could angels choose to fall?

answers.summary: Dennis says angels had free will and a third followed Satan. He cautions against equating that entire third with the particular fallen angels discussed in his separate study.
