questions.question: How did Dennis explain the survival of different races during Noah’s flood?

answers.summary: Dennis offers two possibilities: that two of every flesh included people of the different races, or that the flood was not worldwide; he says he does not know.

questions.question: How did Dennis explain the term heathen?

answers.summary: Dennis relates the Old Testament usage to other nations and idolatry, while distinguishing outsiders who worshiped Israel’s God. He then cites believers in Christ as Abraham’s seed.

questions.question: How did Dennis explain the unforgiving servant in Matthew18?

answers.summary: Dennis says the servant who received forgiveness but imprisoned his own debtor illustrates the obligation to forgive others rather than accepting mercy only for oneself.

questions.question: How did Dennis explain the ungodly not standing in judgment in Psalm 1:5?

answers.summary: Dennis says everyone will be judged and interprets the passage as the ungodly not standing among the righteous.

questions.question: How did Dennis explain the valley of dry bones?

answers.summary: Dennis corrects the listener’s attribution from Jeremiah to Ezekiel and interprets the bones as spiritually dead people revived through teaching God’s Word.

questions.question: How did Dennis explain the water of separation and its ingredients?

answers.summary: Dennis describes Numbers19’s purification after contact with the dead. He reads cedar as continuing life, hyssop as cleansing, scarlet as vital energy and the unyoked female red heifer as life and undiminished strength.

questions.question: How did Dennis explain the way of the spies in Numbers21:1?

answers.summary: Dennis connects it with the route taken by the twelve scouts in Numbers13, contrasting Caleb and Joshua’s confidence with the other scouts’ discouraging report.

questions.question: How did Dennis explain the white hair and eyes like fire in Revelation 1?

answers.summary: Dennis describes the imagery as Jesus in his spiritual body and suggests it conveys the glory and brightness of his appearance.

questions.question: How did Dennis explain the woman and flood in Revelation 12?

answers.summary: Dennis identifies the woman with Eve and symbolically Israel, the child with Christ, the eagle with God’s protection and the serpent’s flood with deception leading to spiritual conflict.

questions.question: How did Dennis explain the Word in John 1:1?

answers.summary: Dennis identifies Logos with Jesus and reads the passage as declaring Jesus with God and as God. He connects that interpretation with Emmanuel, God with us.

questions.question: How did Dennis explain the word perdition?

answers.summary: Dennis says the Greek word means destruction or perishing and identifies the son of perdition with Satan.

questions.question: How did Dennis explain the worms and unquenched fire in Isaiah 66:24?

answers.summary: Dennis connects the imagery with carcasses and the burning refuse heap outside Jerusalem, rather than describing living flesh enduring fire.

questions.question: How did Dennis explain thoughts of sin and lust?

answers.summary: Dennis points to Matthew 5:28, distinguishes finding someone attractive from lust, and emphasizes repentance and forgiveness through Christ.

questions.question: How did Dennis explain to a child why Jesus was killed?

answers.summary: Dennis said the crucifixion fulfilled prophecy and provided forgiveness of sins. He pointed to Psalm 22 and Isaiah 53 in explaining that purpose.

questions.question: How did Dennis explain touching uncleanness in Leviticus 22:5?

answers.summary: Dennis describes creeping things as bugs and relates contact with an unclean person to the bodily-discharge rules in Leviticus 15.

questions.question: How did Dennis explain trees for meat in Genesis 1?

answers.summary: Dennis explains meat in Genesis 1:29–30 as food generally, including fruit, rather than only animal flesh.

questions.question: How did Dennis explain unequal robes if paradise is perfect?

answers.summary: Dennis distinguishes the millennium from the perfected eternity. He places the righteous-acts robes in the earlier setting, where some souls remain mortal and await judgment.

questions.question: How did Dennis explain unleavened bread and the leaven of false doctrine?

answers.summary: Dennis connects unleavened bread with Exodus 12:15 and interprets the leaven warning in Matthew 16:6 as false doctrine spreading through a congregation.

questions.question: How did Dennis explain visiting the fatherless and widows?

answers.summary: Dennis understands visiting as going to see them and relieving distress. He encourages practical help and includes teaching God’s Word as one way to help.

questions.question: How did Dennis explain walking in Christ?

answers.summary: Dennis says accepting Christ should lead a person to try to live as Jesus did, while recognizing that people fall short.

questions.question: How did Dennis explain water and baptism in John 3?

answers.summary: Dennis interprets the water in John 3:5 in relation to birth and encourages baptism, while discussing John 3:16 and Jesus’s example.

questions.question: How did Dennis explain what happens at death?

answers.summary: Dennis says the flesh returns to earth and the spirit returns to God, citing Ecclesiastes 12:6–7 and 2 Corinthians 5:7–8.

questions.question: How did Dennis explain who comes first, Satan or Christ?

answers.summary: Dennis says Satan comes first and points to Matthew 24, Mark 13 and Revelation 13.

questions.question: How did Dennis help a listener unable to find2Esdras7:77?

answers.summary: Dennis directs her to the introduction and page68 of the Goodspeed Apocrypha offered by the Chapel. His page reference is specific to that edition.

questions.question: How did Dennis identify behemoth and Leviathan?

answers.summary: Dennis identifies Job’s behemoth as a dinosaur and regards Leviathan as symbolic of Satan.

questions.question: How did Dennis identify Daniel’s little horn?

answers.summary: Dennis identifies it with the antichrist and connects the desire for worship with 2 Thessalonians 2:4.

questions.question: How did Dennis identify James the Lord’s brother in Galatians?

answers.summary: Dennis identifies him as Jesus’s half brother and the writer of James, sharing Mary as mother while Joseph was not Jesus’s father.

questions.question: How did Dennis identify the branch and seven eyes in Zechariah 3?

answers.summary: Dennis identifies the branch as Christ and the seven eyes as symbolic of the 7,000 elect. He also directs the listener to Zechariah 4:10.

questions.question: How did Dennis identify the queen of heaven?

answers.summary: Dennis identifies her as Ishtar and directs the listener to Jeremiah 7 and 44.

questions.question: How did Dennis identify the sons of God in Genesis 6?

answers.summary: Dennis identifies them as angels, drawing a connection with Job 1:6. In his interpretation they could father children with the daughters of Adam, producing the giants.

questions.question: How did Dennis identify the sons of God in Job 1 and 2?

answers.summary: Dennis describes them as God’s children and says they can be thought of as angels.

questions.question: How did Dennis identify the two beasts in Revelation 13?

answers.summary: Dennis identifies the first as a world political system that receives a wound, and the second as Satan in the role of antichrist, worshiped by those not in the Lamb’s book of life.

questions.question: How did Dennis identify the Zadok priests in the millennium?

answers.summary: Dennis identified the Zadok as priests reigning with Christ in the millennium. He connected that role with overcoming antichrist and refusing the mark, referring to Ezekiel 44 and Revelation 20:4.

questions.question: How did Dennis interpret age language in Isaiah 65:20?

answers.summary: Dennis applies the passage to spiritual bodies and says aging no longer has the same significance. He describes people as approximately the same age because God created the souls together.

questions.question: How did Dennis interpret all nations gathering against Jerusalem?

answers.summary: Dennis connects Zechariah 14:2 with the one-world political beast of Revelation 13.

questions.question: How did Dennis interpret appointed once to die?

answers.summary: Dennis reads it as ruling out reincarnation into another flesh body: the spirit returns to God and each person faces his judgment.

questions.question: How did Dennis interpret awakening to life or contempt in Daniel 12?

answers.summary: Dennis connected Daniel’s contrast with the change to spiritual bodies and distinguished those in the first resurrection from those deceived by antichrist. His reading links Daniel, Corinthians and Revelation rather than supplying a verse-by-verse explanation of both requested verses.

questions.question: How did Dennis interpret Azal in Zechariah 14?

answers.summary: Dennis describes Azal as a separate or selected safe place for the elect when Christ’s feet touch the Mount of Olives.

questions.question: How did Dennis interpret being born of water and Spirit?

answers.summary: Dennis interprets water as birth in the flesh rather than baptism, and relates the passage to his teaching about two bodies and fallen angels refusing birth through a woman.

questions.question: How did Dennis interpret being delivered up to death in Mark 13?

answers.summary: Dennis associates death in that context with Satan and distinguishes the elect’s delivery from the killing of the two witnesses.

questions.question: How did Dennis interpret believers doing greater works?

answers.summary: Dennis suggests that worldwide broadcasting lets teaching reach more people than could physically hear one speaker, presenting that reach as his interpretation.

questions.question: How did Dennis interpret Daniel 11:24?

answers.summary: Dennis applies the verse to his expectation of the antichrist arriving peacefully and prosperously and attracting worship through material benefits; he says the elect will refuse and await Christ.

questions.question: How did Dennis interpret Deuteronomy 22:5 in a listener’s question about same-sex intercourse?

answers.summary: Dennis reads Deuteronomy 22:5 as a figure of speech about sexual roles rather than trousers or skirts. He also points to Leviticus 18:22, 20:13 and New Testament passages for his position. This records his interpretation without turning the pastor’s rhetorical follow-ups into additional listener questions.

questions.question: How did Dennis interpret Deuteronomy 22:5?

answers.summary: Dennis interprets the passage as a figure of speech about sexual roles and says it is not a prohibition on women wearing pants.

questions.question: How did Dennis interpret eunuchs in Matthew 19:12?

answers.summary: Dennis reads the kingdom-related eunuch language spiritually, contrasting faithfulness to Christ with being joined to Antichrist at Christ’s return.

questions.question: How did Dennis interpret foot washing?

answers.summary: Dennis treats washing as an image of cleansing the dirt of sin through Christ. He says he does not practice washing others’ feet but does not prohibit a listener from doing so.

questions.question: How did Dennis interpret heaping coals on an enemy’s head?

answers.summary: Dennis interpreted Romans 12:20 spiritually: offer the enemy the bread of life and living water. He said such treatment may shame a wrongdoer into doing what is right.

questions.question: How did Dennis interpret I kill and make alive in Deuteronomy 32?

answers.summary: Dennis emphasizes God’s ultimate control and power over spiritual life and death, connecting the passage with the one able to destroy body and soul.

questions.question: How did Dennis interpret iron mixed with clay in Daniel 2?

answers.summary: Dennis interprets it as antichrist and fallen angels trying to mingle with human beings, comparing it with his understanding of Genesis 6.

questions.question: How did Dennis interpret Isaiah’s seven women and one man?

answers.summary: Dennis associated the women with the seven thousand who do not bow to Baal or Satan and the man with Christ as bridegroom. He interpreted taking his name as being called Christian.

questions.question: How did Dennis interpret Jephthah’s vow concerning his daughter?

answers.summary: Dennis says he thinks Jephthah dedicated his daughter to lifelong service without marriage rather than burning her as a sacrifice. He presents this as his interpretation of the troubling passage.

questions.question: How did Dennis interpret Jesus asking for the cup to pass?

answers.summary: Dennis stressed submission to God’s will and rejected the interpretation that Jesus was weakening about crucifixion. He identified the cup with wrath to be poured out at Christ’s return.

questions.question: How did Dennis interpret Leviticus 19:28 on tattoos and cuttings for the dead?

answers.summary: Dennis interprets Leviticus 19:28’s markings and cuttings in relation to practices for the dead rather than supplying a blanket rule about every piercing.

questions.question: How did Dennis interpret light and darkness in John 1:5?

answers.summary: Dennis associates light with God and truth and darkness with Satan and deception, describing their opposition.

questions.question: How did Dennis interpret little children in a question about Isaiah 11:6 and the millennium?

answers.summary: Dennis briefly relates the reference to innocence, then ends the program. He does not give a fuller account of literal ages or answer each proposed setting.

questions.question: How did Dennis interpret meeting Christ in the clouds?

answers.summary: Dennis reads clouds as a figure for a large group and stresses that the passage concerns those who died in Christ. He rejects using it as a promise to escape earth.

questions.question: How did Dennis interpret no remembrance of former things?

answers.summary: Dennis reads Ecclesiastes as addressing flesh life. He interprets the lack of remembrance as people being born innocent without memory of a prior earth age.

questions.question: How did Dennis interpret take no thought for tomorrow?

answers.summary: Dennis says today’s trouble is sufficient without adding anxiety about future trouble and summarizes the teaching as avoiding habitual worry.

questions.question: How did Dennis interpret taking God’s name in vain in Exodus 20:7?

answers.summary: Dennis explains taking God’s name in vain in Exodus 20:7 as denying God’s existence or treating him as useless.

questions.question: How did Dennis interpret the dead hearing Christ’s voice in John 5?

answers.summary: Dennis connects the passage with Christ preaching to those who had died, as described in First Peter. He says many believed.

questions.question: How did Dennis interpret the dead knowing nothing in Ecclesiastes?

answers.summary: Dennis applies it to the dead flesh body, while teaching that the spirit and its intelligence have departed to God.

questions.question: How did Dennis interpret the eagles gathering around the carcass?

answers.summary: Dennis prefers the rendering vultures and connects the saying with the bodies of the two witnesses and the crowd watching them. He links their resurrection with Christ’s return.

questions.question: How did Dennis interpret the earth being divided in Peleg’s days?

answers.summary: Dennis interprets the division as brothers dividing property or inheritance, not an earthquake or other natural event.

questions.question: How did Dennis interpret the enmity and bruising in Genesis 3:15?

answers.summary: Dennis interprets the garden event sexually, then identifies hostility between the serpent’s seed and Christ. He connects the bruised heel with the crucifixion and the serpent’s bruised head with a future event.

questions.question: How did Dennis interpret the grasshoppers of Amos 7:1?

answers.summary: Dennis identified them with the locust army of Revelation 9 and connected Joel 1–2 as another witness. He associated that army with Satan’s group.

questions.question: How did Dennis interpret the interval between Genesis 1:1 and 1:2?

answers.summary: Dennis argued that the earth became formless rather than being created that way and tied the change to Satan’s rebellion and katabole. These are his translation and earth-age interpretations.

questions.question: How did Dennis interpret the iron-and-clay toes in Daniel’s image?

answers.summary: Dennis says he believes the ten toes represent the ten rulers associated with Revelation 13 and treats iron mixed with clay as an unstable foundation.

questions.question: How did Dennis interpret the kings of the nations in Revelation 21?

answers.summary: Dennis says he believes they represent peoples of all races who know and help teach the truth.

questions.question: How did Dennis interpret the person taken from the field?

answers.summary: Dennis cited Matthew 24:40 and rejected interpreting the taken person as a desirable rapture escape. He said he intended to keep working until the true Christ’s return at the seventh trumpet.

questions.question: How did Dennis interpret the rich man’s flame in Luke 16?

answers.summary: Dennis regards the flame as symbolic torment on the wrong side of the gulf, in contrast to Lazarus’s comfort. He interprets the requested water spiritually as Christ, the living water.

questions.question: How did Dennis interpret the siege instructions in Jeremiah 6:6?

answers.summary: Dennis applies Jerusalem’s oppression and the command to build siege works against it to antichrist’s presence there.

questions.question: How did Dennis interpret the sun of righteousness with healing in his wings?

answers.summary: Dennis identifies the sun imagery with Christ and the healing with deliverance from death into everlasting life.

questions.question: How did Dennis interpret the torn temple veil?

answers.summary: Dennis sees the tearing from top to bottom at Jesus’ death as symbolizing removal of the barrier to the Father, allowing direct approach through prayer.

questions.question: How did Dennis interpret the tree of knowledge in Genesis?

answers.summary: Dennis identifies the tree with the serpent in his interpretation and connects the account with 2 Corinthians 11:3.

questions.question: How did Dennis interpret the two baskets of figs?

answers.summary: Dennis identifies the good figs with Judah and the bad figs with the people he calls Kenites; this is his interpretation of the passage.

questions.question: How did Dennis interpret the wind comparison in John 3:8?

answers.summary: Dennis compared an unseen wind whose effects can be observed with spiritual bodies in a dimension unseen by people in flesh. This is his explanation of the comparison.

questions.question: How did Dennis interpret the witnesses and the seven-branched candlestick?

answers.summary: Dennis identifies the two witnesses with the olive trees and says they will guide the elect, whom he associates with the candlestick.

questions.question: How did Dennis interpret the woman and eagle’s wings in Revelation 12:14?

answers.summary: Dennis identified the woman with mother Israel, more specifically God’s elect, and the eagle with the Lord. He connected this with the Song of Moses and taught that the period was shortened to five months, citing Revelation 9.

questions.question: How did Dennis interpret the woman’s two eagle wings in Revelation 12?

answers.summary: Dennis identifies the eagle with God’s protection, relates it to Deuteronomy 32, and applies the woman to Israel and the elect.

questions.question: How did Dennis interpret the year of visitation in Jeremiah 23:12?

answers.summary: Dennis says he thinks it refers to the seventh trumpet and the outpouring of God’s wrath at Christ’s return.

questions.question: How did Dennis interpret those in the graves hearing Christ’s voice in John 5?

answers.summary: Dennis interprets the passage in terms of spirits rather than bodies in earthly graves. He connects it with Christ preaching to those who died before the crucifixion.

questions.question: How did Dennis interpret those outside the city in Revelation 22:15?

answers.summary: Dennis says John returns in the vision to his own time on Patmos when describing those outside.

questions.question: How did Dennis interpret tongues in 1 Corinthians 14?

answers.summary: Dennis understands tongues as languages and emphasizes that listeners need an interpreter when they do not understand the speaker’s language.

questions.question: How did Dennis interpret touch not, taste not, handle not?

answers.summary: Dennis locates the wording in Colossians 2 and reads it as exposing human religious regulations rather than God’s commands.

questions.question: How did Dennis interpret wishing Godspeed in 2 John?

answers.summary: Dennis describes Godspeed as a greeting and interprets the warning as a reason not to financially support teaching contrary to Christ’s doctrine.

questions.question: How did Dennis interpret worlds in Hebrews 11:3?

answers.summary: Dennis interprets the word as ages or periods of time rather than the earth’s physical materials and recommends the ministry’s Three World Ages study.

questions.question: How did Dennis place the rich man of Luke 16 in relation to the millennium?

answers.summary: Dennis expects him among the spiritually dead and distinguishes those who previously had an opportunity to hear truth from those who did not. He explicitly says he is not the final judge.

questions.question: How did Dennis pronounce the sacred name in this answer?

answers.summary: Dennis identifies YHVH and pronounces it Yahoveh, then refers listeners to Arnold’s paper on the sacred name.

questions.question: How did Dennis reassure a Christian afraid of physical death?

answers.summary: Dennis says God is God of the living and directs fear toward the one able to destroy the soul rather than those who can only kill the body.

questions.question: How did Dennis reassure a felon asking whether God could accept him?

answers.summary: Dennis encouraged repentance, forgiveness and eternal life. He used God’s patience in 2 Peter 3:9 to emphasize that a criminal record does not remove the invitation to repent.

questions.question: How did Dennis reassure a husband about his ill wife’s use of God’s name?

answers.summary: Dennis emphasizes that God knows her heart and mind and reassures him on the basis of Christ being her Savior. He acknowledges the hardship of illness for both spouses and offers prayer.

sources.lesson: I & II Samuel 30:23 - 1:9; I & II Samuel 30:23 - 1:9

questions.question: How did Dennis reassure a listener about an unbaptized sister with special needs?

answers.summary: Dennis calls the sister innocent and says God knows her heart and mind. He tells this listener not to fear for her salvation.

questions.question: How did Dennis reassure a listener afraid of judgment day?

answers.summary: Dennis points to the great white throne and judgment of works, urges faith and repentance, and stresses that judgment also means rewards for faithful service rather than punishment alone.

questions.question: How did Dennis reassure a listener unable to afford emergency supplies?

answers.summary: Dennis says God can provide for people serving His purpose and uses the provision of manna as an example.

questions.question: How did Dennis reassure a listener with Alzheimer’s about forgetting Scripture and prayers?

answers.summary: Dennis said God knows a person’s disabilities and limitations and is fair about accountability. He encouraged the listener’s continuing prayer without treating impaired memory as a failure of faith.

questions.question: How did Dennis reassure a listener worried about being a bad seed?

answers.summary: Dennis said people he called Kenites could become children of God through accepting Christ. He urged repentance and forgiveness rather than treating the listener as excluded.

questions.question: How did Dennis reassure a mother whose murdered daughter had become an atheist?

answers.summary: Dennis says God alone judges and that he cannot know the daughter’s heart at death. He assures the mother of fair judgment rather than declaring the daughter’s final outcome.

questions.question: How did Dennis reassure someone struggling to remember Bible study?

answers.summary: Dennis says members of Christ’s body have different gifts and responsibilities, and not everyone is called to be a teacher with an excellent memory.

questions.question: How did Dennis reassure someone that God hears prayer?

answers.summary: Dennis uses Manasseh’s prayer as an example and says an ungranted request does not mean God failed to hear it. He advises praying within God’s will.

questions.question: How did Dennis reconcile Abraham being tested with James 1:13?

answers.summary: Dennis distinguishes testing a servant’s faithfulness from using evil to tempt. He interprets Abraham’s experience as proving a servant for spiritual service.

questions.question: How did Dennis reconcile chosen people with God caring for everyone?

answers.summary: Dennis said God cared for all his children and distinguished all twelve tribes from Judah alone. He connected the protected line with Messiah and cited belonging to Abraham through Christ. This is his interpretation of election and lineage.

questions.question: How did Dennis reconcile David not ascending with the spirit returning to God?

answers.summary: Dennis interprets the statement about David as referring to his flesh body. He then explains John 3:13 through his teaching that souls descend from God and enter flesh life.

questions.question: How did Dennis reconcile different numbers of animals on Noah’s ark?

answers.summary: Dennis distinguishes the instructions for clean and unclean animals, discussing replenishment and sacrifice.

questions.question: How did Dennis reconcile eight souls in 1 Peter 3:20 with Noah taking two of every flesh?

answers.summary: Dennis calls the eight people named in 1 Peter 3:20 Noah’s immediate Adamic family. He proposes either additional people aboard the ark or a flood that did not cover the entire earth, relating these possibilities to his interpretation of the survival of different peoples.

questions.question: How did Dennis reconcile everlasting punishment with consuming fire?

answers.summary: Dennis says the destruction is everlasting because those consumed do not return. He regards the lake of fire as temporary rather than endless conscious suffering, connecting that with eternity having no pain, sorrow or death.

questions.question: How did Dennis reconcile Eve’s seduction claim with Christ’s lineage?

answers.summary: Dennis distinguished Cain from the line through Adam and Eve in his serpent-seed interpretation and connected Eve being mother of all living with Christ and eternal life. This preserves his interpretation, not a verified biological ancestry claim.

questions.question: How did Dennis reconcile God judging with judgment committed to the Son?

answers.summary: Dennis cites Christ judging according to the Father’s will and explains Emmanuel as God with us, treating the two descriptions as consistent.

questions.question: How did Dennis reconcile God’s fairness with loving Jacob and hating Esau?

answers.summary: Dennis attributes their standing to what he believes they did in the first earth age rather than in the womb. He understands God’s compassion as given to those who deserve it.

questions.question: How did Dennis reconcile Hebrews 10:26 with forgiveness after repentance?

answers.summary: Dennis interprets the passage as the elect refusing the Holy Spirit’s testimony before the antichrist. He distinguishes that from sins the listener could then repent of and be forgiven.

questions.question: How did Dennis reconcile John 3:13 with the spirit returning to God?

answers.summary: Dennis interprets the passages together as souls first coming from God into earthly life and later returning to him at death. He places the soul in the embryo at conception in his explanation.

questions.question: How did Dennis reconcile killed prophets with protection of the elect?

answers.summary: Dennis distinguishes earlier prophets or remnant from the end-time elect he places alive during antichrist’s appearance. He applies Revelation 9:4’s protection specifically to the sealed in that setting.

questions.question: How did Dennis reconcile knowing the interval after the two witnesses’ deaths with not knowing Christ’s return date?

answers.summary: Dennis says the deaths would indicate the remaining three and a half days in his interpretation, but their date is not known beforehand.

questions.question: How did Dennis reconcile Paul being Roman with belonging to Benjamin?

answers.summary: Dennis distinguishes Roman citizenship from ancestry and quotes Paul identifying himself as an Israelite of Benjamin.

questions.question: How did Dennis reconcile salvation by grace with judgment by works?

answers.summary: Dennis distinguishes undeserved salvation through Christ from judgment of conduct. He says judgment includes rewards for those who love and serve God, as well as accountability for sin.

questions.question: How did Dennis reconcile Satan falling like lightning with Satan still being in heaven?

answers.summary: Dennis interprets Luke10:18 as prophecy of a future casting down and connects it with Revelation12.

questions.question: How did Dennis reconcile Satan tempting Christ with being restrained in heaven?

answers.summary: Dennis distinguishes earlier occasions on earth from his interpretation of Satan’s present restraint behind Christ. He expects expulsion in the war described in Revelation 12.

questions.question: How did Dennis reconcile warnings of tribulation harm with protection of the elect?

answers.summary: Dennis interpreted killing in the question as the death of the soul through refusing the Holy Spirit, and beating as browbeating. He cited Revelation 9 for protection of the sealed and distinguished the deaths of the two witnesses. The captioned beheading citation is damaged and his John the Baptist explanation does not fully settle that citation.

questions.question: How did Dennis reconcile who moved David to number Israel?

answers.summary: Dennis contrasts the wording in Samuel with Chronicles and favors Satan as the provoker, citing James’s teaching that God does not tempt people with evil.

questions.question: How did Dennis relate 2 Peter 3 to the world ages?

answers.summary: Dennis identifies its scoffers with end-time unbelief and interprets the flooded world of verses 5–6 as an earlier earth age rather than Noah’s flood, linking it to Jeremiah 4.

questions.question: How did Dennis relate Christ’s sacrifice to his teaching about the first earth age?

answers.summary: Dennis agrees with the listener’s connection and says God provided a Savior in this age.

questions.question: How did Dennis relate conscience, spirit and guilt?

answers.summary: Dennis describes spirit as the intellect of the soul and says it has a conscience. He urges sincere repentance and accepting forgiveness rather than carrying continuing guilt.

questions.question: How did Dennis relate consequences of rebellion to God providing a way out of temptation?

answers.summary: Dennis distinguishes God providing a way through temptation in 1 Corinthians 10:13 from expecting exemption from the consequences of rebellion in Galatians 6:7.

questions.question: How did Dennis relate death, paradise and resurrection?

answers.summary: Dennis calls the spirit’s return to God at bodily death a form of resurrection. He uses paradise and heaven together while retaining his distinction between the gulf’s two sides.

questions.question: How did Dennis relate deathbed salvation to heavenly robes?

answers.summary: Dennis distinguishes salvation from accumulated righteous works. He interprets the saints’ linen as righteous acts and says a late convert may lack those works despite finding salvation.

questions.question: How did Dennis relate excessive drinking to salvation?

answers.summary: Dennis said drinking alone would not exclude a person from heaven, but qualified this by warning about unlawful conduct and alcohol displacing a relationship with God. He did not portray continual drunkenness as harmless.

questions.question: How did Dennis relate guardian angels to the elect?

answers.summary: Dennis points to Matthew 18:10 and says he believes the little ones described there are God’s elect.

questions.question: How did Dennis relate Israel’s being chosen to people who choose Christ?

answers.summary: Dennis distinguishes Israel’s election in the Old Testament from salvation opened to the nations through Christ, citing all in Christ as Abraham’s seed.

questions.question: How did Dennis relate peaceful living to defending one’s home?

answers.summary: Dennis supports living peaceably where possible while allowing defense of the home and emphasizing the laws applicable in the listener’s state.

questions.question: How did Dennis relate reverence for God to knowledge?

answers.summary: Dennis affirms that reverence encourages study and openness to instruction, contrasting that with despising instruction.

questions.question: How did Dennis relate the new world order to Revelation?

answers.summary: Dennis identifies the first beast of Revelation 13 as the political beast and the second as the antichrist.

questions.question: How did Dennis resolve Hobab and Jethro both being called Moses’ father-in-law?

answers.summary: Dennis says Hobab should be understood as Moses’ brother-in-law, Jethro’s son, and connects him with guidance through the land.

questions.question: How did Dennis respond to a 2016 prediction about Daniel 11:20?

answers.summary: Asked whether the prophecy would be completed in November 2016, Dennis says he does not think so but will watch. The answer reflects the time of the recording.

questions.question: How did Dennis respond to a Bible dictionary entry about Cain’s parentage?

answers.summary: Dennis rejects that particular dictionary entry while saying a dictionary can still be useful; his answer reflects his interpretation of the biblical account.

questions.question: How did Dennis respond to a concern about weekly communion?

answers.summary: Dennis declines to judge another church, says people should decide where to attend, and contrasts weekly communion with Chapel practice.

questions.question: How did Dennis respond to a disabled listener concerned about fighting for God?

answers.summary: Dennis describes the coming conflict as spiritual rather than physical and points to the armor of God in Ephesians 6.

questions.question: How did Dennis respond to a divorced abuse survivor asking about remarriage?

answers.summary: Dennis says she need not remain in an abusive relationship and encourages her to remarry if she finds someone with whom she can be happy.

questions.question: How did Dennis respond to a divorced listener hoping to remarry?

answers.summary: Dennis says divorce can be forgiven and rejects treating divorced people as second-class Christians. He appeals to Jesus forgiving the adulterous woman and to the divorce imagery in Jeremiah.

questions.question: How did Dennis respond to a grieving listener who had cursed God?

answers.summary: Dennis says he is not claiming God caused her disability, and encourages her to repent and return to God, saying her words were not the unforgivable sin.

questions.question: How did Dennis respond to a listener asking about flat-earth claims?

answers.summary: Dennis says he regards the earth as round and does not know where the flat-earth theory came from.

questions.question: How did Dennis respond to a listener asking whether Christians who know the truth are elect?

answers.summary: Dennis describes understanding the antichrist’s appearance before Christ’s return and the Holy Spirit’s witness when the elect are delivered up. He emphasizes recognizing the deception and cites Revelation 2:9 and 3:9.

questions.question: How did Dennis respond to a listener asking whether government divisions would create a rift?

answers.summary: Dennis says there was already a significant rift and encourages listeners to watch developments. His short comment does not identify a specific predicted event.

questions.question: How did Dennis respond to a listener describing trouble in her home?

answers.summary: Dennis discusses setting household rules, anointing the home and filling it with God’s Word.

questions.question: How did Dennis respond to a listener distressed about her brother’s same-sex marriage?

answers.summary: Dennis expresses religious opposition to the marriage and says he regards that position as applying in both Testaments.

questions.question: How did Dennis respond to a listener feeling spiritually opposed within her family?

answers.summary: Dennis urges using what he describes as Christ-given authority in prayer to rebuke Satan and seek protection for home and family.

questions.question: How did Dennis respond to a listener overwhelmed by credit payments?

answers.summary: Dennis recommends a Christian credit counselor to help negotiate manageable payments and warns against judging affordability only by the monthly installment. He does not specifically approve stopping all payments as the listener proposed.

questions.question: How did Dennis respond to a listener troubled by helping arrange an abortion?

answers.summary: Dennis says he would not call the listener’s action the unforgivable sin and advises repentance and seeking forgiveness.

questions.question: How did Dennis respond to a listener who thought his sins left no hope?

answers.summary: Dennis encourages belief in Christ, repentance and forgiveness, then urges the listener to forgive himself rather than regard himself as already finally condemned.

questions.question: How did Dennis respond to a listener whose doctor claimed to be a medium?

answers.summary: Dennis objects to attempts to contact the dead and relates his warning to Saul and the woman at Endor.

questions.question: How did Dennis respond to a listener worried about a sister returning to drugs?

answers.summary: Dennis encourages the listener to be a good example and pray for her sister.

questions.question: How did Dennis respond to a question about 2018 and the fig tree generation?

answers.summary: At the time of the recording, Dennis mentions 40-, 70- and 120-year generations and encourages watching; he does not give a specific prediction.

questions.question: How did Dennis respond to a question about a disruptive person in church?

answers.summary: Dennis discusses removing a disruptive influence and refers to the figurative language in Matthew 5:29.

questions.question: How did Dennis respond to a question about a preacher selling drugs?

answers.summary: Dennis says he cannot explain the situation, but would not attend a church being used to sell drugs.

questions.question: How did Dennis respond to a question about cruelty in 2 Kings 15?

answers.summary: Dennis says people in biblical times were not perfect and compares the passage with his opposition to abortion.

questions.question: How did Dennis respond to a question about faith and life after death?

answers.summary: Dennis points to Romans 10:17 on faith through hearing the Word and describes God’s kingdom as eternal.

questions.question: How did Dennis respond to a question about future bodies being flesh and bones like the risen Jesus?

answers.summary: Dennis says no and discusses transfiguration. He includes Moses among those he believes were taken by God, explaining that this is his inference from Moses appearing with Elijah at the transfiguration and the burial account.

questions.question: How did Dennis respond to a question about gates in the holy city?

answers.summary: Dennis’s short response is that God designed the city that way; he does not give a further explanation.

questions.question: How did Dennis respond to a question about Jesus’ feet?

answers.summary: Dennis says he is unsure whom the listener means and does not know of a biblical passage describing that person’s feet as black. He then recognizes the follow-up as concerning Jesus and points to Revelation 1:14 for hair described as white wool.

questions.question: How did Dennis respond to a question about polygamy?

answers.summary: Dennis says Christians should obey civil law and says polygamy violates it.

questions.question: How did Dennis respond to a question about rebuilt altars in Jerusalem?

answers.summary: Dennis says Christians do not need an altar for sacrifice because Christ was the sacrifice, and points to Hebrews 9.

questions.question: How did Dennis respond to a question about repeated adultery and forgiveness?

answers.summary: Dennis discusses forgiveness with a repentant heart and interprets the question as potentially concerning remarriage after divorce.

questions.question: How did Dennis respond to a question about same-sex marriage?

answers.summary: Dennis states his religious opposition to same-sex marriage and cites passages in Leviticus and the New Testament.

questions.question: How did Dennis respond to a question about someone who died by suicide?

answers.summary: Dennis says the person is in a different dimension and leaves the question of salvation to the Lord.

questions.question: How did Dennis respond to a question about steps to salvation?

answers.summary: Dennis points to belief in Christ and John 3:16.

questions.question: How did Dennis respond to a question about the cloth in Jesus’s tomb?

answers.summary: Dennis discusses the Shroud of Turin as a tradition and says it is not biblical. His answer does not identify a biblical passage about the burial cloth.

questions.question: How did Dennis respond to a question about the earth ending and life on Mars?

answers.summary: Dennis says the earth does not end and describes heaven on a renewed earth, referring to Revelation 21. He does not resolve the question of life on Mars.

questions.question: How did Dennis respond to a question connecting an earthquake with end-time labor pains?

answers.summary: Dennis says the labor pains are growing closer and encourages watching.

questions.question: How did Dennis respond to a request for Genesis 1:46?

answers.summary: Dennis notes that Genesis 1 ends at verse 31 and asks the listener to resubmit the reference. He does not invent the missing verse or resolve the intended question.

questions.question: How did Dennis respond to an unclear question about treating people who died by suicide?

answers.summary: Dennis says the question is unclear, distinguishes the departed from people here in flesh, and leaves salvation between them and the Lord.

questions.question: How did Dennis respond to concern about faithful servants dying violently?

answers.summary: Dennis challenges the listener’s claim about all the apostles, then emphasizes eternal life and reward over the short flesh life. He says faithful servants put God’s will before their own.

questions.question: How did Dennis respond to concern that young people were drifting from God?

answers.summary: Dennis emphasizes teaching God’s love and helping people understand Scripture. He says fear-centered religion can discourage young people and that the ministry seeks to reach every age.

questions.question: How did Dennis respond to Easter greetings while teaching Passover?

answers.summary: Dennis said he responded with a Resurrection Day greeting. He advised planting a seed without assuming he could remove another person’s spiritual blindness or force agreement.

questions.question: How did Dennis respond to fear about prescribed pain medicine and the antichrist?

answers.summary: Dennis tells the listener to follow the treating doctor’s instructions, allows seeking a second opinion, and expresses trust that God will supply what is needed for His work.

questions.question: How did Dennis respond to fear that Jesus was a false name?

answers.summary: Dennis directs the listener to Christ’s model of prayer to the Father and urges sincere prayer from the heart. He treats the Lord’s Prayer as an outline; he does not separately explain the name’s linguistic origin in this answer.

questions.question: How did Dennis respond to feeling persecuted while seeking Christ?

answers.summary: Dennis points to the Beatitudes’ promise concerning persecution for Christ and encourages comparing one’s suffering with the price Christ paid. He acknowledges that some Christians face severe persecution.

questions.question: How did Dennis respond to forgetting what one has read in the Bible?

answers.summary: Dennis acknowledges that not everyone has a strong memory and points to pastors and teachers as help in learning Scripture.

questions.question: How did Dennis respond to lasting distress over seeing a deceased relative?

answers.summary: Dennis distinguishes the dead flesh from the spirit with God and contrasts temporary bodily life with eternity. He says the second death of the soul is the lasting death of concern.

questions.question: How did Dennis respond to purported official social-media pages in this recording?

answers.summary: Dennis says the particular Facebook and Twitter pages described were not official and directs listeners to shepherdschapel.com. This is a historical statement, not a current audit of social accounts.

questions.question: How did Dennis respond to questions about ghosts and contacting the dead?

answers.summary: Dennis suggests familiar spirits as an explanation and warns against trying to contact the dead.

questions.question: How did Dennis respond to reluctance to attend a church that does not teach Scripture?

answers.summary: Dennis criticizes emphasis on money instead of Scripture and cites Christ’s presence where two or three gather in his name.

questions.question: How did Dennis respond to someone claiming a personal prophetic message?

answers.summary: Dennis urges strong caution about a person claiming to be God’s prophet and stresses the preserved words of biblical prophets. He says those who have died are with the Lord, while distinguishing the two sides of the gulf.

questions.question: How did Dennis respond to someone disagreeing with God?

answers.summary: Dennis says God is righteous and the disagreement indicates the person is wrong. He distinguishes God’s love for the person from approval of that person’s conduct.

questions.question: How did Dennis respond to someone struggling to feel compassion?

answers.summary: Dennis says correction can be compassionate and compares it with God chastening those He loves. His forceful illustration is explicitly spiritual, not a recommendation to strike people.

questions.question: How did Dennis respond to the promise of things prepared for those who love God?

answers.summary: Dennis agrees that what God has prepared exceeds present human imagination and connects Paul’s words with Isaiah.

questions.question: How did Dennis respond to using olive oil when troubled by sleeplessness?

answers.summary: Dennis says he sees nothing wrong with the listener’s use of olive oil and recommends prayerful anointing against negative or evil influences. He refers to the elders’ anointing in James; this is spiritual counsel, not a stated medical treatment.

questions.question: How did Dennis respond when a listener asked how light overcomes darkness?

answers.summary: Dennis discusses what he believes about those who followed Satan in the first earth age, points to perilous times in 2 Timothy 3 and urges the listener to stay in God’s Word.

questions.question: How did Dennis respond when a listener contrasted Arnold’s weather answer with Satan’s signs?

answers.summary: Dennis says he would not put weather control beyond Satan’s supernatural abilities and points to Revelation’s fire-from-heaven sign. He also stresses authority in Christ’s name. The listener’s reported Arnold statement remains a reported quotation, not independently verified here.

questions.question: How did Dennis respond when asked if Christians were called people of the way?

answers.summary: Dennis says he is not aware of such a reference. This records his answer rather than a complete search of Scripture.

questions.question: How did Dennis respond when asked why God required blood sacrifice?

answers.summary: Dennis did not explain the historical reason in detail. He stressed that blood sacrifices were no longer required, saying Christ became the final sacrifice and the blood ordinances ended with the cross.

questions.question: How did Dennis say Christ defeated the devil?

answers.summary: Dennis points to Christ’s resurrection and Hebrews 2:14 in explaining that Christ defeated the devil.

questions.question: How did Dennis say he assessed progress through Revelation?

answers.summary: Dennis says to study the events in the book and distinguishes, at the time of this recording, the still-future arrival of the two witnesses and Satan’s expulsion.

questions.question: How did Dennis say Jesus took on the sins of the world?

answers.summary: Dennis points to Christ’s crucifixion for sins and to John 3:16.

questions.question: How did Dennis say people can make God’s day?

answers.summary: Dennis emphasizes loving and obeying God’s instructions, comparing it to the pleasure a parent takes in a cooperative child.

questions.question: How did Dennis say Satan drew away a third of God’s children?

answers.summary: Dennis says he deceived them into following him rather than God, interpreting the stars drawn by the dragon in Revelation 12 as God’s children. He gives no more detailed mechanism.

questions.question: How did Dennis say someone could recognize election and the Spirit’s testimony?

answers.summary: Dennis connected election with knowing what he called God’s overall plan and that antichrist comes first. He told the listener not to rehearse the future testimony, saying the Holy Spirit would supply it at the time.

questions.question: How did Dennis say someone may recognize an answer to prayer?

answers.summary: Dennis advises looking for the outcome of prayer while submitting one’s request to God’s will.

questions.question: How did Dennis say the elect would be prepared to recognize antichrist?

answers.summary: Dennis says the two witnesses first supply truth to the elect. He also defines the unforgivable sin here as refusing the Holy Spirit’s testimony.

questions.question: How did Dennis say to anoint a home?

answers.summary: He describes blessing virgin olive oil, placing a little on the doorpost and ordering evil away in Jesus’ name.

questions.question: How did Dennis spell katabole and direct further study?

answers.summary: Dennis spells it K-A-T-A-B-O-L-E and recommends Companion Bible Appendix 146 for the overthrow interpretation he teaches. He says a Strong’s lookup alone will not supply his full explanation.

questions.question: How did Dennis spell the sacred name?

answers.summary: Dennis gives the consonants Y-H-V-H and omits vowels in his written form.

questions.question: How did Dennis suggest discussing the rapture in a community that teaches it?

answers.summary: Dennis recommends studying the relevant passages and moving on if listeners will not hear the teaching.

questions.question: How did Dennis suggest explaining a grandmother’s death to a grieving daughter?

answers.summary: Dennis recommends first understanding 1 Corinthians 15, then carefully explaining flesh and spiritual bodies and that her grandmother is with God. He suggests tailoring the discussion to what the daughter can understand.

questions.question: How did Dennis suggest finding repeat broadcasts?

answers.summary: Dennis says the requested on-screen repeat notice was not feasible, but that viewers could request the ministry’s satellite schedule. This describes the arrangement at the time of this recording.

questions.question: How did Dennis suggest recognizing possible election?

answers.summary: Dennis says understanding the overall plan, especially antichrist preceding Christ and the ministry’s three-age teaching, may indicate election. He uses qualified language rather than certifying an individual.

questions.question: How did Dennis summarize the first earth age?

answers.summary: Dennis says God’s children were in spiritual bodies, a third followed Satan’s rebellion, and God instituted flesh life as an opportunity for salvation. He says the elect had stood with God and would stand against Antichrist again.

questions.question: How did Dennis think Satan hopes to defeat God?

answers.summary: Dennis describes the aim as a mutiny achieved by deceiving the world into worshiping Satan as God. He says the elect and their Spirit-given testimony prevent universal deception.

questions.question: How did Dennis translate the name Hosea?

answers.summary: Dennis gives Savior or Salvation as the name’s meaning.

questions.question: How did Dennis view a reported successful medical resuscitation?

answers.summary: Dennis says he believes it was God’s will for the person to live and regards doctors and nurses as possible instruments of that help. He does not independently verify the reported event.

questions.question: How did Dennis view someone who died believing in a rapture?

answers.summary: Dennis says a person who died in Christ was not deceived by antichrist; he locates the danger in those alive when the false Christ appears.

questions.question: How did God communicate with people in the Bible?

answers.summary: Dennis describes several ways: speaking face to face with Moses, appearing in dreams to Solomon and others, and conveying temple plans through David.

questions.question: How did Jesus get his last name Christ?

answers.summary: Dennis explains: pastor Murray states that the name Christ comes from the Greek word meaning 'the anointed one,' and it is one of Jesus' names, not his last name.

questions.question: How did large numbers of Israelites receive God’s instructions without messages changing?

answers.summary: Dennis says the word was written on scrolls and read publicly by priests. He also describes the Massorah’s textual checks as a safeguard against alteration.

questions.question: How did Ms. MacDonald come up with the rapture theory? Was the rapture in the original writings of the New Testament?

answers.summary: Dennis says the rapture doctrine began in 1830 and was not in the original New Testament writings. He attributes its spread to a disturbing dream by Miss MacDonald and preachers adopting it. These historical claims are his account in this recording.

questions.question: How did Satan have the power of death?

answers.summary: Dennis says Satan can persuade people to reject God and worship him, exposing them to the second death. He says Christ defeated that power through His resurrection.

questions.question: How did the burning bush get on fire?

answers.summary: Dennis says the burning bush in Exodus 3:2 was a manifestation of God and connects it with God as a consuming fire in Hebrews 12:29.

questions.question: How did the Chapel observe biblical feast days?

answers.summary: Dennis says the Chapel teaches the feast days but does not observe all of them as ancient ordinances. He describes Passover teaching meetings and communion, interpreting Christ as the Christian’s Passover.

questions.question: How do burdens differ from God’s discipline?

answers.summary: Dennis describes chastisement as loving correction of improper conduct. He distinguishes burdens caused by oneself or others and says not to blame God for them.

questions.question: How do I best teach the second grade students to spot false teachers and false doctrine?

answers.summary: Dennis explains: the pastor advised always comparing what is being taught with God's Word. If it doesn't stack up with the Bible, it's false. God's Word is truth and should be the basis for all teaching. The pastor also emphasized keeping the teaching interesting for second graders and considering the audience when teaching.

questions.question: How do I explain to my seven-year-old son that we are no longer celebrating Easter and how can we celebrate Passover?

answers.summary: Arnold recommends explaining Passover truth to the child gently and protecting credibility rather than making the family outsiders unnecessarily.

questions.question: How do I know I am saved in the Holy Spirit and will be with my savior when my time comes?

answers.summary: Dennis directs the listener to John 3:16 for the requirements of salvation. He advises following what can be documented in Scripture rather than treating a church’s traditions as obligations.

questions.question: How do we convey to other family members that we are members of a real church, especially since we tithe and are fed?

answers.summary: Dennis recommends demonstrating Christian conduct to relatives rather than assuming everyone will understand the Chapel’s teaching.

questions.question: How do you feel about preachers healing people?

answers.summary: Arnold explains: the pastor states that preachers do not heal people, and that Christ is the one who heals. He explains that preachers can only anoint and ask God to heal, not perform the healing themselves.

questions.question: How do you know what your gift from God is?

answers.summary: Arnold describes recognition of the false Christ and allowing the Holy Spirit to testify as a gift and purpose for believers who understand.

questions.question: How does 1 Thessalonians 4:13-18 correspond with the seventh trump?

answers.summary: Dennis says the subject of 1 Thessalonians 4:13 onward is where the dead are, rather than a rapture. He explains the cloud as a figure for a large gathering, comparing the cloud of witnesses in Hebrews 12:1. He does not fully spell out the trumpet chronology in this selected answer.

questions.question: How does a person humble himself?

answers.summary: Dennis advises avoiding egotism and glorifying God rather than oneself. He contrasts God exalting the humble with bringing down those who exalt themselves.

questions.question: How does a person realize their calling?

answers.summary: Arnold emphasizes Mark 13 and identifies resisting the false Messiah and possible testimony through the Holy Spirit as a calling in this generation.

questions.question: How does Dennis connect predestination with where souls came from?

answers.summary: Dennis interprets being chosen before the world’s foundation as relating to those who stood with God during Satan’s earlier rebellion, and recommends the Three World Ages study.

questions.question: How does Dennis describe healing in eternity?

answers.summary: Dennis identifies the tree of life in Revelation with Jesus Christ and points to its leaves being for the healing of the nations. He presents it as the cure for illness, anxiety and pain in eternity.

questions.question: How does Dennis distinguish Goliath from the giant killed by Elhanan?

answers.summary: Dennis identifies the latter as Goliath’s brother and points to the parallel Chronicles account.

questions.question: How does Dennis explain baptism with the Holy Spirit?

answers.summary: Dennis refers to John’s distinction between his water baptism and Christ’s baptism with the Holy Spirit, and describes the Chapel’s baptism in the names of Father, Son and Holy Spirit.

questions.question: How does Dennis interpret blessed are the barren?

answers.summary: Dennis reads the passage spiritually as referring to those who have not joined Antichrist and remain faithful for Christ’s return.

questions.question: How does Dennis interpret the astonishing work in Habakkuk 1:5–8?

answers.summary: Dennis connects it with Satan’s future expulsion from heaven and deception of people who mistake Antichrist for Christ. He corrects his spoken reference to Revelation 12.

questions.question: How does Dennis interpret the head covering in 1 Corinthians 11?

answers.summary: Dennis interprets the covering as Christ’s protection rather than cloth and relates Paul’s warning about angels to his fallen-angel teaching.

questions.question: How does Dennis reconcile unquenchable fire with final destruction?

answers.summary: Dennis interprets the Gehenna imagery as an ongoing refuse fire and distinguishes it from the lake of fire, where he teaches final destruction of the condemned.

questions.question: How does Dennis respond to charging substantial money to teach the Bible?

answers.summary: Dennis contrasts serving God with serving money, urging discernment between a ministry focused on teaching and one focused on fundraising.

questions.question: How does Dennis say the seventh trumpet can be recognized?

answers.summary: Dennis says the true Christ will be present and people will no longer be in flesh; a claimant encountered while people remain in flesh is false in his interpretation.

questions.question: How does Dennis view people today claiming to be prophets or Melchizedek?

answers.summary: Dennis urges caution about such claims, distinguishes present pastors and teachers from biblical prophets, and identifies Melchizedek with Christ in his reading of Hebrews 7.

questions.question: How does one know that they have been blessed with the gift of discernment?

answers.summary: Arnold explains: if you're a child of God and you love our father and you love the word, spiritual discernment will always let you know when there is a negative spirit near. You can feel it and you can know it. That is a gift from God to keep you out of trouble.

questions.question: How does the every-tenth-animal illustration explain tithing?

answers.summary: Dennis describes animals passing under the owner’s rod, with each tenth belonging to the Lord. He says the owner must not choose between good and bad animals to alter which one is counted.

questions.question: How important did Arnold consider formal ordination for teaching?

answers.summary: Arnold emphasizes God’s calling and a lived example over formal credentials, referring to unordained people he considered faithful. He briefly describes salvation as letting the Savior save.

questions.question: How is Jesus’ returning sword consistent with the Sermon on the Mount?

answers.summary: Dennis describes the future conflict as spiritual and interprets the sword as Christ’s truthful words defeating God’s enemies.

questions.question: How long before this recording did Dennis say Jesus lived on earth?

answers.summary: Speaking in 2015, Dennis gives the approximate answer of two thousand years earlier.

questions.question: How long did Arnold say Job’s troubles lasted?

answers.summary: Arnold claimed the troubles lasted 21 years, beginning around age 49 and ending around 70, followed by another 140 years of life. His captioned reference to a 48th chapter of Job is invalid; the claim and dates have not been verified against the recording or Scripture.

questions.question: How long did Dennis say a priestly course served?

answers.summary: Dennis says each course served a week from Sabbath to Sabbath, with the 24-course rotation repeated, and all priests serving at the major festivals.

questions.question: How long did Dennis say Noah took to build the ark?

answers.summary: Dennis says the duration is not certain.

questions.question: How long did Dennis say the six days of creation lasted?

answers.summary: Dennis interprets the six days in Genesis 1 as a 6,000-year period in human time, citing 2 Peter 3:8.

questions.question: How long does mourning a spouse last?

answers.summary: Dennis gives no fixed deadline. He acknowledges the pain may last and offers comfort through the shortness of flesh life compared with eternity and the hope of seeing the loved one again.

questions.question: How many children did Lot have by his daughters, and how long were they living in that cave?

answers.summary: Dennis says the duration of Lot’s cave residence is not recorded and describes the two sons born through his daughters in Genesis 19.

questions.question: How many heavens are there?

answers.summary: Arnold says there is one heaven, wherever God is, and distinguishes it from his teaching about successive heaven ages.

questions.question: How many languages did God make?

answers.summary: Arnold tells the child that Scripture does not specify an exact count of languages and points to Genesis 11.

questions.question: How many people did Dennis say Moses brought into the promised land?

answers.summary: Dennis says none because Moses himself was not allowed to enter, and points to Deuteronomy 34:1.

questions.question: How many wives did Solomon have?

answers.summary: Dennis explains: the pastor stated that Solomon had 700 wives and 300 concubines, as written in 1 Kings 11:3. While having multiple wives wasn't prohibited, God warned against multiplying wives, which Solomon overdid, leading to his downfall.

questions.question: How might the elect be transported to testify in Jerusalem?

answers.summary: Dennis says the elect will be delivered to councils and Satan’s synagogues. He does not claim a known transport method: he mentions ordinary air travel and speculates that supernatural transportation may be involved.

questions.question: How often did Dennis say the Chapel took communion?

answers.summary: Dennis refers back to his answer that the Chapel held communion twice annually, at Passover and fall fellowship, to keep it special. He also says individuals may observe communion more often.

questions.question: How old did Dennis estimate Jesus was at crucifixion?

answers.summary: Dennis estimates thirty-two or thirty-three, allowing a ministry beginning around thirty and lasting two or three years. He presents an estimate rather than an exact date.

questions.question: How shall we deal with family members who hurt us?

answers.summary: Arnold refers to 2 Thessalonians 3 and advises boundaries with disorderly relatives without treating them as enemies. His statement about not feeding someone who refuses to work is expressly limited to able-bodied people, not people with disabilities.

questions.question: How should a Christian repent?

answers.summary: Dennis says to approach God with a genuinely repentant heart and mind, acknowledging shortcomings. He stresses that God cannot be deceived and recommends praying in Jesus Christ’s name.

questions.question: How should a person examine themselves before communion?

answers.summary: Dennis says examination includes understanding what Jesus did on the cross and why.

questions.question: How should I pray, and how does Dennis explain the Trinity?

answers.summary: Dennis recommends praying to the Father in Jesus’ name. He describes Father, Son and Holy Spirit through different divine roles and refers the listener to Arnold’s study The Nature of God for a fuller explanation.

questions.question: How should our own will relate to God’s will in prayer?

answers.summary: Dennis says Christian maturity should shift attention from self-will toward God’s will. He advises studying Scripture to learn that will and allowing one’s own desires to be shaped by it.

questions.question: How should parents explain Halloween or Christmas restrictions to children?

answers.summary: Dennis warns that simply blaming religious prohibitions can alienate a child from religion. He advises explaining the holidays’ origins, teaching his understanding of Christ’s conception and birth, and making clear that evil is not being worshiped or celebrated.

questions.question: How should someone respond to a gay person asking about salvation?

answers.summary: Dennis says the listener cannot personally save anyone but can point the person to God. He cites John 3:16 and describes reaching lost people, gay or straight, as the responsibility of believers.

questions.question: How should we behave according to Romans 13:1?

answers.summary: Dennis explains: pastor Murray says we should obey the laws of the land but not agree with the politicians who run our government, and it's okay to exercise our first amendment rights of freedom of speech.

questions.question: How specific was Arnold about Adam’s sin in Eden?

answers.summary: After an initial joke, Arnold said Adam partook of the same fruit and bore responsibility as head of the household in his reading. He explicitly said the account was not more specific and advised leaving it there rather than inventing details.

questions.question: How strongly did Arnold endorse the listener’s symbolic reading of Isaiah 1:17?

answers.summary: Arnold encouraged the listener’s suggested third-level reading of fatherless and widow imagery but declined to comment further. His brief encouragement is not expanded into a fully developed interpretation.

questions.question: How will people buy and sell if worship of the antichrist is required?

answers.summary: Dennis says believers should not worship the antichrist to buy and sell and discusses supplies and trade.

questions.question: How will Satan be deceiving the people during the sixth seal, the sixth trump?

answers.summary: Arnold says Satan will twist Scripture, using Christ’s temptation in Matthew 4 as the example, and recommends checking the original context.

questions.question: How will we know whether it's the Antichrist or Jesus?

answers.summary: Dennis places the antichrist at the sixth trumpet and Christ at the seventh. His practical test concerns the listener’s body: if the listener is still in flesh, someone claiming to be Christ is false, because he teaches that believers change to spiritual bodies when Christ returns.

questions.question: I am a recovering alcoholic, but I want to go to heaven, what should I do?

answers.summary: Dennis urges the recovering alcoholic to remain sober, love God and serve him.

questions.question: I am not sure if I was baptized. I think I was. Should I do it again if I'm not sure?

answers.summary: Dennis Murray suggests checking with your parents or the church where you were baptized for a record. He references Hebrews 6:4-6, warning against being baptized more than once, as it could be seen as re-crucifying Christ. He encourages prayer and reflection on the Scripture.

questions.question: I have a friend who says that God took Paul to heaven. I thought it was John, could you set us straight on this?

answers.summary: Dennis Murray explains that both John and Paul were taken to the third heaven, but they experienced it differently. John was taken in the spirit to the Lord's day, while Paul spoke humbly about a man being taken to the third heaven. He clarifies that there are three heaven ages, not three heavens, as discussed in 2 Corinthians 12:1-2 and Revelation 1:10.

questions.question: I have been married for 28 years and I want to stay married till death do us part, but I'm tired. What should I do?

answers.summary: Dennis recommends prayer and open communication about the marriage’s difficulties and suggests renewing vows as one possible step.

questions.question: I heard they recently found a book of Mary. Can you tell me what you think about that? If there is a printing I could read.

answers.summary: Dennis says he does not know the proposed Book of Mary and recommends comparing outside reading with Scripture rather than accepting it automatically.

questions.question: I receive widows benefits monthly. Would I not accept them when Satan comes? I don't want to do anything that would displease our father.

answers.summary: Dennis says receiving benefits is acceptable but emphasizes refusing to worship the antichrist. He says worship will be demanded for participation in that monetary system and that the elect will consequently be unable to buy and sell. This preserves his qualification rather than promising unrestricted benefits then.

questions.question: I'm curious, do we have a physical church?

answers.summary: Dennis identifies the Chapel’s physical church as being in Gravette, Arkansas, in the recording.

questions.question: If God can't sin and jealousy is a sin, how is it that God says he is a jealous God?

answers.summary: Arnold explains: dr. Murray clarifies that God's jealousy is not sinful. It's a righteous jealousy for His children, protecting them from abuse and bringing correction. This differs from sinful jealousy, which is based on suspicion without fact.

questions.question: If I marry him for these benefits, will I be stealing in God's eyes?

answers.summary: Dennis explains: pastor Murray explains that you wouldn't be stealing, but rather collecting survivors benefits as a spouse is entitled to, but warns against marrying for the benefits alone.

questions.question: If Satan knows he's already defeated, then why does he try, what's the purpose?

answers.summary: Arnold says Satan knows but twists Scripture and expects to deceive people into worshiping him as the returned Christ.

questions.question: If we have passed by the time the Antichrist appears, will we have a chance to stand against him or is it just for the ones that are in the flesh bodies?

answers.summary: Arnold places the testimony against antichrist among those still in flesh bodies, while describing teaching service in the millennium for others.

questions.question: If you don't study your Bible, will you go to hell?

answers.summary: Dennis says neglecting Scripture can increase the likelihood of ending in the lake of fire because a person will not know and follow God’s commandments.

questions.question: If you had an abortion but didn't know God, but now I do, and I've repented, can I be forgiven by God for this?

answers.summary: Dennis says abortion is not the unforgivable sin and encourages sincere repentance, accepting forgiveness and continuing to serve God.

questions.question: If you make a vow to read the Bible every day, but you don't, is that an unforgivable sin?

answers.summary: Dennis Murray says no, but discourages making vows to God that one cannot keep.

questions.question: In Revelation 12:7 and 11, is it a future event or has this already happened?

answers.summary: Arnold treats Satan being cast out in Revelation 12 as future relative to the recording and connects it with his five-month interpretation.

questions.question: In the Bible did God shorten man's lifespan to no longer than 120 years?

answers.summary: Dennis points to Genesis 6:3 for a reduction to 120 years and relates earlier long lifespans to his interpretation of a thousand years as one day with God.

questions.question: In the Bible does it say the lion will lay with the lamb, or the wolf will lay with the lamb?

answers.summary: Pastor Dennis explains that the Bible does not say the lion will lay with the lamb, but the wolf will dwell with the lamb, as stated in Isaiah 11:6. This is possible because after Jesus returns, there will be no more flesh, and no more carnivores, making such coexistence possible.

questions.question: In the first earth age, were we in a spiritual body, and could we fly?

answers.summary: Dennis expects first-age people in spiritual bodies to have flying vehicles rather than necessarily flying like winged birds.

questions.question: In which age did Arnold place the hybrids of his Genesis interpretation?

answers.summary: Arnold places the hybrids in this earth age, not the first, and attributes them to fallen angels and daughters of Adam. This records his theological explanation.

questions.question: Is a deathbed conversion possible?

answers.summary: Dennis uses the vineyard laborers to illustrate equal salvation for those who come late. He also notes the blessings of serving God earlier in life.

questions.question: Is a funeral necessary, and may a person donate their body or organs?

answers.summary: Dennis says a funeral is not required for the deceased, though it can help survivors find closure. He regards donation as a personal decision and praises the benefit of organ donation.

questions.question: Is a person who still struggles with addiction a hypocrite for praying for help?

answers.summary: Dennis distinguishes sincere requests for help from merely acting religious. He encourages professional addiction help alongside prayer and notes that acknowledging the problem is important.

questions.question: Is a spirit in me an angel after I die?

answers.summary: Dennis explains: sheila, the spirit in you is your spiritual body. We have two bodies: a terrestrial and a celestial. When we die, the flesh returns to the earth and the spirit returns to God from which it came.

questions.question: Is accepting Christ before a congregation in church considered baptism?

answers.summary: Dennis explains: the pastor clarifies that baptism is immersion in water, not simply accepting Christ before a congregation, as the word 'baptism' refers to total immersion.

questions.question: Is attending a job training counselor acceptable?

answers.summary: Dennis says yes, provided the training does not require anything immoral, illegal or contrary to God’s word, while acknowledging uncertainty about the exact arrangement.

questions.question: Is being a stay-at-home mother laziness?

answers.summary: Arnold calls raising a family and caring for a home a full-time job and tells the listener not to regard that work as laziness.

questions.question: Is Beulah in the Bible?

answers.summary: Pastor Dennis Murray answered that Beulah is mentioned in Isaiah chapter 62 verse four, referring to God's election and those who are not deceived by the anti-Christ, also linked to the over comers in Revelation chapter 15. Beulah means married and is connected to Hepzibah, meaning my delight is in her.

questions.question: Is bitcoin the monetary currency the antichrist will use to make purchases?

answers.summary: Dennis denies identifying bitcoin as antichrist’s currency and says the important issue in his interpretation is refusing the worship required for antichrist’s money.

questions.question: Is broadcast Bible study acceptable when someone cannot safely drive to church?

answers.summary: Dennis welcomes the listener to study with the Chapel and applies Christ’s promise to be present where believers gather in His name to their shared study.

questions.question: Is every kind of hatred sinful?

answers.summary: Dennis distinguishes hatred of evil from indiscriminate hatred. He points to the things God hates in Proverbs and says Christians should oppose Satan’s harm.

questions.question: Is everything already perfect in heaven?

answers.summary: Dennis says present heaven is not yet perfected because Satan is still there. He distinguishes this from eternity after final judgment.

questions.question: Is failing to respond to an altar call the unpardonable sin?

answers.summary: Dennis says no. He identifies the unforgivable sin as one of God’s elect refusing the Holy Spirit when delivered before the antichrist, referring to Luke 12:10–13. He says that situation had not yet occurred at the time of this recording.

questions.question: Is God's wrath greater for those who claim to be preachers but engage in immoral activities?

answers.summary: Dennis says judgment begins at God’s house and that God will not bless a supposed ministry that condones the abuses the listener describes. He explicitly declines to decide whether the listener is personally safe there.

questions.question: Is Isaiah 53:2 talking about the first earth age?
