questions.question: Where did Dennis locate biblical woes?

answers.summary: Dennis distinguishes the woes beginning in Isaiah 28 from those in Matthew 23, which he relates to the Beatitudes.

questions.question: Where did Dennis locate David’s sin with Bathsheba and against Uriah?

answers.summary: Dennis points to 2 Samuel 11, recounting the adultery, failed attempt to conceal it, and Uriah’s fatal assignment. He adds the prophetic confrontation in chapter 12.

questions.question: Where did Dennis locate earthquakes in diverse places?

answers.summary: Dennis directs the listener to Matthew 24:7 and Mark 13:8. He distinguishes the close of a world age from the physical world ending.

questions.question: Where did Dennis locate his teaching about God and national rulers?

answers.summary: Dennis points to Romans 13:1 and interprets national rulers as holding their positions under God’s authority.

questions.question: Where did Dennis locate Jesus cooking fish on shore?

answers.summary: Dennis directs the listener to John 21, recounting the empty catch, Jesus’ instruction to cast on the right, and the prepared fish and coals when the disciples came ashore.

questions.question: Where did Dennis locate judgment beginning at the house of God?

answers.summary: Dennis cited 1 Peter 4:17 and applied it especially to teachers and ministers. He urged serious study and care not to mislead others.

questions.question: Where did Dennis locate milk and meat as images for biblical learning?

answers.summary: Dennis cites Hebrews5:12 and distinguishes initial salvation teaching from maturing into deeper study. He values evangelists’ introductory work while urging pastors to teach beyond it.

questions.question: Where did Dennis locate people besides Adam and Eve in Genesis?

answers.summary: Dennis distinguishes his reading of the creation in Genesis 1 from the man Adam in Genesis 2.

questions.question: Where did Dennis locate shaking the dust off one’s feet?

answers.summary: Dennis points to Matthew, Mark and Luke and distinguishes the stated instruction from the listener’s added wording about washing hands and forgiving.

questions.question: Where did Dennis locate the account of the rich man seeing Lazarus across a gulf?

answers.summary: Dennis points to Luke 16 and corrects the listener’s description: Lazarus is called a beggar, not a blind man in that passage.

questions.question: Where did Dennis locate the four levels of chastisement?

answers.summary: Dennis points to Leviticus 26:16, 21, 23 and 27 and says repentance returns a person to the first level.

questions.question: Where did Dennis locate the future heavenly city, and how did he describe its size?

answers.summary: Dennis says Revelation depicts it descending to earth. He describes its equal dimensions as 12,000 furlongs, approximately 1,500 miles each, and cautions against imagining its inhabitants as flesh bodies.

questions.question: Where did Dennis locate the image of smoke in God’s nostrils?

answers.summary: Dennis directs the listener to Isaiah 65:4–5, applying it both to eating swine’s flesh and to a holier-than-thou attitude.

questions.question: Where did Dennis locate the prodigal-son account, and what lesson did he draw?

answers.summary: Dennis directs the listener to Luke 15:11 onward and emphasizes returning when one gets off track. He compares the father’s welcome with God’s joy when a child returns to him.

questions.question: Where did Dennis locate the prohibition on work on the seventh month’s tenth day?

answers.summary: Dennis identifies it as the Day of Atonement and directs the listener to Leviticus23 and16.

questions.question: Where did Dennis locate the red-heifer ritual?

answers.summary: Dennis points to Numbers 19 and explains the ashes’ use in purification from contact with death. He then contrasts that cleansing with the greater cleansing attributed to Christ’s blood in Hebrews.

questions.question: Where did Dennis locate the rose of Sharon and lily of the valley?

answers.summary: Dennis identifies Song of Solomon 2:1 as containing both expressions.

questions.question: Where did Dennis locate the Song of Moses?

answers.summary: Dennis corrects the listener’s reference to Deuteronomy 32 and describes its translation as accurate.

questions.question: Where did Dennis locate the song of the Lamb?

answers.summary: Dennis points to Revelation 15:3 and offers his opinion that the song is the book of Psalms.

questions.question: Where did Dennis locate the songs of Moses and the Lamb?

answers.summary: Dennis locates Moses’ song in Deuteronomy 32:1–43 and says he believes the Psalms are the Lamb’s song. He connects both with the overcomers’ celebration.

questions.question: Where did Dennis locate the temple in 2 Thessalonians 2:4?

answers.summary: Dennis interprets it as God’s sanctuary in Jerusalem, connecting the claimed throne with the north side of Jerusalem in Isaiah 14. He does not give a verified construction status for a current building.

questions.question: Where did Dennis place eternity?

answers.summary: Dennis says eternity will be on earth and points to God’s throne descending in Revelation 21.

questions.question: Where did Dennis place free-will people during the millennium?

answers.summary: Dennis distinguishes the elect as Christ’s bride with access to His presence from others outside the millennial temple. He says most free-will people will have been deceived and remain spiritually dead until the millennium ends.

questions.question: Where did Dennis place God’s eternal kingdom?

answers.summary: Dennis says it will be on earth, linking the Lord’s Prayer with the descending throne and new creation in Revelation 21.

questions.question: Where did Dennis place Native Americans in his creation teaching?

answers.summary: Dennis identifies Native Americans among the ethnic peoples he associates with the sixth-day creation in Genesis 1. This is his stated interpretation of the listener’s question.

questions.question: Where did Dennis place the fallen angels and their offspring?

answers.summary: Dennis cites Jude for fallen angels being held in chains until judgment; he labels his placement of their offspring on the unfavorable side of the gulf as what he imagines.

questions.question: Where did Dennis place the historical Philistines geographically?

answers.summary: Dennis says the area of Palestine is close to their biblical geographical region. He does not establish a modern population’s ancestry in this answer.

questions.question: Where did Dennis place the saying that judgment begins at the pulpit?

answers.summary: Dennis points to judgment beginning at the house of God in 1 Peter 4:17 and relates the pulpit to that house.

questions.question: Where did Dennis place those already dead when Christ returns?

answers.summary: Dennis says they are already with the Lord and reminds the listener of the two sides of the gulf.

questions.question: Where did Dennis place those of the first resurrection during the millennium?

answers.summary: Dennis says they reign with Christ on earth for a thousand years and directs listeners to Ezekiel 44 for his description of their setting.

questions.question: Where did Dennis point a listener asking about dogs in heaven?

answers.summary: Dennis points to Isaiah 11 and expresses his belief that animals will be present in eternity.

questions.question: Where did Dennis point a listener asking about God’s seal and the Song of the Lamb?

answers.summary: Dennis points to Revelation 9:4 for the seal, which he interprets as God’s Word in the mind, and Revelation 15:3 for the songs of Moses and the Lamb sung by overcomers. He says he believes the latter encompasses all the songs.

questions.question: Where did Dennis point for another witness to Jude 1:6?

answers.summary: Dennis points to Revelation 12 and describes Michael defeating Satan and his angels.

questions.question: Where did Dennis point for changing God’s truth into a lie?

answers.summary: Dennis points to Romans 1:25.

questions.question: Where did Dennis point for Christ preaching to the dead?

answers.summary: Dennis points to 1 Peter 3:18–19 and 4:5–6 and interprets the passage as Christ preaching to those who had died.

questions.question: Where did Dennis point for God refusing further intercession for a people?

answers.summary: Dennis points to Jeremiah 15:1, explaining that even Moses or Samuel interceding would not reverse the announced rejection in that setting.

questions.question: Where did Dennis point for helping a family member during the millennium?

answers.summary: Dennis interprets Ezekiel 44 as allowing the Zadok to help an immediate relative who is spiritually dead, followed by a seven-day cleansing before returning to service.

questions.question: Where did Dennis point for his opposition to the fly-away doctrine?

answers.summary: Dennis points to Ezekiel 13 and interprets its condemnation of false prophets and hunting souls to make them fly as relevant to that teaching.

questions.question: Where did Dennis point for Jesus driving out the money changers?

answers.summary: Dennis directs the listener to Mark 11:15 and the following verses.

questions.question: Where did Dennis point for knowledge being increased?

answers.summary: Dennis points to Daniel 12:4.

questions.question: Where did Dennis point for leaving parents and becoming one flesh in marriage?

answers.summary: Dennis pointed to Genesis 2:24: a husband leaves his parents, cleaves to his wife, and the two become one flesh.

questions.question: Where did Dennis point for lights dividing day and night?

answers.summary: Dennis directs the listener to Genesis 1:14 rather than Romans.

questions.question: Where did Dennis point for nations gathered against Jerusalem?

answers.summary: Dennis points to Zechariah 14:2 and connects it with events before the second advent.

questions.question: Where did Dennis point for prophets wanting to understand later revelations?

answers.summary: Dennis cites Daniel’s inability to understand sealed prophecy and Jesus’ statement that prophets and kings desired to see and hear what the disciples experienced.

questions.question: Where did Dennis point for rulers described as children?

answers.summary: Dennis cites the statement that babes shall rule in Isaiah 3:4.

questions.question: Where did Dennis point for Satan being turned to ashes?

answers.summary: Dennis points to Ezekiel 28 and identifies the king of Tyrus in that passage with Satan.

questions.question: Where did Dennis point for seeking the Lord and finding Him?

answers.summary: Dennis points to Deuteronomy 4:29 and recalls David’s instruction to Solomon to seek God rather than forsake Him.

questions.question: Where did Dennis point for spiritual slumber?

answers.summary: Dennis points to Romans 11:8 and Isaiah 29:9–10 and distinguishes their wording from the word stupor in the listener’s question.

questions.question: Where did Dennis point for teaching about flesh and spiritual bodies?

answers.summary: Dennis points to 1 Corinthians 15 and 2 Corinthians 5, and discusses being absent from the flesh and present with the Lord.

questions.question: Where did Dennis point for the destruction of the first earth age?

answers.summary: Dennis points to Jeremiah 4:22 and following verses and Hebrews 12:26, connecting the destruction with his teaching about Satan’s rebellion.

questions.question: Where did Dennis point for the moon becoming blood?

answers.summary: Dennis cites Joel 2:31, Acts 2:20 and Revelation 6:12 and connects them with being prepared for antichrist.

questions.question: Where did Dennis point for the northern tribes’ Assyrian captivity?

answers.summary: Dennis points to 2 Kings 15–16 and 1 Chronicles 5:6.

questions.question: Where did Dennis point for the punishment of premeditated murder?

answers.summary: Dennis points to Numbers and Deuteronomy and distinguishes premeditated murder from accidental killing and defending a country.

questions.question: Where did Dennis point for the seventh day being holy?

answers.summary: Dennis points to Exodus 20:10–11.

questions.question: Where did Dennis point for the sparrow and the hairs of one’s head?

answers.summary: Dennis points to consecutive verses in Matthew 10.

questions.question: Where did Dennis point for what goes around comes around?

answers.summary: Dennis referred to mischief returning on a person’s head and to reaping what one sows as biblical expressions of that idea.

questions.question: Where did Dennis point to discuss helping family during the millennium?

answers.summary: Dennis points to Ezekiel 44:25 and interprets the Zadok’s contact with relatives as helping family members during the millennium.

questions.question: Where did Dennis point to eye for eye?

answers.summary: Dennis points to Exodus 21:24, Leviticus 24:20 and Matthew 5:38.

questions.question: Where did Dennis point to Mary’s other children?

answers.summary: Dennis points to Matthew 13, names James, Joses, Simon and Judas as Jesus’ half brothers, and distinguishes this Judas from Judas Iscariot. He says the following verse also mentions sisters without naming them.

questions.question: Where did Dennis point to the word Christian in Scripture?

answers.summary: Dennis directs the listener to Acts 26:28 and 1 Peter 4:16.

questions.question: Where did Dennis point to traditions making void God’s word?

answers.summary: Dennis directs the listener to Matthew 15, Mark 7 and Isaiah 29, discussing the traditions of the elders.

questions.question: Where did Dennis recommend reading about the Last Supper?

answers.summary: Dennis recommends Luke 22, beginning around verse 7, for the Last Supper.

questions.question: Where did Dennis recommend studying tribal banners and the constellations?

answers.summary: Dennis recommends Companion Bible Appendix 12 and Bullinger’s Witness of the Stars, distinguishing his constellation discussion from horoscope predictions.

questions.question: Where did Dennis say Christ will return?

answers.summary: Dennis points to the Mount of Olives, connecting the ascension account with the promised return and Zechariah’s description.

questions.question: Where did Dennis say Israel obtained gold after leaving Egypt?

answers.summary: Dennis says he knows of no passage saying they found it in the desert. He points instead to goods received from Egyptians and later spoils from defeated enemies.

questions.question: Where did Dennis say judgment begins at the house of God?

answers.summary: Dennis directs the listener to 1 Peter 4:17.

questions.question: Where did Dennis say the bound angels are?

answers.summary: Dennis says they are bound in heaven and refers to Jude 1:6 and the conflict in Revelation 12 when discussing their return.

questions.question: Where did Dennis say the demons in the pigs story did not want to return?

answers.summary: Dennis says they did not want to return to Satan, whom he locates restrained in heaven rather than in hell. This is his interpretation of the episode.

questions.question: Where did Dennis say unbelievers go at death?

answers.summary: Dennis describes two sides of a gulf in paradise and directs the listener to Luke 16 and, for further description, 2 Esdras in the Apocrypha.

questions.question: Where did Dennis suggest studying the history of fallen angels?

answers.summary: Dennis suggests Companion Bible Appendix 25, Genesis 6 and Revelation 12 and describes his teaching about three influxes.

questions.question: Where did Dennis think the great white throne judgment takes place?

answers.summary: Dennis says he thinks it will be on earth.

questions.question: Where did Jesus say get behind me, Satan?

answers.summary: Dennis points to the temptation in Luke 4. He says Christ rejected Satan’s offer in exchange for worship and tells believers to resist in Jesus’ name.

questions.question: Where did Jesus say he had foretold all things?

answers.summary: Dennis identifies Mark 13:23 and says the words conveyed through prophets, disciples and apostles supply what believers need to avoid Antichrist’s deception.

questions.question: Where did the man and birds go in Jeremiah 4:25?

answers.summary: Arnold interprets Jeremiah 4 as destruction of the first age rather than annihilation of God’s children, who would then pass through flesh life.

questions.question: Where did the word Christian come from?

answers.summary: Arnold explains Christian as Christ-man or a believer in Christ and points to Acts 11:26.

questions.question: Where do people go when they die?

answers.summary: Dennis distinguishes the flesh returning to earth from the spirit returning to God. He says everyone goes to the Lord, who is the judge.

questions.question: Where do you get the meaning of numbers from?

answers.summary: Dennis recommends Companion Bible Appendix 10 for his approach to the spiritual significance of numbers.

questions.question: Where does Dennis expect Antichrist to appear first?

answers.summary: Dennis says Jerusalem, specifically the Mount of Olives. He presents this as an imitation of Christ’s return and compares the white-horse imagery in Revelation.

questions.question: Where does Dennis find his teaching about the katabole?

answers.summary: Dennis connects the term with foundation-of-the-world passages, interpreting it as Satan’s earlier rebellion, and relates it to a third following the dragon.

questions.question: Where does Dennis find righteous acts associated with heavenly robes?

answers.summary: Dennis points to works following the dead and the fine linen representing the righteous acts of the saints.

questions.question: Where does Dennis find the change to spiritual bodies?

answers.summary: Dennis points to the last trumpet and the corruptible becoming incorruptible, also citing Zechariah’s description.

questions.question: Where does God promise never to leave or forsake His people?

answers.summary: Dennis cites Hebrews but qualifies the promise with the call to love and serve God. He also cites Chronicles saying that those who forsake God will be forsaken.

questions.question: Where does it say in the Bible that during the end times you should need to prepare and stockpile your food and water?

answers.summary: Arnold says stockpiling is not a specific biblical command but treats reasonable preparation and a pantry as common sense.

questions.question: Where does it state the Scriptures are the wisdom of God?

answers.summary: Arnold points to Proverbs 1:7 and says wisdom comes from God.

questions.question: Where does Scripture describe believers as joint heirs with Christ?

answers.summary: Dennis points to Romans 8:17 and includes its qualification about suffering with Christ.

questions.question: Where does Scripture describe Enoch?

answers.summary: Dennis distinguishes the Enoch in Cain’s genealogy from the Enoch in Adam’s genealogy. He says the latter was translated by God rather than dying in flesh, comparing him with Elijah.

questions.question: Where does Scripture identify Jesus’ mother?

answers.summary: Dennis points to Gabriel’s visit to Mary and the prophecy of a virgin bearing Emmanuel, meaning God with us.

questions.question: Where does Scripture mention wars and rumors of wars?

answers.summary: Dennis points to Matthew and Mark and emphasizes the instruction not to be troubled.

questions.question: Where does Scripture say John leapt in Elizabeth’s womb?

answers.summary: Dennis points to Luke 1:41 and says the event occurred soon after Jesus was conceived, when Mary visited Elizabeth.

questions.question: Where does the tenth in tithing come from?

answers.summary: Dennis says tithe means a tenth, illustrating it with one calf from ten being dedicated to God.

questions.question: Where in Father's letter does it say old men will have minds of children?

answers.summary: Dennis explains: the pastor says the reference is likely Isaiah 3:4, where it states that babes shall rule, though the exact wording may differ.

questions.question: Where in Goodspeed’s Apocrypha is the description of paradise?

answers.summary: Dennis corrects the reference to 2 Esdras chapter 7, verse 77 and following. He notes that editions differ because of manuscript sources, so the passage is not in every Apocrypha edition.

questions.question: Where in the Bible can I find that God married Israel?

answers.summary: Arnold cites Isaiah 54:5 and Jeremiah 3:8 for marriage and divorce imagery concerning God and Israel, relating restoration to salvation.

questions.question: Where in the Bible can I find the Jesus prayer?

answers.summary: Dennis says the exact prayer quoted by the listener is not in the KJV and directs him to Jesus’ model prayer to the Father in Matthew 6:9. He discourages repeating only a canned prayer and encourages speaking from the heart.

questions.question: Where in the Bible does it say how old Jesus was when he was crucified?

answers.summary: Pastor Dennis Murray states that the Bible does not explicitly state Jesus' age at crucifixion. However, he explains that Jesus was about 30 when he was baptized and began his ministry, and estimates he was 32 or 33 when he was crucified based on the number of Passovers celebrated.

questions.question: Where in the Bible does it say that it is a sin to lust after your own wife?

answers.summary: Dennis says he does not believe Scripture forbids sexual desire toward one’s own wife. He distinguishes that from the indiscriminate lust he discusses in connection with Matthew 5:28.

questions.question: Where in the Bible does it say that Jesus said to one of the disciples, as you say not as I say?

answers.summary: Dennis points to Matthew 27:11, identifying the exchange as Christ’s answer to Pontius Pilate rather than to a disciple.

questions.question: Where in the Bible does it say that Satan's angels had sex with women and giants were born?

answers.summary: Dennis points to Genesis 6 for the fallen angels and giants in his interpretation.

questions.question: Where in the Bible does it say there is going to be 7,000 people who believe the false Christ is coming first, then the real Christ is coming next?

answers.summary: Arnold points to Romans 11’s quotation about 7,000 not bowing to Baal and also includes called believers among the nations.

questions.question: Where in the Bible does it say to be absent from the body is to be present with the Lord?

answers.summary: Arnold points to 2 Corinthians 5:7–8 and 1 Corinthians 15 for his teaching about being with the Lord after leaving the flesh.

questions.question: Where in the bible is it that says he who digs a pit will fall in it?

answers.summary: Dennis points to Proverbs 26:27 for the person who digs a pit falling into it and interprets it as trouble returning on its maker.

questions.question: Where in the Bible is the first Earth age mentioned?

answers.summary: Dennis points to Genesis 1, Jeremiah 4, 2 Peter 3 and Revelation 12 for his first-earth-age teaching.

questions.question: Where in the word does it tell us not to abstain from fellowship with other Christians?

answers.summary: Dennis explains: asked about fellowship, Dennis first discusses when to separate from people promoting teaching contrary to Scripture. He cites 2 Thessalonians 3:14 and 2 John 9–10. His response does not resolve every part of the listener’s separate question about attending a local church.

questions.question: Where is eyes have not seen what God has prepared?

answers.summary: Dennis identifies First Corinthians 2:9.

questions.question: Where is God described as married to Israel?

answers.summary: Dennis points to the spreading of a skirt in Ezekiel 16:8 and explains it as a Hebrew marriage figure.

questions.question: Where is heaven?

answers.summary: Dennis does not settle its present physical location in this answer. He says God’s throne will come to a renewed earth for eternity and points to Revelation 21.

questions.question: Where is it Faith by hearing and the word of God in the Bible you're speaking of Romans chapter 10 verse 17?

answers.summary: Dennis points to Romans 10:17 for faith coming by hearing God’s Word.

questions.question: Where is it found in the Bible, let the dead bury the dead?

answers.summary: Arnold points to Matthew 8:22 and interprets the father as still dying, with other relatives able to care for him while the disciple follows Christ.

questions.question: Where is it in the Bible that a woman can divorce her husband if he prevents her from worshiping God?

answers.summary: Dennis points to 1 Corinthians 7:15 and the chapter’s discussion of believing and unbelieving spouses, while noting that the verse does not literally use the proposed divorce wording.

questions.question: Where is it written in the Bible to not build house onto house?

answers.summary: Arnold points to Isaiah 5:8 for joining house to house.

questions.question: Where is Jesus’ conversation with the woman at the well?

answers.summary: Dennis identifies John 4 and recounts Jesus knowing her marital history and offering living water that satisfies thirst.

questions.question: Where is Mary mentioned besides Jesus’ birth?

answers.summary: Dennis points to Mary at the crucifixion, where Jesus entrusted her care to John. He separately labels the account of her later travel to England as historical rather than biblical.

questions.question: Where is Passover taught in the Bible?

answers.summary: Dennis points to the first Passover in Exodus and the feast instructions in Leviticus. He emphasizes Christ becoming the Passover lamb for Christians.

questions.question: Where is Samson’s life recorded?

answers.summary: Dennis directs the listener to Judges chapters 13 through 16.

questions.question: Where is Satan during the millennium?

answers.summary: Dennis says Satan is confined in the abyss for the thousand years, released briefly afterward, and ultimately goes into the lake of fire.

questions.question: Where is the account of the woman whose body was sent to Israel’s tribes?

answers.summary: Dennis identifies Judges 19 and explains that the Levite sent the remains as a warning about the crime, leading to the war involving Benjamin.

questions.question: Where is the color amber found in the Bible?

answers.summary: Dennis explains: pastor Murray states that amber is found in Ezekiel 1:4, where it describes the color of the vehicle that brought the throne of God to earth.

questions.question: Where is the key of David mentioned?

answers.summary: Dennis points to Revelation 3:7 and connects his interpretation of the key with recognizing those who falsely claim Judah’s identity in the synagogue-of-Satan passage.

questions.question: Where is the Nazarite vow described?

answers.summary: Dennis directs the listener to Numbers 6 and distinguishes vows for a specified period from lifelong dedication.

questions.question: Where is the passage about children ruling the people?

answers.summary: Dennis directs the listener to Isaiah 3:4, concerning children as princes and babes ruling.

questions.question: Where is the passage about laying down one’s life for a friend?

answers.summary: Arnold cites John 15:13 and says it applies to people as well as Jesus.

questions.question: Where is the promise about two or more gathered in Christ’s name?

answers.summary: Dennis cites Matthew 18:20 and applies gathering in Christ’s name to studying the Word together through the broadcast.

questions.question: Where is the scripture that says when you see the false one standing where he ought not?

answers.summary: Arnold points to Mark 13:14 and interprets the abomination standing where it ought not as the personal desolator, antichrist.

questions.question: Where might the wording about the desert becoming green be found?

answers.summary: Dennis distinguishes translations, pointing to Joel in the New American Standard Bible rather than claiming that wording occurs in the King James Version. He contrasts it with Jeremiah’s fruitful field becoming wilderness.

questions.question: Where the Bible does it say that Jesus was born on September 26th or 29th?

answers.summary: Pastor Dennis Murray suggests understanding the Course of Abia and recommends ordering Pastor Arnold Murray's CD, 'Christmas'.

questions.question: Where was Jesus during the years not described in Scripture?

answers.summary: Dennis says it cannot be documented biblically and refers to a Glastonbury tradition about journeys with Joseph of Arimathea.

questions.question: Where will Jesus reign after the millennium?

answers.summary: Dennis says Jesus and God Almighty will reign in Jerusalem throughout eternity. He connects the return to the Mount of Olives with Revelation’s description of God and the Lamb as the temple.

questions.question: Where will the anti-Christ appear, and will he be in the flesh?

answers.summary: Dennis says the antichrist will be cast from heaven rather than born as a human. He infers an appearance on the Mount of Olives from the antichrist’s impersonation of Christ and says this precedes Christ’s return. His location argument is an inference in this answer.

questions.question: Where would one be able to obtain these manuscripts?

answers.summary: Arnold recommends Green’s interlinear as an accessible resource for Hebrew, Greek and Aramaic texts alongside Strong’s Concordance.

questions.question: Which Apocrypha passage did Arnold say he liked to read?

answers.summary: Arnold recommended a Goodspeed edition and a passage captioned Ezra chapter 7 verse 77 for imagery of heaven. He explicitly distinguished enjoying it from teaching it as biblical authority and acknowledged that some Apocrypha material is questionable. The exact captioned citation is not silently standardized.

questions.question: Which Apocrypha translation did Dennis recommend?

answers.summary: Dennis recommends Goodspeed and notes the Apocrypha’s inclusion in the 1611 KJV edition the ministry offered, while finding that edition harder to use for study.

questions.question: Which Bible and tools did Arnold recommend for checking Hebrew meanings?

answers.summary: Arnold recommended the Companion Bible and Strong’s Concordance for checking English words against Hebrew meanings. He criticized the NIV and used his interpretation of Ezekiel 13 as an example; his paraphrase is not reproduced as a KJV quotation.

questions.question: Which Bible chapter did Arnold recommend for planting seeds?

answers.summary: Arnold said he used the whole Bible but particularly liked Mark 13 for explaining the elect’s destiny and the Spirit’s testimony before false Messiah. He did not require every witness to be a great scholar.

questions.question: Which Bible did Dennis say he read and recommend for study?

answers.summary: Dennis says he reads the Authorized King James Version and recommends the Companion Bible’s study notes and appendices as aids to understanding language, customs and figures of speech.

questions.question: Which Bible did Dennis say the Murray family used for teaching?

answers.summary: Dennis describes indexed red-letter KJV editions from World Publishing given by his mother to Arnold, himself and David. He says that edition was no longer available at recording time and recommends the Companion Bible for study.

questions.question: Which Bible study tools did Arnold recommend to a listener choosing a Bible?

answers.summary: Arnold recommends the Companion Bible with Strong’s Concordance and says they help an English reader examine the original languages.

questions.question: Which Bible translation did Arnold recommend, and how did he describe the Apocrypha?

answers.summary: Arnold recommends the KJV and Companion Bible and describes the Apocrypha as books printed between the Testaments in the original KJV.

questions.question: Which book did Arnold recommend about Joseph of Arimathea and Jesus’ youth?

answers.summary: Arnold named Traditions of Glastonbury and described Joseph of Arimathea as Jesus’ uncle in that tradition. He connected it with tin trading, a voyage and early Christianity in Glastonbury. These are the traditions he recommended, not independently verified biography.

questions.question: Which book did Arnold recommend for learning to live well in flesh life?

answers.summary: Arnold recommended Ecclesiastes as instruction for people living under the sun, including happiness, care of the body and learning from recurring human experience.

questions.question: Which book did Arnold recommend for witnessing to members of another church?

answers.summary: Arnold recommended the Bible as the book for witnessing truth. He declined to name the particular church and did not recommend an additional named handbook.

questions.question: Which book did Dennis recommend to a listener studying the ten northern tribes?

answers.summary: Dennis recommends Missing Links Discovered in Assyrian Tablets as the ministry’s offered resource on the northern tribes after Assyrian captivity. This is a report of his recommendation, not independent validation of its claims.

questions.question: Which commandment violations did Arnold describe as especially hurtful?

answers.summary: Arnold singles out envy and jealousy, apart from murder, and encourages prayer for release from jealousy.

questions.question: Which Companion Bible appendix did Dennis recommend for Christ’s birth date?

answers.summary: Dennis names appendix179 section3, explaining that its calculation connects Zechariah’s course of Abijah and John’s birth with Jesus’ conception and birth.

questions.question: Which Companion Bible appendix discusses the three world ages?

answers.summary: Dennis directs the listener to Appendix 195 on ages and dispensations.

questions.question: Which Companion Bible cross-reference did Arnold propose correcting in this broadcast?

answers.summary: Arnold said the listener’s reported Psalm 88 marginal reference was a copyist error and proposed Psalm 44:22 instead. The attached page and edition are unavailable, so this is his suggested correction rather than an instruction to alter every edition.

questions.question: Which country did Arnold identify as the target of Russia in his prophetic interpretation?

answers.summary: Arnold distinguished Judah from what he called true Israel and identified the latter with the United States. He expected a different judgment at Jerusalem. These are his historical and prophetic identifications, not verified geopolitical predictions.

questions.question: Which did Dennis place first, the one-world government or Hamon Gog?

answers.summary: Dennis places the one-world political beast before the battle.

questions.question: Which fish did Arnold call clean to eat?

answers.summary: Arnold specified fish with scales, cited Leviticus 11:12, and contrasted them with bottom-feeding scavengers. This summary preserves his stated criterion without adding another criterion he did not mention in this answer.

questions.question: Which half of the five-month tribulation did Dennis assign to Satan’s personal appearance?

answers.summary: Dennis assigns it to the latter half, interpreting the half-hour silence as two and a half months and distinguishing the political beast from the subsequent appearance that heals its wound.

questions.question: Which John did Dennis identify as the disciple Jesus loved?

answers.summary: Dennis identifies John the apostle, son of Zebedee and brother of James.

questions.question: Which kind of archaeology magazine did Arnold recommend for biblical study?

answers.summary: Arnold suggested a publication described in the captions as Biblical Archaeology and obtaining it through a magazine seller. The precise publication title is not clear enough to identify confidently.

questions.question: Which king did Dennis identify as receiving an extension of life?

answers.summary: Dennis identifies Hezekiah, says God answered his prayer with fifteen more years, and names Isaiah as the prophet bringing the message.

questions.question: Which kingly titles did Dennis cite for Jesus?

answers.summary: Dennis cites king of Israel, king of Salem or peace, and King of kings and Lord of lords.

questions.question: Which language did Dennis say the New Testament was written in?

answers.summary: Dennis says Greek, with some Aramaic words, and recommends a King James Bible with Strong’s Concordance.

questions.question: Which military formation did Arnold say he served with?

answers.summary: Arnold said he served with the First Marine Division on a special attachment near the northern reservoir. This records his recollection without supplying a more specific regiment not clearly given in the captions.

questions.question: Which names did Dennis associate with God’s presence?

answers.summary: Dennis cites Emmanuel as God with us and Ezekiel’s final city name as the Lord is there, then mentions Shekinah glory.

questions.question: Which nations descended from Lot’s daughters?

answers.summary: Dennis identifies the Moabites and Ammonites, from Moab and Ammon, and notes Ruth’s Moabite ancestry in David’s family.

sources.lesson: I & II Samuel 30:23 - 1:9; I & II Samuel 30:23 - 1:9

questions.question: Which of Arnold’s sons did he identify as older?

answers.summary: Arnold identifies Dennis as the elder and David as younger.

questions.question: Which Old Testament religious holiday did Dennis say the Chapel observes?

answers.summary: Dennis identifies Passover, explaining that Christ became the believers’ Passover and high Sabbath.

questions.question: Which original biblical languages did Dennis name?

answers.summary: Dennis names Hebrew with some Chaldee for the Old Testament, including parts of Daniel, and Greek for the New Testament.

questions.question: Which passage did Arnold compare with Saddam Hussein’s disheveled capture appearance?

answers.summary: Arnold corrected his recollection to Daniel 4:33 and compared Nebuchadnezzar with Saddam Hussein as a type involving Babylon. This is his historical analogy rather than proof of prophetic identity.

questions.question: Which passage did Arnold offer a caregiver distressed by a relative’s accidental injury?

answers.summary: Arnold offers 1 Corinthians 10:13 to comfort the caregiver, recognizes her care and says accidents can happen.

questions.question: Which passage did Arnold recommend about consulting mediums?

answers.summary: Arnold recommended 1 Samuel 28:7–8 and studying familiar spirits and witchcraft in Strong’s. He opposed seeking messages through mediums and said God could convey a message without them. His reference to an ancient penalty is not a call for private retaliation.

questions.question: Which passage did Arnold recommend for a wedding service?

answers.summary: Arnold recommended Matthew 19:6 and said he used it in wedding services.

questions.question: Which passage did Arnold recommend for someone entering police service?

answers.summary: Arnold recommended Psalm 144 for a listener concerned about possible use of force in police service. He applied it to protection of the public and military service, not as a blanket legal authorization.

questions.question: Which passage did Arnold recommend to help children see a purpose in studying Scripture?

answers.summary: Arnold recommended Mark 13, emphasizing purpose, a role in God’s plan and the Holy Spirit’s testimony. He suggested that seeing themselves addressed by Scripture would encourage the children to study. This is his pastoral application.

questions.question: Which passage did Arnold suggest about people judging a marriage?

answers.summary: Arnold tentatively suggested 1 Timothy 4:3 and opposed others judging marriage or food. He added an unclear qualification about marrying someone God created to be received. That limitation remains unresolved rather than expanded into a rule he did not explicitly explain.

questions.question: Which passage did Arnold suggest for a rebellious spirit and bringing thoughts to God?

answers.summary: Arnold recommended Luke 10:19, interpreting it as authority over evil spirits and Satan. He urged accepting that authority and anointing oneself and the home. He did not separately explain the listener’s phrase about taking every thought captive.

questions.question: Which passage did Arnold suggest for strength after bereavement?

answers.summary: Arnold recommends memorizing 1 Corinthians 10:13 for troubled times and reassures the listener that deceased loved ones are with the Father.

questions.question: Which passage did Dennis cite for Satan twisting Scripture?

answers.summary: Dennis pointed to Matthew 4:6 and Psalm 91:11, using the temptation of Jesus to warn against a slight distortion of Scripture and deliberately testing God. His account is a paraphrase, not a substitute for the verses.

questions.question: Which passage did Dennis give for house upon house?

answers.summary: Dennis corrects a prior reference and identifies Isaiah 5:8.

questions.question: Which passages did Arnold cite for Satan coming at the sixth trumpet?

answers.summary: Arnold cites Revelation 6:12, 9:13 and 16:12 in his sixth-seal, trumpet and vial interpretation, contrasting them with Christ at the seventh.

questions.question: Which passages did Arnold discuss when asked about confusion over the rapture?

answers.summary: Arnold discusses 1 Thessalonians 4 and 2 Thessalonians 2 and says the son of perdition comes before the gathering to Christ.

questions.question: Which passages did Arnold give for a question about disciplining children?

answers.summary: Arnold directs the listener to Proverbs 13:24 and Hebrews 12. This brief answer supplies references in response to the listener’s question; it does not develop limits or practical methods of discipline.

questions.question: Which passages did Arnold give for the continued existence of Israel’s scattered tribes?

answers.summary: Arnold rejected the reported claim that the people disappeared after AD 70. He cited Matthew 10:6 and James’s opening address to scattered tribes. This response supplied biblical references, not independent proof of the identity of modern nations.

questions.question: Which passages did Arnold recommend to someone who regarded Jesus only as a dead prophet?

answers.summary: Arnold recommended John 14 and Isaiah’s Emmanuel prophecy to explain his understanding of Christ as God with us. He also connected Psalm 22 with the crucifixion and Psalm 23 with resurrection life; these are his applications.

questions.question: Which passages did Arnold suggest to comfort a mother grieving her son?

answers.summary: Arnold recommends 1 Corinthians 10:13 and Hebrews 13’s promise that God will not leave or forsake his people.

questions.question: Which passages did Arnold suggest to encourage a discouraged friend?

answers.summary: Arnold recommends Psalm 91 and John 14, emphasizing God’s love and the comfort of the Holy Spirit.

questions.question: Which passages did Dennis cite about forgiveness of sins?

answers.summary: Dennis cites Matthew 9:6 for the Son of Man’s authority to forgive and Mark 11:25 concerning the Father’s forgiveness.

questions.question: Which passages did Dennis cite about Jesus being nailed to the cross?

answers.summary: Dennis cites Colossians2:14 in discussing what was nailed to the cross and Psalm22:16’s pierced hands and feet as prophecy of the crucifixion.

questions.question: Which passages did Dennis cite when asked about same-sex marriage?

answers.summary: Dennis interprets the cited Old and New Testament passages as condemning same-sex sexual conduct. He says he is explaining his reading of Scripture rather than instructing hatred toward people.

questions.question: Which passages did Dennis connect with fallen angels returning?

answers.summary: Dennis connects the warning about angels in Corinthians, Satan’s expulsion in Revelation, and Christ’s comparison with Noah’s days. He interprets these as a future recurrence of Genesis 6.

questions.question: Which passages did Dennis give against lying?

answers.summary: Dennis points to Proverbs’ list of things God hates, including a lying tongue, and to Jesus’ description of the devil as a liar and father of lies.

questions.question: Which passages did Dennis give for covering a multitude of sins?

answers.summary: Dennis cites turning a sinner from error in James5 and love covering sins in1Peter4. He distinguishes the wording from the listener’s recollection about good works.

questions.question: Which passages did Dennis give for his belief that the soul is present at conception?

answers.summary: Dennis cites John the Baptist responding in Elizabeth’s womb and God knowing Jeremiah before birth as support for his belief.

questions.question: Which passages did Dennis recommend for anxiety?

answers.summary: Dennis points to Jesus’ teaching about God caring for birds and his people, and to the assurance of help to endure temptation.

questions.question: Which passages did Dennis recommend for maintaining faith during hardship?

answers.summary: Dennis recommends Hebrews 11, the promise of strength to face temptation in 1 Corinthians 10:13, and Romans 10:17 on faith growing through hearing God’s word.

questions.question: Which passages did Dennis recommend for signs preceding Christ’s return?

answers.summary: Dennis directed the listener to Matthew 24 and Mark 13 and recommended studying those chapters rather than giving a new date or list of contemporary predictions.

questions.question: Which passages did Dennis suggest discussing with a believer in the rapture?

answers.summary: Dennis points to Ezekiel 13 and the gospel armor in Ephesians 6 as starting points for discussion.

questions.question: Which passages did Dennis use to identify sons of God as angels?

answers.summary: Dennis points to the gathering with God in Job 1:6 and to the sons of God in Genesis 6, whom he identifies as fallen angels.

questions.question: Which peoples did Dennis place in the sixth-day creation?

answers.summary: Dennis places all peoples there except the man Adam whom he distinguishes in Genesis 2. This is his interpretation of the creation accounts.

questions.question: Which Pilgrim documentary did Dennis identify for a listener?

answers.summary: Dennis identifies the historical Chapel offering as Faith of Our Fathers by E.Raymond Capt. Availability and donation amounts in this old broadcast are not current confirmations.

questions.question: Which prophet did Dennis identify when asked about John 1:25?

answers.summary: Dennis points back to John 1:23 and identifies Isaiah. This records his answer without harmonizing the listener’s verse reference.

questions.question: Which Scripture did Arnold offer a listener concerned about distance from a disruptive relative?

answers.summary: Arnold refers to 2 Thessalonians 3:6 onward and reassures the listener. The saved question does not specify every action she has taken, so the answer is not generalized into approval of an unstated behavior.

questions.question: Which Strong’s Concordance edition did Arnold recommend in this broadcast?

answers.summary: Arnold recommended the version carried by the ministry and alleged fewer numbering errors than some other editions. He did not name a publisher or edition in this answer, and the reply does not establish current stock or comparative accuracy.

questions.question: Which Strong’s entry did Dennis give for ruach?

answers.summary: Dennis gives Hebrew entry 7307 and explains ruach in terms of wind, breath and spirit, using Holy Ruach to refer to God’s Spirit.

questions.question: Which Strong’s number did Arnold give for again in Hebrew?

answers.summary: Arnold gives 3254 and connects the word with continuing in his explanation of Genesis 4.

questions.question: Which study Bible did Arnold recommend for Hebrew and Greek help?

answers.summary: Arnold recommends the Companion Bible as an aid to studying the Hebrew and Greek behind the English text.

questions.question: Which study did Dennis recommend for comforting older Christians about death?

answers.summary: In this recording Dennis recommends the ministry study Where Are the Dead?, numbered 30475, saying listeners often find its teaching comforting. Availability has not been checked.

questions.question: Which things did Dennis list as hated by God in Proverbs6?

answers.summary: Dennis lists pride, lying, shedding innocent blood, devising evil, running to mischief, false witness and sowing discord, emphasizing division among brethren.

questions.question: Which tribe did Dennis identify as Samson’s?

answers.summary: Dennis identified Samson as a Danite through his father Manoah and directed the listener to Judges 13. The captioned question’s reference to Africa is uncertain; his answer clearly identifies the tribe of Dan.

questions.question: Which tribes did Arnold associate with Jesus’ ancestry?

answers.summary: Arnold described Jesus as having Judah’s royal line and Levi’s priestly line through his interpretation of Mary’s family. He referred to Luke 1 and connected the combination with Melchizedek.

questions.question: Which tribe’s standard did Dennis associate with Virgo?

answers.summary: Dennis points to Bullinger’s Companion Bible note on Numbers 2:7 and says it associates Virgo with the standard of Zebulun.

questions.question: Which trumpet did Arnold say his audience was in?

answers.summary: Arnold says the fifth trumpet was a time of learning, including learning to identify the antichrist.

questions.question: Which trumpet did Dennis say his audience was awaiting?

answers.summary: Dennis says they are in the fifth trumpet, awaiting Antichrist at the sixth, followed by Christ’s return at the seventh. This records his teaching at the time of the broadcast.

questions.question: Which two tribes did Dennis identify with Judah after the kingdom divided?

answers.summary: Dennis identifies Judah and Benjamin as the southern kingdom and the other ten tribes as the northern kingdom, dating the division to Rehoboam.

questions.question: Which verse did Arnold recommend when a change of heart feels difficult?

answers.summary: Arnold recommended 1 Corinthians 10:13 for reassurance about enduring trials and finding a way out. A nearby captioned sentence about never testing is incomplete, so it is not presented as a direct quotation or an unlimited promise.

questions.question: Which verse did Arnold suggest for a listener’s question about claiming to be without sin?

answers.summary: Arnold tentatively suggested 1 John 1:8. The listener’s captioned wording refers to not lying, so his suggested reference is recorded as tentative rather than silently rewriting the question.

questions.question: Which verse did Dennis cite about failing to support one’s family?

answers.summary: Dennis points to1Timothy5:8 and applies it to parents who refuse to provide for their household. His answer concerns unwillingness to provide.

questions.question: Which women prophets did Arnold recommend studying?

answers.summary: Arnold named Huldah and Deborah and suggested looking up prophetess in Strong’s Concordance. He cited 2 Kings 22:14. His later identification of the father of four prophesying daughters is uncertain in the captions and is not corrected or endorsed here.

questions.question: Who are the 144,000 sealed, and will they reign with Christ?

answers.summary: Dennis identifies twelve thousand from each tribe, describes the seal as God’s word in their minds, and connects their protection and reign with Revelation 9 and 20.

questions.question: Who are the dead in Ezekiel 44:25 in Dennis’s interpretation?

answers.summary: Dennis reads the section as millennium teaching about spiritually dead people, not flesh corpses. He distinguishes them from participants in the first resurrection over whom the second death has no power.

questions.question: Who are the Kenites, and are they all condemned?

answers.summary: Dennis identifies Kenites with descendants of Cain, says they are not black people as a group, and says a Kenite who accepts Christ is not automatically condemned.

questions.question: Who baptized Jesus?

answers.summary: Dennis identifies John the Baptist and recalls John’s initial reluctance, the Spirit descending like a dove and the heavenly declaration about the Son.

questions.question: Who besides the very elect did Arnold expect to overcome Antichrist?

answers.summary: Arnold said the listener had omitted the 144,000, whom he expected to recognize fulfilled prophecy after hearing the elect’s testimony. He also included kings and queens of the ethnic peoples who would overcome.

Arnold answered no, referring to kings and queens of the ethnic peoples and to Revelation 7’s innumerable group washed in the Lamb’s blood. He distinguished people already in heaven before Antichrist’s earthly deception.

questions.question: Who can help family members during the millennium?

answers.summary: Dennis says the Zadok serving Christ in the millennial temple may go to immediate family members to help them. He distinguishes this from the presently uncrossable gulf and says returning to the temple involves a seven-day cleansing after contact with the spiritually dead.

questions.question: Who did Arnold credit for his understanding of the Bible?

answers.summary: Arnold credited years of study and research together with the Holy Spirit. He did not name a particular human teacher in this brief answer.

questions.question: Who did Arnold credit with assembling the Companion Bible?

answers.summary: Arnold distinguishes God and the biblical writers from Bullinger’s editorial and study work. He praises the outlines and language helps. Biographical details he recalls, including a death year, are not independently verified and remain excluded as precise historical facts.

questions.question: Who did Arnold identify as the Comforter, and did he say it is present now?

answers.summary: Arnold identifies the Comforter as the Holy Spirit promised by Christ and received at Pentecost. He describes its help through Scripture, understanding and doing God’s work.

questions.question: Who did Arnold identify as the main writer of Psalms?

answers.summary: Arnold says David wrote most of Psalms.

questions.question: Who did Arnold identify as the writer of Revelation?

answers.summary: Arnold distinguishes God as the source of Scripture from John as the scribe. He identifies John on Patmos as the person who recorded Revelation and associates him with the epistles of John.

questions.question: Who did Arnold say Cain feared after leaving Eden?

answers.summary: Arnold identifies them with peoples he reads as a sixth-day creation and relates the answer to Cain’s wife. This is his ancestry interpretation rather than established population history.

questions.question: Who did Arnold say can approach God or Christ in the millennium?

answers.summary: Arnold distinguishes approaching Christ during the millennium from approaching the Father afterward. He refers to Ezekiel 44 and the role of the elect as priests. Part of the listener’s wording is unclear even to the speaker.

questions.question: Who did Arnold say fights the final battles?

answers.summary: Arnold identifies the final battles with Hamon-Gog and Armageddon and says God fights them. His political and national associations remain prophetic interpretations rather than established present-day identities.

questions.question: Who did Arnold say God addressed in let us make man in our image?

answers.summary: Arnold says God addressed his children and connects the passage with his teaching about the first earth age.

questions.question: Who did Arnold say receives strong delusion in 2 Thessalonians 2?

answers.summary: Arnold applies the passage to people accepting the false Christ after rejecting the warning that the antichrist comes first. He connects it with the sixth and seventh trumpets and says ignorance does not make that worship acceptable.

questions.question: Who did Dennis identify as bridegroom and bride in Matthew 25?

answers.summary: Dennis identifies Christ as the bridegroom and the prepared virgins as the bride, interpreting sufficient oil as truth that prevents deception.

questions.question: Who did Dennis identify as he in Second Thessalonians 2:7?

answers.summary: Dennis identifies him as Satan, held in heaven by Michael until being cast out. He bases his reading on the connection to the previous verse and Revelation’s war in heaven.

questions.question: Who did Dennis identify as Israel’s twelve patriarchs?

answers.summary: Dennis identified the patriarchs as Jacob’s twelve sons and the fathers of Israel’s tribes, directing the listener to the blessings in Genesis 49.

questions.question: Who did Dennis identify as Nahum?

answers.summary: Dennis identified Nahum as the seventh minor prophet and associated his prophecy with Nineveh’s downfall.

questions.question: Who did Dennis identify as Noah’s father?

answers.summary: Dennis identifies Lamech in Genesis 5 and distinguishes him from the Lamech in Genesis 4.

questions.question: Who did Dennis identify as prophets for the final generation?

answers.summary: Dennis identifies the two witnesses of Revelation 11. He relates their role to the olive branches in Zechariah 4, interpreting their oil as truth supplied to God’s elect.

questions.question: Who did Dennis identify as selling his birthright for food?

answers.summary: Dennis corrects the listener’s Isaiah reference to Esau, who sold his birthright to Jacob. He emphasizes Esau’s disregard for the inheritance in his explanation.

questions.question: Who did Dennis identify as the elect lady in 2 John?

answers.summary: Dennis interprets the elect lady as Mother Israel.

questions.question: Who did Dennis identify as the rest of the dead in Revelation 20?

answers.summary: Dennis interpreted the rest of the dead as people outside the first resurrection who had worshiped antichrist. He distinguished a spiritual body from a soul still liable to die and said the second death has no power over those in the first resurrection.

questions.question: Who did Dennis identify as the speakers in Psalm 91:15?

answers.summary: Dennis reads the verse as Christ calling upon the Lord and being delivered, then connects its trouble-and-deliverance theme with future deliverance of believers.

questions.question: Who did Dennis identify as us in let us make man in our image?

answers.summary: Dennis identifies the angels, emphasizing that God is not alone and created souls for His pleasure.

questions.question: Who did Dennis say brought death to Egypt’s firstborn?

answers.summary: Dennis points to the Lord speaking in Exodus 11 and identifies the Lord himself as the one acting.

questions.question: Who did Dennis say cursed Canaan?

answers.summary: Dennis says Noah cursed Canaan and explains the passage using his interpretation of uncovering a father’s nakedness.

questions.question: Who did Dennis say God addressed when saying let us make man in our image?

answers.summary: Dennis says God was speaking to the angels and points to the sons of God in Job 1.

questions.question: Who did Dennis say would teach and learn during the millennium?

answers.summary: Dennis said those who overcome antichrist would reign with Christ and teach others. He described the students as people who had not had an opportunity to hear truth before Christ’s return at the seventh trumpet.

questions.question: Who did Dennis say wrote Psalm 55, and what is a maskil?

answers.summary: Dennis attributes it to David and explains maskil as instruction, describing the psalm as instruction concerning enemies.

questions.question: Who did God divorce?

answers.summary: Dennis explains: the pastor references Jeremiah 3:8, explaining that God divorced Israel because she, like Judah, was committing adultery symbolically through idolatry, worshiping other gods than the Heavenly Father, but God will take her back and make things right.

questions.question: Who does Dennis think was the young man who fled in Mark 14?

answers.summary: Dennis gives John Mark as his opinion and notes that others identify Lazarus.

questions.question: Who does the man without a wedding garment represent?

answers.summary: Dennis interprets him as representing those spiritually unprepared for Christ’s return, placing the scene at the beginning of the Millennium.

questions.question: Who is Core in Jude?

answers.summary: Dennis identifies Core as the Greek form of Korah in Numbers, a relative of Moses and Aaron who led a rebellion and was swallowed by the earth with his followers.

questions.question: Who is entitled to take communion?

answers.summary: Dennis says the Chapel allows anyone who wishes to participate in communion rather than requiring personal worthiness.

questions.question: Who is God referring to when he says 'us' in Genesis 11:7?

answers.summary: Dennis interprets us in Genesis 11:7 and 1:26 as God addressing his children, the angels.

questions.question: Who is the woman in the wilderness in Revelation 12?

answers.summary: Dennis identifies her with Israel and more specifically God’s elect, persecuted when Satan is cast out.

questions.question: Who traded his birthright for red pottage, according to Dennis?

answers.summary: Dennis identifies Esau trading to Jacob and interprets Esau’s disregard as consistent with his first-age explanation of God’s hatred of Esau.

questions.question: Who was Joseph in God’s plan?

answers.summary: Dennis identifies Joseph as a patriarch whose sons Ephraim and Manasseh each headed a tribe, giving him a double portion. He calls Joseph a type of Christ as deliverer because his position in Egypt preserved Israel from famine.

questions.question: Who was the woman that cast a piece of millstone on Abimelech's head and broke his skull wide open?

answers.summary: Pastor Dennis Murray says her name is not written, but she cracked Abimelech's head open like an egg. He ordered his servant to kill him to avoid being remembered as killed by a woman.

questions.question: Who will stand before Antichrist if people are raptured away?

answers.summary: Dennis rejects the premise that God’s elect fly away, teaching that they stand equipped with the gospel armor.

questions.question: Who wrote Ecclesiastes?

answers.summary: Dennis identifies the writer as David’s son Solomon, whom he also identifies as the writer of Proverbs and Song of Solomon. He connects Solomon’s wisdom with his request to God for wisdom to govern Israel.

questions.question: Who wrote the Apocrypha?

answers.summary: Dennis says it contains writings attributed to different people, giving Ezra and Manasseh as examples. He distinguishes editions and recommends the Goodspeed translation.

questions.question: Who wrote the Massorah?

answers.summary: Dennis distinguishes biblical authorship from the Massorah, which he describes as a priestly system of copying checks and symbols intended to detect alterations to the text.

questions.question: Whom did Arnold identify as the nations’ kings and queens?

answers.summary: Arnold interpreted the nations in Revelation 21 as gentile or ethnic peoples with their own leaders. He compared those leaders with the elect and said their people would listen to teachers from among them.

questions.question: Whom did Arnold identify as the witnesses of Isaiah 43:10?

answers.summary: Arnold applied the verse particularly to God’s elect. He also directed the listener to Isaiah 43:26 and encouraged prayer about God’s promises and study to understand them.

questions.question: Whom did Arnold mean by ethnos?

answers.summary: Arnold described ethnos as peoples outside the ten tribes in his interpretation and stressed that it was an honorable designation. He appealed to the nations being present in the concluding vision of Revelation. This is his definition and application in this answer.

questions.question: Whom did Dennis expect to accompany antichrist?

answers.summary: Dennis says fallen angels and the locust army would accompany him in his interpretation.

questions.question: Whom did Dennis expect to return with Christ?

answers.summary: Dennis says the army returning with Christ would be from the right side of the gulf, referring to Luke 16 and Revelation 19.

questions.question: Whom did Dennis hold responsible for evil?

answers.summary: Dennis places much responsibility on Satan but also says human beings contribute through their own actions; he rejects blaming God as the origin of evil.

questions.question: Whom did Dennis identify as God’s chosen people?

answers.summary: Dennis answers Israel from Deuteronomy 7:6 and explicitly says this does not mean God does not love His other children.

questions.question: Whom did Dennis identify as his and Arnold’s mentors?

answers.summary: Dennis named Arnold Murray as his mentor and Roy Gillespie as Arnold’s mentor. This is biographical attribution only; no teaching from Gillespie is introduced here.

questions.question: Whom did Dennis identify as the author of Hebrews?

answers.summary: Dennis answers by reading his Bible’s heading attributing Hebrews to Paul; he gives no further authorship argument in this answer.

questions.question: Whom did Dennis identify as the beast that kills the two witnesses?

answers.summary: Dennis identifies it as antichrist. He distinguishes Revelation 13’s political system from antichrist and connects the system and false prophet with the lake of fire in Revelation 19.

questions.question: Whom did Dennis identify as the bride of Christ?

answers.summary: Dennis identifies the bride with those who remain spiritually faithful to Christ and do not worship the antichrist.

questions.question: Whom did Dennis identify as the eight souls on Noah’s ark?

answers.summary: Dennis names Noah, his wife, their three sons and their wives, and distinguishes those eight from his interpretation of other flesh on the ark.

questions.question: Whom did Dennis identify as the idol shepherd in Zechariah11:17?

answers.summary: Dennis identifies the figure as antichrist.

questions.question: Whom did Dennis identify as the Queen of the South?

answers.summary: Dennis identifies her with the Queen of Sheba who visited Solomon, exchanged gifts and returned home.

questions.question: Whom did Dennis identify as the woman bearing the male child in Revelation12?

answers.summary: Dennis identifies her as Eve rather than Babylon and interprets the scene through the line leading to Messiah. He describes Satan’s attempts to destroy that line and the chapter as spanning multiple ages.

questions.question: Whom did Dennis list as named by God before birth?

answers.summary: Dennis lists Ishmael, Isaac, Solomon, Josiah, Cyrus, John the Baptist and Jesus and gives passages for each.

questions.question: Whom did Dennis say God addressed in let us make man in our image?

answers.summary: Dennis says God addressed angels rather than the humans about to be created, and connects the image language with resemblance between humans, angels and God.

questions.question: Whom did Dennis say Jacob encountered while wrestling?

answers.summary: Dennis identifies the figure as the angel of the Lord, relates it to Jacob naming Peniel and recommends his Worthy message covering Genesis32.

questions.question: Whom did Dennis suggest as the other disciple in John 18:15?

answers.summary: Dennis rejects the listener’s suggestion of Judas and offers Nicodemus or Joseph of Arimathea as possibilities because of their connection with the high priest. He states this as his view.

questions.question: Whom does he refer to in Mark 3:30, and how does Dennis relate this to blasphemy?

answers.summary: Dennis says the scribes were accusing Jesus of having an unclean spirit, though Jesus had the Holy Spirit. He relates the episode to the divided-house teaching and directs the listener to Luke 12 for his unforgivable-sin explanation.

questions.question: Whose blood does Dennis identify on Christ’s vesture in Revelation 19?

answers.summary: Dennis interprets the blood as that of the enemy and emphasizes Christ’s return as a conquering figure.

questions.question: Whose word is meant when the word of the LORD came to someone?

answers.summary: Dennis identifies uppercase LORD in that Old Testament formula with Yahweh, and answers that it is Yahweh’s word.

questions.question: Why accept Christ if everyone receives a spiritual body at His return?

answers.summary: Dennis distinguishes receiving a spiritual body from receiving immortality. He says those in the first resurrection are beyond the second death, whereas others remain liable to the death of the soul and await judgment.

questions.question: Why are the Chapel teachers confident about what they teach?

answers.summary: Dennis attributes their confidence to study, reliance on God’s word rather than human traditions, and the Holy Spirit.

questions.question: Why call Jesus wept the shortest verse when Rejoice evermore also has two words?

answers.summary: Dennis agrees both have two words, but says Jesus wept has fewer letters.

questions.question: Why can we teach Revelation from Zechariah 14?

answers.summary: Dennis says Zechariah 14 and Revelation describe the same prophetic events rather than placing Zechariah later in the Bible.

questions.question: Why did Arnold ask listeners to submit only one or two broadcast questions at a time?

answers.summary: Arnold said a letter requiring more questions than could fit in a session might be set aside to avoid taking up the whole program. He recommended resubmitting a short letter or calling and explained that he did not have time to answer individually by mail. This describes that broadcast’s format.

questions.question: Why did Arnold call David a man after God’s own heart?

answers.summary: Arnold emphasizes David’s courage, experience protecting sheep, reliance on God against Goliath and the messianic lineage.

questions.question: Why did Arnold divide his five-month period into two halves?

answers.summary: Arnold connected Revelation’s symbolic hour with five months and its half-hour silence with half of that interval. He consequently described two periods of two and a half months. This records his prophetic interpretation.

questions.question: Why did Arnold emphasize asking in Christ’s name?

answers.summary: Arnold distinguished titles and different forms of the name from the importance of approaching the Father through Christ. He treated this as an expression of belief rather than resolving the question by counting the seventeen occurrences mentioned by the listener.

questions.question: Why did Arnold encourage water baptism?

answers.summary: Arnold says Christ set an example through water baptism. He distinguishes the outward act from Christ’s forgiveness of sins.

questions.question: Why did Arnold interpret Ezekiel 28 as referring to Satan?

answers.summary: Arnold emphasizes the protecting cherub, the language of creation and the judgment in Ezekiel 28:18–19. He relates that description to Satan and the son of perdition. This reports his reading of the passage.

questions.question: Why did Arnold recommend dedication rather than baptism for a baby?

answers.summary: Arnold recommended parents dedicating the child and themselves to Christian care. He described baptism as a choice a baby cannot make and pointed to Jesus being baptized as an adult. The captioned oil phrase is unclear and is not silently reconstructed.

questions.question: Why did Arnold reject a rapture before tribulation?

answers.summary: Arnold points to Ezekiel 13 and 2 Thessalonians 2 and says the false Christ comes first while believers have work to do.

questions.question: Why did Arnold reject the rapture teaching?

answers.summary: Arnold points to Ezekiel 13 and explains 1 Thessalonians 4 as referring to believers already risen with Christ, distinguishing the sixth and seventh trumpets.

questions.question: Why did Arnold say Abram fought the king who had defeated other enemies?

answers.summary: Arnold said earlier helpful actions did not excuse the later taking of Lot and other captives and possessions. He applied the story to the danger of doing useful things while also violating God’s commands; some names and family terms in the captions are unclear.

questions.question: Why did Arnold say Cain’s offering was not accepted?

answers.summary: Arnold assumes it was not firstfruits and adds his Cain-parentage interpretation. The assumption and theological claim are not presented as an independently established explanation.

questions.question: Why did Arnold say David used the words My God, why hast thou forsaken me?

answers.summary: Arnold says Psalm 22 reflects David’s own distress and then becomes prophecy through the Holy Spirit.

questions.question: Why did Arnold say doing right can remain difficult after accepting Christ?

answers.summary: Arnold described opposition after turning away from Satan and urged confidence in Christ’s power. He also advised leaving friendships that keep drawing the believer into bad habits rather than repeatedly forcing an unreceived message.

questions.question: Why did Arnold say Egypt repeatedly featured in the biblical accounts named by a listener?

answers.summary: Arnold described Egypt as used in God’s purposes and as a place of safety for Jesus’ family under threat. A named servant is inaudible in the captions. His additional prediction and historical claim about Egypt’s continuous nationhood are attributed, not independently verified.

questions.question: Why did Arnold say Elijah was taken without dying?

answers.summary: Arnold briefly agrees with the listener that this relates to Elijah returning in the end times. He does not give a separate supporting reference in that short answer.

questions.question: Why did Arnold say Enoch was taken by God?

answers.summary: Arnold affirmed transfiguration and associated Enoch’s being taken with preaching against fallen angels. He appealed to Genesis and Jude within that interpretation.

questions.question: Why did Arnold say false teachers are able to continue?

answers.summary: Arnold places responsibility on people who teach or follow human traditions rather than Scripture. He connects the existence of false teaching with free will, personal accountability and God’s provision of Scripture for testing what is taught.

questions.question: Why did Arnold say fellowship with like-minded believers can feel spiritually stronger?

answers.summary: Arnold described believers’ shared love of God’s word as minds and spirits meshing, connected it with Christ’s presence among those gathered and anticipated continued fellowship in eternity.

questions.question: Why did Arnold say God hardened Pharaoh’s heart?

answers.summary: Arnold said the events would reveal the living God rather than the various gods people worshipped. He emphasized God’s care for Egyptian people as well, though the wording of his recalled Exodus 7:5 explanation shifts between peoples.

questions.question: Why did Arnold say God has not destroyed Satan already?

answers.summary: Arnold says Satan is being used to test whom people love and says Satan’s judgment will be fulfilled after that purpose ends.

questions.question: Why did Arnold say God made humans?

answers.summary: Arnold connects human life with his teaching on Satan’s rebellion, the prior age and a chance to choose whom to follow.

questions.question: Why did Arnold say God should be the judge?

answers.summary: Arnold said God knows people’s thoughts and cannot be deceived, so he can judge accurately. He contrasted that with human courts’ ability to make mistakes. He did not separately develop the child’s second question about why Satan impersonates God.

questions.question: Why did Arnold say God still allows Satan to live?

answers.summary: Arnold described Satan’s continued existence as a test of people’s fidelity, using Job as an example. He said God gives believers power to resist and emphasized discipline and love for God and others.

questions.question: Why did Arnold say Jesus rose in his body?

answers.summary: Arnold connects the bodily resurrection and transfiguration with demonstrating the resurrection to unbelievers.

questions.question: Why did Arnold say Jesus was baptized despite being without sin?

answers.summary: Arnold says Jesus was showing people the way and setting the example.

questions.question: Why did Arnold say Jesus was crucified rather than Moses?

answers.summary: Arnold referred to Hebrews 2:14 and said Christ entered flesh and died to destroy death, which he identified with the devil.

questions.question: Why did Arnold say Job received blessing again at the end?

answers.summary: Arnold said Job continued serving God and had done nothing to make him ineligible for renewed blessing. He emphasized Job’s patience and the lesson not to accept his friends’ uninformed accusations as God’s teaching.

questions.question: Why did Arnold say Judas had to identify Jesus?

answers.summary: Arnold says it was dark and the captors did not know where Jesus was; Judas led them there and identified him with a kiss.

questions.question: Why did Arnold say Matthew 24:22 speaks of flesh being saved?

answers.summary: Arnold said people were still in flesh bodies and interpreted the shortened days as protection from a convincing false Christ. He contrasted the shortened period with seven years and said he expected the elect to withstand deception. These are his prophetic interpretations.

questions.question: Why did Arnold say Matthew gives Joseph’s genealogy for Jesus?

answers.summary: Arnold explains it through adoption and contrasts Matthew with his reading of Mary’s line in Luke 3. His royal and priestly ancestry conclusions remain his interpretation.

questions.question: Why did Arnold say olive oil was chosen for anointing?

answers.summary: Arnold associated the choice with his belief that olive oil was pure and beneficial to the body. His broad claims comparing fats and oils are not independently verified medical conclusions.

questions.question: Why did Arnold say people enter flesh life after his first earth age?

answers.summary: Arnold said this life lets people choose whether to love God or Satan. He believed some elect volunteered to teach truth, but time ran out before he provided the requested biblical documentation.

questions.question: Why did Arnold say Revelation 12 uses several names for Satan?

answers.summary: Arnold says Revelation 12 uses several names for Satan and relates each name to the role he is playing, such as the serpent in the garden.

questions.question: Why did Arnold say Revelation’s chapters and seals are not simply chronological?

answers.summary: Arnold described seals as truths to understand, trumpets as commands executed and vials as wrath. He interpreted the first white-horse rider as antichrist and made a cheap-fabric bow claim. These are his lexical and prophetic interpretations, not independently verified dictionary meanings.

questions.question: Why did Arnold say Satan cannot postpone God’s plan indefinitely?

answers.summary: Arnold said Satan cannot choose to remain in heaven indefinitely and will be cast out when Michael acts. He also described Satan’s pride as sustaining his belief that he can change the outcome. One restraint phrase is inconsistent in the captions and needs audio checking; no exact release date is established here.

questions.question: Why did Arnold say Satan was jealous of God?
