answers.summary: Arnold briefly answers that Satan thought himself better than God. Time runs out before he separately develops why many angels followed him.

questions.question: Why did Arnold say Satan would still try to deceive the elect?

answers.summary: Arnold said Satan believes he is capable of winning even the elect. He warned the listener not to underestimate Satan’s deceptive appeal rather than assuming he would avoid those who recognize him.

questions.question: Why did Arnold say seeing the Son means seeing the Father?

answers.summary: Arnold cites Christ’s statement in John 14:9.

questions.question: Why did Arnold say some listeners were only recently hearing his Kenite teaching?

answers.summary: Arnold attributed that to lack of teachers and scholars and connected it with his interpretation of Revelation’s approved churches. His accusations about ancestry and religious groups are unverified doctrinal claims and do not establish modern people’s lineage.

questions.question: Why did Arnold say the Companion Bible does not print Christ’s words in red?

answers.summary: Arnold said it simply is not a red-letter edition. He recommended following the subject and speaker through its outlines and using a separate red-letter KJV if helpful.

questions.question: Why did Arnold say the rich man addressed Abraham rather than God?

answers.summary: Arnold said Abraham was the person the rich man saw embracing Lazarus across the gulf, so Abraham was the one he addressed. He connected Abraham with blessing many peoples.

questions.question: Why did Arnold say the two witnesses must die?

answers.summary: Arnold reasoned that the witnesses had not previously died and associated them with Elijah and Moses. He explicitly framed part of this as an assumption based on the transfiguration and said their resurrection would document Christ’s arrival.

questions.question: Why did Dennis avoid showing the congregation on television?

answers.summary: Dennis says he respects congregants’ privacy, does not want clothing or camera concerns distracting them and wants viewers focused on Scripture.

questions.question: Why did Dennis believe Cain and Abel were twins?

answers.summary: Dennis interprets the word again in Genesis 4:2 as continued labor and says the brothers had different fathers.

questions.question: Why did Dennis call Psalm 37:7,20,34 triplets?

answers.summary: Dennis says their three-line Hebrew form sets them apart from four-line verses. He uses them to emphasize that the wicked do not ultimately prevail.

questions.question: Why did Dennis describe Paul’s conversion as compelled?

answers.summary: Dennis distinguishes free choice from his interpretation of being chosen before the foundation of the world. He regards Paul’s Damascus-road encounter and commission as an example of God directing a chosen vessel.

questions.question: Why did Dennis distinguish David’s flight from Saul from fighting Goliath?

answers.summary: Dennis says Goliath was an enemy, whereas David remained loyal to Saul as God’s anointed. David therefore fled rather than kill Saul.

questions.question: Why did Dennis exclude catfish from permitted food?

answers.summary: Dennis applies the requirement that aquatic food have both fins and scales. He notes that catfish lack scales and describes them as scavengers.

questions.question: Why did Dennis favor advance healthcare directives?

answers.summary: Dennis says communicating wishes beforehand can spare loved ones uncertainty if a person later becomes unable to speak for themselves.

questions.question: Why did Dennis favor the KJV over the NIV in this answer?

answers.summary: Dennis says the ministry did not offer the NIV and primarily taught from the KJV because it works with Strong’s for original-language study. He acknowledges using additional translations too.
Dennis refers back to his earlier explanation about using it with Strong’s Concordance to investigate original-language words.

questions.question: Why did Dennis mention both 1948 and 1967 in discussing the fig tree?

answers.summary: Dennis prefers 1948 in his interpretation but allows 1967 as a possibility and identifies the latter with the Six-Day War. He does not present the interpretation as certain.

questions.question: Why did Dennis Murray become a preacher?

answers.summary: Dennis says he admired his father and wanted to follow his example.

questions.question: Why did Dennis offer Biblical Mathematics despite disagreeing with its rapture teaching?

answers.summary: Dennis considers Ed Vallowe’s work useful for biblical numerics while rejecting its rapture teaching. He urges readers to distinguish useful material from claims they believe conflict with Scripture.

questions.question: Why did Dennis pray over one stack of papers and read questions from another?

answers.summary: Dennis explains that one stack contains prayer requests and the other contains questions submitted for on-air answers.

questions.question: Why did Dennis prefer silver to gold for barter in this answer?

answers.summary: Dennis relates precious metals to his teaching about refusing the antichrist’s currency and prefers silver for smaller exchanges. This records his historical view, not investment advice or a guarantee of value.

questions.question: Why did Dennis recommend Appendix 45 for different lists of Israel’s tribes?

answers.summary: Dennis recommends Companion Bible Appendix 45 for the differing lists of Israel’s tribes and the reasons particular tribes are omitted or included.

questions.question: Why did Dennis recommend baptism, and did he require repeating it after every sin?

answers.summary: Dennis points to Jesus’ example and Peter’s instruction to be baptized, but says subsequent sins call for repentance rather than repeated baptism.

questions.question: Why did Dennis recommend olive oil for anointing?

answers.summary: Dennis refers to James 5:14 and explains the oil as olive oil, encouraging the listener to follow the instruction.

questions.question: Why did Dennis regard mushrooms as outside the permitted plant foods?

answers.summary: Dennis reasons from Genesis’ reference to seed-bearing herbs and distinguishes mushrooms, which reproduce by spores. This is his interpretation of the food passage.

questions.question: Why did Dennis say Abel is absent from the genealogy in Genesis 5?

answers.summary: Dennis says Abel died before having children, so there was no line of descendants to record.

questions.question: Why did Dennis say Abel was absent from Genesis 5?

answers.summary: Dennis says Abel had no children and that the genealogy follows the line through Seth leading to David and Christ.

questions.question: Why did Dennis say animal sacrifices ceased, and what feast did the chapel keep?

answers.summary: Dennis attributes the change to Christ’s sacrifice rather than the Ark’s location. He says the chapel keeps Passover without burnt offerings because Christ became its Passover.

questions.question: Why did Dennis say Christians should have one spouse today?

answers.summary: Dennis contrasts ancient population growth with the civil-law setting of his answer. He says Christians should obey the law and describes monogamy as the law in his country.

questions.question: Why did Dennis say Christmas is absent from Leviticus?

answers.summary: Dennis places Leviticus’s feast instructions before Christ’s conception and crucifixion, contrasting the old covenant with life under grace in Christ.

questions.question: Why did Dennis say dinosaurs were created?

answers.summary: Dennis says they were created for God’s pleasure, as he understands Revelation 4:11.

questions.question: Why did Dennis say early converts sold their possessions?

answers.summary: Dennis explains it as enabling travel to teach the Word at a time without modern broadcasting.

questions.question: Why did Dennis say God allowed an evil spirit upon Saul?

answers.summary: Dennis interprets it as creating a separation between Saul and the loyal David so David could become king. He emphasizes that David would not kill Saul because Saul had been God’s anointed.

questions.question: Why did Dennis say God allowed pregnancies in his interpretation of Genesis 6?

answers.summary: Dennis answers through free will, saying God did not make all people act identically and applies that reasoning to the women in the account.

questions.question: Why did Dennis say God allows evil?

answers.summary: Dennis emphasizes that most people have free will rather than being programmed to love God. He also points to the perilous times described in 2 Timothy 3, while distinguishing his teaching about the elect.

questions.question: Why did Dennis say God created people and the world?

answers.summary: Answering an eight-year-old, Dennis points to Revelation 4:11 and says creation is for God’s pleasure.

questions.question: Why did Dennis say God created the second earth age despite continuing evil?

answers.summary: Dennis describes it as an expression of God’s patience and desire for repentance rather than destroying the children who followed Satan in his first-age teaching.

questions.question: Why did Dennis say God did not create only obedient angels?

answers.summary: Dennis says God wanted freely chosen love rather than robotic compliance. He distinguishes this from the elect, whose prior loyalty he believes gives them a destined role in testimony against Antichrist.

questions.question: Why did Dennis say God gave people the Bible?

answers.summary: Dennis described it as instruction for how to live, follow God’s ways and receive his blessings.

questions.question: Why did Dennis say God hardened Pharaoh’s heart?

answers.summary: Dennis says God’s wonders were multiplied so the Israelites would recognize His authority.

questions.question: Why did Dennis say God let Adam name the animals?

answers.summary: Dennis says God placed Adam in charge of the garden and gave him the right to name them.

questions.question: Why did Dennis say God placed people in this flesh life?

answers.summary: Dennis relates it to his teaching of a prior rebellion, saying God gave His children an opportunity to choose allegiance and sent Christ as the way of salvation.

questions.question: Why did Dennis say God rejected Cain’s offering?

answers.summary: Dennis interprets Cain’s offering as lacking firstfruits and love, contrasting it with Abel’s firstlings and describing Cain’s subsequent anger and jealousy.

questions.question: Why did Dennis say God sent the flood?

answers.summary: Dennis relates the flood to his teaching about the fallen angels’ offspring and Satan’s attempt to obstruct the lineage of Christ.

questions.question: Why did Dennis say he could not personally take every telephone call?

answers.summary: Dennis says personal calls would consume the time needed to study and prepare broadcasts and services. He describes applying the same availability rule to all students.

questions.question: Why did Dennis say he was baptized?

answers.summary: Dennis says Jesus set the example. He also says a person need not be baptized again after every sin, but should repent.

questions.question: Why did Dennis say Jacob could win his wrestling encounter with God?

answers.summary: Dennis says God allowed Jacob to win. He connects the encounter with Genesis 32:28 and the new name Israel, explaining the victory as something God permitted to make a point.

questions.question: Why did Dennis say Jesus began His public ministry at about thirty?

answers.summary: Dennis attributes the timing to God’s plan rather than giving special significance to thirty or thirty-three. He also notes Jesus teaching in the temple as a child.

questions.question: Why did Dennis say Judah and Israel became separate?

answers.summary: Dennis attributes the split under Rehoboam to Solomon’s idolatry, distinguishes the ten tribes from Judah and Benjamin, and expects eventual reunion.

questions.question: Why did Dennis say Moses did not lead Israel into the promised land?

answers.summary: Dennis says Moses struck the rock and claimed a role in the miracle instead of obeying the command to speak and sanctify God. He identifies Joshua as the subsequent leader.

questions.question: Why did Dennis say our relationship with God depends on us?

answers.summary: Dennis says God remains the same while people change, and urges seeking rather than forsaking Him.

questions.question: Why did Dennis say people go to heaven before judgment on earth?

answers.summary: Dennis says the Lord is presently in heaven, so the departed are with Him there. He places the final throne and judgment on earth and interprets the dead before the throne as spiritually dead.

questions.question: Why did Dennis say Psalms 14 and 53 repeat similar words?

answers.summary: Dennis notes that their opening verses are very similar rather than entirely identical, attributes both to David, and says the wording suited the circumstances.

questions.question: Why did Dennis say Saint John when referring to the Gospel?

answers.summary: Dennis says it follows his KJV’s title and helps distinguish the Gospel from John’s epistles; he denies that the wording signals allegiance to a particular church.

questions.question: Why did Dennis say Satan is released after the millennium?

answers.summary: Dennis explains the release as a test of whether God’s children will follow God or the devil. He points to Revelation 20, calls Michael the binding angel as his belief, and says some will follow Satan into the lake of fire. He distinguishes Satan’s later power from his role as antichrist.

questions.question: Why did Dennis say Satan wanted a third to follow him in the first age?

answers.summary: Dennis says Satan wanted God’s children to worship him instead of God, interpreting the dragon and stars in Revelation 12 accordingly.

questions.question: Why did Dennis say Satan would be released on earth despite existing evil?

answers.summary: Dennis treats the event as part of a test of allegiance to God or Satan, relating it to his first-earth-age interpretation. He warns that he believes many will mistake antichrist for Christ.

questions.question: Why did Dennis say Solomon had Adonijah killed?

answers.summary: Dennis interprets Adonijah’s request to marry Abishag as a renewed claim to David’s throne after Solomon had initially spared him on condition of good conduct.

questions.question: Why did Dennis say some church teaching creates confusion?

answers.summary: Dennis attributes confusion in this answer to false teaching, especially the rapture doctrine. He contrasts humanly devised salvation schemes with salvation through Jesus Christ.

questions.question: Why did Dennis say some references to gods use a lowercase g?

answers.summary: Dennis says such references usually concern false gods or idols rather than the heavenly Father.

questions.question: Why did Dennis say Son is capitalized in Luke 15:31?

answers.summary: Dennis explains it as the first word of the sentence in the prodigal-son account, rather than a reference to the Son of God.

questions.question: Why did Dennis say spiritual bodies need clothing?

answers.summary: Dennis connects heavenly linen with righteous acts and says the robe covers nakedness. He encourages righteous works using that imagery.

questions.question: Why did Dennis say the 144,000 turn away from Antichrist?

answers.summary: Dennis says they begin to worship Antichrist but recognize truth when they hear the witness of the 7,000, whom he calls the very elect. He cites passages about those who did not bow to Baal.

questions.question: Why did Dennis say the angel casts the fiery censer to earth?

answers.summary: Dennis relates the action to answering the saints’ prayers and points back to the preceding verse for context.

questions.question: Why did Dennis say the broadcast schedule changed in this recording?

answers.summary: Dennis says he was well and attributes that recording’s changed schedule to technical difficulties; the answer concerns the historical broadcast.

questions.question: Why did Dennis say the disciples could not help the boy in Matthew 17?

answers.summary: Dennis emphasizes Jesus’ statement about their unbelief and the need for faith. He does not explain the fasting part of the listener’s question here.

questions.question: Why did Dennis say the elect would be unable to buy or sell?

answers.summary: Dennis says access to the antichrist’s currency would require worshiping him, which the elect would refuse. He also discusses keeping supplies for disruptions.

questions.question: Why did Dennis say the King James Bible often needs explanation?

answers.summary: Dennis discusses the age of the language and the role of teachers, while recommending the Authorized King James Version.

questions.question: Why did Dennis say the ministry celebrates December 25?

answers.summary: Dennis says they celebrate it as Christ’s conception, describing the Word becoming flesh as the reason for celebration.

questions.question: Why did Dennis say the prophet in 1 Kings 13 died?

answers.summary: Dennis says the prophet disobeyed God’s instruction after listening to another man and draws a lesson about following God’s word.

questions.question: Why did Dennis say the sinless Jesus was crucified?

answers.summary: Dennis says Jesus took the world’s sins and defeated death through crucifixion and resurrection, fulfilling his purpose in coming in flesh.

questions.question: Why did Dennis say the tree of knowledge was in the garden?

answers.summary: Dennis describes the instruction concerning the tree as a test of obedience.

questions.question: Why did Dennis say the witnesses’ bodies would be left in the open?

answers.summary: Dennis affirmed Christ’s resurrection and said the exposed bodies would prevent a claim that someone stole the witnesses’ bodies. He expected their rising to be seen and connected it with Christ’s return.

questions.question: Why did Dennis say unclean animals were used for transport?

answers.summary: Dennis distinguishes dietary status from usefulness as beasts of burden, describing asses and mules as animals used to carry loads.

questions.question: Why did Dennis say Uzzah was struck down while steadying the ark?

answers.summary: Dennis says the instructions for carrying the ark were already given in the law. He contrasts using poles and authorized bearers with copying the Philistines’ use of an ox cart.

questions.question: Why did Dennis sometimes consult the Moffatt translation?

answers.summary: Dennis says a different wording can help a difficult passage make sense while he is studying the King James Version. He particularly values Moffatt’s handling of pronouns and notes differences in chronological arrangement.

questions.question: Why did Dennis teach that Cain was Satan’s son?

answers.summary: Dennis interprets the events in Eden and the reference to conception as support for this teaching. He also points to the separate genealogies of Cain and Adam and describes Cain and Abel as twins with different fathers.

questions.question: Why did Dennis think a listener cried during prayer?

answers.summary: Dennis suggests love, humility or regret may cause tears, and says growing in one’s relationship with God can make prayer less emotionally overwhelming. He encourages forgiveness rather than remaining burdened by past sins.

questions.question: Why did Dennis think a listener cried while praying?

answers.summary: Dennis suggests it may reflect love and emotion toward God; he offers a guess, not a definite diagnosis of the experience.

questions.question: Why did Dennis think many churches did not teach the distinction between antichrist and Christ’s return?

answers.summary: Dennis says human traditions have displaced biblical teaching in many churches and relates that failure to the predicted deception and Christ’s criticism of churches in Revelation.

questions.question: Why did Dennis think Mary went to live with John rather than Joseph?

answers.summary: Dennis explicitly calls his belief that Joseph had died speculation, since it is not written. He also believes Mary could help John establish the church and distinguishes an offered historical book from the biblical text.

questions.question: Why did Dennis think other churches did not teach the ministry’s September-birth interpretation?

answers.summary: Dennis gives his opinion that teachers do not understand it; he does not establish the listener’s proposed commercial explanation involving Santa Claus.

questions.question: Why did Dennis think rapture believers might still accept antichrist despite not being raptured?

answers.summary: Dennis says expectations and apparent miracles could lead them to accept the impostor as Christ. He again interprets Thessalonians as describing deceased believers already with Christ.

questions.question: Why did Dennis think Revelation often goes untaught?

answers.summary: Dennis says some teachers mistakenly treat it as sealed and others do not understand it. He emphasizes that revelation means revealing.

questions.question: Why did Dennis think some people strongly hold to rapture teaching?

answers.summary: Dennis says he sees it as reassurance of escaping tribulation, which he rejects. He points to Christ returning to earth as his reason for expecting believers to remain.

questions.question: Why did Dennis think wise Solomon still took disapproved wives?

answers.summary: Dennis says the lesson is the weakness of flesh: wisdom does not make a person incapable of sin.

questions.question: Why did Father choose a serpent to raise on the pole for his children to worship?

answers.summary: Dennis says the raised serpent in Numbers 21 was not intended for worship and connects it with Christ being raised on the cross, while noting its later destruction when worshiped.

questions.question: Why did God destroy the families and relatives of those who worshipped the golden calf, even though they did not participate?

answers.summary: Dennis rejects the premise that Exodus 32 says innocent relatives were killed and quotes verse 33 about those who sinned. For the separate question about wartime bans, he refers to Deuteronomy 7:1–8 and interprets the destruction as preventing Israel from mixing with those peoples. This is an account of his reading, not a present-day instruction.

questions.question: Why did God need someone to protect the mercy seat?

answers.summary: Arnold explains the protecting cherub in terms of freely given love and the possibility of pride and rebellion, referring to Ezekiel 28.

questions.question: Why did Jesus have to die?

answers.summary: Dennis tells the young listener that Jesus came in flesh to defeat the devil’s power of death, connecting this with victory over death and the grave.

questions.question: Why did Jesus return to life when Abel did not?

answers.summary: Dennis says Jesus came to defeat the devil’s power of death. He explains that without Christ’s resurrection death would have prevailed and there would be no salvation or eternal life.

questions.question: Why did Jesus say get behind me Satan to Peter?

answers.summary: Dennis interprets Peter’s opposition to Christ’s announced death as interference with God’s plan. He says Jesus addressed Satan acting through Peter at that moment.

questions.question: Why did Jesus say My God, why hast thou forsaken me?

answers.summary: Dennis interprets the words as teaching from Psalm 22 and pointing to its crucifixion prophecy, not as God actually abandoning Jesus.

questions.question: Why did Jesus speak in parables?

answers.summary: Dennis says parables sometimes concealed meaning from the whole crowd while addressing disciples and the elect. He describes deeper meaning and notes that Jesus later explained some parables, including the sower in Matthew 13, to the disciples.

questions.question: Why did John the Baptist send two of his disciples to Jesus asking if he was the one who should come or if they should look for another?

answers.summary: Dennis interprets John the Baptist’s question as asking whether the kingdom would arrive then or await another advent.

questions.question: Why did Judah dwell in the land of the Kenites, and what is the city of palm trees?

answers.summary: Dennis identifies the city of palm trees as Jericho and says living in a place does not by itself establish sexual relations with its inhabitants.

questions.question: Why did Lamech speak to his wives about his killing and vengeance?

answers.summary: Dennis interprets the speech as Lamech boasting about the killing, rather than establishing a separate divine promise.

questions.question: Why do Deuteronomy 12 and 14 seem to differ about clean and unclean?

answers.summary: Dennis says clean and unclean in Deuteronomy 12:15 refer to the person eating, not to different kinds of food. He uses that distinction to explain the apparent inconsistency.

questions.question: Why do translations say doctors or teachers in Luke 2:46?

answers.summary: Dennis explains that the Greek didaskalos can be rendered doctor, master or teacher, so he does not regard that wording difference as a substantive disagreement.

questions.question: Why do you always say if you have eyes to see and ears to hear?

answers.summary: Pastor Arnold Murray explains that having eyes to see and ears to hear refers to spiritual perception, not physical ability, emphasizing that many spiritually blind and deaf people have their spiritual eyes wide open.

questions.question: Why do you preach the moon is bad when it lights up the night sky?

answers.summary: Dennis denies teaching that the moon itself is bad and distinguishes his interpretation of solar and lunar prophetic time periods.

questions.question: Why does 1 Corinthians 14 mention interpretation if Acts 2 was understood by everyone?

answers.summary: Dennis interprets Corinthians as foreign languages requiring translation for listeners who do not know them. He contrasts the cloven tongue of Acts 2, understood by all, and associates that with the elect’s future testimony.

questions.question: Why does Dennis teach an earth older than six thousand years?

answers.summary: Dennis notes that Genesis says in the beginning without giving that age, and interprets the earth becoming void in connection with his teaching of successive earth ages.

questions.question: Why does Exodus 17 say Moses should strike the rock, but Numbers 20 say he should speak to the rock?

answers.summary: Dennis distinguishes Exodus 17 and Numbers 20 as separate events. He says Moses obeyed the command to strike the rock in the first and went wrong in the second when commanded to speak to it, speaking as though God needed his help. This summary is limited to the reviewed distinction.

questions.question: Why does God let people appear to get away with wrongdoing?

answers.summary: Dennis says apparent success does not mean anyone escapes accountability: God keeps records and judges works. He uses Psalm 37 to caution against being troubled by the apparent prosperity of evildoers.

questions.question: Why does God's mercy seat need protection from the likes of Satan?

answers.summary: Dennis interprets Ezekiel 28 as Satan having been assigned to protect the mercy seat but wanting to occupy it instead. He says that place belongs to Christ and gives this as his explanation for the protection imagery.

questions.question: Why does the Chapel use the King James Version?

answers.summary: Dennis recommends it because it can be used with Strong’s Concordance to trace words to the original languages and clarify difficult passages.

questions.question: Why does the name change to Judea in the New Testament?

answers.summary: Arnold attributes the Judah–Judea wording to language and translation and describes Judean as a geographic designation by residence or birth.

questions.question: Why don't you say 'Yah' or 'Yah' when referring to God, but use 'Yeshua' for Jesus?

answers.summary: Arnold says he does use Yahweh and refers to his teaching that the divine name is embedded in Esther’s Hebrew text.

questions.question: Why is Cain not listed as a descendant of Adam?

answers.summary: Dennis says Cain is absent from Adam’s genealogy in Genesis 5 because, in his interpretation, Cain’s father was the serpent. He places Cain’s line in Genesis 4 and says Abel died before having offspring. These ancestry claims remain attributed to Dennis’s interpretation.

questions.question: Why is rapture not a Bible word according to Dennis?

answers.summary: Dennis attributes rapture teaching to human tradition rather than God’s Word. This short reply gives no further exposition.

questions.question: Why is the least in heaven greater than John the Baptist?

answers.summary: Dennis contrasts John’s flesh condition with heavenly spiritual existence, citing the statement that flesh and blood cannot inherit God’s kingdom.

questions.question: Why might a large-print Strong’s lack the entry for again in John 3:3?

answers.summary: Dennis directs the listener to the edition’s appendix-number supplement and says the word means from above. He advises checking the front cover or requesting the missing supplement.

sources.lesson: I & II Samuel 30:23 - 1:9; I & II Samuel 30:23 - 1:9

questions.question: Why might relatives listen during the Millennium, and what are the seven days?

answers.summary: Dennis interprets Ezekiel 44 as allowing the elect to help immediate relatives. He thinks seeing their participation in the first resurrection may change relatives’ attitudes; he distinguishes the thousand-year period from the seven-day cleansing before returning to the temple.

questions.question: Why might someone cry easily at spiritual songs or others’ experiences?

answers.summary: Dennis suggests the listener is compassionate and sensitive, and says he has noticed compassion among God’s elect.

questions.question: Why pray in Jesus’ name?

answers.summary: Dennis says Jesus taught prayer to the Father. In his understanding, praying in Jesus’ name identifies the petitioner as a Christian claiming Christ’s promises. He also warns against praying merely to be seen by other people.

questions.question: Why was Thomas called the Twin?

answers.summary: Arnold says Thomas was called the Twin because he was a twin and explains Didymus in John 11:16 as twin.

questions.question: Why were false worshippers punished for making a golden idol if there was no law without Moses?

answers.summary: Arnold rejects the premise that no divine command existed before Moses, pointing to God’s instruction to Adam and Eve in the garden.

questions.question: Why were spies sent into Canaan if God had already described the land?

answers.summary: Dennis says the people doubted God and petitioned Moses, who petitioned the Lord. He directs the listener to Deuteronomy for the circumstances behind the scouting mission.

questions.question: Why would Dennis not give a listener names of nearby Chapel students?

answers.summary: Dennis cites confidentiality and safety. He mentions voluntary contact through Chapel bumper stickers but warns listeners to be careful when meeting strangers.

questions.question: Why would God need a vehicle in Ezekiel’s vision?

answers.summary: Dennis interprets Ezekiel’s vision as God bringing His throne to earth to communicate with Ezekiel. He suggests the vehicle relates to transporting the entire throne rather than implying God otherwise needs transportation.

questions.question: Why would it take 1,000 years for the Lord's day, especially with spiritual bodies?

answers.summary: Dennis Murray explains that if you take the thousand years literally, it might seem like a long time. However, in spiritual bodies, time has very little significance. He points to 2 Peter 3:8, where one day with the Lord is as 1,000 years, and 1,000 years as one day.

questions.question: Why would someone agree to be a king’s cupbearer despite the danger?

answers.summary: Dennis describes it as a highly trusted position with closeness to the king and potential privileges, citing Nehemiah.

questions.question: Will a period of peace necessarily precede Christ’s return?

answers.summary: Dennis rejects the proposed guarantee and cites wars and rumors of wars, saying he expects true peace with Christ’s return.

questions.question: Will a person remember the circumstances of death?

answers.summary: Arnold says God remembers and that the person does not forget the circumstances if they were known.

questions.question: Will a truck driver retain their ability to drive after receiving a spiritual body?

answers.summary: Dennis does not expect truck driving to continue unchanged in spiritual life and points to 1 Corinthians 15:52 and Zechariah 14:12 for the change.

questions.question: Will angels be visible when they come?

answers.summary: Arnold answers yes, explaining that angels can be seen when present in the same dimension.

questions.question: Will anyone still be alive when everyone changes to spiritual bodies?

answers.summary: Dennis says yes: people will be alive in spiritual bodies, with no flesh remaining at Christ’s return.

questions.question: Will Christ return in a cloud or on a white horse?

answers.summary: Dennis interprets the cloud as an angelic multitude and says it is compatible with Christ riding the white horse in Revelation. He expects an accompanying army that includes departed relatives. He does not separately answer whether every nation sees Him simultaneously.

questions.question: Will Christians recognize Antichrist?

answers.summary: Dennis warns that many will wrongly recognize him as Jesus Christ and be deceived.

questions.question: Will everyone have changed bodies in the millennium, and what is Sabbath rest?

answers.summary: Dennis says all bodies change but some people remain spiritually dead through the millennium. He then identifies Christ as Sabbath rest to rely upon daily.

questions.question: Will God be upset with me if I forget what I learned due to my learning disability?

answers.summary: Dennis cites Luke 12:48 and says God knows people’s abilities and limitations. He expresses his belief that God values a disabled listener’s effort and explains that teachers are provided to help people learn. His reassurance does not require perfect recall.

questions.question: Will God forgive me for not taking care of my kids during my divorce?

answers.summary: Dennis says sincere repentance can bring forgiveness for failing to care for one’s children and emphasizes accepting forgiveness rather than permanent self-condemnation.

questions.question: Will God hold difficulty remembering Scripture against someone affected by injury or medication?

answers.summary: Dennis says God knows a person’s capabilities and limitations. He does not condemn prescribed medication, while cautioning that some pain medicines can be addictive.

questions.question: Will God remember children who do not enter eternity?

answers.summary: Dennis says he cannot answer whether God will remember them. He points instead to the promise that sorrow and pain pass away and affirms his belief that God will not suffer sorrow in eternity.

questions.question: Will God’s enemies be finally destroyed before the millennium?

answers.summary: Dennis distinguishes spiritual deadness from flesh death and final death of the soul. He places final judgment and the second death after the millennium rather than treating people presently called dead as already annihilated.

questions.question: Will God’s Word change when Satan is destroyed?

answers.summary: Dennis says God’s Word does not change, regardless of Satan’s presence. He interprets the passing of heaven and earth as an earth-age transition, with the earth remaining the future location of God’s throne.

questions.question: Will my husband be okay in paradise even though he didn't yet know that Satan comes to earth first?

answers.summary: Dennis reassures the listener that if her husband died believing in Christ, he is saved. He distinguishes that from the danger of deception for people still living in flesh when the antichrist comes.

questions.question: Will our appearance resemble the alien pictures a listener sent?

answers.summary: Dennis reassures the listener that people will not resemble the pictured spacemen. He appeals to Genesis 1:26 and says people look like those in whose image God made them.

questions.question: Will people be in flesh during the final battles named in this question?

answers.summary: Dennis says the battles he discusses occur after Christ returns, so people will be in spiritual bodies rather than flesh.

questions.question: Will people expecting a rapture recognize Antichrist when no rapture happens?

answers.summary: Dennis warns that Antichrist’s supernatural miracles and healing of the political beast’s deadly wound will be convincing. He advises planting seeds without assuming one can force relatives to understand.

questions.question: Will people other than God’s elect be present when Antichrist arrives?

answers.summary: Dennis says yes, and says many will mistake Antichrist for Jesus. He identifies those written in the Lamb’s book of life as the exception to worldwide deception.

questions.question: Will places like the mountains of Colorado be totally remade on earth in the end times?

answers.summary: Pastor Dennis Murray says God will remake the earth, wiping away tears and sorrow, and replacing all things with something much better, as described in Revelation chapter 21, verses 1-4.

questions.question: Will Satan be here before World War III or after?

answers.summary: Dennis says he does not expect a World War III and stresses that Satan appears before Christ returns. This is his prediction in the recording, not an independently verified forecast.

questions.question: Will Satan come from a country such as Russia?

answers.summary: Dennis says Satan comes from heaven, where he presently is, rather than from an earthly country.

questions.question: Will Shepherd’s Chapel need to announce Antichrist’s arrival?

answers.summary: Dennis says the listener will not need a special announcement from the ministry. He expects widespread broadcasts claiming Christ has returned, with those not in the Lamb’s book deceived.

questions.question: Will souls come out of graves at the last trumpet?

answers.summary: Dennis teaches that souls already return to God at death. He distinguishes the Gospel account of opened graves as a sign of Christ’s victory and says those still living change from flesh when Christ returns.

questions.question: Will spiritual bodies need sleep?

answers.summary: Dennis does not give a definite answer. After joking about a meal and nap, he says rest is in Christ and suggests sleep is possible, relating spiritual life to angels and their food.

questions.question: Will temperatures change when Satan is on earth?

answers.summary: Dennis says he does not expect a difference, citing God’s promise of continuing heat and cold, seasons, and day and night while the earth remains.

questions.question: Will the elect have food and water while held before Satan?

answers.summary: Dennis expects their needs to be met during imprisonment, adding that God can provide if their captors do not, as in Israel’s wilderness experience.

questions.question: Will the four wheels found in Ezekiel one be our transportation in heaven? What will our transportation be?

answers.summary: Dennis describes the Ezekiel vehicle’s amber color as polished bronze and recommends Arnold’s Horses of the Bible study. He does not give a clear, detailed answer about the listener’s own future transportation; the recommendation is kept separate from such a promise.

questions.question: Will the Lord let us know who the anti-Christ is and how not to serve the wrong one?

answers.summary: Dennis points to Matthew 24, Mark 13 and Luke 21 for warnings about antichrist pretending to be Jesus.

questions.question: Will the old flesh body come out of the grave for eternity?

answers.summary: Dennis says the spirit returns to God at death and the old flesh is no longer needed. He distinguishes the people coming from graves after the crucifixion as a one-time sign of Christ defeating death.

questions.question: Will the third heaven and earth age also pass away?

answers.summary: Dennis says no, identifying it as the never-ending kingdom, while distinguishing the passing of earlier ages.

questions.question: Will the two witnesses be in Jerusalem the whole time they are here on earth?

answers.summary: Arnold says Jerusalem is where the two witnesses die but does not confine all their activity to that location.

questions.question: Will the two witnesses stay in Jerusalem or move about?

answers.summary: Dennis says they will be where God’s elect are and interprets the two sons of oil as conveying truth to the elect.

questions.question: Will there be babies in heaven, or are spiritual bodies the same age?

answers.summary: Dennis describes spiritual bodies as young adults and says physical age differences do not apply to them.

questions.question: Will this earth age end even if people change their ways?

answers.summary: Dennis says this age will end and distinguishes the millennium from the eternity that follows. He describes an age as a period of time rather than the physical world itself.

questions.question: Will today’s technology be used after Christ returns?

answers.summary: Dennis says he does not think so. He speculates that future technology will far exceed human inventions and contrasts it with present equipment that fails or wears out.

questions.question: Will we be able to see our pets again after they have passed away? Please give me scripture from the Bible.

answers.summary: Dennis appeals to Isaiah 11:6 and interprets animals there as being in spiritual bodies. Asked whether people will see their pets, he says he believes so, retaining that qualification rather than presenting a guarantee.

questions.question: Will we be delivered before the two witnesses? Will we be delivered up before the two witnesses or after?

answers.summary: Dennis places being delivered up after the two witnesses have appeared and after the antichrist is present. He allows that the witnesses could still be teaching the elect while some are delivered, citing Revelation 11.

questions.question: Will we be in flesh bodies when the two witnesses appear and will we see them on television as a world news event?

answers.summary: Arnold expects the two witnesses to become publicly known and to lead the elect; he treats television coverage as probable rather than certain.

questions.question: Will we live on earth or in heaven?

answers.summary: Dennis distinguishes returning to the Father at death from eternity, when he says God’s throne will be on earth.

questions.question: Will we retain our age at death in heaven?

answers.summary: Dennis says age and time are not relevant to spiritual bodies. He expresses his belief that people will appear as young adults, approximately Christ’s age at crucifixion, rather than retaining old age.

questions.question: Will we see God renew the heaven and earth?

answers.summary: Dennis expects those who enter eternity to see the renewed heaven and earth in Revelation 21 and distinguishes them from those destroyed in Revelation 20.

questions.question: Will we still be in our Earthly bodies when we are delivered up before the synagogues of Satan?

answers.summary: Arnold says the elect are still in flesh bodies when delivered up and refers to Mark 13 and Luke 21.

questions.question: Would a believer share a spouse’s sin if the spouse followed the one-world system?

answers.summary: Arnold says each person is accountable for their own conduct and says accepting food brought by the spouse is not itself a sin.

questions.question: Would a caregiver buying necessities for me mean I worship Antichrist?

answers.summary: Dennis says arranging purchases through a caregiver does not itself amount to worship. He emphasizes refusing Antichrist worship and trusting God to provide His elect with what they need.

questions.question: Would Abraham have gone through with sacrificing his son, Isaac, had the angel of the Lord not stopped him?

answers.summary: Dennis says he thinks Abraham would have completed the sacrifice and points to Abraham’s faith in Hebrews 11. He treats the episode as a type of the sacrifice of God’s Son and emphasizes that the Lord provided the ram.

questions.question: Would Shepherd’s Chapel issue a pastor’s certificate to a nonlocal listener?

answers.summary: Dennis says the ministry ordains only local pastors because it cannot supervise what distant applicants teach under its name.

questions.question: Would the wine Jesus turned water to make a person drunk if abused?

answers.summary: Dennis Murray states that wine will make you drunk if you drink too much in a short period of time. He explains that the wine Jesus turned water to was most definitely fermented and therefore intoxicating.

questions.question: Would you explain the Scripture where He says, 'If you forgive not those that have wronged you, neither can God forgive you your trespasses,' in Mark 11:25-26.

answers.summary: Dennis Murray explains that forgiving others is necessary to be forgiven by God, but clarifies that forgiving does not mean forgetting. He emphasizes that forgiving someone who has wronged you takes time to rebuild trust, and that forgiving yourself is also important as God has already forgiven your sins. He warns that bringing up past sins repeatedly shows a lack of belief in God's forgiveness.
